column9: All three checks positively confirm the finding. The two strings differ only in markdown table-cell padding whitespace (`diff` after `tr -s ' '` is identical), which is not a paraphrase.  METHOD CAUTION: my first fetch used the generic filename `hooks.md` in the shared scratchpad and was overwritten mid-analysis by another process — the 883-line SDK page silently became the 3173-line main Hooks reference, briefly making `DirectoryAdded` appear nonexistent. Re-fetched twice to distinct filenames, identical md5 (450577f8dc11d660071fac7c31c3eb14) both times, before trusting the result.  (2) THE CLAIM'S PREMISE HOLDS. `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md` (3173 lines, "# Hooks reference") has ZERO `DirectoryAdded` hits and enumerates exactly 30 events. The SDK page lists those same 30 plus `DirectoryAdded` = 31. So "absent from hooks.md's own table" is literally true, and it explains why our doc comments say 30: that count is correct against the main reference page and simply does not see the SDK page's 31st. `agent-sdk/hooks` is row 30 of `scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv`, so it is a checked Claude contract source under AGENTS.md, not an out-of-scope platform page.  (3) REPO STATE CONFIRMED. `grep -ran DirectoryAdded packages apps` → 0 hits (with `-a`, so NUL-byte files are covered). Cited `hooks-runtime.ts:25` is accurate (the union begins there; 30 names = 28 Claude + `McpServerStart` + `McpToolCall`) and its doc comment does account for exactly two deferrals (`MessageDisplay`, `TeammateIdle`), leaving `DirectoryAdded` unaccounted.  ONE LAYER DOWN — the consequence is real, nothing upstream absorbs it. `mapExternalHookEventName` (`format-adapters.ts:622-646`) resolves in strict order: dialect table → `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL_HOOK_EVENT_REASONS` → warning. There is NO generic fallback. `CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT_MAP` (:123-152) has exactly 28 entries and `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL_HOOK_EVENT_REASONS` (:99-102) exactly 2, so a Claude plugin declaring a `DirectoryAdded` hook falls through to `plugin.format.unknown_hook_event` — reported as a typo rather than as a recorded deferral, which is the opposite of the design intent stated at :634-635 ("A documented-but-unemitted event is a deferral, not an unknown name").  ONE LAYER UP — not an owner decision, not a product difference, not a sibling-subsystem mixup. inert-worklist §3 item 5 IS about `hooks-runtime.ts`, but it scopes "do not revive" to the dead executor (`PluginHookRuntime`/`runHooks`/`parseHookOutput`/`createHookRegistryFromProjection`) and explicitly preserves `PluginHookEventName` because three production files import it — verified at `hooks-automation.ts:47` and `format-adapters.ts:11`. And no name confusion: `CwdChanged` is a distinct SDK-page row (:179) that we DO map (`format-adapters.ts:143`), separate from `DirectoryAdded` (:181).  CORROBORATION: `changelog.md:20` independently announces it — "Added `DirectoryAdded` hook that fires after `/add-dir` or the SDK `register_repo_root` control request registers a new working directory mid-session" — so two Claude doc pages carry the event, not one.

column9: All three checks confirm the finding, and no upstream/downstream layer rescues it.  (1) The quoted sentence exists verbatim at hooks.md:1082: "In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), Setup hooks receive a `trigger` field set to either `\"init\"` or `\"maintenance\"`:". The firing rule is also verbatim at :1061 — "Fires only when you launch Claude Code with `--init-only`, or with `--init` or `--maintenance` in [non-interactive mode](/docs/en/headless) with the `-p` flag. It doesn't fire on normal startup." — and the matcher table at :1063-1067 maps `init` -> `claude --init-only`/`claude -p --init`, `maintenance` -> `claude -p --maintenance`.  (2) packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:107 says exactly what was claimed: `await options.emit('Setup', { hook_event_name: 'Setup', source: 'pi-runtime', lifecycle_version: 1 })`, inside `pi.on('session_start', ...)` behind a `sessionStarted` once-guard. A `grep -a` for `'Setup'` across packages/ and apps/ shows this is the ONLY Setup emitter in the repo — no host-side emitter supplies a `trigger`.  (3) Layer up: the frozen contract row at packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:38 declares Setup as `kind: 'observational'`, `terminalDelivery: 'once-per-session'`, `redactedPayload: ['source', 'lifecycle_version']` — the absence of `trigger` is baked into the versioned contract, not an oversight at the emitter. apps/cli/src/index.ts has no `--init-only`, `--init`, or `--maintenance` flag at all. Layer down: the two same-named restriction sets are about hook TYPES, not gating — CLAUDE_RESTRICTED_LIFECYCLE_EVENTS (format-adapters/claude.ts:152) and LIFECYCLE_RESTRICTED_HOOK_EVENTS (automations/types.ts:152) only limit Setup/SessionStart to `command`+`mcp_tool` handlers, and format-adapters.ts:124/183/200 maps an imported Claude plugin's `Setup` hook straight through to the Nessy `Setup` event. packages/shared/src/automations/conditions.test.ts:661-668 asserts the consequence directly: `matcherMatchesSdk(claude('init'), 'Setup', {source: 'pi-runtime'})` is `false` while `claude('*')` is `true` — i.e. an imported Setup hook is catch-all and fires every session.  Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions). Not a rebrand, corporate-gateway, or dropped-subscription product difference either.  It IS a gap the fork has already recorded and deliberately deferred — but recorded is not closed. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-inert-unit-b.md:24 tables it as "**no counterpart**"; :311 says "`Setup` carries `source` (doc: `trigger`)"; :322 says "Nessy's `Setup` fires every session start (Claude's only under `--init-only` / `-p --init` / `-p --maintenance`)" — both under the heading "Propagation found — reported, not fixed", with register category at :289 "documented, not implemented — Nessy has no --init/--maintenance launch mode". Shipped code carries the same reason at packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:347 (MATCHER_INERT_AGENT_EVENTS) and emits a registration-time `plugin.hooks.matcher_never_matches` warning. Real consequence: a Claude plugin's Setup hook, whose documented purpose is "one-time dependency installation or scheduled cleanup that you trigger explicitly from CI or scripts", runs on every Nessy Pi session start.

Both execution authorities use it: the direct spawn (`hook-command.ts:737`) and the host's sandboxed runner (`packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4488`, whose own comment says "One builder for both execution authorities"). So an imported Claude hook doing `input=$(cat); jq -r .error` gets null.  - Layer up (the emit path): `emitAutomationEvent` → `dispatchAutomationAgentEvent` (`automations/lifecycle-hook-dispatcher.ts:24`) → `AutomationSystem.executeAgentEvent` (`automation-system.ts:629`) pass `input` through untouched; nothing maps `error_code` → `error`.  - Absence checks run with `grep -a`: `error_details` has ZERO occurrences anywhere in `packages/` or `apps/` outside build `dist/` bundles — no producer, no type field (`automations/types.ts` declares `error?`, `error_code?`, `last_assistant_message?` but no `error_details`). `last_assistant_message` has a producer only for `Stop` (`pi-agent.ts:7304-7306`) and `SubagentStop`; `emitStopFailureHookOnce` takes only a code string, so the API error text available at all three call sites (`pi-agent.ts:6760`, `:6800`, `:6803`) is never forwarded.  - Sibling-subsystem check: the one place `error` DOES arrive is the Claude-SDK backend, where the SDK itself builds the input and `buildSdkHooksForConfig` (`plugins/hooks-automation.ts:1644-1648`) spreads it verbatim — which is exactly why `getMatchValueForSdkInput` keeps the `?? input.error` fallback. That path is not ours to emit, and `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` is off by default. The finding is correctly scoped to Nessy's own emitter. One layer down — the second emitter does not rescue it.** `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6423` (the host-side `runPiPromptGate`) re-emits the event so a block can be honoured before `send({type:'prompt'})`, and it is deliberately kept "byte-identical" to the bridge's shape: `{ hook_event_name: 'UserPromptExpansion', source: 'pi-before-agent-start', lifecycle_version: 1 }`. No producer anywhere supplies the five documented fields.  **3b. One layer up — the matcher confirms the consequence.** `packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:161` `getMatchValueForSdkInput` has case arms for 17 events; `UserPromptExpansion` is **not** among them, so it hits `default: return ''` (with the reason spelled out at utils.ts:233-234). `UserPromptExpansion` is also **not** in `MATCHERLESS_AGENT_EVENTS` (utils.ts:260-269), so `matchesBasePredicate` (utils.ts:286) does not short-circuit to `true` — a narrowing matcher is regex/exact-compared against `''` and never fires. But the callback then re-runs `executePluginHookAutomations` → `pluginMatcherMatches` → `matcherMatchesSdk` → the same `''`, so the hook is dropped on the second pass. Independently recorded at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md:62` ("the Claude-SDK path re-enters the same check … so it is not an escape"). Additionally `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` defaults **off** and Pi is the shipped default backend, so the Pi bridge is the live path.  **Not an owner decision.** The nine dated decisions in `2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 are `SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD`, `availableModels`/`enforceAvailableModels`, `autoMode.classifyAllShell`, `ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops`, `plugins/hooks-runtime.ts`, `SdkMcpServerConfig.required`, `SessionMirrorStore.delete`, `MirrorSessionKey.subpath`/`listSubkeys`, and `listSessionSummaries`/`listSessions`. It goes the other way: the same file lists it in **§2 Live defects → user-visible** (line 62, the "9 matcher-bearing events return `''`" row, sized **large**) and in **§5 as unit U-B**. column5: `Bash(*)` is equivalent to `Bash` and matches all Bash commands. As a deny rule, both forms remove the tool from Claude's context.

column7: `Bash(*)` parses to `{ kind: 'bash', pattern: '*' }` — a pattern matcher, not a tool matcher. Context removal is decided by `isWholeCapabilityDeniedByPermissionDsl`, which only inspects `rule.matcher.kind === 'tool'`, so a `deny: ["Bash(*)"]` leaves the Bash tool definition in the model's context and denies every call it makes instead of hiding the tool. Same for `PowerShell(*)`.
column9: The doc sentence is real, but the claimed consequence is false — this is the repo's canonical false positive: "the identifier really is unwired, but the consequence is false because something upstream already handled it."  1. DOC — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md` line 82: "`Bash(*)` is equivalent to `Bash` and matches all Bash commands. As a deny rule, both forms remove the tool from Claude's context." Not a paraphrase.  2. CITED FILES — the observations are individually true, and both are irrelevant to the claim.    - `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/claude-permission-rules.ts:310` really does return `{ rule: { action, match: { kind: 'bash', pattern: specifier } } }`. But that raw matcher is compiled at `permission-dsl.ts:347` into `{ kind: 'bashPattern', pattern, action }` — the claim stops at the parser and never follows the compile step.    - `permission-dsl.ts:900-905` really is `isWholeCapabilityDeniedByPermissionDsl`, and it really only inspects `rule.matcher.kind === 'tool'`. **But that function has ZERO production callers.** Repo-wide `rg -a 'isWholeCapabilityDeniedByPermissionDsl' . --glob '!node_modules'` returns only its own declaration, one comment reference at :977, and two assertions in `permission-dsl.test.ts:547-548`. It does not decide context removal. The claim named the wrong function.  3. ONE LAYER UP/DOWN — the behaviour is implemented, doc-cited in-code, and wired to the signed manifest.    - The real decider is `isWholeToolDenyForIdentity` (`permission-dsl.ts:930`), whose `case 'bashPattern'` at :951-958 carries the exact quoted sentence as its comment and returns `matcher.pattern.trim() === '*' && identity.permissionName === 'Bash'`.    - It is applied by `filterCapabilityIdentitiesByWholeToolDeny` (`permission-dsl.ts:972`), called in production at `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:1759`, whose result becomes `allowedBindingNames` on the manifest passed to `finalizePiExecutionManifest` — i.e. the tool is removed from the SIGNED manifest the subprocess advertises, not merely gated.    - Positive control, both green (`bun test`, 22 pass / 0 fail / 116 expects): `permission-dsl.test.ts:484` asserts `kept('Bash')` and `kept('Bash(*)')` produce the identical surviving list while `kept('Bash(git *)')` keeps bash; and `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/whole-tool-deny-manifest.test.ts:155` is an `it.each` row literally labelled `'the equivalent Bash(*) form'` that asserts the advertised manifest's `tools[].binding.piName` does NOT contain `bash` and that the gate still denies. Both halves of the doc sentence are enforced, and enforcement plus removal are asserted together so neither substitutes for the other.  4. THE PowerShell TAIL IS DOUBLY UNFOUNDED. The quoted context-removal sentence at :82 is Bash-specific; the PowerShell section at :235-237 says only "a bare `PowerShell` or `PowerShell(*)` matches every command" — it never claims context removal. And there is no PowerShell tool in this harness to remove: `rg -a "permissionName: 'PowerShell'" packages apps` returns nothing, and `harness-tool-descriptor.ts` has no `powershell` hit at all. PowerShell exists here only as a rule dialect (`claude-powershell-rule.ts`), not as an advertised tool.  Not an inert-worklist row and not a fork product difference — `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` has no `Bash(*)`/whole-tool entry. The only places this claim's text appears in the repo are the sweep documents that generated it: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.md:38` and `docs/superpowers/specs/data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json`.

(2) IT IS A RECORDED, DATED, REASONED DEVIATION — not a discovery. Three places already carry it:   - docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-marketplace-entry-authority.md:232, in a section titled "## 6. `plugin-marketplaces.md` rows we do not implement", whose preamble states each row was "Verified against the page as fetched 2026-07-29, not copied from the sweep. Each row was checked in the tree before it was written down."   - docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:184 (generated from that plan's category string).   - docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:696, which already inventories `blockedMarketplaces` among the ~15 managed-only keys under R25.   The recorded reason, verbatim: "S9 implements the allowlist only. On a managed fleet the allowlist is the stronger control, since anything unlisted is already refused, so the blocklist adds reach not safety." column9: The divergence survives the challenge, but two of its evidence claims are wrong and must be corrected before it is used.  LEG 1 — QUOTE: CONFIRMED VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md` -> line 507 contains the claimed text as an exact substring (Python `in` test = True). The claim truncates before the line's trailing `See [`strictPluginOnlyCustomization`](/docs/en/settings#strictpluginonlycustomization)`, which is a truncation, not a paraphrase. Not a refutation.  LEG 2 — CITED FILE:LINE: ONE OF THREE IS WRONG. In `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts`, `:177` really is `allowManagedHooksOnly` and `:203` really is `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`, but `:129` is `readonly allowedMcpServers?: readonly ManagedMcpEntryV1[]` — an MCP allowlist, not a managed-only lock. And the OUR STATE sentence "We implement the per-surface locks allowManagedHooksOnly, allowManagedMcpServersOnly and allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly" is false for the middle one: `grep -ran allowManagedMcpServersOnly --include=*.ts` returns 6 hits, ALL of them prose inside comments (`sandbox-settings.ts:357,459`, `permissions-config.ts:1007`, `managed-only-locks.test.ts:236`, `managed-policy.ts:737,1321`) — it is not a field of `ManagedPiPolicyV1` and not in `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS`. Its absence is a recorded decision with a reason: `docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:93` files it under "What we do not implement" with category `inapplicable — one tier carries these keys` — "Nessy has no user, project or local settings surface that carries allowedMcpServers or deniedMcpServers at all... Adding the key would declare a lock that enforces nothing."  LEG 3 — GREP -> 0 IS FALSE, BUT THE CONSEQUENCE SURVIVES. `grep -ran strictPluginOnlyCustomization packages apps` returns 5 hits, not 0: `packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js:333323` and the four copies at `apps/electron/{,dist/}resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js`. All are gitignored build output (`git check-ignore` confirms `.gitignore:7:dist`) carrying a vendored zod schema: `strictPluginOnlyCustomization: preprocess(t => Array.isArray(t) ? t.filter(r => hU.includes(r)) : t, union([boolean, array(enum(hU))])).optional().catch(undefined)` with `hU = ["skills","agents","hooks","mcp"]`. The string occurs EXACTLY ONCE per bundle, so the parsed field is never read by name — declared, not enforced. No first-party `.ts`/`.tsx` file references it (only docs do). So the identifier claim is sloppy but the behavioural claim stands.  LAYER UP / LAYER DOWN — NO UPSTREAM HANDLER, NO SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM CONFUSION. `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` (managed-policy.ts:501-534) is 34 keys and none of them locks skill or agent ORIGIN; `refuseUnknownKeys` (:727-733) drops any unknown key with disposition `stripped`, so an admin document carrying `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` is silently degraded rather than honoured. There is no second settings surface that could absorb it: the only `managed-settings.json` references are `managed-env.ts:27` (a comment), `self-config-deny.ts:74-87` (deny-path computation) and `managed-policy-loader.ts:57` (our `managed-policy.json` sits in the same directory). The surfaces the doc names really do load from user/project scope here: project skills at `packages/shared/src/skills/storage.ts:485-486,523-524` (`PROJECT_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR`) and project subagents at `packages/shared/src/capabilities/project-contribution-detect.ts:215` (`.claude/agents`) — gated only by the per-user trust/consent flow, which is a user decision, not an admin lock. Plugin-scope keys (`allowedPluginKeys`/`deniedPluginKeys`/`enabledPlugins`) narrow plugins, never user or project skills/agents.  OWNER-DECISION CHECK — NOT ONE OF THE NINE. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 lists SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions. `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` is not among them.  PRODUCT-DIFFERENCE CHECK — DOES NOT APPLY. This is not a dropped subscription flow, a gateway retarget or a rename. The fork invests heavily in exactly this surface (a 34-key managed Pi policy with `allowManagedHooksOnly`, `disableAllHooks`, `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`, `sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly`, `sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly`), so a missing admin lock is a gap in a surface we are deliberately building, not a scoped-out one.  PRIOR-REGISTRATION — PARTIAL, AND WORTH KNOWING. The gap is already noted in three places but never as a closed decision: `docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:95` records only the `mcp` surface as `documented, not implemented — a settings key we do not carry`; `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:46` lists it among admin locks and `:559` (R30) among skill/agent visibility controls; `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-rules-tier.md:34` notes it has no `rules` surface. It appears in neither `2026-07-29-deviation-register.md` nor `2026-07-30-parity-report.md`, so the skills/agents half has no owner ruling.

column9: The doc quote is genuine (verbatim at `permissions.md:472`), but the finding fails checks 2 and 3.  **1. It is a dated, recorded deviation decision with a stated reason — not a defect.** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-deviation-unit-5.md:115` carries the row under "## Deviations recorded": Subject `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` (`settings.md:411`, `sandboxing.md:239`), Category `documented, not implemented — the documented default 'true' is conditioned on 'sandbox.enabled', an opt-in Nessy has no analogue of: supervised-process isolation here is unconditional, so porting the default verbatim would auto-approve EVERY Bash command. Honouring the key needs the opt-in surface it hangs off plus the four carve-outs at sandboxing.md:124–:127 … A settable-but-unread key would be the exact "declared on one path, enforced on another" defect this series keeps finding, so no key was added`. It is not one of the nine in `2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3, but it is the same class of artifact and lives in the mechanism AGENTS.md names as where a deviation's reason lives.  **2. The cited evidence names the wrong subsystem.** `packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts` defines `SandboxSettingsV1`/`resolveSandboxSettings`, which govern **supervised-process isolation** — threaded to `ProcessSupervisor` (`packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation.ts:39`, `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/sandbox-permission-rules.ts`, `managed-policy.ts:1360`). `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` is a **Bash-tool permission** key. Its Nessy analogue site is the pre-tool-use permission path (`packages/shared/src/agent/core/pre-tool-use.ts` step 5h + `core/bash-seatbelt.ts`), not this schema. Asserting absence from `sandbox-settings.ts` is the sibling-subsystem mirror the audit history warns about.  **3. One layer down, the consequence is false by design.** `pre-tool-use.ts:1475-1476`: "Opt-in macOS seatbelt Bash sandbox. **Permission and prompt decisions use the original command, while actual execution receives this wrapped form.**" Sandboxing in Nessy is an execution-wrapping step applied *after* and *independently of* the approval decision — sandbox status is deliberately never an input to the prompt. Two facts make importing Claude's coupling actively unsafe here: the sandbox is opt-in and **default off** (`storage.ts:1124 getMacosSeatbeltBashSandboxEnabled()` → `?? false`, read at `claude-agent.ts:1319` and `pi-agent.ts:3801`), and the shipped profile is currently a wildcard — `bash-seatbelt.ts:87 SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD: boolean = true` returns `(allow default)` under a dated owner decision (2026-07-21, reaffirmed 2026-07-29). An `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed=true` analogue would auto-approve every Bash command behind a sandbox that permits everything.  **4. The stated evidence is also factually wrong on its own terms.** `grep -ran autoAllowBashIfSandboxed packages apps` returns **5 hits, not 0** — `packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js:350289`, `apps/electron/{dist/,}resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js` (all gitignored build bundles; `.ts` source is genuinely 0, so the conclusion survives but the quoted command does not). And the schema is not "only `excludedCommands`, the four filesystem root lists and the two domain lists": `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS` (`:172-180`) is `excludedCommands, deniedReadRoots, deniedWriteRoots, additionalWritableRoots, allowUnsandboxedCommands, network, filesystem` — three flat root lists, plus `filesystem.{disabled,allowRead,allowManagedReadPathsOnly}` (`:183`) and `network.{deniedDomains,allowedDomains,allowManagedDomainsOnly}` (`:182`). The "only" list erases `allowUnsandboxedCommands`, which is itself a documented Claude sandbox key we **do** implement (`:75`, boolean-AND across layers).

It sits in the `### Managed-only settings` table under `## Managed settings`. `disableSideloadFlags` is line 501 of the same table. No paraphrase. This part does not refute.  **2. This fork accepts none of those four flags. `parseArgs` at `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/apps/cli/src/index.ts:51-165` enumerates every accepted flag (`--url`, `--token`, `--workspace`, `--timeout`, `--json`, `--tls-ca`, `--send-timeout`, `--source`, `--mode`, `--output-format`, `--json-schema`, `--no-cleanup`, `--disable-spinner`/`--no-spinner`, `--verbose`/`-v`, `--safe-mode`, `--server-entry`, `--workspace-dir`, `--provider`, `--model`, `--api-key`, `--base-url`, `--help`/`-h`, `--version`, `--validate-server`); the `default:` arm pushes any unknown `-`-prefixed arg into `rest`, which never reaches a plugin/agent/MCP loader. The only other `process.argv` consumers repo-wide are `--generate-token` and `--allow-insecure-bind` (`packages/server/src/index.ts:49,347`) and `--debug` (`apps/electron/src/main/logger.ts:16`). Meanwhile we *do* honour `strictKnownMarketplaces` (`managed-policy.ts:141`, matched by `managed-marketplace-entries.ts:612-616`). So the bypass the setting exists to close cannot occur — this is trap shape 3 from the inert-worklist §4: the identifier really is unwired, and the consequence is false because the surface it guards does not exist.  **3b. column5: The `content` array in a tool result accepts `text`, `image`, `audio`, `resource`, and `resource_link` blocks. You can mix them in the same response.
column6: A tool result's `content` array may carry `resource` and `resource_link` blocks in addition to text/image/audio, and the runtime converts a resource link into a text block naming the link.
column7: The MCP proxy's result reducer handles exactly `text`, `image` and `audio`. A `resource` block's payload (`resource.text` / `resource.blob`, the actual content) and a `resource_link` block are both skipped by the loop, so in any result that also contains a text block the resource content is silently lost — the `JSON.stringify(result)` fallback only fires when zero parts were extracted.
column9: Refuted on subsystem mismatch — the exact recurring false positive AGENTS.md names ("identically-named symbols in a sibling subsystem"). The quote and the code are both accurate; the mapping between them is not.  (1) QUOTE: verbatim at custom-tools.md:455. But the finding stopped two sentences early. The full line reads: "…You can mix them in the same response. In TypeScript, THE SDK saves audio blocks to disk and Claude receives a text block with the saved file path; in Python, THE SDK drops audio blocks from the tool result and logs a warning. THE SDK converts resource link blocks to a text block containing the link's name, URI, and description." Every conversion the sentence promises is attributed to the Agent SDK acting on a handler's return value.  (2) CODE: confirmed. packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:2138-2166 handles only `text` and `image`/`audio`; `resource`/`resource_link` fall through, and `parts.join('\n') || JSON.stringify(result)` fires the raw-JSON fallback only when zero parts were extracted. `grep -ran resource_link` over packages/ and apps/ (NUL-safe, node_modules excluded) returns nothing repo-wide. One layer down, NessyMcpClient.callTool (packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:478-503) forwards the MCP SDK result untouched, so nothing upstream converts the block first.  (3) SUBSYSTEM — the refutation. custom-tools.md governs IN-PROCESS SDK custom tools (`tool()` + `createSdkMcpServer`) and explicitly routes the other case elsewhere at line 859: "To connect to external MCP servers (filesystem, GitHub, Slack) instead of building your own, see Connect MCP servers." mcp-pool.ts IS that external-MCP client pool — the sibling subsystem the page hands off. The surface this page actually governs in our fork is packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:600-633, where every pool tool is wrapped by the SDK's own `tool()` helper; its handler returns `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text: result.content }] }`. A text-only content array is a permitted use of the documented API — the five block types are options a handler MAY return, not an obligation it must satisfy. And because we ship the Claude Agent SDK unmodified, the resource-link→text conversion the sentence describes is present in our runtime for any handler that does return such a block.  There is also no Claude contract on the other side to diverge from: agent-sdk/mcp.md, the page custom-tools.md defers to for external servers, is 900 lines containing zero occurrences of `resource_link`, "resource block", "content block", "content array" or "audio". Claude publishes no documented rule for how a host reduces an external MCP server's result content blocks, so no Claude doc page is violated by mcp-pool.ts's reducer.  Not one of the nine owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3, and not a fork product difference (subscription flows, gateway, rename) — it fails on the doc-mapping, not on either of those.  Residual, offered as an observation rather than a finding: the underlying behaviour is real. An external MCP server returning a text block alongside an embedded `resource` block loses the `resource.text`/`resource.blob` payload, because the non-empty `parts` array suppresses the JSON.stringify fallback. If anyone wants to file that, the contract source is the MCP specification's EmbeddedResource/ResourceLink content types, not agent-sdk/custom-tools.md — and it must be scoped to the MCP client pool, naming both backends (Pi and Claude share the pool), not to the SDK custom-tool surface.

The key is absent because its only security-relevant value is permanently on; adding it could only WEAKEN the boundary.  (4) `credentials` — IMPLEMENTED, AND STRICTER THAN CLAUDE'S. The per-domain proxy layer (R19) is deliberately parked. `socat` occurs in our source only in a shellguard test corpus and two docblocks. A path override for a binary we never spawn is not a gap.  (6) `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` — DATED RECORDED DECISION with a reason, in the deviation register's source plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-deviation-unit-5.md:115, category `documented, not implemented`: "the documented default `true` is conditioned on `sandbox.enabled`, an opt-in Nessy has no analogue of: supervised-process isolation here is unconditional, so porting the default verbatim would auto-approve EVERY Bash command ... A settable-but-unread key would be the exact 'declared on one path, enforced on another' defect this series keeps finding, so no key was added". (Not in inert-worklist §3, which indexes inert identifiers rather than absent keys, but the same class: a decision with a written reason.)  Provenance note: this row is not an independent observation. It is verbatim docs/superpowers/specs/data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json:307-309 (duplicated at :3959-3961) — an unchallenged sweep row, which per AGENTS.md is the weakest evidence state. column5: * `npm`, `file`, `directory`: not supported for host pattern matching
column6: `strictKnownMarketplaces` accepts eight source types: `github`, `git`, `url`, `npm`, `file`, `directory`, `hostPattern`, `pathPattern`.
column7: `parseManagedMarketplaceEntry` handles only `github`, `url`, `hostPattern`, `pathPattern`; every other kind hits `default` and returns `managed marketplace allowlist entry declares an unsupported source`. An administrator writing the documented `{ "source": "git", "url": "https://gitlab.example.com/tools/plugins.git" }` has the entry stripped, so that marketplace can never be allowlisted in its documented form.
column9: The quote and the code citation are both accurate; the CONSEQUENCE is false, and I measured it false.  1. QUOTE — verbatim. `settings.md:1008` reads exactly "* `npm`, `file`, `directory`: not supported for host pattern matching". The 8-type enumeration under "All supported source types" (`:934`-`:1013`) is real too. Doc half of the claim stands.  2. CODE — exact. `managed-marketplace-entries.ts:167-207` is `parseManagedMarketplaceEntry`; only `github`/`url`/`hostPattern`/`pathPattern` have cases, and `default:` (`:205-206`) returns ``managed marketplace allowlist entry declares an unsupported source "…"``. Measured against the claim's own example: `{"source":"git","url":"https://gitlab.example.com/tools/plugins.git"}` → `[]`, drop `{at:"strictKnownMarketplaces[0]", reason:'…unsupported source "git"', effect:"stripped"}`.  3. CONSEQUENCE — refuted by measurement (probe at scratchpad `mkt-probe-91fc.test.ts`, 5 pass; repo suite `managed-marketplace-entries.test.ts` 11 pass):    - `{"source":"url","url":"https://gitlab.example.com/tools/plugins.git"}` → **allows that exact marketplace**. `matchesManagedMarketplaceEntry` case `url` (`:584-588`) compares `entry.url === identity.raw`, and `identity.raw` is the byte-identical string the admin/user types at add.    - `{"source":"hostPattern","hostPattern":"^gitlab\\.example\\.com$"}` → allows both `https://gitlab.example.com/tools/plugins.git` and `git@gitlab.example.com:tools/plugins.git`, rejects `gitlab.com`. This is the form BOTH pages prescribe for exactly this case: the bullet one line ABOVE the quoted sentence says "`git`: extracts hostname from the URL (supports both HTTPS and SSH formats)", and `plugins/org.md#allowlist-with-strictknownmarketplaces (was line 771 of the retired plugin-marketplaces page)` says "prefer a `hostPattern` entry over a literal URL so all forms match". The quoted sentence is not evidence that `git` needs its own entry type — it is part of the passage explaining that `hostPattern` IS how `git` sources are admitted.    - `file`/`directory` → `pathPattern`, which `settings.md` itself defines as "regex pattern matched against the `path` field of `file` and `directory` sources". Measured: an anchored pathPattern admits the doc's own `/usr/local/share/claude/acme-marketplace.json` and `/opt/acme-corp/approved-marketplaces`, and rejects a sibling path.    So "that marketplace can never be allowlisted" is false — only the JSON spelling is rejected.  4. DIRECTION — fail-closed, not silent. Measured: the stripped `git` entry leaves an empty allowlist, so the marketplace is BLOCKED, never admitted. A dropped allowlist entry can only narrow. The drop is recorded through `ManagedDropSink` with a reason naming the source, which matches Claude's own documented managed-settings behaviour (`settings.md:186`: "strips that entry, records a warning, and enforces every remaining valid policy").  5. `npm` names a marketplace source Claude itself cannot produce. `plugins/cli-reference.md#plugin-marketplace-add (was line 953 of the retired plugin-marketplaces page)` — the reference for `claude plugin marketplace add <source>` — lists four forms only: "GitHub `owner/repo` shorthand, git URL, remote URL to a `marketplace.json` file, or local directory path". `npm` appears in that page only as a PLUGIN source inside a catalog (§ npm packages, `:392-437`). Nessy's `plugins/source-resolver.ts:51` likewise has no npm branch. An `npm` allowlist entry would grant a marketplace kind neither product can register.  6. The normative matching spec — `plugin-marketplaces.md` § "How restrictions work" `:764-771`, the section this file cites throughout its header — defines matching semantics for exactly four source types: GitHub, URL, hostPattern, pathPattern. Our four are precisely those four.  Not an inert-worklist §3 row (checked all nine — none concerns marketplace source types), and not a brand/gateway product difference. The refutation rests on the measured consequence, not on a recorded decision.

The key's entire documented job (settings.md:266) is to "Reject the `--plugin-dir`, `--plugin-url`, `--agents`, and `--mcp-config` CLI flags at startup, which users could otherwise pass to bypass `strictKnownMarketplaces` for a single run." **Our product accepts none of those four flags.** Positive control for the absence (per the repo's own rule): the same grep enumerates our real flag surface at `apps/cli/src/index.ts:80-138` — `--url`, `--token`, `--workspace`, `--timeout`, `--json`, `--tls-ca`, `--send-timeout`, `--source`, `--mode`, `--output-format`, `--json-schema`, `--no-cleanup`, `--disable-spinner`, `--no-spinner`, `--verbose`, `--safe-mode`, `--server-entry`, `--workspace-dir`, `--provider`, plus `--api-key`, `--base-url`, `--model`, `--name`, `--strict`, `--stdin`, `--validate-server`, `--version`, `--help`. There is no bypass to close, so "not enforced at startup" is not a missing behaviour — it is a control with no attack surface in a desktop app that has no sideload flags. The sentence's operative content ("Enforced on marketplace add and on plugin install, update, refresh, and auto-update, so a marketplace added before the policy was set cannot be used to fetch plugins", "checked before downloading, so they never touch the filesystem") is implemented for the allowlist at `packages/shared/src/marketplace/registry-source.ts:684-703`, whose comment cites the same upstream sentence and gates the single chokepoint where a registry catalog is fetched — covering browse refresh, background auto-update and `upgrade()`'s eager re-stage — and runs before `fetchRegistryCatalog`, i.e. before the clone. (c) Pre-recorded deviation with a stated reason, covering **both** keys in one entry: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-marketplace-entry-authority.md:232` — "S9 implements the allowlist only. On a managed fleet the allowlist is the stronger control, since anything unlisted is already refused, so the blocklist adds reach not safety." Harvested to `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:184`. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in inert-worklist §3, but the same class of artifact — a decision with a recorded reason. The finding's own CLAIMED OUR STATE concedes this ("Recorded as a known deviation in the register"), which makes it a re-report of a closed decision rather than a new divergence. What survives: `blockedMarketplaces` genuinely has no reader, and an admin can pin an allowlist but cannot block a single named source. That narrow absence is real. A per-server approve/reject list IS applied to exactly these records one layer above the cited files.  1. QUOTE — verbatim. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings.md` line 272: "Automatically approve all MCP servers defined in project `.mcp.json` files." (followed by a v2.1.196 clause). `disabledMcpjsonServers` at :263, `enabledMcpjsonServers` at :274. Confirmed.  2. CITED LINES — accurate. `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:995` is `if (context.projectTrustState === 'trusted') {`, and `:1067` is where `.mcp.json` becomes records. `packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:180-217` is `parseMcpServersDocument`, which parses shape only and gates nothing. That half of the claim holds.  3. ONE LAYER UP — REFUTES THE CONSEQUENCE. `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:704-708` filters the native inventory before the resolver ever sees it:      if (record.kind === 'mcp' && !isManagedMcpServerAllowed(managedPiPolicy, {       name: record.logicalName,       ...record.mcpServerIdentity,     })) return false  `mcpServerRecords` emits "One qualified inventory record per declared MCP server (never one per file)" (native-sources.ts:472), so this runs per project `.mcp.json` server, in a trusted project, and drops denied ones. So that "we are ahead" note does not cover this finding — but it is also not the reason the finding fails; storage-runtime.ts:704 is.  Not in `2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 (nine decisions checked: seatbelt wildcard, availableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, three SessionMirrorStore rows — none is this). column5: Unprivileged containers need the nested-sandbox setting described in [Sandboxing troubleshooting](/docs/en/sandboxing#troubleshooting).
column6: Running the sandbox inside an unprivileged container requires the nested-sandbox setting (`enableWeakerNestedSandbox`).
column7: No such key exists in `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS`; `resolveLinuxIsolation` builds an `unshare`/`firejail` profile and fails closed with `process-isolation-unavailable` when the namespace cannot be created, so a supervised session cannot run inside an unprivileged container at all.
column9: Refuted on two independent grounds: it is an already-recorded deviation, and its stated mechanism is wrong.  **1. The doc sentence is real.** `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments.md` line 106 carries the quote verbatim: "You can layer the built-in Bash sandbox inside the container for per-command restrictions. Unprivileged containers need the nested-sandbox setting described in [Sandboxing troubleshooting](/docs/en/sandboxing#troubleshooting)." The setting name is also correct — `sandboxing.md:458` names `enableWeakerNestedSandbox` and explains it makes "the inner sandbox bind-mount the container's existing `/proc` instead" of a fresh one.  **2. The cited code is accurate, as far as it goes.** `packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:172-180` — `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS` holds exactly seven entries (`excludedCommands`, `deniedReadRoots`, `deniedWriteRoots`, `additionalWritableRoots`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands`, `network`, `filesystem`); `enableWeakerNestedSandbox` is absent (verified `grep -ran`, zero hits anywhere in `packages/`). The precondition is present too: our bwrap invocation passes `'--proc', '/proc'` at `packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/filesystem-isolation.ts:304` — precisely the fresh-`/proc` mount the doc says fails in an unprivileged container.  **3. THE REFUTATION — this is an already-recorded deviation, and the "OUR STATE" text is copied from our own register.** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:288` already reads: "**not implemented** — sandbox-environments.md:106 -- \"Unprivileged containers need the nested-sandbox setting\", i.e. enableWeakerNestedSandbox, which makes bubblewrap bind-mount the container's existing /proc instead of a fresh one. We have no such key: resolveLinuxIsolation fails closed with process-isolation-unavailable, so Nessy cannot run inside an unprivileged container at all." That row was harvested from `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-sandbox-network-enforcement.md:191` — item 5 of a nine-row list Task 3 of that plan wrote deliberately, categorising every remaining line of this exact doc page as `not implemented` or `inapplicable`. Per AGENTS.md, a plan's category string is where a deviation's reason lives. It is NOT one of the nine inert-worklist §3 owner decisions (I checked; none of the nine concerns sandboxing keys), but it is a dated, landed, generated-register entry covering this page line-for-line. Our own sweep data already says so: `docs/superpowers/specs/data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json:1030` notes that "`autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` and `enableWeakerNestedSandbox` … carry dated \"documented, not implemented\" decisions in the deviation register."  **4. One layer down, the mechanism is also wrong** — the "consequence is false" shape AGENTS.md warns about. `resolveLinuxIsolation` does *not* reliably "fail closed with `process-isolation-unavailable`" inside an unprivileged container. `resolveTrustedIsolationLauncher` (`packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/trusted-isolation-launchers.ts:23-37`) is a `realpathSync` + `isFile()` + `accessSync(X_OK)` check with **no runtime probe**. So with bwrap installed — the normal case in any container image meant to sandbox — `applyFilesystemIsolation` returns `status: 'enforced'`, and the `if (filesystem.status !== 'enforced') throw` at `linux.ts:49` never fires. The plan is built and the failure lands *later, at spawn*, as bwrap's own "Can't mount proc" error, not as `process-isolation-unavailable`. Only the network leg probes at all (`usableUnsharePath` spawnSync's `unshare -n true`, `network-isolation.ts:27-31`), and even it throws only when firejail is *also* missing.  **5. Sibling-subsystem naming error.** The claim says `resolveLinuxIsolation` "builds an `unshare`/`firejail` profile". Those are the two *network* backends (`network-isolation.ts:39`). The filesystem layer — the one the doc's setting is actually about — is **bwrap-preferred**, firejail-fallback (`filesystem-isolation.ts:263, 313`). Naming unshare/firejail hides the fact that the affected component is exactly bubblewrap.

column5: **Built-in Bash sandbox**: the only approach Claude Code enforces itself. Deliver the `sandbox` settings keys through [managed settings](/docs/en/settings#settings-files), either as a file managed by your MDM or through [server-managed settings](/docs/en/server-managed-settings) on Claude.ai.
column6: The built-in Bash sandbox is the only approach the product enforces itself, delivered through the `sandbox` settings keys in managed settings.
column7: Managed delivery of a `sandbox` block exists and is parsed tolerantly, but the deliverable key set is a strict subset (no `enabled`, `failIfUnavailable`, `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed`, `credentials`, `bwrapPath`, `socatPath`), so the documented enforcement configuration cannot be deployed verbatim.
column9: The quote exists verbatim at sandbox-environments.md:124, and the cited evidence is accurate at the identifier level: sandbox-settings.ts:394 strict-keys the managed `sandbox` block against SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS (:172-180 — excludedCommands, deniedReadRoots, deniedWriteRoots, additionalWritableRoots, allowUnsandboxedCommands, network, filesystem), and none of the six named keys is in it. The CONSEQUENCE is false — the inert worklist's own recurring false-positive #3 ("the identifier really is unwired while the consequence is false, because something upstream already handled it").  The claim truncates line 124, dropping the third sentence — "See Enforce sandboxing with managed settings for the keys to deploy and how to keep developers from widening the policy" — and then measures us against settings.md's full 30-row key table instead of the enforcement config that section actually specifies. That config is sandboxing.md:400-406: {"sandbox":{"enabled":true,"failIfUnavailable":true,"allowUnsandboxedCommands":false}}, plus "Add excludedCommands", "Add sandbox.credentials entries for credential directories such as ~/.aws and ~/.ssh", and the two lock keys.  Measured against that, key by key: - allowUnsandboxedCommands:false — SHIPS, deliverable via managed policy, is a floor the user layer cannot unlock (host-sandbox-settings.ts:46-49), wired at SessionManager.ts:3580 and enforced at the spawn: process-supervisor.ts:467-470 throws `process-isolation-unsandboxed-commands-disallowed`. - excludedCommands — SHIPS, same path (SessionManager.ts:3579, process-supervisor.ts:476-481). - allowManagedReadPathsOnly / allowManagedDomainsOnly (the "keep developers from widening" half) — both SHIP (SANDBOX_FILESYSTEM_KEYS/SANDBOX_NETWORK_KEYS at :182-183). - enabled — no key because isolation is not opt-in here. ProcessSupervisor.start calls resolveProcessIsolation unconditionally for every supervised process (process-supervisor.ts:185); the only two bypasses are the two documented keys above (resolveIsolationDowngrade, :463-482). There is no state in which an admin would need to write `enabled: true`. - failIfUnavailable — no key because there is no warn-and-run-unsandboxed path to suppress. When no backend can express the policy, resolveProcessIsolation THROWS `process-isolation-unavailable:<platform>:<profile>[:<reason>]` with remediation text (isolation-remediation.ts) and the spawn fails. Claude's default is the opposite; the key exists to buy what we do unconditionally. - credentials — no key, but the protection the doc's advice buys is a built-in unconditional floor: credentialDenyRoots(homedir(), CONFIG_DIR) is seeded into the deny layer at host-sandbox-settings.ts:61-66 and names ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.nessy, ~/.netrc, ~/.gnupg, ~/.kube, browser cookie stores (credential-deny-roots.ts:102-136) — i.e. the exact two dirs the doc tells the admin to add. It is deliberately retained even when filesystem.disabled is set (isolation.ts:56-63, sandbox-settings.ts:798-806), and the code cites Claude's own sandboxing.md:271 "There is no built-in credential deny list" as why it composes its own. On this key we are STRICTER than the documented configuration. - bwrapPath / socatPath — a written decision already on disk: managed-composition.ts:56-60, "sandbox.bwrapPath and sandbox.socatPath have no counterpart in our schema; there is nothing to compose for them." socatPath configures Claude's sandbox network proxy, which this fork does not have (our network dimension is a boolean egress denial across three backends — isolation.ts denyNetworkEgress). - autoAllowBashIfSandboxed — a DATED RECORDED DEVIATION, not a defect: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-deviation-unit-5.md:115, category "documented, not implemented", reason "the documented default `true` is conditioned on `sandbox.enabled`, an opt-in Nessy has no analogue of: supervised-process isolation here is unconditional, so porting the default verbatim would auto-approve EVERY Bash command."  Not one of the nine §3 owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md (those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) — but two of the six keys carry equivalent dated decisions in the plans, and three more are absent because their enforcing state is the fork's unconditional floor.  Residual truth worth keeping, and it is narrower than the row: sandbox.credentials.envVars (deny/mask, injectHosts, allowPlaintextInject) has no analogue — our floor denies credential FILES, not secret environment variables — and that half needs network.tlsTerminate we also lack. That is a specific missing capability, not "the documented enforcement configuration cannot be deployed".

column9: The doc quote is genuine and the two code observations are literally true, but the finding is refuted on two independent grounds: it is a dated owner decision already on the tracker, and its stated consequence is already delivered one layer up.  1) QUOTE — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md` line 243 carries the sentence exactly as quoted, in § "Protect credentials". `deny`/`mask`, `injectHosts` and `allowPlaintextInject` are all real (`:267`, `:275`-`:279`, `:293`, `:301`). No refutation here.  2) CODE — LITERALLY TRUE, BUT `:321` IS MISCHARACTERIZED. `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS` (packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:172-180) is `excludedCommands, deniedReadRoots, deniedWriteRoots, additionalWritableRoots, allowUnsandboxedCommands, network, filesystem` — no `credentials`. `grep -ran credentials` on that file returns only `:321` and `:324`; `injectHosts`/`allowPlaintextInject`/sandbox-`envVars` return zero repo-wide. But `:318-327` does not misapply anything: it says "`settings.md:200`'s `sandbox.credentials` row applied to the sub-block we actually have", i.e. a deliberate, argued borrow of the doc's ONLY published nested-block tolerance rule, quoted in full with the reason ("Returning `undefined` for a wholly invalid `network` is what makes the rest of `sandbox` still apply"). The sibling site says so outright — `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:1164`: "Shaped like `settings.md:200`'s `sandbox.credentials` row, which is the doc's only nested-document case". Reading that as a misapplied citation is the reverse of what the comment does.  3) OWNER DECISION — this is R19, parked. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:690` is row R19, status ⏸, scope "Egress proxy and domain policy: HTTP CONNECT + SOCKS5 per session, wildcard allow/deny, first-use approval …, **`mask` mode for named env vars**", marked "**PARKED by owner decision 2026-07-28 — 'нужно всё разрешить, ограничения будут потом'**", with the plan deliberately retained (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-egress-proxy.md`). That plan scopes the whole block: `:15` "there is **no mask/deny path for `credentials.envVars` today** — Task 4 adds `deny` there"; `:31` lands the documented `mask`-without-`tlsTerminate` failure. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:218` carries "R19 — `credentials.envVars` `mask` … Half-shipped, then parked by owner decision — so nothing is live". It is NOT one of inert-worklist §3's nine (those are a different set), but it is an equivalent dated owner decision recorded in three places. More: this exact sweep's sibling row was already dispositioned once — audit `:478` records "the three newer `sandbox` keys and the egress-disclosure item (R19, parked by owner decision)" among findings that "belonged to an existing row or a parked owner decision", and notes the disclosure premise was refuted outright.  4) CONSEQUENCE REFUTED UPSTREAM (trap shape #3). `credentials.files` protection ships, unconditionally, by a different name: `credentialDenyRoots` (packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/credential-deny-roots.ts:96) seeds `deniedReadRoots` at the same isolation boundary via `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/host-sandbox-settings.ts:61`, `managed-policy-resolution.ts:225` and `packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/script-sandbox.ts:83`. Its list includes `~/.ssh` and `~/.aws` — the doc's own two example entries — plus `~/.nessy`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.kube`, `~/.docker`, `~/.npmrc`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.config/gh|gcloud`, `~/.azure`, browser cookie/login stores, and `~/Library/Keychains`. Claude's page states the opposite default at `:271`: "There is no built-in credential deny list, so only the files and variables you list are restricted." So on the `files` half a default Nessy install is STRICTER than a default Claude install; what is missing is the configurability, not the protection. Only the env-var half (`envVars` deny, and `mask`, which needs the TLS-terminating proxy that R19 parked) has no analogue — and that is exactly what R19's plan holds.  Net: the shipped state is deliberate and recorded, one half of the claimed exposure does not exist, and the `:321` half of the evidence describes a documented design choice as an error.

column9: The quote is real and the cited line is real — but the row is a line item inside a dated owner decision, and its stated our-state is factually wrong.  1) QUOTE — VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md` line 324 carries the sentence character-for-character, including the `{/* min-version: 2.1.219 */}` comment. No paraphrase. Confirmed.  2) CITED LINE — ACCURATE. `packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:182` is exactly `const SANDBOX_NETWORK_KEYS = ['deniedDomains', 'allowedDomains', 'allowManagedDomainsOnly'] as const;`. `grep -rani strictallowlist` (with `-a`, so NUL-byte files are covered) over the whole repo returns ZERO production/source hits — only `docs/superpowers/plans/` and the sweep's own JSON. The identifier really is unread. Confirmed.  3) LAYER UP — IT IS A PARKED OWNER DECISION. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:690`, row 8: **R19 ⏸ "PARKED by owner decision 2026-07-28 — «нужно всё разрешить, ограничения будут потом»"**, with the plan deliberately retained "for when restrictions are wanted". That plan is `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-egress-proxy.md`, and `strictAllowlist` is an unchecked task in it at `:26` — verbatim the same contract ("DENY instead of prompt. Honored only from user / managed / CLI `--settings`") the finding restates. Instead of restricting, commit `d214cb63` deliberately OPENED egress (shell moved from the `workspace` profile to `networked`). This is not one of the nine §3 decisions in `2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md`, but it is a dated owner decision of the same class, recorded in the audit rather than the worklist. Audit `:478` already records an earlier finder hitting this same row and being told it belonged to R19.  4) LAYER DOWN — THE PREMISE "INSTEAD OF PROMPTING" HAS NO LOCUS HERE. Claude enforces the host allowlist with a proxy OUTSIDE the sandbox (same page, `:321`). This fork ships no such proxy, so its sandbox egress decision is binary by construction: `sandbox-settings.ts:830` — `export type SandboxEgressDecisionV1 = 'open' | 'denied';` with `:827` "There is no third value, and that is a platform fact rather than a design preference," backed by measured evidence at `:845-873` (Seatbelt rejects `(remote ip "github.com:443")` and even an IP literal with `host must be * or localhost`; `unshare -n`/`firejail --net=none` are whole-namespace; the Windows profile has one `network.enabled` boolean). There is no per-host prompt for a sandboxed command to convert into a deny, so a `strictAllowlist` reader added alone would be inert. The fork's honest substitute already ships and is emitted, not silent: `resolveSandboxNetworkEnforcement` (`:900`) returns every configured `allowedDomains`/`deniedDomains` entry as an `unenforceable` diagnostic naming the reason, consumed in production at `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:200` and `SessionManager.ts:290`; `/doctor` prints `sandboxed-command egress: open` on a default install (audit `:478`).  5) SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM NEAR MISS. The only domain-prompt path that exists is in the PERMISSION layer, not the sandbox layer: `pre-tool-use.ts:1986-1996` prompts only when the Bash base command is literally `curl` or `wget`, checked against a session whitelist (`permission-manager.ts:475/483`). It reads neither `allowedDomains` nor `deniedDomains` and any other binary bypasses it. Wiring `strictAllowlist` there would be trap #4 — right name, wrong subsystem.  6) THE CLAIMED OUR-STATE IS WRONG ON ITS SECOND HALF. "`allowManagedDomainsOnly`, which is managed-only" is false in this fork: `sandbox-settings.ts:599` composes it as `all.some(layer => layer.network?.allowManagedDomainsOnly === true)` — an OR across EVERY layer, deliberately (`:85-87`: "restricts, so it is boolean-OR … the tighter side wins"). Any layer can set it, so the fail-closed lever is strictly more reachable than the row asserts. A row whose our-state is wrong cannot be dispatched as written.

column9: REFUTED — not on the facts, but on the category. The quote and the code reading are both correct; the gap is a dated owner decision recorded in four places, and this exact finding was already filed once and demoted.  **1. Quote — VERBATIM, confirmed.** `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md` (505 lines) carries at **:436** exactly: "To point Claude Code at your proxy, set the proxy ports in [sandbox settings](/docs/en/settings#sandbox-settings):", under § *Custom proxy configuration* (:427), followed by the `httpProxyPort: 8080` / `socksProxyPort: 8081` JSON block. `network.tlsTerminate` is cited separately at :279, :301, :330, :468.  **2. Cited file:line — accurate, both anchors.** `packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:182` is `const SANDBOX_NETWORK_KEYS = ['deniedDomains', 'allowedDomains', 'allowManagedDomainsOnly'] as const;` — none of the three proxy keys. `networkSection()` (:246-250) throws `invalid sandbox network setting: ${key}` on anything else. `:900` is `resolveSandboxNetworkEnforcement`, whose only two returns are `egress: 'denied'` (:906, under `allowManagedDomainsOnly`) and `egress: 'open'` (:914). There is indeed no sandbox egress proxy.  **3. One layer up — the decision is recorded, dated, and quoted in the source file itself.** - **In the code, three lines above the cited :900**: `sandbox-settings.ts:867-868` — "So on every backend we have, outbound network is one bit. The per-domain layer is the egress proxy (R19), **deliberately parked**." The `NO_DOMAIN_FILTER` constant (:870) carries the measured reason: Seatbelt rejects `(remote ip "github.com:443")` with "host must be * or localhost", `unshare -n`/`firejail --net=none` are whole-namespace switches, the Windows profile has one `network.enabled` boolean. - **Parity audit (source of truth), row 8 = R19**, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:690`, status ⏸: "Egress proxy and domain policy: HTTP CONNECT + SOCKS5 per session… **PARKED by owner decision 2026-07-28 — «нужно всё разрешить, ограничения будут потом»**". It records the opposite action being taken deliberately: commit `d214cb63` **opened** egress (shell moved `workspace` → `networked`), with a pinned e2e assertion so a flip back is deliberate. - **The plan is retained, and its contract source is this very section**: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-egress-proxy.md` (14 KB, on disk) — "**Contract source:** `code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md` § "Network isolation", § "Protect credentials", **§ "Custom proxy configuration"**, § "Security limitations"". Its global constraints already specify the `tlsTerminate` behaviour verbatim (:31, :79). - **The three keys were explicitly scoped out, not overlooked**: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-sandbox-network-enforcement.md:171-172` — "Three of the twelve were already recorded elsewhere — … and **`strictAllowlist`/`tlsTerminate`/`httpProxyPort` in `2026-07-28-egress-proxy.md`**". - **`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:218`** — "R19 — `credentials.envVars` `mask` | Cited: substitution requires TLS termination, and the docs themselves specify the failure mode for `mask` without `tlsTerminate` | Half-shipped, then **parked by owner decision** — so nothing is live". - **This finding has already been filed once and demoted.** Audit :475-480: "Three belonged to an existing row or a parked owner decision: … **the three newer `sandbox` keys and the egress-disclosure item (R19, parked by owner decision** — and the disclosure premise was refuted outright: `doctor` prints `sandboxed-command egress: open` on a DEFAULT install, which the finder missed by checking only the `unenforceable` path)." - **The coverage map already carries the verdict**: `2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:163`, row 72 `sandboxing` → ⏸, "1 open: R19".  The sweep's own note (`specs/data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json:1030`) asserts "these six have no recorded decision" — that is the load-bearing error. The decision exists in the audit row, the retained plan, the deviation audit, and a comment 32 lines above the cited line.  **Sibling-subsystem trap, for completeness.** Nessy *does* ship proxy + custom CA + mTLS — but that is **R26**, the app's own outbound trust chain (`apps/electron/src/main/network-proxy.ts`, `packages/shared/src/config/network-*.ts`), a different boundary. `2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:709` flags the conflation explicitly: "Note the deliberate asymmetry with R19, where the *sandbox* egress proxy does offer `sandbox.network.socksProxyPort` — the planner must not conflate them." Naming R26's shipped proxy as coverage here would be equally wrong in the other direction.

column9: The quote is real and the cited line is accurate, but the finding's CONSEQUENCE sentence is false on two of its three limbs and already-recorded on the third.  **1. Quote verified verbatim.** `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md` line 456 carries it exactly: "Set [`allowAppleEvents`](/docs/en/settings#sandbox-settings) to `true` in your user, managed, or CLI settings to allow them." All seven identifiers are real sandbox settings (`settings.md:425-428, 436-438`).  **2. Cited code is accurate.** `packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:172-180` is the closed seven-entry `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS` list (`excludedCommands`, `deniedReadRoots`, `deniedWriteRoots`, `additionalWritableRoots`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands`, `network`, `filesystem`); `:182` and `:183` are the `SANDBOX_NETWORK_KEYS` / `SANDBOX_FILESYSTEM_KEYS` sub-lists. `assertKnownKeys` (`:216-221`) throws on anything else. `grep -ran` over first-party source confirms zero hits for all seven. (The only repo-wide hits are `packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js`, gitignored build output bundling `@earendil-works/*` node_modules — `git check-ignore` exit 0, untracked — and the Codex wire types the finding already names. So the identifier half stands.)  **3. REFUTATION A — the second half of the very line quoted gives a workaround we DO have.** Line 456 does not end where the finding stops reading. Its last sentence: "Alternatively, add the command to `excludedCommands` to run it outside the sandbox." `excludedCommands` is `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS[0]` — the first entry of the exact block cited as evidence — and it is enforced end to end: `SessionManager.ts:3579` -> `process-supervisor.ts:77,476` -> a recorded `downgrade.reason === 'excludedCommands'` receipt (`:211`) and a risky-band prompt (`pre-tool-use.ts:2100-2124`). So the documented workaround for `open`/`osascript` error -600 is available, not unavailable. This is the exact two-sentence-line trap the brief warns about.  **4. REFUTATION B — the Go-tool TLS symptom cannot arise here, and its workaround exists anyway.** Line 455 reads in full: "List these tools in `excludedCommands` to run them outside the sandbox. If you are using `httpProxyPort` with a MITM proxy and custom CA, set [`enableWeakerNetworkIsolation`](/docs/en/settings#sandbox-settings) to `true` instead." Two independent refutations. (i) The primary workaround is again `excludedCommands`, which we have. (ii) What `enableWeakerNetworkIsolation` buys — access to `com.apple.trustd.agent` — Nessy grants UNCONDITIONALLY: `NETWORK_SANDBOX_MACH_SERVICES` (`packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/mach-services.ts:93-98`) lists `com.apple.SystemConfiguration.configd`, `com.apple.TrustEvaluationAgent`, `com.apple.trustd` and `com.apple.trustd.agent`, emitted into every network-capable profile at `filesystem-isolation.ts:210` alongside `(allow network*)` (`networked` and `plugin-mcp`, per `isolation/darwin.ts:41-42`). Our default posture is already the 'weaker' one that setting exists to reach. And `httpProxyPort` does not exist in Nessy at all, so the branch that calls for the setting is unreachable. The claim that this workaround is 'unavailable' inverts the actual state.  **5. REFUTATION C — the third limb is an already-recorded deviation, ruled on earlier in this same sweep.** `enableWeakerNestedSandbox` / unprivileged containers is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:288`, a dated `documented, not implemented` row generated from `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-sandbox-network-enforcement.md:191`, and it is finding f030 of this sweep (already refuted as a recorded decision). The Unix-socket half is register line 175: "sandboxing.md:80 makes the seccomp filter the only thing that blocks Unix domain sockets ... Our bwrap argv passes no seccomp option." Both are recorded reasons, not new defects.  **6. Sibling-subsystem / consequence-vs-identifier errors in the remaining keys.** `network.allowMachLookup` is not absent as a capability — mach-lookup policy is implemented and deliberately narrowed to a probe-derived allowlist (`mach-services.ts:65-71, 93-98`, rationale at `:1-45`, plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-sandbox-mach-and-protected-paths.md`); it is a built-in constant rather than a user key. `network.allowLocalBinding`, `allowUnixSockets` and `allowAllUnixSockets` have nothing to un-block: the darwin networked/plugin-mcp profile emits a blanket `(allow network*)` (`filesystem-isolation.ts:210`), which already permits localhost bind and AF_UNIX connect, and on Linux we install no seccomp filter at all (`grep -ran seccomp` over `packages/session-tools-core/src` -> 0), so the syscall filter those keys switch off does not exist. The non-networked profile's `(deny network*)` denies everything by design; that is the profile's purpose, not a missing knob.  **7. `allowAppleEvents` specifically is a recorded security decision, not an oversight.** `mach-services.ts:6-35` records the probe: a bare `(allow mach-lookup)` let `sandbox-exec -p '<profile>' /usr/bin/pbpaste` return 0, and reached `com.apple.CoreServices.coreservicesd` / `com.apple.lsd.mapdb` — "which is how `open` launches an arbitrary application outside the sandbox." The LaunchServices names are listed under "What is deliberately NOT here." Adding `allowAppleEvents` would re-open precisely the hole that file was written to close. (Checked `2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` section 3: none of the nine owner decisions concerns a sandbox settings key, so this is a plan-recorded decision rather than an inert-worklist one.)

column5: The deny rules resolve symlinks: when a symlink appears at a protected settings file path after startup, the sandbox adds its target to the deny list for the next command, so a linked settings file can't be edited through the link.
column6: The sandbox settings-file write denies resolve symlinks, so a symlink appearing at a protected settings path has its target added to the deny list for the next command.
column7: `selfConfigDenyWriteRoots` builds the deny set lexically; the file contains no `realpath`, `lstat` or symlink handling, so a settings file symlinked out of the protected directory stays writable from inside the sandbox.
column9: REFUTED — textbook "the identifier really is unwired, but the consequence is false because something upstream already handled it".  1. DOC SENTENCE: verbatim, confirmed. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md` line 478 contains the quoted sentence exactly. Reading the WHOLE line matters: it is gated `{/* min-version: 2.1.210 */}` and ends "Before v2.1.210, the deny rules didn't resolve symlinks." So this is a recent Claude addition — and we already match it.  2. CITED FILE: the literal claim about the file is TRUE but irrelevant. `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation/self-config-deny.ts:47` `selfConfigDenyWriteRoots` does build its list with a plain `join`, and `grep -a` confirms the file has no `realpath`/`lstat`/`readlink`/`symlink`. It is a pure, platform-parameterised NAME LIST — canonicalisation is deliberately not its job.  3. ONE LAYER UP — the behaviour is implemented, in the single funnel every backend passes through. In `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation.ts`: - `:313-338` `resolveProcessIsolation` composes the write-deny set and terminates it with `.flatMap(root => denyRootPair(root, 'write'))` — so EVERY root `selfConfigDenyWriteRoots` returns is piped through it, alongside the credential floor, the shared-git roots and the settings-file `deniedWriteRoots`. - `:211-219` `denyRootPair` returns `[lexical, canonical]`, where `canonical = nearestExistingRealpath(resolve(root))`. - `:113-130` `nearestExistingRealpath` is `realpathSync` with an ENOENT walk-up to the nearest existing ancestor (needed precisely because `<workspace>/.claude` and `/etc/nessy` usually do not exist), and an EACCES/EPERM fallback to the path as written. - `:132-152` quotes the claimed sentence VERBATIM in the code comment as the reason both halves exist. We in fact go BEYOND the doc: Claude adds only the target; we keep the path AS WRITTEN too, because `unlink` acts on the link and not its target, so the link cannot be removed and replaced with an ordinary file at the protected name.  4. "for the next command" = per-spawn re-resolution, satisfied. `resolveProcessIsolation` is invoked inside `ProcessSupervisor.start` (`packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:185`), so a link created after startup is re-paired before the next command is spawned.  5. POSITIVE CONTROL, run live on this darwin host — not a profile-text assertion but a real kernel test. `packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation.test.ts:327` ("refuses the protected path, refuses it through a symlink, and leaves a sibling alone") spawns real `/bin/bash` under the composed Seatbelt profile, symlinks `<workspace>/.claude -> <workspace>/linked-claude`, and asserts the write through the link fails with `Operation not permitted`, that `linked-claude/settings.json` was never created, that BOTH `(deny file-write* (subpath …))` entries appear in the profile, and that `rm` of the link itself is refused. A sibling `settings.json` in the same writable root still writes, so this is a deny of one tree and not a retreat to a read-only workspace. Result: `1 pass, 0 fail, 10 expect() calls`. `process-supervisor.test.ts:383,413` assert the same pair contract for the read and write deny paths.  The exact bypass the finding predicts ("a settings file symlinked out of the protected directory stays writable from inside the sandbox") is the scenario this test executes and measures as BLOCKED. Not an inert-worklist §3 owner decision and not a fork product difference — it is simply implemented, one call frame above the cited line.  Minor real nit, not a gap: the JSDoc block at `isolation.ts:132-152` documents `denyRootPair` but physically sits above `readAllowRootPair` (which has its own block at `:154-163`), leaving the actual `denyRootPair` at `:211` uncommented. Cosmetic doc drift only; behaviour is as tested.

column9: All three checks pass; the finding survives. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp.md, line 375 reads in full: "For the streamable HTTP transport, use `\"type\": \"http\"` instead. In `.mcp.json` and other JSON config files, `\"streamable-http\"` is accepted as an alias for `\"http\"`. The programmatic `mcpServers` option accepts only `\"http\"`." The claimed sentence is the middle sentence, character-for-character. The third sentence is the second-half trap and it does NOT reverse the conclusion: it restricts the alias to JSON config files, which is exactly the surface our parser owns. agent-sdk/mcp is row 32 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a Claude contract page, not a Codex/MCP-registry page. (2) CITED FILES CONFIRMED. packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:119 `if (type === 'http' || type === 'sse')`, :144 `if (type === 'ws')`, :163 `if (type === undefined || type === 'stdio')`, :177 `return null` — a closed set with no alias arm; :211 emits `Ignoring ${label} server "${slug}": unsupported MCP server config`. The adapter's closed set is real but the line drifted: it is packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1040 (`rawTransport === 'stdio' || 'http' || 'sse' || 'ws'`), not :1034, which is inside the preceding comment. (3) CONSEQUENCE TESTED SEPARATELY, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. Ran parseMcpServersDocument over two entries in one document: {type:'http',url:...} and {type:'streamable-http',url:...}. Output: only `control_http` survives; warnings = ["Ignoring .mcp.json server \"alias_streamable\": unsupported MCP server config"]. The control proves the rig works, so the absence is a real absence. LAYER UP: no normalizer exists between file and parser. `grep -a` for streamable-http across packages/ and apps/*/src returns zero hits in our own source; the same closed set is repeated independently at codex.ts:905, native-sources.ts:454, plugins/schema.ts:624, mcp-pool.ts:183 and plugins/types.ts:170, so nothing upstream rewrites the value.
