column5: When a tool result is larger than 25,000 tokens, the full output is saved to a file and the tool result is replaced with an error message that names the file path, so the agent can read the output back in portions.
column6: MCP tool results larger than 25,000 tokens are persisted to disk, and the limit is raised with `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS`.
column7: `TOKEN_LIMIT = 12000` is the persist threshold and there is no `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` (or Nessy-prefixed) env reader anywhere. The per-tool `_meta["anthropic/maxResultSizeChars"]` half IS implemented, clamped to the documented 500,000 ceiling.
column9: All three checks confirm the finding. (1) The quoted sentence exists VERBATIM in curl'd https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp.md, line 891, under '### Tool output exceeds maximum allowed tokens'. The whole line is three sentences and the other two reinforce rather than reverse it: 'The SDK applies the same MCP output limit as Claude Code.' before it, and 'Raise the limit with the MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS environment variable.' after it, plus a pointer to /docs/en/mcp#mcp-output-limits-and-warnings 'including how a server can declare a higher per-tool limit'. Cross-checked against code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md: ':1022 Default limit: the default maximum is 25,000 tokens', ':1021 Configurable limit ... MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS', ':1040 up to a hard ceiling of 500,000 characters'. (2) The cited lines say exactly what was claimed: packages/shared/src/utils/large-response.ts:42 'export const TOKEN_LIMIT = 12000' and :57 'export const MAX_DECLARED_RESULT_SIZE_CHARS = 500_000'. (3) Layer up and layer down both hold, and the subsystem is the right one. Layer down: MCP tool results reach the guard at packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:2171 (guardLargeResult inside callTool), which passes maxResultSizeChars from declaredResultSizeChars() reading _meta['anthropic/maxResultSizeChars'] (MCP_MAX_RESULT_SIZE_CHARS_META_KEY, mcp-pool.ts:213; clamp at large-response.ts:620-628) but passes NO contextWindow, so the effective persist threshold on the MCP path is the flat TOKEN_LIMIT of 12000 via tokenLimitFor(undefined) (large-response.ts:141-147, 633). The persist-to-disk shape itself matches the doc (saveLargeResponse -> long_responses/, formatLargeResponseMessage names the absolute path), so the divergence is the NUMBER and the missing override, not the mechanism. Layer up: the other production guard site, claude-agent.ts:1829, passes contextWindow, which can only LOWER the threshold (min(TOKEN_LIMIT, 10% of window), floor 2000) - nothing anywhere raises it to 25000. Absence verified binary-safe with grep -ran across the repo excluding node_modules/.references/dist: MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS appears ONLY in docs (parity audit :1787, r-queue-doc-verification :342, the two doc-sweep JSONs) and in zero source files; no NESSY_-prefixed counterpart exists either, and large-response.ts contains no process.env read at all. This is not a rename artifact: the same file's sibling knob IS ported under the fork prefix (mcp-pool.ts:1959 reads NESSY_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT for CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT), so the pattern exists and this one env var simply has no counterpart. Not an owner decision: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions - none touch MCP output limits. Not a deliberate product difference either (no subscription-flow, gateway or rename involvement). The 12000 value does carry a reason in its own doc comment (lowered from 15k after a base64-heavy result poisoned a session), and 2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:342 flags the area as needing a decision, but neither is a recorded ruling that the user-facing override may be absent.

column5: If you deploy a `managed-mcp.json` file, Claude Code loads only the servers that file defines. Users cannot add, modify, or use any other MCP servers, including plugin-provided servers.
column6: A `managed-mcp.json` file at a system path takes exclusive control: only its servers load, and `claude mcp add` is refused.
column7: No reader for the file at any of the three documented system paths (grep -a for `managed-mcp.json` hits docs and comments only). There is no exclusive-control mode and therefore no way to express the documented "disable MCP entirely" pattern — `deniedMcpServers` blocks only what it names. Recorded in docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:91.
column9: Legs 1 and 2 hold, but leg 3 fails: the finding's load-bearing consequence is false, and it fails in exactly the sibling-list shape AGENTS.md warns about.  (1) QUOTE - VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-mcp.md` (361 lines) line 43, under `## Exclusive control with managed-mcp.json`, carries the claimed text as an exact substring. Reading the WHOLE line: it is three sentences, and the third is "The file also suppresses claude.ai connectors unless you [allow them alongside the managed set](#allow-claude-ai-connectors-alongside-the-managed-set)." That is a truncation, not a paraphrase, and it does not reverse the conclusion. Not a refutation.  (2) ABSENCE - CONFIRMED. `grep -rlacF 'managed-mcp.json' packages apps` returns five files, ALL of them built bundles (`packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js`, `apps/electron/{dist/,}resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js`), and both distinct hit sites are zod `.describe()` prose inside a vendored Claude Code settings schema, not a reader. `grep -rnaF` over `packages/*/src` and `apps/*/src` is empty. No path constant matches `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/`, `/etc/claude-code/` or `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\`, and `grep -rna 'exclusive control|exclusive-control'` over `packages apps` (minus dist) is empty, so the `claude mcp add` refusal string does not exist either. The cited evidence range is real: `managed-policy.ts:1573` is `export function isManagedMcpServerAllowed(...)`, whose docblock at `:1558-1571` cites `managed-mcp.md` § *How a server is evaluated*. So the FIRST half of OUR STATE - no `managed-mcp.json` reader, no exclusive-control mode, no add-time refusal - is true, and it is recorded at `docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:91` under "What we do not implement" with the category `documented, not implemented - a separate deployment channel`.  (3) CONSEQUENCE - FALSE. OUR STATE says "There is no exclusive-control mode and therefore no way to express the documented 'disable MCP entirely' pattern - `deniedMcpServers` blocks only what it names." It examined only the denylist. The instrument for deny-all is the SIBLING list, and the same page documents it: managed-mcp.md:145 - "| `allowedMcpServers` | All servers allowed | No servers allowed | Only matching servers allowed |" for unset / empty array / populated. The vendored Claude schema in our own bundle repeats it: "If empty array, no servers are allowed."  We implement that, and it is tested. `parseManagedMcpEntryList` preserves `[]` (`root[field] === undefined ? undefined : parse(...)`, `managed-policy.ts:1307-1312`, emitted at `:1447`), and `evaluateManagedMcpServer` (`managed-mcp-entries.ts:489-509`) returns `true` only when `allowed === undefined` or something matches - an empty array falls through every branch to `allowed.some(...)` === false. Pinned by `managed-mcp-entries.test.ts:324` (`isManagedMcpServerAllowed(lists({allowedMcpServers: []}), SERVER)` -> `false`) and `:346` (`strict({allowedMcpServers: []}).allowedMcpServers` -> `[]`).  It reaches both populations the doc's Disable-MCP row names. `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:704` and `:709` drop every native MCP inventory record that fails the gate, and `:730-733` drops every PLUGIN-provided MCP candidate (`isManagedMcpServerAllowed(managedPiPolicy, pluginMcpServerIdentity(candidate))`) - so "including plugin-provided servers" is covered by the same seam.  And it is deliverable at a system path. `packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:48-50` reads the rebranded managed file at `/Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json` (darwin), `/etc/nessy/managed-policy.json` (linux) and `%ProgramData%\Nessy\managed-policy.json` (win32). No user, project or local tier carries `allowedMcpServers` at all (recorded at `managed-mcp-access.md:94`, which is why `allowManagedMcpServersOnly` is `inapplicable - one tier carries these keys`), so the empty allowlist is already authoritative without the lock the page requires alongside it.  So an administrator CAN express the documented outcome "No servers load anywhere" on this fork today, with an admin-only file at a system path, covering plugin servers. What is missing is the DEPLOYMENT half of `managed-mcp.json` (pushing a fixed server set out to users, which no Nessy key does) and the add-time refusal feedback (`sources.CREATE` does not consult the policy - recorded at `managed-mcp-access.md:97`; a denied server is filtered at load, so it never runs, but the user sees silent disappearance rather than an error).  Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in `2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` section 3 - I checked all nine; none concerns MCP deployment. Partly, but not wholly, a de-brand difference: the system-path managed file is genuinely just renamed (ClaudeCode -> Nessy), and the claude.ai-connector clause of the quoted section is inapplicable (we have no claude.ai connectors), but the fixed-server deployment channel is a real absence.  Refuted because leg 3 could not be positively confirmed: the finding's practical consequence is contradicted by shipped, tested behaviour, and its OUR STATE names the wrong list.

column5: Claude Code answers `roots/list` with the session's launch directory plus every [additional working directory](/docs/en/permissions#working-directories) you've granted with `--add-dir`, `/add-dir`, or the `additionalDirectories` setting.
column6: Claude Code answers `roots/list` with the launch directory plus every additional working directory, and sends `notifications/roots/list_changed` when that set changes.
column7: The MCP client is constructed with `capabilities: options?.elicitationHandler ? { elicitation: { form: {}, url: {} } } : {}` — the `roots` capability is never advertised, so `roots/list` is never requested and no `list_changed` roots notification is emitted. A server that scopes its own filesystem access via roots gets nothing. Confirmed absent repo-wide with `grep -a`.
column9: All three checks confirm the finding; nothing refutes it. (1) QUOTE IS VERBATIM. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md returns the sentence character-for-character on line 108 (Python substring test: True). Note: a first curl produced a truncated 33 KB body; the full 80 866-byte fetch is the one verified. Reading the WHOLE line does not reverse the conclusion, it strengthens it — the line is five sentences: 'CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is the stable project root and doesn't change when you add or remove working directories mid-session. A server that limits its own filesystem access to a set of allowed directories should implement the MCP roots/list request instead. Claude Code answers roots/list with the session's launch directory plus every [additional working directory](/docs/en/permissions#working-directories) you've granted with --add-dir, /add-dir, or the additionalDirectories setting. Claude Code sends notifications/roots/list_changed when that set changes. Before v2.1.203, roots/list returned only the launch directory and Claude Code didn't send notifications/roots/list_changed.' The second sentence explicitly routes allowed-directory scoping to roots/list rather than to the project-dir env var, and the fourth sentence independently confirms the list_changed half of the claimed behaviour. (2) CITED CODE MATCHES. packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:310-324 constructs `new Client({name:'nessy-agent',version:'1.0.0'}, {capabilities: options?.elicitationHandler ? {elicitation:{form:{},url:{}}} : {}})`. The only capability ever declared is elicitation, and only when a handler is supplied; the R24 comment above it states the policy 'advertise only what we honour'. packages/shared/src/mcp/__tests__/client-transport.test.ts:78-90 pins that surface exactly (`sdkClient._capabilities.elicitation` toEqual `{form:{},url:{}}`, undefined without a handler) — so the capability set is deliberately narrow and roots is not in it. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, and it holds. Absence: `grep -ra` (NUL-safe) for roots/list, ListRoots, listRoots, sendRootsListChanged, RootsListChangedNotification over packages/ and apps/ returns ZERO hits in Nessy source. The only hits are inside built bundles and third-party binaries, and each was opened and confirmed to be the vendored MCP SDK's own protocol table, not an implementation: packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js and apps/electron/dist/resources/bridge-mcp-server/index.js each contain `ListRootsRequestSchema = RequestSchema.extend({method: literal("roots/list")})` plus its entry in `ServerRequestSchema`, with `setRequestHandler(ListRoots` count = 0 in both; the remaining hits are the prebuilt codex-app-server binaries. No `registerCapabilities` call exists anywhere in the repo, so nothing adds roots after construction either. LAYER UP — is something upstream already handling it? No, and this is the check that could have refuted it. Nessy's pool is the ONLY MCP client that connects third-party servers, so no host SDK's roots implementation is ever in the path: claude-agent.ts:1136-1150 builds `Options['mcpServers']` from in-process `sourceProxies` ('Per-source proxy servers from centralized MCP pool… the pool owns all source connections centrally', claude-agent.ts:474-477) rather than handing raw MCP configs to the Claude SDK, and mcp/pool-server.ts:211-213 re-exposes the same pool to Codex/Pi as `nessy-pool-proxy` with `capabilities: {tools:{listChanged:true}}`. LAYER DOWN — sibling MCP clients omit roots too, so there is no other client that answers: api-source-pool-client.ts:20 passes no capabilities argument at all and validation.ts:411-413 passes `capabilities: {}`. SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM TRAP checked and cleared: the ~60 other `roots` hits in the repo are unrelated same-name symbols in different subsystems — sandbox/filesystem containment (session-tools-core credential-deny-roots.ts, pi-harness/isolation.ts), `--add-dir` memory-file scoping (capabilities/native-sources.ts), test temp-dir arrays, Codex FuzzyFileSearchParams.roots, and client.ts:886's own 'plugin-mcp-working-directory-outside-authorized-roots' (which contains where a plugin MCP PROCESS is launched, and never reaches the wire as a roots/list answer). NOT AN OWNER DECISION: the nine dated decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, and listSessionSummaries — none is MCP roots. The parity audit corroborates rather than excuses: 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1787 lists roots/list among grep-absence claims 're-confirmed absent repo-wide at the time', and grep over docs/ finds no plan and no parity row for it. NOT A DELIBERATE FORK DIFFERENCE: this touches no dropped subscription flow, no gateway routing and no rename — and the fork already owns the exact inputs a roots/list answer needs, so this is a missing surface rather than a missing concept: `additionalDirectories` is a first-class persisted setting (config/storage.ts:132, config/validators.ts:191/227) resolved by packages/shared/src/agent/additional-directories.ts into a `roots: string[]`, and `--add-dir` roots are already modelled in capabilities/types.ts:197-201. One imprecision in the original wording, too small to refute: it is the SERVER that sends `roots/list` to the client, not the client that requests it; the accurate mechanism is that without the declared capability a spec-compliant server never asks, and a server that asked anyway would get a 'Method not found' because no ListRootsRequestSchema handler is registered.

column5: When configuring MCP servers via JSON in `.mcp.json`, `~/.claude.json`, or `claude mcp add-json`, the `type` field accepts `streamable-http` as an alias for `http`.
column6: `"streamable-http"` is a valid value of the `type` field wherever MCP servers are configured in JSON.
column7: Our `.mcp.json` parser and the Claude plugin adapter both accept only `stdio|http|sse|ws`; an entry copied verbatim from an MCP server's own documentation is dropped with `unsupported MCP server config`.
column9: All three checks pass. (1) DOC: the sentence exists VERBATIM at line 78 of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md (HTTP 200, 1282 lines): "When configuring MCP servers via JSON in `.mcp.json`, `~/.claude.json`, or `claude mcp add-json`, the `type` field accepts `streamable-http` as an alias for `http`." The line is two sentences and the second one REINFORCES rather than reverses: "The MCP specification uses the name `streamable-http` for this transport, so configurations copied from server documentation work without modification." (One early curl of the same URL returned the agent-sdk/mcp page instead - CDN variance - but two independent re-fetches were byte-identical and both carry the sentence at line 78.) (2) CITED CODE: packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:119 is exactly `if (type === 'http' || type === 'sse') {`; the function then handles 'ws' (:144) and `undefined|'stdio'` (:163) and returns null (:177) for anything else. The Claude plugin adapter's closed set is packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1040 (`rawTransport === 'stdio' || ... 'http' || 'sse' || 'ws' ? rawTransport : undefined`); the claim cited :1034, a comment line six lines up inside the same block - trivial line drift, same location. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, with a positive control: running parseMcpServersDocument on `{mcpServers:{alias:{type:'streamable-http',url:...}, plain:{type:'http',url:...}}}` returns only `["plain"]` and emits the warning verbatim as claimed - `Ignoring .mcp.json server "alias": unsupported MCP server config` (project-config.ts:211). ONE LAYER UP: nothing normalizes the alias before the parser. The live materialization path (packages/shared/src/mcp/runtime-pool-servers.ts:456-466) JSON.parses the raw file text and passes it straight to parseMcpServersDocument, and loadProjectMcpServers (:218-236) does the same; `grep -rn -a -i streamable` over the repo finds the token ONLY in vendored apps/electron/dist bundles, docs-site prose, and unrelated MCP-SDK transport class names - there is no alias table anywhere in our own source. ONE LAYER DOWN: native-sources.ts:mcpServerRecords creates an inventory record per server name regardless of `type`, so the entry is inventoried and then silently dropped at materialization - it never reaches the pool. SIBLING SUBSYSTEMS CHECKED: the Codex adapter has the same closed set (codex.ts:905, stdio|http|sse), and MCP *Sources* (a Source config.json spelling it `transport`, not `type`) are a different subsystem that always connects over Streamable HTTP anyway (validation.ts:158-164) - the finding names the right subsystem (.mcp.json reader + Claude plugin adapter), so the 'wrong sibling' refutation does not apply. NOT AN OWNER DECISION: none of the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 covers this (they are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions). NOT A DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE: `.mcp.json` is a repository-owned shared contract file, and this very parser is written against this very page - it cites `mcp.md:707`, `:735`, `:138` and `:147` inline - so the page is a contract we opted into, not a Claude-subscription/rename surface we dropped.

column5: If your MCP server uses an authentication scheme other than OAuth, such as Kerberos, short-lived tokens, or an internal SSO, use `headersHelper` to generate request headers at connection time.
column6: `headersHelper` runs a command at connection time whose stdout JSON is merged into the connection headers, with `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME`/`CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL`/`CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` in its environment and a 10-second timeout.
column7: Not implemented for any transport. Both readers detect the field and emit a warning (`"headersHelper" is not implemented for any transport; it was ignored`) and a deferred-capability record; the server still connects with static headers only.
column9: All three checks pass in the finding's favour; the divergence is real. (1) VERBATIM. The quoted sentence exists word-for-word at mcp.md:761, under the heading '### Use dynamic headers for custom authentication'. I read the WHOLE line: it is a two-sentence line and the second sentence REINFORCES rather than reverses — 'Claude Code runs the command and merges its output into the connection headers.' Every element of the claimed behaviour is verbatim-supported in the same section: 'The command must write a JSON object of string key-value pairs to stdout'; 'The command runs in a shell with a 10-second timeout, from the session's current working directory'; 'Dynamic headers override any static `headers` with the same name'; and the env table lists exactly CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME (server name), CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL (server URL) and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT ('Set only when a plugin provides the server'). The field is also documented for ws at mcp.md:147 and listed among plugin server fields at mcp.md:320. So the doc side is not a paraphrase and not cherry-picked. (2) CITED LINES. Both citations say what was claimed. packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:147-148 is `if (raw.headersHelper !== undefined) { problems.push('"headersHelper" is not implemented for any transport; it was ignored'); }`, preceded by the docblock at :139-143 'headersHelper is READ AND REPORTED, NOT IMPLEMENTED — there is no dynamic header generator anywhere in this codebase for any transport'. packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1047-1058 pushes the warning 'Claude MCP server "<name>" declares headersHelper, which is not implemented for any transport; static headers still apply.' AND `deferred.push({ externalKind: 'mcp', reasonCode: 'plugin.deferred.claude_mcp_headers_helper_unsupported' })` — so the deferred-capability record is real, on the plugin path. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, both layers. Nothing upstream or downstream implements it. Binary-safe `grep -rna --binary-files=text 'headersHelper'` over packages/*/src and apps/*/src returns 25 hits in 6 files and every one is a reader, a docblock, or a test — there is no executor, no spawn, no shell call. `grep -rna --binary-files=text 'CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME|CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL'` over packages, apps and scripts returns ZERO hits, so the documented helper environment is not constructed anywhere. One layer down at the vendored runtime: packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js contains headersHelper exactly 3 times (lines 350316, 350319, 350320) and all three are `headersHelper: l3.string().optional()` inside the sse/http/ws zod schemas — the Pi SDK ACCEPTS the field and never consumes it, so no downstream layer silently rescues the behaviour. Our readers strip it before the pool anyway. No sibling-subsystem misnaming is possible: headersHelper is a single MCP-config field name and the only two parsers of it are the two cited. (4) NOT AN OWNER DECISION. I read all nine dated entries in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions). headersHelper is not among them and appears nowhere in that file. It is instead an OPEN, recorded deviation: 2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:369 and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-mcp-surfaces.md:117/:142/:154 name it 'documented, not implemented', and the parity audit's N8 row (:726) closes ws transport while leaving this explicitly open. (5) NOT A FORK PRODUCT DIFFERENCE. headersHelper is transport-level MCP auth, not a Claude/ChatGPT subscription flow, not a rebrand, not gateway-specific. If anything the fork is the doc's own stated audience — 'Kerberos, short-lived tokens, or an internal SSO' is precisely a corporate-gateway deployment. One correction to the finding's OUR STATE, which makes our position WORSE than claimed, not better, and therefore does not refute it: 'Both readers detect the field and emit a warning' is FALSE for the .mcp.json reader on http and sse. In project-config.ts the headersHelper check sits ONLY inside the `if (type === 'ws')` arm (:144-153); the http/sse arm (:119-134) never touches raw.headersHelper, and parseMcpServersDocument (:190-213) has no generic unknown-key sweep. I proved this with a positive control rather than by reading alone — a temporary bun test through parseMcpServersDocument, since deleted, with the ws case as the control that shows the rig can observe the warning: WS -> ['.mcp.json server "events": "headersHelper" is not implemented for any transport; it was ignored.']; HTTP -> config {"type":"http","url":"https://x.test/mcp"}, warnings []; SSE -> config {"type":"sse","url":"https://x.test/mcp"}, warnings []. So on the transport the doc's own two examples use ('type': 'http'), a project .mcp.json headersHelper is dropped in total silence — the exact failure mode the code comment at :141-143 says it exists to prevent ('an operator ends up debugging a 401 that has nothing to do with their token'). The only test covering that warning, mcp/__tests__/ws-transport.test.ts:46-57, uses type 'ws', which is why the hole survived.

column5: For security reasons, Claude Code prompts for approval before using project-scoped servers from `.mcp.json` files.
column6: Project-scoped `.mcp.json` servers require per-server approval before use, resettable with `claude mcp reset-project-choices`.
column7: The only gate is whole-workspace trust; inside a trusted project every `.mcp.json` server is materialized without an individual approve/reject step, and none of `enabledMcpjsonServers`, `disabledMcpjsonServers`, `enableAllProjectMcpServers` or a reset command exists.
column9: Quote and cited lines are accurate, but the load-bearing sentence of the claimed our-state — "The only gate is whole-workspace trust; inside a trusted project every `.mcp.json` server is materialized without an individual approve/reject step" — is false in three separate ways. This is the mcp.md twin of f029 (settings.md) and fails for the same reason, verified independently here.  1. If you need to reset these approval choices, use the `claude mcp reset-project-choices` command." The second sentence reinforces rather than reverses. column5: The server took longer than the default 30-second startup timeout. A stdio server's first run can be slow while `npx` downloads the package. Increase the limit with the [`MCP_TIMEOUT`](/docs/en/env-vars) environment variable, in milliseconds:
column6: The MCP server startup timeout is 30 seconds by default and is raised with the `MCP_TIMEOUT` environment variable in milliseconds.
column7: The 30 s default matches (`MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`), but it is a compile-time constant overridable only through a programmatic `connectTimeoutMs` option — there is no `MCP_TIMEOUT` (or Nessy-prefixed) env reader, so an operator cannot raise it.

column5: When you install a plugin that declares dependencies, Claude Code resolves and installs them automatically and lists which dependencies were added at the end of the install output.
column6: Installing a plugin that declares dependencies resolves and installs them automatically, fetching each at the highest `{plugin-name}--v{version}` git tag that satisfies the range.
column7: No auto-install and no tag enumeration. The module header records the reason: no marketplace source in this repo enumerates git tags, so resolving a range against "whatever the catalog currently holds" would make `~2.1.0` silently mean latest. The identifier facts are all accurate: `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn` has zero readers anywhere in packages/ or apps/ (grep -a: the only hits are the claude.ts:1583 comment, two plan docs and the deviation register), no `cross-marketplace` error code exists (grep -a for 'cross-marketplace|crossMarketplace' over all .ts returns one comment at plugins/types.ts:703), and `PluginDependencyDescriptor.marketplace` really is carried and consumed (dependencies.ts:91,99; management-service-v2.ts:711,714,748). The CONSEQUENCE is what fails, in the exact 'enforcement one layer up' shape AGENTS.md and inert-worklist section 4 item 3 warn about. The doc scopes the refusal to auto-install: ':81' reads 'Claude Code refuses to AUTO-INSTALL a dependency that lives in a different marketplace', and ':104' blesses the escape hatch 'Users can still install the dependency manually first, which satisfies the constraint without changing the allowlist.' Nessy auto-installs no plugin dependency at all -- verified one layer down: `resolvePluginDependencyErrors` (dependencies.ts:68-140) only resolves declared dependencies against ALREADY-INSTALLED subjects and emits dependency-unsatisfied / dependency-version-unsatisfied / range-conflict, and `resolveTransitiveDependencies` (management-service-v2.ts:696-728) throws `plugin.manage.dependency-not-installed` rather than fetching; nothing in the plugin install path resolves a dependency from a marketplace. So every cross-marketplace dependency Nessy can ever satisfy is one the user installed manually, which is precisely the path ':104' says satisfies the constraint WITHOUT the allowlist. The trust property the field protects -- 'This prevents one marketplace from silently pulling in plugins from a source you have not reviewed' -- is therefore satisfied strictly more conservatively than Claude, not violated. What differs is only the diagnostic string (dependency-unsatisfied / dependency-not-installed instead of a `cross-marketplace` error naming the field), not the security outcome. It is also an already-recorded deviation with a written reason, harvested by scripts/regenerate-deviation-register.py from docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-plugin-dependencies-and-monitors.md:243 into docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:392 (and an earlier one at 2026-07-29-marketplace-entry-authority.md:226). It is NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3 -- I checked all nine and none concerns marketplaces or dependencies -- so it is refuted as a false consequence plus a recorded deviation, not as a section-3 owner decision.

column5: Claude Code sets the [`CLAUDECODE`](/docs/en/env-vars) environment variable to `1` for every command it runs through the Bash and PowerShell tools, and for [hook](/docs/en/hooks) commands.
column6: Every subprocess the Bash/PowerShell tool and hook commands spawn carries an environment marker announcing that it is running inside the coding agent; third-party CLIs gate behaviour on it.
column7: Nessy sets no equivalent marker in tool subprocesses. The only `CLAUDECODE` references in the repo REMOVE it from a child env (`apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:62` strips it to dodge the Claude SDK nesting guard) and there is no `NESSYCODE`/`NESSY_CODE` replacement anywhere. This is not the ordinary brand-prefix rename: the variable is read by third-party tools, not by us, so no NESSY_-prefixed name substitutes for it, and CLIs that adapt their output for agent use (non-interactive mode, no colour, machine-readable output) do not adapt for Nessy.
column9: Quote is verbatim (first sentence of plugin-hints.md line 17) and the cited file:line is exactly as claimed (apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:60-62 destructures CLAUDECODE out of the child env with the stated Claude-SDK-nesting reason; packages/server/src/__tests__/smoke.test.ts:44,173 do the same). The finding fails on the other two checks. (1) DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE. Read whole, this page defines one mechanism: CLAUDECODE (and CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION from v2.1.172) gates a CLI's <claude-code-hint /> stderr marker, and line 149 states 'The hint protocol only takes effect for plugins listed in the official Anthropic marketplace, claude-plugins-official. Anthropic curates that marketplace at its discretion' — a rebranded T-Bank fork cannot list there, so the protocol has no terminus for us. Asserting CLAUDECODE=1 from a non-Claude product is a brand claim, and it contradicts a boundary this repo records in shipped source: packages/shared/src/plugins/data-paths.ts:94-96 — the generic plugin runtime env 'Emits Nessy names plus the unbranded PLUGIN_* compatibility aliases — never Claude aliases' — with CLAUDE_* names emitted ONLY under an explicit per-plugin claude-plugin-env-v1 / codex-plugin-env-v1 compat profile (data-paths.ts:111-155). A blanket CLAUDECODE=1 on every Bash and hook subprocess has no such profile. (2) THE CLAIMED OUR-STATE IS FALSE AS AN ABSOLUTE. Bash-tool subprocesses do not get the raw host env: local-tools/runtime.ts:232-259 routes through runCommand into ProcessSupervisor, which defaults to the 'restricted' environment profile (process-supervisor.ts:717-733) whose hostEnvironment() filters process.env through the RESTRICTED_HOST_ENVIRONMENT allowlist at process-supervisor.ts:703-711. That allowlist contains NESSY_AGENT_VERSION, which apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:145 sets to app.getVersion() in the same process that constructs SessionManager (index.ts:711) and therefore the supervisor (SessionManager.ts:3574). So in the packaged desktop app every Bash-tool subprocess DOES carry a Nessy-presence env marker; what is missing is only that it wears a name third-party CLIs do not know. Separately, on the Claude backend (NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE=1) the vendored node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude binary — 19 CLAUDECODE occurrences — is what runs Bash, so those subprocesses get the real marker from Claude Code itself; that is precisely why server-spawner.ts:62 must strip it. (3) THE CONSEQUENCE IS INVERTED. There is no <claude-code-hint /> reader anywhere in packages/ or apps/ (grep -ra, zero hits outside docs). Setting CLAUDECODE=1 would make gating CLIs emit raw hint tags that Nessy cannot strip, injecting them into model context — a regression, not a fix. The two absences are coupled and coherent, and the restricted allowlist already strips an inherited CLAUDECODE from Bash subprocesses, so the phase1 companion worry ('any CLI that gates on a variable we do inherit would leak the raw tag') is handled one layer down as well. Not listed in inert-worklist section 3 or 4, but it is the product-difference carve-out the task names.

column5: You can include any field from the [plugin manifest schema](/docs/en/plugins-reference#plugin-manifest-schema), such as `description`, `version`, `author`, `commands`, and `hooks`, plus these marketplace-specific fields: `source`, `category`, `tags`, `strict`, and `relevance`.
column6: A marketplace plugin entry may carry `category`, `tags`, `relevance` (marketplace-specific) plus any manifest field including `license`, `keywords`, `repository`.
column7: `MARKETPLACE_ENTRY_CARRIED_FIELDS` carries only the path fields plus `displayName`, `description`, `version`, `author`, `homepage`, `defaultEnabled`, `dependencies`. `category`, `tags`, `relevance`, `license`, `keywords` and `repository` are dropped at catalog parse and never reach the adapter — grep for `'category'`/`'tags'`/`'license'`/`'keywords'` in that file returns zero. `category` and `tags` are the documented organisation/search axes, so a marketplace that categorises its plugins loses that in our Discover list.
column9: Doc sentence CONFIRMED verbatim at plugins/marketplace-reference.md#entry-and-plugin-json (was line 195 of the retired plugin-marketplaces page) (whole line read; single sentence after a one-clause preamble, no reversal). The IDENTIFIER claim is also accurate: MARKETPLACE_ENTRY_CARRIED_FIELDS (external-catalog-adapters.ts:153) carries the 7 path fields plus displayName/description/version/author/homepage/defaultEnabled/dependencies, and `grep -a` returns zero for category/tags/relevance/license/keywords in that file. The finding is refuted on its CONSEQUENCE, on four independent grounds. (1) It is a deliberate, reasoned, TESTED decision, not an oversight. The allowlist's own docblock at :141-152 states it: 'Deliberately an ALLOWLIST, not a copy of the entry: a catalog row is untrusted input from a repository the user may not control, and a key no adapter reads has no business travelling through the install record onto disk. The metadata half is the subset the Claude adapter actually consumes (normalizeClaudePluginBundle).' A committed regression test pins it: marketplace/__tests__/external-catalog-adapters.test.ts:406-431 places `relevance: { keywords: ['review'] }` on an entry under the comment 'Not a field any adapter reads - must not travel with the definition' and asserts fields keys equal ['description','mcpServers','skills','version']. The finding's own example field is the one the test names. (2) WRONG LAYER - the stated consequence is unreachable from the cited line. `fields` is a MANIFEST OVERLAY consumed by the format adapter, not the browse-row source. The Discover row is MarketplaceCatalogItem (marketplace/types.ts:340-400), built by proposalToCatalogItem (registry-catalog-items.ts) from entryDescription/entryVersion/capabilities/source - and that interface has no category/tags/keywords member at all. Carrying `category` into `fields` would put it in a manifest overlay whose target type, NessyPluginManifest (plugins/types.ts:715-758), also has no category/tags/license/keywords/repository. (3) NOT MARKETPLACE-ENTRY-SPECIFIC - our plugin.json reader drops exactly the same fields: schema.ts:501-525 rebuilds the manifest copying only description/publisher/homepageUrl/defaultEnabled/dependencies, and `grep -c -a license` returns 0 in format-adapters/claude.ts, plugins/schema.ts and plugins/types.ts. So this is a uniform 'we do not model informational metadata' property applied identically to plugin.json and to a marketplace entry, not a divergence at the catalog parse. (4) NO DOCUMENTED BEHAVIOUR IS MISSED, and the drop is not a rejection. The quoted sentence establishes only that an entry MAY carry these fields; the doc tables gloss them as 'Plugin category for organization' / 'Tags for searchability' / 'Discovery tags' and no page in the Claude Code corpus (plugin-marketplaces.md, discover-plugins.md, plugins.md, plugins-reference.md) documents Claude Code reading, rendering or filtering by category, tags or keywords. plugins/manifest-reference.md#unrecognized-fields (was lines 470-471 of the retired plugins-reference page) states the opposite posture verbatim: 'Claude Code ignores top-level fields it does not recognize. You can keep metadata from another ecosystem in plugin.json and the plugin still loads.' Our parser does the same - ExternalPluginCatalogPluginDto has an index signature, unknown keys emit no diagnostic and the entry still resolves and installs. Finally the 'Discover list' phrasing names a SIBLING SUBSYSTEM: Nessy's Discover shelves group per-registry (MarketplaceBrowsePage sections keyed by marketplaceRegistryId), and the tag/tenant/profession facet vocabulary that does exist belongs to the corporate Skills Market API (marketplace/client.ts:123-133,185-188), a different data source from a Claude marketplace.json - so there is no category axis for an external catalog to lose. Not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (checked; those are the seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) - but it is the same class: a decision with a written reason and a guarding test. Separately: `relevance` is already tracked on its own as coverage-map row 60 (plugin-relevance, red), so folding it into this row double-counts a registered gap; and that row's note ('relevance passes inside the marketplace entry fields') is contradicted by the test above and should be corrected to 'dropped at parse'.

column5: Set the `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR` environment variable to point at this directory.
column6: A pre-populated, read-only plugins directory can be pointed at with an environment variable so container/CI images start with marketplaces and plugin caches already present, with a second variable to install directly into that path at build time.
column7: No seed-directory concept exists. `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR`, `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR`, `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_KEEP_MARKETPLACE_ON_FAILURE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS` and `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_PREFER_HTTPS` all return zero hits under `--include='*.ts'` repo-wide, and there is no NESSY_-prefixed equivalent for any of them. The offline/airgap escape hatch the page recommends (`KEEP_MARKETPLACE_ON_FAILURE`) therefore has no counterpart, which matters for a corporate-network fork.
column9: Quote verified verbatim at plugins/org.md#seed-containers-and-ci (was line 635 of the retired plugin-marketplaces page) (two-sentence line, second half does not reverse it). The narrow identifier half is true: no CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR / layered read-only seed directory exists. But the finding is refuted on both its evidence and its consequence. (1) EVIDENCE FALSE AS STATED: the claim says all five names 'return zero hits under --include=*.ts repo-wide'. PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR returns 5 hits -- packages/shared/src/workspaces/paths.ts:11 and :99, workspaces/index.ts:46, plus two in __tests__/paths.test.ts. Bare-name grep collision with a real managed-cache-root constant; the sweep never re-ran its own command. (2) CONSEQUENCE FALSE for the variable the finding singles out as mattering: KEEP_MARKETPLACE_ON_FAILURE is an OPT-IN in Claude Code to stop it deleting and re-cloning a marketplace whose background pull failed. Our fork does the non-destructive thing UNCONDITIONALLY, by design. packages/shared/src/marketplace/registry-source.ts mergeFailedFetch keeps the previous catalog under the failed fetch's signature and explicitly refuses to delete the on-disk copy ('after a failed refresh it is the only surviving copy, and removing it turns a recoverable state into an unrecoverable one'), citing the same bug one subsystem over from mcp.md. upgrade() (:857-870) on a non-persistable fetch leaves the row and its signature untouched and returns typed fetch-failed / fetch-timeout, 'so the catalog the user can still browse stays the catalog an install resolves against'. There is no destructive default here to need an escape hatch from -- the airgap resilience the page sells via the flag is our floor, not our gap. (3) PREFER_HTTPS likewise: packages/shared/src/plugins/source-resolver.ts:115-116 -- 'Claude clones shorthand over SSH by default (:553); we resolve to the HTTPS repository URL because codeload is the acquisition route this app has.' The flag's effect is our unconditional default. (4) GIT_TIMEOUT_MS is not absent as a concept: REGISTRY_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 45_000 (registry-source.ts:54) with an options.fetchTimeoutMs override (:323) and a distinct 'fetch-timeout' upgrade reason -- configurable, just not env-driven. (5) The seed directory's container/CI intent is served by a deliberate product difference, not left open: admin pre-provisioning arrives through server-delivered managed settings (packages/shared/src/config/managed-delivery.ts, gateway /api/v1/cli/managed-settings) as extraKnownMarketplaces, registered idempotently by PluginRegistrySource.ensureDeliveredMarketplaces() (:341-378) under the same strictKnownMarketplaces allowlist an interactive add passes, with catalogs cached to disk. This fork delivers policy through its corporate gateway rather than through container env vars. Not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (checked; none touches marketplaces or seeding).

column5: Plugins can include a `settings.json` file at the plugin root to apply default configuration when the plugin is enabled. Currently, only the `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` keys are supported.
column6: A plugin may ship a `settings.json` at its root whose `agent` key activates one of the plugin's own subagents as the main thread, and whose values outrank a `settings` block in `plugin.json`.
column7: The file is detected and recorded as a deferral only — `CLAUDE_RETAINED_SURFACE_FIELDS` carries `{ externalKind: 'settings', field: 'settings', defaultPath: 'settings.json' }`, which pushes a `plugin.deferred.claude_settings` row and nothing else. Neither key is read anywhere: `grep -ran "subagentStatusLine" --include='*.ts' .` returns zero hits repo-wide. A plugin whose whole purpose is to change the main thread's agent installs and silently does nothing.
column9: All three checks confirm the finding. (1) The quote is VERBATIM at plugins.md:298, and reading the whole section rather than the one line strengthens it: :300 says "Setting `agent` activates one of the plugin's custom agents as the main thread, applying its system prompt, tool restrictions, and model", and :308 says "Settings from `settings.json` take priority over `settings` declared in `plugin.json`. Unknown keys are silently ignored." Nothing in the second half reverses the claim. (2) The cited state is accurate, with a 5-line citation drift: the row is at packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:2275, not :2270 (:2270 is a comment about `dependencies`). It reads exactly `{ externalKind: 'settings', field: 'settings', defaultPath: 'settings.json' }`, and addClaudeRetainedSurfaceDeferrals (:2278-2317, called at :270 with the bundle rootDirectory) fires on existsSync(<root>/settings.json), pushes `plugin.deferred.claude_settings` (reasonCode template at :2302) and, unlike the `themes` row, carries no `refusal` diagnostic, so the author is told nothing at install. `grep -ran subagentStatusLine` over the repo returns hits only inside docs/superpowers/specs/data/*.json (the sweep's own files) — zero source hits, confirmed with -a. (3) One layer up and one layer down both hold. Sibling-subsystem check: packages/shared/src/plugins/plugin-settings.ts also owns a file literally named settings.json, but it is the per-plugin data-path option store for MCPB user_config descriptors (the only producer of PluginSettingDescriptor is format-adapters/mcpb.ts:130) and has nothing to do with a Claude plugin-root file; claude.ts:2084's `'settings'` is a member of CLAUDE_UNREAD_LSP_FIELDS, an LSP server knob, a third unrelated `settings`. Consequence check, separate from the identifier: the fork has NO main-thread-agent override at all — no mechanism anywhere reads an agent name and installs it as the main thread — so nothing upstream honours the key by another route. The nearest live analogue, plugin-shipped output styles, IS honoured (capabilities/runtime-output-styles.ts, resolver.ts:612), which is the positive control proving plugin-shipped default-behaviour surfaces are otherwise wired; the settings.json path is the one that is not. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (SEATBELT wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) and not in the deviation register. Not a deliberate product difference either: importing Claude plugin bundles is a supported first-class surface of this fork, unrelated to the dropped subscription flows or the rebrand.

column5: Any folder under a skills directory that contains a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` manifest is loaded as a plugin named `<name>@skills-dir` on the next session, with no marketplace and no install step.
column6: A folder under a skills directory containing `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` loads as a plugin named `<name>@skills-dir` with no marketplace and no install step, discovered in place rather than copied into the cache.
column7: Not implemented. `grep -ran "skills-dir"` over the repo hits only plan/spec prose — including `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:197` which itself records "skills-dir plugins undetected (B1, still not started)". Skill discovery walks `.claude/skills` at project and ancestor depth (`native-sources.ts` line ~1065, tagged `d${depth}`) but never checks a skill folder for a plugin manifest, so a bundle laid out this way contributes its SKILL.md and silently drops its agents, hooks and MCP servers.
column9: All three checks pass; the divergence survives. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md` -> line 375, exact match. The whole line continues 'Scaffold one with `plugin init`. Unlike a marketplace install, the plugin is discovered in place rather than copied into the plugin cache.' -- it reinforces the claim, it does not reverse it. The surrounding section (lines 372-411, '## Skills-directory plugins') adds a three-row table (`:381`-`:382`: `<skills-dir>/foo/SKILL.md` with no manifest = a plain skill; `<skills-dir>/foo/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` = 'A plugin `foo@skills-dir`, which can bundle its own skills, agents, hooks, and more'), a scope table (`~/.claude/skills/` personal, `<cwd>/.claude/skills/` project-behind-trust), `:401`'s no-ancestor-walk warning, and `:408`/`:411` 'There is no `uninstall` step because nothing was installed from a marketplace' / `claude plugin disable my-tool@skills-dir`. `:874` and `:911` repeat it for `plugin init`. (2) CITED EVIDENCE. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:197` reads verbatim: '| P7 | Skill listing capped at 4 000 chars / 180 per entry vs Claude's 1 536 per entry; output styles unscanned; skills-dir plugins undetected (B1, **still not started**) | Give B1 a start date or re-home the three rows | ~ medium |'. Corroborated by `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-skills-invocation.md:557` ('**Skills-directory plugins** (`<name>@skills-dir`) -- that is the B1 batch.') and by the B1 row in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:701`, which lists 'skills-dir plugins' among B1's items, declares 'B1 fully closed 2026-07-30 (`6cdbd80e`)', and never mentions the item again -- neither in the closed list nor in the 'Genuinely remaining' list nor in the two items recorded as leaving B1 (`bin/`-on-PATH, dependency auto-install). It was dropped silently, not implemented and not decided. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-b1-audit.md` contains no skills-directory-plugin measurement either (its only `skillsDir` hit, `:109`, is about the Claude adapter's `CLAUDE_DEFAULT_SKILLS_DIR` in manifest path resolution -- B1a, a different subsystem). (3) ONE LAYER UP AND DOWN, consequence verified separately from the identifier. Every skills-directory scanner in the fork is the single function `skillRecords` in `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:266-310`, called from exactly five sites (`:903` `~/.agents/skills`, `:904` `<configDir>/skills`, `:949` `<workspaceRoot>/skills`, `:1016` `.nessy-agent/skills`, `:1065` `.agents/skills` per ancestor depth). It admits an entry only when `join(slugPath, 'SKILL.md')` exists (`:282`-`:283`) and emits `kind: 'skill'`; it never stats `.claude-plugin/`, never reads a manifest, and there is no other kind it can emit. Nothing upstream handles the case: `grep -rn "\.claude-plugin" --include=*.ts` over `packages/`+`apps/` returns manifest readers only in the install/marketplace path -- `format-adapters/claude.ts:145` (bundle adapter, runs on a staged bundle), `plugin-manifest-probe.ts:51` (a `raw.githubusercontent.com` GET for a marketplace DETAIL page), `registry-catalog-fetcher.ts:167`, `marketplace/repository-install.ts:22`, `workspaces/storage.ts:284`. Every one of those requires an install that stages into the plugin cache; even the `local-path` source kind (`plugins/types.ts:933`, `install-service.ts:513`, `source-resolver.ts:378`) runs `createPluginStagingArea`, so it is a copy-with-install-step, the opposite of the doc's 'discovered in place'. `management-service-v2.ts` / `store-v2.ts` have no disk-discovery entry point at all (`grep -i discover` yields one unrelated OAuth comment). NOT AN OWNER DECISION: none of the nine dated decisions in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` section 3 (seatbelt wildcard, `availableModels`, `autoMode.classifyAllShell`, `ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops`, `hooks-runtime.ts`, `SdkMcpServerConfig.required`, `SessionMirrorStore.delete`, `MirrorSessionKey.subpath`, `listSessionSummaries`) touches skills-directory plugins. NOT A REBRAND DIFFERENCE: the absent thing is the mechanism (in-place plugin discovery from a skills tree, no marketplace, no install), which is missing whatever the directory is named. POSITIVE CONTROL for the absence: the same `grep -a` sweep does find live non-prose `skills-dir` hits -- `packages/shared/src/config/watcher.ts:511` (a debounce key string), `format-adapters/manifest-paths.ts:30` and two test files (a `custom-skills-dir` fixture name), and `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-marketplace-entries.test.ts:56`, which asserts that a managed-policy entry `{ source: 'skills-dir' }` is DROPPED as invalid -- so the grep is not silently skipping the tree, and the one place the token does reach shipped policy code rejects it, which is consistent with the feature being absent rather than hidden.

column5: `restartOnCrash`        | Whether to restart the server after it crashes. Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to leave a crashed server stopped instead of restarting it
column6: Eight optional LSP fields govern server lifecycle and diagnostics injection, two of them with defaults (`restartOnCrash` defaults to `true`, `diagnostics` defaults to `true`).
column7: All eight are parsed as declared-but-unread: `CLAUDE_UNREAD_LSP_FIELDS` lists `transport`, `initializationOptions`, `settings`, `startupTimeout`, `shutdownTimeout`, `restartOnCrash`, `maxRestarts`, `diagnostics`, and the reader emits a `plugin.format.claude_lsp_fields_unread` warning naming them. The capability that reaches the runtime carries only `command`, `args`, `languages`, `env`, `workspaceFolder`. An author who sets `diagnostics: false` to suppress automatic diagnostic injection, or `restartOnCrash: false` on a server that crash-loops, gets neither.
column9: Quote and identifier both check out; the CONSEQUENCE attached to the quoted field is false by measurement. (1) Quote verbatim at plugins/manifest-reference.md#lspservers (was line 262 of the retired plugins-reference page), whole line read, no reversing second half; the only adjacent qualifier is :266 ('restartOnCrash and shutdownTimeout require Claude Code v2.1.205 or later'), which does not reverse it. (2) Cited claude.ts:2075 sits inside the doc-comment (2053-2090) for CLAUDE_UNREAD_LSP_FIELDS at :2081; the eight names match exactly, the warning plugin.format.claude_lsp_fields_unread is emitted at :2158-2164, and the capability built at :2166-2177 carries only command/args/languages/env/workspaceFolder. So the declared-but-unread half is CONFIRMED. (3) The claim's harm for restartOnCrash is inverted. Nessy has no LSP restart mechanism at all: LspService.fail() (pi-harness/lsp-service.ts:382-387) is terminal, the read loop throws 'lsp-process-closed' on process exit (:282), and nothing respawns; SessionManager provisions LspService once per agent construction (getOrCreateAgentUnchecked, :11597-11660) and shouldRetainPiLspService only disposes a non-ready service at the NEXT agent construction. The repo's own deviation audit already states it: 'a crashed server stays failed forever' (2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:153). So an author who sets restartOnCrash:false gets exactly the documented outcome (crashed server left stopped), and there is no crash-loop for the flag to stop. 'gets neither' is refuted for the very field the quoted sentence is about; the divergence on that field runs the other way (the documented default true is what we do not implement). Secondary: the whole plugin-LSP surface is Pi-only (provider === 'pi' at :11597 and :12313), a harness this fork built itself, so Claude's supervisor semantics were never being mirrored. Not one of the nine inert-worklist section 3 owner decisions, but it is a recorded scope decision - docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-instruction-memory-and-diagnostics.md 'Deliberately out of scope': 'restartOnCrash / maxRestarts. Absent repo-wide; LSP crash handling is terminal by design today ... Restart policy is its own decision' and 'A per-server diagnostics flag. Nothing parses one' - and it is tracked open as parity-audit row P8. The channel choice (warning diagnostic, not a deferred row) is itself a measured decision recorded at claude.ts:2053-2080 and plan 2026-07-31-plugins-and-marketplace.md C5.

column7: The option schema, the sensitivity split, the storage-source restriction and the `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY>` export are all built; the `${user_config.*}` substitution into MCP/LSP configs and skill/agent content is not, and the surface carries its own deferral row `plugin.deferred.claude_user_config_substitution`.
