column9: The quoted sentence exists verbatim at plugins/manifest-reference.md#environment-variables (was line 577 of the retired plugins-reference page) (whole line reads: 'Each value is available for substitution as ${user_config.KEY} in MCP and LSP server configs and hook commands. Non-sensitive values can also be substituted in skill and agent content. All values are exported to hook processes as CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY> environment variables, where <KEY> is the option key uppercased.' — note :579 then carves the shell back out: shell-form hook commands, monitor commands and MCP headersHelper REJECT ${user_config.*}). The claimed OUR STATE is stale and its consequence is false. Commit 2a1f6cb7 (2026-07-30, 'fix(plugins): a plugin's user config reaches its MCP, LSP and skill surfaces') added packages/shared/src/plugins/user-config-substitution.ts — a 355-line module that substitutes ${user_config.KEY} into MCP command/args/cwd/env/url/headers (substituteMcp, :251) and LSP command/args/env/workingDirectory/workspaceFolder (substituteLsp, :280), plus pluginUserConfigContentValues (:341) for the non-sensitive skill-content subset. It is WIRED, not dead: packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:1837-1865 calls PluginUserConfigValues + substitutePluginCapabilityUserConfig on every mcp/lsp candidate and builds skillUserConfig for skill candidates; packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:685-687 performs the skill-body expansion. 23 tests pass across packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/user-config-substitution.test.ts and packages/shared/src/capabilities/__tests__/plugin-user-config-substitution.test.ts. The stated consequence — 'A plugin whose MCP server config references ${user_config.api_endpoint} therefore starts with the literal placeholder' — is wrong twice over: the value IS substituted, and when a referenced key is UNSET the capability is disabled with unavailableReason 'user-config-missing' plus a plugin.user_config.unset diagnostic (resolver.ts:1859-1879, asserted by the test 'refuses the MCP capability and names the field, never a value'), so it never starts with a literal placeholder either. This is the repo's documented recurring false positive in its exact shape: the cited identifier is real but the consequence was already handled a layer up. Not an inert-worklist §3 owner decision (no user_config row there) and not a deliberate product difference. What genuinely survives is smaller and differently shaped: (1) the deferral row at format-adapters/claude.ts:2263-2267 is STALE — 2a1f6cb7 never touched claude.ts, so the compatibility report still emits plugin.deferred.claude_user_config_substitution and format-adapters.test.ts:2718 still asserts it, over a comment claiming the substitution is unbuilt; (2) AGENT content is genuinely not substituted — resolver.ts:1863 gates skillUserConfig on candidate.kind === 'skill', and the separate 'agent' binding (resolver.ts:1237-1249) carries no pluginUserConfig, so :577's 'skill and agent content' is half-covered.

column5: When omitted, discovered Skills are enabled and the Skill tool is available, matching CLI behavior.
column6: Omitting the `skills` option enables every discovered user and project skill from the filesystem locations `settingSources` names; passing a list or `[]` is the only way to narrow it.
column7: `buildClaudeSessionOptions` returns only `systemPrompt`, `settingSources` and (for a child) `maxTurns`; `skills` is never set, and `settingSources` is spelled `['user', 'project', 'local']`. So every `SKILL.md` under `~/.claude/skills/` and `<cwd>/.claude/skills/` is enabled inside a Claude-backend session, chosen by the SDK rather than by Nessy's capability resolver — the resolver's own visibility state, `enabled:false` policy and skill listing do not reach that set. Conformant with this page; the divergence is that Nessy has a second, authoritative skill-gating system that the Claude backend does not project onto the SDK.
column9: Leg 1 passes: the sentence exists verbatim at line 33 of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/skills.md, and the rest of that line ('Pass "all" ... or [] to disable all. When you set `skills`, the SDK adds the Skill tool to `allowedTools` automatically.') does not reverse it. Leg 2 half-fails: the named function does not exist. `grep -rn buildClaudeSessionOptions` over packages/ and apps/ returns nothing; the real helper is `buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions` (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:272-308), and the cited :301 is the closing brace of its systemPrompt literal. Its own doc comment says it is a three-option SLICE ('The turn-shape SDK options Nessy passes explicitly ... Extracted from chatImpl's inline options object so the three shapes are testable'), NOT the session options object. `settingSources: ['user','project','local']` at :305 and the absence of `skills` are both real. Leg 3 refutes the finding: the actual Options object is assembled at claude-agent.ts:1213-1630 and one layer down it disables the SDK skill mechanism outright. :1118 `const disallowedTools: string[] = ['EnterPlanMode','ExitPlanMode','AskUserQuestion','Skill'];`, wired in at :1626, and :1629 `plugins: []` carrying the comment at :1627-1628 'No plugins — skills are handled by BaseAgent.chat() via read-before-execute (the model reads SKILL.md files directly, enforced by PrerequisiteManager)'. The installed SDK typings define the effect precisely (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:1303-1307): disallowedTools tools 'will be removed from the model's context and cannot be used, even if they would otherwise be allowed.' So the SDK Skill tool is absent from every Claude-backend turn and no SDK-discovered SKILL.md is invocable. The claimed consequence — 'every SKILL.md under ~/.claude/skills/ and <cwd>/.claude/skills/ is enabled ... chosen by the SDK rather than by Nessy's capability resolver' — is therefore false: Nessy's resolver (BaseAgent.buildPinnedCapabilityContext / capabilityTurnRuntime.view, materializeRuntimeSkillInvocation, PrerequisiteManager) is the only skill path that reaches the model, exactly as intended. This is also the repo's documented sibling-subsystem trap: the live `Skill` handling at pre-tool-use.ts:134/1435 and SessionManager.ts:964 is Nessy's OWN skill tool name, not the SDK's discovered-skill tool. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (that list's skill row is `SkillMetadata.disallowedTools`, an unrelated frontmatter field) — it is simply an implemented architectural choice, not an inert contract.

column5: The `` !`<command>` `` syntax runs shell commands before the skill content is sent to Claude.
column6: Dynamic context uses an inline `` !`<command>` `` placeholder that may appear anywhere in the body, whose output replaces the placeholder in place, with a ` ```! ` fenced block for multi-line commands.
column7: `runtimeSkillContextCommand` recognises a different syntax: a bare `!command` that must be the FIRST non-empty top-level body line, backticks not part of the form, fenced blocks skipped as prose, and a second `!` line throwing `runtime-skill-context-command-ambiguous`. Output is appended (`outputs.join('\n\n')`) rather than substituted at the placeholder. The docs' own example skill (`- PR diff: !`gh pr diff``, three placeholders inside list items) yields zero substitutions here; a skill whose first line IS `` !`git diff HEAD` `` passes the backticks through to the Bash permission evaluator as part of the command string.
column9:
All three checks pass and the consequence was reproduced by execution, not inferred.  (1) QUOTE VERBATIM. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md line 494 reads exactly: "The `` !`<command>` `` syntax runs shell commands before the skill content is sent to Claude. The command output replaces the placeholder, so Claude receives actual data, not the command itself." The second sentence of the two-sentence line reinforces rather than reverses: it states substitution-at-the-placeholder explicitly. Corroborated on the same page: :518 "Each `` !`<command>` `` executes immediately", :519 "The output replaces the placeholder in the skill content", :524 substitution "runs once over the original file", :526 "only recognized when `!` appears at the start of a line or immediately after whitespace" (so mid-line placeholders after whitespace ARE legal), and :528-536 the ` ```! ` fenced form for multi-line commands. The docs' own quickstart at :82 puts `` !`git diff HEAD` `` under a `## Current changes` heading and :89 says Claude Code "replaces the line with its output".  (2) CITED LINE. packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-context.ts:32 is `if (!first || !first.startsWith('!')) return undefined` — exactly as claimed. :20-31 walks lines, toggling a `fenced` flag on any /^\s*```/ line and skipping fenced content and blanks, and takes the FIRST surviving line as `first`. :33 `const command = first.slice(1).trim()` — everything after the bare `!` becomes the command, backticks are not part of the recognised form and are not stripped. :48 throws `runtime-skill-context-command-ambiguous` on a second top-level `!` line. There is no other implementation: `grep -ran` over packages/apps finds exactly one caller (base-agent.ts:2412) and one other `` !` `` site (format-adapters/claude.ts:655), which merely CLASSIFIES the pattern as `bash-execution` capability metadata and performs no substitution.  (3) CONSEQUENCE, TESTED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER. Ran the real exported function against the docs' own bodies (bun, importing the shipped module):   - docs' `pr-summary` skill body (three `` !`gh …` `` placeholders inside list items) => undefined. Zero substitutions.   - docs' quickstart `summarize-changes` body (`## Current changes` then a standalone `` !`git diff HEAD` `` line) => undefined. Zero substitutions — the doc's own worked example is inert here.   - body whose first line IS `` !`git diff HEAD` `` => command string "`git diff HEAD`", backticks included.   - documented multi-line ` ```! ` fenced block => undefined; the fence toggle at :24 classifies it as prose. Downstream: base-agent.ts:2446 returns `outputs.join('

')` and :2805 folds that string into `messageParts` as its own block joined with '

' — appended, never substituted at a placeholder. Permission side: SessionManager.ts:4595 builds `const permissionInput = { command: request.command, cwd: pinnedCwd }` and :4597 feeds it straight to `shouldAllowToolInMode('Bash', input, …)` plus `evaluatePermissionDslV1` — so the backtick-wrapped string is what the Bash allowlist matches against and what would be executed, where in bash `` `git diff HEAD` `` is command substitution, not the command.  NOT AN OWNER DECISION. 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 lists nine dated decisions (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) — none covers skill dynamic-context syntax. The only §3-adjacent skills row is `SkillMetadata.disallowedTools`, a different field. The introducing commit b83ccd05 ("feat(plugins): activate portable plugin peripherals", Step 5 "Govern skill shell context") records the 32 KiB/5 s budget and "inject the result as volatile context" but records no decision to diverge from the placeholder syntax. Not a branding/rename difference and not a dropped-subscription-flow difference.  SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM CHECK. The composer `!` shell gate (SessionManager.ts:2708, :16263) is user-typed composer shell, a different subsystem; the finding correctly names the skill dynamic-context path. session-tools-core/src/validation.ts:241 independently confirms the repo's own understanding is a one-shell "inline expansion" for a skill's `` !`command` `` blocks.  One narrowing the claim omits, which does not rescue it: materializeRuntimeSkillContext returns '' unless `capabilityTurnRuntime.provider === 'pi'` and the skill has `pluginRuntime` set (base-agent.ts:2407, :2411), so user/project skills and the whole Claude backend never run a command at all. That widens the gap rather than closing it.

column5: To disable this behavior for skills and custom commands from user, project, plugin, or [additional-directory](#skills-from-additional-directories) sources, set `"disableSkillShellExecution": true` in [settings](/docs/en/settings).
column6: Dynamic context injection applies to skills and custom commands from user, project, plugin and additional-directory sources.
column7: Two divergences on one line. (1) Our executor runs only for skills with `skill.pluginRuntime` set and only when `runtime?.provider === 'pi'` — a user or project skill, and any skill on the Claude backend, never executes its command. (2) `disableSkillShellExecution` has no reader anywhere in the repo, so the managed-settings kill switch the page recommends for exactly this capability cannot be applied.
column9: Quote verified verbatim at skills.md:539, but that line has four sentences and the finding read only the first. Both halves of the claimed divergence fail. CITATION: base-agent.ts:2391 is a bare closing brace inside latestSkillSelections; the real gates are :2405 (runtime?.provider !== 'pi') and :2411 (!skill?.pluginRuntime), inside materializeRuntimeSkillContext (:2401). HALF 1 (scope): that our host executor runs only for plugin skills is the recorded deliberate posture, not drift. The parity audit's Deliberate-differences table (2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1547) states 'No shell execution from skill/command bundle text (!`cmd`, @file detected and deferred) | Keeps a prompt-injection and supply-chain surface closed. The defect is the silence, not the refusal', and the closure is visible in code: format-adapters/claude.ts:655 classifies !`...` as bash-execution and emits a plugin.deferred.claude_command_dynamic_substitution diagnostic (:741-749), so custom commands are detected-and-deferred, not silently dropped. The narrow re-opening for plugin skills is its own recorded unit — commit b83ccd05 'feat(plugins): activate portable plugin peripherals', plan step 5 'Govern skill shell context' (docs/current-plans/pi-claude-post-parity.md at that commit), which specifies exactly the executor contract, the 32 KiB cap and the 5 s timeout now in capabilities/runtime-skill-context.ts. HALF 1 is also factually wrong about the Claude backend: claude-agent.ts:305 passes settingSources ['user','project','local'] to the Claude Agent SDK and claude-agent.ts:1627-1628 sets plugins: [] because 'skills are handled by BaseAgent.chat() via read-before-execute'. Per agent-sdk/skills.md:20 and :28 the SDK itself discovers and loads user/project skills from ~/.claude/skills and .claude/skills under those very setting sources, so on that backend the SDK owns the substitution — 'any skill on the Claude backend never executes its command' is not established and is contradicted by who owns the path. HALF 2 (kill switch): the identifier is genuinely absent from our TypeScript (0 hits in *.ts under packages/apps/scripts), but the consequence is false twice over. (a) On the Claude backend the setting IS live: it is declared in the shipped SDK's own settings type, node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:4922 'Disable inline shell execution in skills and custom slash commands from user, project, or plugin sources', and is present in the claude binary and in the bundled apps/electron/resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js — with settingSources user/project/local the SDK reads it from the same settings.json the page names. (b) On Pi, where our own executor runs, an administrator CAN forbid skill-originated shell — this is the 'enforcement one layer up' trap. SessionManager.runtimeSkillContextExecutor (:4521) authorizes every command as a Bash call carrying semanticId 'skill-context' (:4670-4674) against capabilityRuntime.managedPermissionDsl (:4580), which is this.managedPiPolicy.permissionDsl (:4096) — the admin-delivered managed policy, applied with managedPermissionRulesOnly. permission-dsl.ts:648 matches {kind:'tool', semanticId} against request.semanticId, so a managed rule {action:'deny', match:{kind:'tool', semanticId:'skill-context'}} denies exactly this capability and nothing else; a bash-kind deny covers it too. On deny the executor throws before any spawn and writes a receipt outcome 'denied' / code 'permission_denied' / isolationProfile 'not-started' (:4683-4686), and SessionManager.process-supervisor.test.ts:341-371 is the positive control for a managed DSL deny blocking the sibling command-hook runner on the identical wiring. So the kill switch the page recommends exists here under this fork's own admin surface (managed permission DSL + per-capability plugin toggles, itself a recorded deliberate difference in the audit's section 4) rather than under Claude's settings key name. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3, but the same file's addendum documents the provider === 'pi' gating pattern this finding rediscovered.

column5: The `skillOverrides` setting controls skill visibility from your [settings](/docs/en/settings) instead of the skill's own frontmatter.
column6: A settings key overrides per-skill visibility from settings rather than frontmatter, with four states, absent meaning `on`, and `off` also hiding the skill from SDK and Remote-Control command lists.
column7: No reader. `grep -ran "skillOverrides"` over the repo hits only two planning documents (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-session-scheduling.md:193` and the r-queue verification spec). None of the four states exists, so the only way to hide a skill checked into a shared repo is to edit its SKILL.md.
column9: All three checks pass and no refutation was found. (1) The quoted sentence exists VERBATIM at skills.md:637 under the heading '### Override skill visibility from settings'. The whole line is three sentences and none of them reverses the conclusion: 'The `skillOverrides` setting controls skill visibility from your [settings](/docs/en/settings) instead of the skill's own frontmatter. Use it for skills whose SKILL.md you don't want to edit, such as ones checked into a shared project repo. The `/skills` menu writes it for you: highlight a skill and press `Space` to cycle states, then `Enter` to save to `.claude/settings.local.json`.' The four-state table (on / name-only / user-invocable-only / off), 'A skill that is absent from `skillOverrides` is treated as "on"' (:652) and the v2.1.199 SDK/Remote-Control clause (:650) are all present as claimed. (2) The cited repo evidence is accurate: `grep -ran skillOverrides` (with -a, so NUL-bearing files are not skipped) hits docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-session-scheduling.md:193 and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:264,:559 plus this sweep's own output files. Zero hits under packages/ or apps/. A case-insensitive sweep for every plausible Nessy renaming of the key (skilloverride, skill_override, skillVisibility, name-only/nameOnly, user-invocable-only/userInvocableOnly) finds no settings key of any spelling; packages/shared/src/config/{storage.ts,validators.ts,config-defaults.json} and pi-harness/managed-policy.ts carry no skill-visibility key at all. (3) One layer up and down, the CONSEQUENCE was verified separately from the identifier and it holds for the subsystem named. Candidate refutations checked and each ruled out: (a) Plugin capabilities DO have a persisted settings-side toggle (`setCapabilityEnabled` -> capabilities.json via packages/shared/src/capabilities/policy-store.ts, tri-state per scope global<workspace<project with a managed tier on top) - but that store's own docblock scopes it to plugin capabilities, its PolicyTarget is {pluginKey, pluginInstanceId}, and Claude's page explicitly exempts plugin skills ('Plugin skills are not affected by `skillOverrides`. Manage those through `/plugin` instead.'), so this is the sibling subsystem, not the mechanism, and it cannot reach a native SKILL.md. (b) Native capabilities in resolver.ts:1595 derive `enabled` from `record.sourceEnabled`, which native-sources.ts sets only from a Source's `sources/<slug>/config.json` `enabled` field - skills have no such config file. (c) The only other native disable path is `sessionSelection.transientlyDisabledKeys` (resolver.ts:739,:1574,:1618,:1774), which is transient by design AND has no producer anywhere outside resolver.ts - so even the session-scoped half is unwired. (d) `Skill(name)` permission rules are not an escape either: `Skill` appears in BUILT_IN_TOOLS (pre-tool-use.ts:134) but there is no `Skill` entry in PI_TOOL_BINDINGS, from which PERMISSION_RULE_TOOL_NAMES is derived, and skills are invoked via `[skill:name]` markers through extractModelSkillInvocations, not through a permission-gated `Skill` tool. (e) Project detect-consent (capabilities/project-contribution-detect.ts) and project trust are per-project and all-or-nothing (and resolver.ts:1623 applies trustState only to `kind === 'hook'`), not a per-skill override. (f) The model-facing listing, prompt-builder.ts buildSkillListingPart, filters solely on `disableModelInvocation` - a frontmatter field - confirming the listing side reads no settings override. Not an owner decision: none of the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 concerns skill visibility (they are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions). Not a deliberate fork difference either: skill visibility is unrelated to the dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows, the corporate gateway, or the NESSY_ renaming. On the contrary, the parity audit itself names this gap - 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1651 lists 'settings-level "restrict skill access" and "override skill visibility"' among what P7/P9 closed their frontmatter rows without, routed to R30a; R30's closure notes cover argument substitution, `effort`, `paths` and the /doctor surface, and never mention shipping skillOverrides. So the row is marked done on a scope that never included this half.

column5: To raise the budget, set the [`skillListingBudgetFraction`](/docs/en/settings#available-settings) setting (e.g. `0.02` = 2%) or the `SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET` environment variable to a fixed character count.
column6: The skill listing has a character budget that scales with the model's context window, is raisable by a settings key or an environment variable, and caps each entry's combined `description` + `when_to_use` at 1,536 characters.
column7: None of `skillListingBudgetFraction`, `SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET` or `skillListingMaxDescChars` has a reader. The 1,536 constant exists (`MAX_DERIVED_DESCRIPTION_CHARS`) but is applied only as a ceiling on a description DERIVED from the body, not to the listing entry; the listing path instead clamps each catalog entry's description at a hard 512 chars (`capability-catalog.ts:107`, `clampedText(input.description, 'description', 512, …)`) with no context-window scaling and no per-entry cap of 1,536.
column9: Doc quote is VERBATIM (skills.md line 920, first sentence of a four-sentence line; the rest adds skillOverrides "name-only" and skillListingMaxDescChars, and does not reverse the claim). The cited evidence line is also correct: packages/shared/src/skills/storage.ts:81 is `const MAX_DERIVED_DESCRIPTION_CHARS = 1_536;`, applied only to a description DERIVED from the body. And `grep -ran` (NUL-safe) over all .ts/.tsx/.js/.json outside node_modules/dist returns ZERO hits for skillListingBudgetFraction, SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET and skillListingMaxDescChars, so the identifier half of the claim is true. The finding is refuted on step 3: the stated OUR STATE names the WRONG SUBSYSTEM and therefore reports a false consequence. `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/capability-catalog.ts:108` (not :107 -- line 107 is `kind: input.kind,`) is NOT the skill listing path. It is the Pi-harness capability/tool catalog whose kinds are `'builtin' | 'session' | 'plugin' | 'mcp' | 'app'` (capability-catalog.ts:9) -- there is no skill kind -- and whose own comment at :84-88 says the clamped text is "Free text shown to the model in `mcp__tool_search` results." That is the sibling-subsystem trap named in AGENTS.md and in inert-worklist section 4 shape 4. The REAL skill listing is `PromptBuilder.buildSkillListingPart()` (packages/shared/src/agent/core/prompt-builder.ts:403-447), and it does have a listing character budget and a per-entry description cap: `SKILL_LISTING_MAX_CHARS = 4_000` (:105) enforced at :433 with a truthful "(N more skills not listed)" overflow at :441-444, and `SKILL_LISTING_DESCRIPTION_MAX_CHARS = 180` (:113) applied per entry by `boundedListingText` (:126-131). So "no listing budget" and "512 chars per entry" are both wrong; the true numbers are 4,000 total and 180 per entry. The deviation is also RECORDED WITH A REASON, not undiscovered: prompt-builder.ts:107-113 cites Claude's figure explicitly -- "Claude truncates a skill's `description` (plus `when_to_use`) at 1,536 characters in its own listing, but that is a per-entry cap against a much larger listing budget; here one verbose skill must not be able to consume the whole block, so an entry gets one line" -- and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-skills-invocation.md states it as a Global Constraint (:64-67: the listing "must be bounded by a stated budget, and the budget must be a constant with a comment saying what it costs, not a magic number"), with a measured cost table at :580-590. The driver is architectural and fork-specific: the listing rides Pi's CACHED system prefix and is paid on every request of every session (prompt-builder.ts:99-104), which is also why a fixed constant was chosen over a context-window fraction. It is NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3 (those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) -- it is a plan-recorded design decision instead.

column5: Add `context: fork` to your frontmatter when you want a skill to run in isolation.
column6: Four frontmatter fields govern where and how a skill runs: `context: fork`, `background` (default `true` for a fork as of v2.1.218), `hooks` scoped to the skill's lifecycle, and `shell: bash|powershell` for inline command blocks.
column7: All four are explicitly parsed-and-dropped: `IGNORED_SKILL_FIELDS` maps `context` → 'skills do not run in a forked subagent context here', `background` → "it only applies with 'context: fork', which is not implemented", `hooks` → 'per-skill hook scopes are not implemented', `shell` → 'inline shell blocks always run under bash'. The list is deliberate and documented in-file; a skill that sets `context: fork` runs inline in the main conversation instead of in an isolated subagent, which is a behaviour inversion rather than a no-op.
column9: All three checks pass; nothing refutes the finding. (1) VERBATIM: `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md` (933 lines, fetched 2026-08-02) line 547 reads in full: "Add `context: fork` to your frontmatter when you want a skill to run in isolation. The skill content becomes the prompt that drives the subagent. It won't have access to your conversation history." The quoted sentence is the first of three on that line and the two that follow reinforce rather than reverse it. The other three fields are in the frontmatter reference table: `:271` `background` — "Only applies with `context: fork`. Set to `false` to wait ... Default: `true`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.218 or later."; `:272` `hooks` — "Hooks scoped to this skill's lifecycle."; `:274` `shell` — "Shell to use for !`command` and ```! blocks in this skill. Accepts `bash` (default) or `powershell`." The claimed behaviour is accurate on every field, including the v2.1.218 default. (2) CITED LINE: packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.ts:246 declares `IGNORED_SKILL_FIELDS` and :247-:250 carry the four mappings word for word as claimed ('skills do not run in a forked subagent context here'; "it only applies with 'context: fork', which is not implemented"; 'per-skill hook scopes are not implemented'; 'inline shell blocks always run under bash'). The in-file comment block at :223-:245 states the reasoning, so the finding does not misrepresent our state. (3) LAYER UP / LAYER DOWN — the consequence was verified separately from the identifier. Down: the map's only consumer is validation.ts:352, which emits an author-facing WARNING from `skill_validate`; nothing else reads it. `rg -na` across packages/ and apps/ finds no read of a skill-frontmatter `context` key anywhere — not in packages/shared/src/skills/{types,storage}.ts, not in packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-context.ts, not in the Claude plugin format adapter (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts maps no skill `context`). This repo does have a fork mechanism (`FORK_AGENT_NAME = 'fork'`, packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:208; R29a/R29b, docs/architecture/fork-subagents.md, /subtask), but it is the Agent-tool/`/subtask` conversation fork that INHERITS the parent conversation — the opposite of skills.md:547's fresh, history-less subagent — and no skill frontmatter routes into it. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 — none of the nine concerns skill frontmatter. Only wording quibbles: the fields are not 'parsed' into anything (SkillMetadataSchema is .passthrough(); they are warned about and dropped), and 'behaviour inversion' overstates it slightly — dropping the field yields the same inline behaviour a fieldless skill would get, so the divergence is a missing isolation guarantee rather than an inverted one.

column9: All three checks pass, so the gap survives. (1) The quote is VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md` line 128 reads exactly `* The nested one appears under a directory-qualified name, `apps/web:deploy`.` The whole surrounding block reinforces rather than reverses it: line 122 (`Skills also load from nested `.claude/skills/` directories below your working directory. The five `skillRecords(` call sites in the file (`:903` `~/.agents/skills`, `:904` `<configDir>/skills`, `:949` workspace `skills`, `:1016` `.nessy-agent/skills`, `:1065` the ancestor walk) are the complete set; none takes a descendant directory. (3) One layer up and one layer down both check out, including the two named traps. UP: the fork DOES have a lazy, file-touch-triggered delivery channel — `base-agent.ts:1152 getPathScopedRulePreToolUseContext` composes `cache.pathScopedRules + cache.pathGatedSkills + nestedInstructionProbe()` and dispatches activations on every file-touching tool call — but its three consumers are path-scoped rules, `paths:`-gated skills ALREADY in the inventory, and nested INSTRUCTION files (`activateNestedInstructionFiles` -> `discoverNestedInstructionFiles`, whose loop iterates `PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES` only, `native-sources.ts:846`). So the exact mechanism the doc describes exists in this repo for AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md and was deliberately not extended to skill directories. Nothing upstream already handles it: the consequence is real, verified separately from the identifier. DOWN / sibling-subsystem trap: `grep -rain 'directory-qualified|qualified name|apps/web:deploy'` over `packages/` returns only unrelated hits — `native-sources.ts:250 qualifiedKey()` is an internal dedupe key (`kind::scope::workspaceId::projectKey::discriminator::logicalName`), never a model- or user-facing skill name; `TurnCard.tsx:709` 'qualified name (workspaceId:slug)' is the WORKSPACE-scoped naming subsystem, not directory-scoped; `automations/types.ts:427` is MCP tool naming. column5: Because the inputs above are read regardless of `settingSources`, an SDK process can pick up host-level configuration and per-directory memory.

column7: `buildClaudeSessionOptions` sets `settingSources: ['user', 'project', 'local']` and nothing else. None of `autoMemoryEnabled`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY`, `disableClaudeAiConnectors`, `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS` or `strictMcpConfig` appears anywhere in the repo (repo-wide `grep -ran` excluding node_modules returns zero). Consequences for this fork specifically: a Claude-backend session writes memories into `~/.claude/projects/`, outside Nessy's config dir and outside its capability inventory; and when the opt-in Claude Pro/Max login is used, the user's claude.ai MCP connectors attach to the session without passing Nessy's MCP source approval, which `mcpServers: {}` explicitly does not suppress.
column9: Doc sentence CONFIRMED verbatim at line 100 of claude-code-features.md, inside a <Warning> whose subject is multi-tenant isolation. The rest of the finding does not survive. (1) WRONG FUNCTION NAME: there is no `buildClaudeSessionOptions` in this repo; the function at packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:272-308 is `buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions`, a deliberate three-option TURN-shape slice (systemPrompt / settingSources / optional child maxTurns), not the session options object. Same misnomer already recorded in the f057 verdict. Cited line :301 is the `}` closing `systemPrompt`; `settingSources` is :305. (2) THE ABSENCE GREP IS FALSE AS STATED. `grep -ranE 'autoMemoryEnabled|CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY|disableClaudeAiConnectors|ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS|strictMcpConfig' . | grep -v node_modules` returns 5 hits, not zero. Two of them are RECORDED OWNER DECISIONS in docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:93 'What we do not implement': claude.ai connectors + `disableClaudeAiConnectors` are categorised `inapplicable` ('We have no claude.ai account-side MCP connectors. Nessy's connector Sources are materialized from PLUGIN manifests ... and have no claude.ai origin to suppress'), and `--mcp-config`/`--strict-mcp-config` filtering is likewise `inapplicable` ('We have no such CLI flags'). Auto memory is a tracked queue row, not an unknown gap: 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1670-1676 item 12 already names `autoMemoryEnabled`, `autoMemoryDirectory` and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY` as a subsystem to cover. Only `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS` is genuinely absent everywhere. (3) THE LOAD-BEARING CONSEQUENCE IS FALSE, ONE LAYER UP -- the repo's textbook 'identifier unwired, consequence already handled upstream' shape. The claim is that 'a Claude-backend session writes memories into ~/.claude/projects/, outside Nessy's config dir'. It does not. packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:221-226 (`workspaceClaudeConfigDir`) + :254-255 (`buildClaudeSubprocessEnv`) set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to `<CONFIG_DIR>/workspaces/<workspaceId>/claude-config` for every Claude SDK subprocess, assigned AFTER envOverrides so an ambient host value cannot win. It is live, not dead code: `getDefaultOptions` (options.ts:276) is the only SDK options builder and it calls it, and SessionManager.ts:11840 and :18699 both put `NESSY_WORKSPACE_ID: managed.workspace.id` into envOverrides on the real session path (guarded by packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/workspace-claude-config-dir.test.ts). Per env-vars.md:356 `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` overrides '(default: `~/.claude`). All settings, session history, and plugins are stored under this path', and memory.md:356 puts auto memory at `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/` -- i.e. under that same directory. So auto memory lands at `~/.nessy-agent/workspaces/<id>/claude-config/projects/<project>/memory/`: inside Nessy's config dir, and additionally isolated PER WORKSPACE, which is stricter than the CLI default the doc describes. The doc's own multi-tenant advice is 'run each tenant in its own filesystem' -- which is materially what the per-Workspace config dir already does; the CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY half of that advice addresses cross-tenant leakage that per-Workspace redirection has already removed. (4) Product-shape context: `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` defaults OFF, so the Claude Pro/Max card is absent from default builds -- the claim concedes the opt-in but the residual is smaller than framed.

column5: If you already have hooks in your project's `.claude/settings.json` and you set `settingSources: ["project"]`, those hooks run automatically in the SDK with no extra configuration.
column6: With `settingSources` including `"project"`, hooks from the workspace's own `.claude/settings.json` execute inside the SDK session with no extra configuration.
column7: We opt into `'project'` and `'local'` unconditionally, so a cloned repository's `.claude/settings.json` hooks run in a Claude-backend session. Nessy has its own project-trust gate for exactly this class of content — `native-sources.ts:995` reads project resources only when `context.projectTrustState === 'trusted'` — but that gate governs the Nessy capability runtime, not the Claude SDK subprocess, which reads the same files independently. The two trust boundaries disagree for the same directory.
column9: REFUTED AS A DOC DIVERGENCE, though the underlying security observation is real and was already on record. (1) QUOTE: verbatim, line 190 of the fetched .md. The line is two sentences; the first ('Both types execute during the same hook lifecycle.') does not reverse it. (2) EVIDENCE LINE: drifted. claude-agent.ts:301 is the closing brace of the systemPrompt object; the actual `settingSources: ['user', 'project', 'local']` is line 305, inside buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions. Content confirmed, anchor stale (older plans anchored :301 too). (3) THE REFUTATION: this page is not violated - it is satisfied. Line 84 of the same page says 'Omitting `settingSources` is equivalent to ["user", "project", "local"]', and the code comment at claude-agent.ts:302-304 says exactly that: 'Omitting this loads all three sources (CLI defaults). Spelling out the same three keeps today's behavior - including CLAUDE.md discovery, which needs project - while making the choice visible instead of implicit.' We implement the documented default verbatim, and the finding's own 'our state' text concedes that project hooks run. There is no gap against this page; the row is classified 'gap' but names no behaviour the page specifies and we lack. What it actually describes is a Nessy-internal inconsistency between two trust subsystems, which this page neither specifies nor governs. (4) ALREADY RECORDED: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-phase4-findings.md:347-350 states the identical seam under 'Two doors this unit does not close, both recorded rather than faked' - 'we pass settingSources: [user,project,local] to that SDK, so an opened repository's own .claude/settings.local.json can set outputStyle and the SDK honours it inside the preset, whatever our resolver decides. The trust gate this unit added covers our resolver and not the SDK's.' It is carried into the generated deviation register (2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:237) via the output-style-contract plan. Same door, sibling symptom (outputStyle instead of hooks). It is NOT one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3 - I read all nine and none is this. (5) CONSEQUENCE, VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, AND IT HOLDS - so I do not refute on that ground: resolveSpawnCwd (claude-agent.ts:3045-3067) prefers session.sdkCwd, and sessions/storage.ts:200 sets `sdkCwd = options?.workingDirectory ?? getSessionDirPath(...)`, so for a project session the SDK subprocess cwd IS the opened repository. Nessy's own gate is real and does cover the same file: native-sources.ts:995 opens the trusted-only branch, and :1051-1059 reads `.claude/settings.json` / `.claude/settings.local.json` as project-scope 'permission' records inside it. And the upstream gate that could have made the consequence false does not: I disassembled the installed native binary (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude). `$D()` builds the allowed-source list from the settingSources allowlist plus flagSettings/policySettings with no trust check; `kvl()` collects `hooks` from [userSettings, projectSettings, localSettings] filtered only by `allowManagedHooksOnly`; and Claude Code's own workspace-trust predicate short-circuits in SDK mode - `function fve(){if(kr())return!0;return Ip()}` with `function kr(){return!Nt.isInteractive}`, so hasTrustDialogAccepted never gates a non-interactive subprocess. The trust-boundary disagreement is therefore genuine. (6) TWO SCOPING CORRECTIONS the finding overstates: it is project sessions only - a workspace-only session gets sdkCwd = Nessy's per-session directory, and the page (line 86) says project settings.json and hooks load only from <cwd>/.claude/ with no parent-directory fallback, so no repository hooks load there; and NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE defaults OFF, which since SDK 0.2.113 means the native claude binary is not bundled, so the Claude backend cannot spawn at all in a default packaged build.

column5: The SDK sets the `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_SDK_FILE_CHECKPOINTING` environment variable internally only when `enable_file_checkpointing` (Python) or `enableFileCheckpointing` (TypeScript) is enabled on the session performing the rewind; the bare CLI never sets it.
column6: File checkpointing must be turned on per-session through the SDK option; when it is not, the session performing a rewind has no checkpoint data and the rewind cannot restore anything.
column7: `enableFileCheckpointing` occurs 0 times in `claude-agent.ts` (verified with `grep -ac`, so a NUL byte cannot be hiding it). The SDK query options object built around `claude-agent.ts:1245` passes `cwd`, `includePartialMessages`, `tools`, `permissionMode`, `allowDangerouslySkipPermissions`, `hooks` and the turn-shape options — never `enableFileCheckpointing`. Nessy's own `createFileCheckpoint` has only two non-test callers (Pi's local tool runtime and the Nestor Cloud executor); Claude's Write/Edit/NotebookEdit calls all execute inside the SDK subprocess, so nothing on the Claude path writes a checkpoint.
column9: Doc sentence verified verbatim at line 767 of the curl'd page (whole line read; the surrounding troubleshooting block does not reverse it). The cited repo facts are all accurate: grep -ac enableFileCheckpointing packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts -> 0 (the file really does carry NUL bytes, so -a mattered), grep -ac rewindFiles -> 0, the SDK Options literal opens at claude-agent.ts:1213 and never names either symbol, file-checkpoints.ts:571 is createFileCheckpoint, and its only two non-test callers are packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1644 and packages/shared/src/agent/backend/nestor-cloud/tool-executor.ts:155. The finding is still refuted on two independent grounds. (1) WRONG CONTRACT / WRONG SUBSYSTEM. The quoted sentence governs the SDK's own rewind API - Query.rewindFiles() and claude -p --rewind-files - and the 'File rewinding is not enabled' error they raise. Nessy never calls that API (rewindFiles occurs 0 times repo-wide outside docs). Nessy's rewind is an independent engine: revertFileCheckpoint / rewindToMessage (SessionManager.ts:13687, :13776) read OUR manifest at <sessionPath>/file_checkpoints/, never the SDK store. So the missing option is not the cause of an empty Claude rewind, and setting it would not change one observable byte - it would populate a store no Nessy code reads. This is trap #3 from inert-worklist section 4 in its causal form: the identifier really is unwired, but the stated causal chain is false. (2) DATED RECORDED DECISION WITH A WRITTEN REASON - not one of the nine in inert-worklist section 3, but a plan-level one, which AGENTS.md treats as exactly the same kind of artifact ('A plan is where a deviation's reason lives'). docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-25-claude-backend-turn-contract.md Task 6 ran this precise investigation and concluded 'Scope chosen: none. Stopping and reporting, per the plan's stop condition,' naming two blockers that make Query.rewindFiles() unreachable: claude-agent.ts:2345 nulls this.currentQuery in chatImpl's finally while rewind is a between-turns action after strictDrainSessionForMutation, so no subprocess exists to receive the SDKControlRewindFilesRequest; and rewindFiles takes an SDK user-message UUID that nothing on the Claude path captures. The plan then lists 'Setting enableFileCheckpointing: true on its own' as deliberately NOT done, because with no reachable caller it is a speculative unused option. docs/architecture/file-checkpoint-rewind.md:124 and :130 carry the same verdict as shipped architecture record. The underlying product gap is real but is already an open, tracked row, not a new divergence: 2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md P4 (Tier 2), which also corrects the harm this finding inherits - the SDK store lands in ~/.claude/file-history/, not the working dir.

column5: For background subagents only, `CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS` sets a stall watchdog that fires when a `run_in_background` subagent stops producing output; it is not a total-runtime deadline.
column6: A background subagent that stops producing output is caught by a stall watchdog, which aborts it, marks the task failed and surfaces the error to the parent with any partial result.
column7: No stall or idle watchdog exists for background subagents. `runBackground`/`runAllAndSeal` is bounded only by the abort signal; there is no output-idle timer. Repo-wide `grep -ran 'STALL|stallTimeout|watchdog'` over `packages/shared/src`, `packages/pi-agent-server/src` and `packages/server-core/src` returns no match, while the same sweep for `NESSY_*TIMEOUT*` returns `NESSY_ASK_USER_TIMEOUT_MS`, `NESSY_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT` and `NESSY_BROWSER_OPEN_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS` — so the grep is a working positive control, not a false absence.
column9: The quoted sentence EXISTS VERBATIM (hosting.md line 341, 'Known limitations' table, row 'No per-subagent wall-clock deadline'; whole line read, the second half does not reverse it). The cited file:line is also real: subagent-tool.ts:605-616 is the background-dispatch return and the Pi orchestrator has no output-idle timer there. The finding still fails on four counts. (1) WRONG SUBSYSTEM, the exact trap named in inert-worklist section 4 item 4. agent-sdk/hosting.md governs the Claude Agent SDK, and CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS is a knob of the Claude Code binary itself. This fork vendors that binary and the implementation is live inside it: node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude contains 'g=je.CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS||600000' inside the async-agent loop (adjacent to turnStartTime, setMode("responding"), shouldNotifyOwner). Nessy does not scrub it: claude-agent.ts:915 deletes only CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. So on the backend this page is about, the stall watchdog is present and honoured with its 600000 ms default. The consequence ('no stall or idle watchdog exists for background subagents') is therefore false for the subsystem the doc names, and packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts is Nessy's own Pi orchestration, not an Agent SDK run_in_background subagent. (2) THE CLAIMED POSITIVE CONTROL IS FALSE. The finding asserts grep -ran 'STALL|stallTimeout|watchdog' over packages/shared/src, packages/pi-agent-server/src and packages/server-core/src 'returns no match'. It does match, in a named directory: packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6076 ('truly hung subprocesses are caught by the stdio death watchdog') and, substantively, packages/shared/src/mcp/validation.ts:230-419, which implements a real two-timer connect watchdog with an explicit IDLE arm (createConnectWatchdog(connectIdleMs, connectCeilingMs), watchdog.kick(), Promise.race([client.connect(transport), watchdog.promise])). An absence claim whose own grep is demonstrably wrong does not stand. (3) THE DOC'S PRIMARY PRESCRIPTION IS IMPLEMENTED. The row is a documented LIMITATION of the SDK, not a required feature, and its first sentence is 'Cap each subagent with maxTurns in its AgentDefinition.' Nessy carries maxTurns end to end: packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:401/418-419/451 validates it (positive integer, string-or-number), packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:163 carries it onto the descriptor, and spawner.ts:571-574 forwards it with the comment 'The host enforces maxTurns and clamps permissionMode against the parent'. So the named mitigation is built on the Pi path too, and the claim that the run is 'bounded only by the abort signal' is wrong on top of maxTurns, stop_task and the capability-generation teardown reachable through registerBackgroundChildTask's BackgroundTaskRegistry entry. (4) THE CLAIMED BEHAVIOUR EMBELLISHES THE DOC. The page says only that the watchdog 'fires'; 'aborts it, marks the task failed and surfaces the error to the parent with any partial result' appears nowhere on the page. Finally, this is not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3, and it is not a deliberate product difference (subscription-flow drop, gateway targeting, NESSY_ rename) - it is refuted on subsystem misattribution plus a false absence, not on scope. The coverage map already verdicts agent-sdk/hosting as green, 'all built' via R6.

column9: All three checks pass; the gap survives, with two corrections to the original 'our state'. (1) QUOTE IS VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts.md` line 54 begins exactly: "The SDK reads CLAUDE.md when the matching setting source is enabled: `'project'` loads `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/CLAUDE.md` from the working directory, and `'user'` loads `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`." CLAUDE.md loading is controlled by setting sources, not by the `claude_code` preset." Line 360 restates it. And this is NOT an SDK-only quirk: `memory.md:60` (the load-order table) gives Project instructions as "`./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md`" and `memory.md:69` says "A project CLAUDE.md can be stored in either `./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md`", so the CLI contract is the same. (2) CITED LINES ARE ACCURATE. `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:82` is `export const PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES = ['AGENTS.md', 'CLAUDE.md', 'CLAUDE.local.md'];` and `:845` is `for (const fileName of PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES) { ... const absolutePath = join(dir, fileName);`. Every one of the five production consumers joins a bare name onto a DIRECTORY, never onto `.claude`: `:845` (nested), `:987` (workspace root), `:1077` (ancestor walk, `join(dir, name)`), `:1088` (working directory, `join(workingDirectory, name)`). `grep -ran "CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"` shows the only path-building use is `:1056`, `join(workingDirectory, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, name)` for `settings.json`/`settings.local.json`; `CLAUDE_RULES_DIR` (`:727`) is `.claude/rules`. No NUL-byte blind spot: every absence grep used `-a`. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. A probe calling the production entry point `buildNativeCapabilityInventory` on a trusted temp project holding BOTH `<root>/CLAUDE.md` and `<root>/.claude/CLAUDE.md` returned exactly one instruction record (`logicalName: 'CLAUDE.md'`, `sourcePath: <root>/CLAUDE.md`) and zero records of any kind whose JSON mentions `.claude`. The control fires, the subject does not. The legacy route is the same: `readProjectContextFile(root)` from `packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts` returned `null` for the `.claude/CLAUDE.md`-only fixture (`CONTEXT_FILE_PATTERNS` at `:31` is directory-level, and its user tier is `~/.nessy-agent`, `:136`). ONE LAYER UP / DOWN, both traps checked. UP: the lazy channel IS wired in production — `base-agent.ts:1162 nestedInstructionProbe()` -> `:1175 activateNestedInstructionFiles` -> `:1252 discoverNestedInstructionFiles` — so it is not an unwired identifier; but it is triggered by a file READ and delivers to message history, so it does not satisfy the launch-time `'project'`-source contract the quote describes. DOWN / sibling subsystem: `.claude/` IS read by this fork for three other things (`settings.json` and `settings.local.json` as permission records at `native-sources.ts:1050-1058`, and `.claude/rules/` as a memory tier at `:1110`), so naming the wrong subsystem is ruled out — the divergence is specifically the instruction-file location, inside a `.claude/` interop surface the fork otherwise implements. NOT AN OWNER DECISION: none of the nine dated entries in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) touches instruction-file discovery, and `grep -ran '\.claude/CLAUDE\.md' docs/` finds no decision to decline the location — only `2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:536/545`, which scoped R28 to `.claude/rules/` and recorded `.claude/CLAUDE.md` as a documented `--add-dir` target, i.e. unimplemented rather than declined.
