column5: Telemetry is off until you set `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1` and choose at least one exporter.
column6: Setting the telemetry enable switch plus at least one exporter makes the agent export spans, metrics and structured log events over OTLP to a collector.
column7: There is no telemetry emitter. `grep -ran 'startSpan|tracer|trace_id|traceparent|TRACEPARENT'` over `packages` and `apps` returns zero non-test hits, and no `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY`, `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS`, `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` or `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` reader exists. The only OTEL surface is a five-entry allowlist/classification of exporter-transport variables used by the managed-settings approval dialog, which passes them through without anything consuming them. `packages/shared/src/agent/runtime-telemetry.ts` is an in-process per-turn record, not an OTLP export. (The Claude backend inherits the process env, so an operator who exports the variables would get telemetry from the SDK's own `claude` subprocess; the Pi and Codex runtimes, which are the shipped defaults, emit nothing.)
column9: Doc sentence confirmed verbatim (observability.md:41, whole line; the trailing second sentence 'The most common configuration sends all three signals over OTLP HTTP to a collector.' does not reverse it). The cited evidence is real but the finding's central factual claims are false. (1) 'There is no telemetry emitter' is wrong: packages/shared/src/telemetry/usage-metrics.ts is a full OTLP/HTTP metrics exporter (interval flush, shutdown drain, delta/cumulative temporality, nessy.token.usage + nessy.cost.usage sums) and packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/otlp-telemetry.ts is a full OTLP/HTTP logs exporter (batched resourceLogs, six-event closed set, HMAC-salted workspace/session hashes, one retry). (2) 'no CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY ... reader exists' is wrong: usage-metrics.ts:301-306 telemetryOptedIn() reads env.NESSY_ENABLE_TELEMETRY as primary and env.CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY as the compat alias, and it is the gate for BOTH signals (otlp-telemetry.ts:43,200). 'no OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER / OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER reader' is wrong: otelExporterDisabled() (usage-metrics.ts:318-325) reads both selectors and honours 'none' as a hard disable, called at usage-metrics.ts:336 and otlp-telemetry.ts:202. (3) The claim that the managed-settings allowlist passes OTEL vars through 'without anything consuming them' is the inference that fails: parseConfig in both exporters consumes OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, _HEADERS, _TIMEOUT and OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL — four of the five allowlisted entries — plus the per-signal _METRICS_ENDPOINT/_LOGS_ENDPOINT overrides and _METRICS_TEMPORALITY_PREFERENCE. (4) Consequence check one layer up and one layer down: both are wired end to end, not inert. storage-runtime.ts:272-273 constructs them; SessionManager.recordUsageMetrics (:3004) is called from the single usage-event site at :18382 whose own comment says 'The one emission site every backend passes through ... Pi, the Claude SDK, Codex and Nestor Cloud all land here'; emitPiTelemetry (:2984) feeds the log exporter; shutdown drains at :19246; and both hosts pass them through (apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:723, packages/server/src/index.ts:241). (5) The parenthetical 'the Pi and Codex runtimes, which are the shipped defaults, emit nothing' is exactly backwards — Pi is the only runtime carrying BOTH signals, since the harness log exporter is deliberately Pi-gated (:2988) while metrics are deliberately not provider-gated. The coverage map already records this page as built (2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:184, row B2, green). Not an inert-worklist section 3 decision; the residual gaps are recorded deliberate fork decisions (bank-fork privacy posture in the usage-metrics header, NESSY_ prefix rename with Claude compat alias).

column5: On `subtype="success"` it is `True` when the final model request failed, meaning the agent loop completed but the last API call returned an error.
column6: A result message with `subtype: "success"` can still be a failure: `is_error` is true and `api_error_status` carries the HTTP status when the agent loop finished but the final API call errored.
column7: `adaptResult` resolves the terminal reason from `stop_reason` and `subtype` only: `msg.subtype === 'success' ? undefined : ...`. Neither `is_error` nor `api_error_status` is read anywhere on the Claude path (`grep -an 'is_error|api_error'` over `backend/claude/event-adapter.ts` matches only the assistant-message `error` field at :295 and the auth `msg.error` at :660; `claude-agent.ts` has no hit at all). A turn that ends `subtype: "success", is_error: true, api_error_status: 529` is emitted as `{ type: 'complete', usage }` with no `terminalReason` and no error event, i.e. indistinguishable from a clean success.
column9: Quote is verbatim (python.md:1665, whole line reads '* `is_error`: `True` when the conversation ended in an error state. Always `True` on the `error_*` subtypes. On `subtype="success"` it is `True` when the final model request failed, meaning the agent loop completed but the last API call returned an error.'), and the IDENTIFIER half of the finding is true: adaptResult (event-adapter.ts:578-585) derives terminalReason from stop_reason + subtype only, and grep -a shows no read of is_error, api_error_status or terminal_reason anywhere on the Claude result path. But the CONSEQUENCE is false, which is exactly this repo's recurring false-positive shape: something one layer up already handled it. Disassembling the shipped CLI (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude) shows the success-result emitter derives BOTH flags from the last assistant message and nothing else: `if(vs.type==="assistant"){ ... Eo=Boolean(vs.isApiErrorMessage), wr=vs.apiErrorStatus??null }` then `yield{type:"result",subtype:"success",is_error:Eo,api_error_status:wr,...}`. That assistant message is built exclusively by the factory `tc({content,apiError,error,errorDetails})`, which sets `isApiErrorMessage:!0` AND `error:<SDKAssistantMessageError>`; `nRn` then stamps `r.apiErrorStatus=e.status`. Every one of the 44 `return tc({...})` branches supplies an error code (a 529 lands in `if(e instanceof es && e.status>=500)` -> `error:"server_error"`; the terminal fallbacks use `error:"unknown"`). The wire serializer `function*Fct` forwards it unconditionally: `yield{type:"assistant",message:r.message,parent_tool_use_id:null,session_id:kt(),uuid:r.uuid,error:r.error,...}`. So the very message that makes is_error true and carries api_error_status arrives at our adapter one message BEFORE the result, with `error` set, and adaptAssistant (event-adapter.ts:294-300) intercepts it first -- `if ('error' in message && message.error) { events.push(await this.callbacks.mapSDKError(...)); return; }` -- yielding a typed_error built by mapClaudeSdkAssistantError (claude-agent.ts:2660-2675, claude-sdk-error-mapper.ts:210). Covered by an existing test: claude-event-adapter.test.ts:231 'should handle SDK errors via callback' asserts assistant {error:'rate_limit'} -> typed_error. A 529 turn is therefore NOT 'indistinguishable from a clean success' and NOT emitted with 'no error event'. Not an inert-worklist section 3 owner decision (none of the nine touch this) and not a deliberate fork difference.

column5: Per-call timeout for `session_store.load()` and `list_subkeys()` during resume materialization, in milliseconds
column6: The store's `load()` and `list_subkeys()` calls during resume materialisation are bounded by a per-call timeout, defaulting to 60 seconds.
column7: Only `append` is timed out — `appendWithEnvelope` races the call against `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000`. The load path has no timeout at all: `restoreSessionFromMirror` does a bare `await store.load(...)`, and `restoreMissingMirroredSessions` calls it in a serial loop over every session directory during the pre-listing boot sweep. A mirror root on a stalled network mount therefore hangs session listing at startup indefinitely instead of failing after a bounded wait. (The quoted sentence is the `load_timeout_ms` row on agent-sdk/python.md; session-storage.md documents the same `load` call but does not restate the bound.)
column9: Fails all three checks. (1) CITATION. The quoted sentence does not exist on the cited page: the word 'timeout' occurs ZERO times in all 306 lines of agent-sdk/session-storage.md (grep -aic 'timeout' = 0; 'per-call' = 0). It is verbatim on agent-sdk/python.md:868, a ClaudeAgentOptions field row, with a differently-worded TypeScript twin at agent-sdk/typescript.md:431 marked '*Alpha.*'. The finding self-discloses this, but a finding filed under slug agent-sdk/session-storage whose contract sentence lives on another page is the citation failure the protocol treats as refuting outright. session-storage.md imposes no timeout requirement of any kind. (2) WRONG SUBSYSTEM. typescript.md:431 reads: 'Timeout in milliseconds for each `sessionStore.load()` and `sessionStore.listSubkeys()` call during resume materialization. If the adapter doesn't settle within this window, the query fails instead of hanging. Ignored when `sessionStore` is not set.' That bounds the SDK calling ARBITRARY USER-SUPPLIED adapter code (S3/Redis/Postgres over the network) and its documented outcome is to FAIL THE QUERY. packages/shared/src/sessions/mirror/ is not that surface. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-session-mirror-store.md:7 records the owner decision in the plan header: 'No shipped runtime consumes Claude's SDK option - the page is a design template, so the interface shape is portability guidance, not a compatibility surface', and the names were deliberately changed to SessionMirrorStore/MirrorSessionKey to avoid colliding with the local store-v2 SessionStore. There is exactly ONE adapter: config/session-mirror-settings.ts:37-38 throws 'unknown session mirror adapter' for any name but 'directory' (host.ts:76-78 carries the same note), so the pluggable-network-backend hazard class the bound exists for cannot be configured in this fork. (3) CONTRACT INVERSION. The documented behaviour on timeout is that the query FAILS. Our restore is deliberately the opposite and says so at restore.ts:76 and :90 - 'Never throws - a broken mirror must not break session open' - returning false. Adopting the documented bound verbatim would make a mirror stall fail session open, reversing a shipped intentional deviation. (4) THE list_subkeys HALF IS A DATED OWNER DECISION. 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 item 8: 'MirrorSessionKey.subpath + SessionMirrorStore.listSubkeys - 2026-07-28-session-mirror-store.md, Task 4: subagent-transcript restore via listSubkeys is contract-ready in the adapters but has no host producer yet - the queue mirrors only the main session JSONL today ... (exactly the documented consequence of the missing half).' restore.ts never calls listSubkeys, so half the claimed behaviour has no call to bound, by recorded decision. (5) CONSEQUENCE OVERSTATED ON ITS OWN FACTS. The identifier claim is literally true - restore.ts:129 is a bare `await store.load(...)` and SessionManager.ts:7573 awaits restoreMissingMirroredSessions inside initialize() before initGate.markReady(), so a stall there would block IPC. But the claimed remedy does not deliver the claimed benefit for the claimed scenario: the only adapter reads via fs/promises.readFile (directory.ts:74) on a filesystem path, and on a hung NFS/SMB mount that pins a libuv threadpool thread in an uninterruptible kernel wait - a Promise.race would resolve the JS promise while the thread stays pinned, and with UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=4 every other fs op in the process stalls regardless. Blast radius is also narrower than stated: restore.ts:98 returns immediately when no sessionMirror is configured (the default, 'absent config = no mirror, zero overhead'), and restore.ts:111 skips every session whose local jsonl is present and readable, so the normal boot performs zero mirror reads.

column5: Sessions are stored under `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl`, or under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl` if you set the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable, where `<encoded-cwd>` is the absolute working directory with every non-alphanumeric character replaced by `-` (so `/Users/me/proj` becomes `-Users-me-proj`).
column6: The SDK's resumable transcripts live under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so relocating that variable relocates the resume corpus.
column7: buildClaudeSubprocessEnv sets env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to <workspaceRoot>/claude-config whenever NESSY_WORKSPACE_ID is present, with no migration of any pre-existing projects/ transcripts and no per-workspace fallback lookup. The function's own doc-comment enumerates the hazards as 'TWO HAZARDS :356 NAMES, BOTH CHECKED AND CLEAR' — credentials and settings — even though the env-vars sentence it quotes says 'All settings, session history, and plugins are stored under this path'. Session history is the third hazard and is not addressed.
column8: packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:255 (`if (workspaceConfigDir) env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR = workspaceConfigDir;`), hazard list at packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:196; no migration — `grep -ran "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR" --include="*.ts" packages apps` returns only options.ts and plugins/data-paths.ts
column9: DOC SENTENCE CONFIRMED VERBATIM, sessions.md line 272, inside a <Tip>. Reading the WHOLE line changes what it demands: the Tip opens 'If a `resume` call returns a fresh session instead of the expected history, the most common cause is a mismatched `cwd`.' and closes 'If your resume call runs from a different directory, the SDK looks in the wrong place. The session file also needs to exist on the current machine.' Its subject is the <encoded-cwd> half, not the config-dir half, and it prescribes no migration and no fallback lookup. Line 274, the next non-blank line, prescribes the mitigation this fork actually built: 'To resume sessions across machines or in serverless environments, mirror transcripts to shared storage with a SessionStore adapter.' CITED CODE CONFIRMED AS FACT: options.ts:255 is `if (workspaceConfigDir) env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR = workspaceConfigDir;`, the hazard heading is at :196, and `grep -ran CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR --include=*.ts packages apps` returns only options.ts, plugins/data-paths.ts and tests. Every code fact in the finding is true. THE CONSEQUENCE IS FALSE, ONE LAYER UP AND ONE LAYER DOWN -- four ways. (1) NO LOOKUP IS POSSIBLE TO OMIT. `workspaceClaudeConfigDir` (options.ts:221-226) is `join(getWorkspaceRootPath(workspaceId), 'claude-config')` -- a pure deterministic function of the Workspace id, mkdir'd on demand, assigned AFTER envOverrides so an ambient host value cannot win (guarded by agent/__tests__/workspace-claude-config-dir.test.ts:43-52). Within a Workspace the transcript is written and read at the identical path on every spawn. There is no per-Workspace state to fall back to; a 'fallback lookup' would have nothing to look up. Steady-state resume is unaffected. (2) THE FRAGILE HALF -- THE ONE THE DOC ACTUALLY WARNS ABOUT -- IS HANDLED WITH MORE MACHINERY THAN THE DOC DESCRIBES, NOT LESS. `sdkCwd` is pinned at session creation and never moves: claude-agent.ts:1260-1266 'Use sdkCwd for SDK session storage - this is set once at session creation and never changes. This ensures SDK can always find session transcripts regardless of workingDirectory changes'; SessionManager.ts:14319-14325 `preserveSdkCwd` -- 'Never move `sdkCwd`, whatever the session's message count ... that same launch directory is the ONLY thing a resume can fall back to when the worktree is gone ... would silently delete the anchor'; a fork carries the PARENT's sdkCwd (SessionManager.ts:9088-9091, claude-agent.ts:3053) precisely so 'cross-CWD branches (e.g., worktree <-> main repo) fail with No conversation found' does not happen; and `resolveSpawnCwd` (claude-agent.ts:3045-3067) is a four-candidate, existence-checked fallback chain. That IS the per-session fallback lookup the finding says is missing, on the axis the doc names. (3) THE SDK JSONL IS NOT THIS FORK'S RESUME CORPUS OF RECORD, SO RELOCATING IT DOES NOT RELOCATE THE RESUME CORPUS. sessions/mirror/types.ts:5-7: 'Local disk is written FIRST and stays authoritative.' The user-visible transcript is `StoredSession.messages` in the workspace-partitioned v2 session store; that is what the UI renders and what a `SessionBundle` carries across machines. SessionManager.ts:18950-18953 proves the ownership on the move path: it regenerates `sdkCwd` for the target workspace because 'The source sdkCwd points to a path on the originating server which doesn't exist here', and ships `messages` in the bundle regardless -- i.e. the design already assumes the SDK jsonl does not travel. (4) A MISSED SDK TRANSCRIPT IS DETECTED AND RECOVERED, NOT SILENT. claude-agent.ts:1937-1966 detects the SDK's silent empty resume (`wasResuming && !receivedAssistantContent && !_isRetry`), clears sdkSessionId, calls `buildRecoveryContext()` (base-agent.ts:1944-1971) fed by SessionManager.ts:11913 `getRecoveryMessages` -- Nessy's OWN stored messages -- yields 'Restoring conversation context...' and retries. So the entire worst case of 'no migration' is a bounded, user-visible context truncation (last 6 messages, 1000 chars each) on the FIRST turn after upgrade for sessions that predate the redirect. Not loss of the resume corpus. THE 'THIRD HAZARD NOT ADDRESSED' CLAIM IS CONTRADICTED BY THE REPO'S OWN RECORDED VERIFICATION. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:166 already states '`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` moves storage off `~/.claude` (so the sweep must be config-dir-relative, and this is also B3's per-workspace `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` item)' -- the session-history consequence was written down at the moment the B3 item was specified, not overlooked. Same file :402 fact 12 repeats it from sessions.md. AND IT IS A RECORDED DECISION, NOT A DEFECT: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-isolation-hardening.md:82-95 Task 3 specifies the per-workspace redirect deliberately, in the shape plugins/data-paths.ts already used, with gate 'two workspaces do not see each other's config'. Per-Workspace session history IS the intent of that change -- a Workspace's sessions belonging to that Workspace is the product shape, so 'session history moves' is the feature, not an unhandled hazard. It is not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (checked; none matches), but it is a decision recorded in a plan, which the repo rule treats identically. RESIDUAL, AND IT IS A COMMENT NIT ONLY: env-vars.md:356 names four things (settings, session history, plugins, credentials); the doc-comment's 'TWO HAZARDS `:356` NAMES, BOTH CHECKED AND CLEAR' undercounts what the quoted sentence enumerates even though the two it omits are non-hazards here (session history moving per-Workspace is the intent; plugins were already redirected per-plugin by plugins/data-paths.ts:115/131). Also worth noting in passing: that plan has no `## Tracker` section, which the Editing Rules require. Neither is a behavioural divergence from the cited page.

column5: Only commands that work without an interactive terminal are dispatchable through the SDK; the `system/init` message lists the ones available in your session.
column6: The set of dispatchable slash commands is discovered from the system/init message's slash_commands array.
column7: The init branch of the Claude event adapter captures only `msg.tools`; `slash_commands` has no reader anywhere in the repo (`grep -ra "slash_commands" packages apps` → 0 hits). The session therefore cannot tell the user, or itself, which commands the running CLI actually offers.
column8: packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:625 (init branch reads `msg.tools` only); absence confirmed with `grep -ra "slash_commands" packages apps` (0 hits)
column9: Doc sentence verified verbatim (slash-commands.md line 9, last of a three-sentence paragraph; nothing later in the line reverses it) and the cited code is accurate: packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:622-630 adaptSystem's init branch captures only msg.tools, and `grep -ran "slash_commands" packages apps` returns 0 hits while node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:3994 does declare `slash_commands: string[]`. The IDENTIFIER claim therefore holds. The CONSEQUENCE — 'the session cannot tell the user, or itself, which commands the running CLI actually offers' — is false, and it names the wrong subsystem. Slash-command discovery in this fork does not live in the Claude event adapter; it is a first-party, backend-independent subsystem that does not consult the CLI at all: (1) packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts scans .nessy-agent/commands and .agents/commands (workspace root + trust-gated project root) for markdown commands; (2) SessionManager.listCustomSlashCommandSummaries (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:16016-16048) merges those native commands with plugin prompt/workflow commands, skill commands and MCP prompt commands and serves them over RPC_CHANNELS.workspace.LIST_CUSTOM_SLASH_COMMANDS ('workspace:listCustomSlashCommands', channels.ts:305, handler workspace.ts:72); (3) apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/AppShell.tsx:1408 loads that list and apps/electron/src/renderer/components/ui/slash-command-menu.tsx renders it alongside Nessy's own built-ins (agents, automations, compact, context, create-skill, create-plugin, export, init, memory, model, clear, help, subtask, usage, every permission mode, recent folders). So the session DOES tell the user which commands it offers. It also tells itself: the agent-callable SlashCommand tool carries its own whitelist and /help listing (packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/slash-command.ts:10,29-35; pi-agent.ts:5403-5424). Reading msg.slash_commands would in fact be WRONG here, because Nessy is the executor, not a pass-through. A custom command is resolved and body-expanded server-side (SessionManager.resolveCustomSlashCommand at :16080, invoked from rpc/sessions.ts:317-325) and sent as an ordinary prompt — the CLI never sees the '/name' token, so the CLI's dispatchable set does not bound ours. Only ONE command is ever handed to the SDK verbatim, guarded by the fork's own constant SDK_SLASH_COMMANDS = ['compact'] (claude-agent.ts:1665-1674). Everything else in the SDK's list (/clear, /context, /usage, bundled code-review/verify skills) is either a Nessy-owned UI command with different semantics or not a Nessy command at all; merging the CLI's array into the composer menu would advertise commands Nessy does not dispatch and would make the menu differ per backend, which is unacceptable when Pi is the default backend and NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE is off by default. Not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (none concerns slash commands), but it matches false-positive shapes 3 and 4 recorded in section 4 of that same file: enforcement one layer up, and an identically-named concern in a sibling subsystem.

column5: The `/clear` command resets the conversation to an empty context, so subsequent prompts start with no prior conversation history.
column6: /clear is an SDK-dispatchable command that resets conversation context, alongside /compact.
column7: ClaudeAgent's dispatch allowlist is `const SDK_SLASH_COMMANDS = ['compact'] as const;`. Every other slash command — /clear, /context, /usage — falls through to buildTextPrompt and is sent as an ordinary context-wrapped prompt rather than dispatched as a command.
column9: All three checks pass, so the finding stands. (1) QUOTE — verbatim at slash-commands.md:212, under the heading '### `/clear` - Reset conversation context'. The rest of that two-sentence line does not reverse it ('The previous conversation remains on disk and can be returned to by passing its session ID to the resume option'), and the page's other qualifiers do not rescue us: :214's 'no practical effect' caveat is scoped to one-shot query() calls that start with EMPTY context, whereas every ClaudeAgent turn passes `resume: this.sessionId` (claude-agent.ts:1607) so context is non-empty; and :217's version gate ('/clear in the SDK requires Claude Code v2.1.117 or later') is satisfied — the bundled binary reports '2.1.183 (Claude Code)' (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude --version, SDK 0.3.183). (2) STATE — the constant is exact, at claude-agent.ts:1665, not the cited :1643 (line drift only; :1643 is now `attemptedBranchCutoff`). It is the only definition of that identifier in the repo (grep -a; the only other hit is the built apps/electron/dist/main.cjs:404259), so no sibling-subsystem confusion. (3) CONSEQUENCE — verified separately and independently of the identifier, and nothing upstream or downstream handles /clear. Upstream: the composer menu ships a `clear` entry (slash-command-menu.tsx:162, asserted by slash-command-menu.test.tsx:29), composer capabilities expose it to every backend (`slash: { commandIds: 'all' }`, composer-capabilities.ts:103), and dispatchSlashCommandAction falls through all the UI-handler branches to MESSAGE_COMMANDS.clear = '/clear' (slash-command-actions.ts:57) and calls submitCommand, i.e. it is sent as an ORDINARY MESSAGE (FreeFormInput.tsx:1034 -> onSubmit). Mid-path: SessionManager.sendMessage's only command classifier is parseSessionCommand (SessionManager.ts:15095) and BaseAgent.chat's only one is the same function (base-agent.ts:2758); session-command.ts claims ONLY /compact and /subtask, so /clear takes the composed-context branch — which means by the time chatImpl sees it the pinned capability block is already prefixed and the `^\/([a-z]+)` match at :1670 cannot even fire. Downstream: buildTextPrompt (claude-agent.ts:2429-2468) pushes contextParts first and the user text last, so the model receives '/clear' as trailing prose. The one function that would implement it, clearSessionMessages (sessions/storage.ts:457, doc-comment 'Used for /clear command'), has NO production caller (only the index.ts re-export), and agent.clearHistory() likewise has no non-test caller. Not an owner decision: none of the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 touches slash commands (they are the seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, and three SessionMirrorStore rows). Not a de-brand or dropped-subscription product difference either — the /clear menu entry is shipped and user-reachable. The parity report even marks `agent-sdk/slash-commands` as 'all built' (2026-07-30-parity-report.md:161). The nearest prior art is the parity audit's S15 note (2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md, ~:527): '/clear and /help are dead the same way and deliberately NOT classifier-claimed until implemented' — an explicitly OPEN follow-up ('until implemented'), i.e. corroboration of this finding, not a decision to leave it.

column5: A result can also end with subtype `success` but no `structured_output` value, for example when the run completes without the agent producing a structured output. Treat that case as a failure as well.

column5: An Agent tool call that omits the [`run_in_background`](/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript) input launches a background subagent, and Claude sets `run_in_background: false` when it needs the result before continuing.
column6: An Agent tool call that omits run_in_background runs as a background subagent, regardless of nesting depth.
column7: The spawner's background default is `args.background ?? (depth === 1)` — top-level spawns default to background, nested spawns default to foreground. A nested Agent call that omits the input therefore blocks where Claude would detach it.
column9: The quote is verbatim (agent-sdk/subagents.md:186) and the cited code is accurate (spawner.ts:540-546 is literally `args.background ?? (depth === 1)` for the non-fork, non-definition-background case), but the CONSEQUENCE is false: the depth budget is enforced one layer up, before the background expression ever runs. spawner.ts:513 computes `depth = (args.depth ?? 0) + 1` and spawner.ts:518 refuses `depth > (cfg.maxDepth ?? DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH)` with 'Subagent depth limit exceeded'. DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH is 1 (spawner.ts:110) and DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG.depth is 1 (harness-manifest.ts:107); the shipped host never overrides it -- SessionManager's manifest seed (SessionManager.ts:4152-4164) sets contextSeed/sessionDepth/sessionIsFork/forkSubagent/tierModelMap and never `depth`, and configureSpawnerForGeneration (pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1279) takes maxDepth straight from that config. A nested Agent call therefore arrives with sessionDepth 1, computes depth 2 > 1, and is REFUSED -- it never reaches line 540, so it does not 'block where Claude would detach it'. The host mirrors the same refusal independently (child-session-service.ts:576 `depth > maxDepth` -> child-session-budgets-invalid). Consequently every spawn that can succeed at all has depth === 1, and `args.background ?? (depth === 1)` always yields true: an omitted `background` is background-by-default at every reachable depth, which is exactly the documented behaviour. Two further layers make nesting unreachable in practice: the built-in agent definitions carry only read/bash/edit/write/grep/find/ls (definitions.ts:157-158, no `subagent` tool), and a fork -- the one child that inherits the parent's full tool pool -- already defaults to `args.background ?? true` (spawner.ts:543) and its own nested spawn hits the same depth refusal. The nested-foreground arm becomes reachable only if a host explicitly raises `orchestrator.depth` above 1, a configuration the product never ships. The genuine divergence behind this row is the nesting-depth default (ours 1, Claude's 3 as of v2.1.219), which is already filed separately as f164; f077 double-counts it and attributes it to the wrong mechanism. Not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3, but the depth-keyed default is deliberate and documented (packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:86, docs/architecture/extension-first-pi-agent-runtime.md:307, spawner.ts:522-533).

One of `"completed"`, `"max_turns"`, `"tool_deferred"`, `"aborted_streaming"`, `"aborted_tools"`, `"hook_stopped"`, `"stop_hook_prevented"`, `"background_requested"`, `"blocking_limit"`, `"rapid_refill_breaker"`, `"prompt_too_long"`, `"image_error"`, `"model_error"`, `"api_error"`, `"malformed_tool_use_exhausted"`, `"budget_exhausted"`, `"structured_output_retry_exhausted"`, `"tool_deferred_unavailable"`, or `"turn_setup_failed"`.
column6: The result message carries terminal_reason naming why the loop ended, across a 19-value vocabulary.
column7: The Claude result adapter never reads msg.terminal_reason. It derives the reason from stop_reason==='refusal', then from subtype via a 4-entry table, with everything unrecognized collapsing to 'provider_error'. A run ending subtype:'error_during_execution' with terminal_reason:'prompt_too_long' (or hook_stopped, stop_hook_prevented, aborted_tools, blocking_limit, rapid_refill_breaker, image_error, model_error) is reported to the user as an undifferentiated provider error even though the SDK put the specific cause on the same message. The installed SDK 0.3.183 does declare the field (`terminal_reason?: TerminalReason`, 12 values).
column8: packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:581-585 and the 4-entry table at :50-57; field confirmed present in node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts
column9: Doc sentence is verbatim (curl of agent-sdk/typescript.md, the bullet list under 'Several fields on the result carry diagnostic detail beyond subtype'; neighbouring bullets do not reverse it). The identifier half of the finding is also true: event-adapter.ts:581-585 derives terminalReason from stop_reason==='refusal' then the 4-entry CLAUDE_RESULT_SUBTYPE_REASON table at :50-57 with an unrecognized-subtype fallback to 'provider_error', and `grep -ra terminal_reason` over packages/ and apps/ finds zero reads in source (only comments, tests and plans). The installed SDK 0.3.183 declares the field (sdk.d.ts:6333, 12 values) and the bundled native binary really emits it (`terminal_reason: Pr.value?.reason` on the result). The CONSEQUENCE, which is what was filed, is false in both halves of its own enumerated list. (1) Five of the eight named values -- prompt_too_long, image_error, model_error, blocking_limit, rapid_refill_breaker -- are, in the very binary we bundle, ALWAYS preceded by an assistant API-error message the loop yields before it returns the reason: `tc({content: ..., error: 'invalid_request'})` for prompt_too_long/image_error/blocking_limit/rapid_refill_breaker (blocking_limit's content is literally the constant OF="Prompt is too long") and `error:'rate_limit'` for the model_error arm, and the SDK forwards that code to the consumer (`yield {type:'assistant', ..., error: r.error}`). Our adapter consumes exactly that one layer up: event-adapter.ts:293-301 -> claude-agent.ts:2660 mapSDKErrorToTypedError -> claude-sdk-error-mapper.ts, which has a dedicated 'Context Window Exceeded' branch keyed on 'prompt is too long'/'context window' plus 'Rate Limit Exceeded' and an 'Invalid Request' fallback that already advises /compact. So the user gets a specific, actionable typed error card, not an undifferentiated provider error, and the premise 'the SDK put the specific cause on the same message' is wrong -- the cause arrives earlier, on a different message, and we do read it. This is the repo's documented recurring false positive: the identifier is unwired, the consequence is handled upstream. (2) The other three named values -- hook_stopped, stop_hook_prevented, aborted_tools -- sit in the binary's CLEAN-turn bucket (the reason switch routes completed/stop_hook_prevented/hook_stopped/tool_deferred/max_turns/aborted_streaming/aborted_tools to Ie('turn'), and only blocking_limit/rapid_refill_breaker/prompt_too_long/image_error/model_error to Oe('turn', reason)), and the result subtype is chosen by `Gmo(lastMessage, stop_reason)` -- the shape of the last message -- not by the reason at all. A hook_stopped or stop_hook_prevented turn whose last message is assistant text or a user tool_result block ends `subtype:'success'`, where our adapter emits NO terminal reason; it is never reported as 'provider_error'. Aborted_streaming/aborted_tools in this product are user-initiated stops that already carry AbortReason.UserStop/Redirect from our own abort path. (3) The '19-value vocabulary' is the current CLI's; the version we ship has 12 and lacks api_error, budget_exhausted, structured_output_retry_exhausted, tool_deferred_unavailable, turn_setup_failed, background_requested and malformed_tool_use_exhausted, so most of the claimed vocabulary is not readable today. (4) Mapping from the subtype rather than from terminal_reason is a recorded decision, not an oversight: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-structured-output.md:49 -- 'the docs, not the installed typings, are the contract for our own terminal vocabulary (we map from the SUBTYPE, not from the SDK's terminal_reason field)' -- and AgentTerminalReason is a deliberately unified cross-backend vocabulary pinned to AbortReason (packages/core/src/types/message.ts:910-948: 'this list deliberately mirrors it rather than introducing a second one'), not a mirror of Claude's enum. It is NOT one of the nine inert-worklist section 3 owner decisions, and not a de-brand/dropped-subscription product difference.

column5: If a user might take longer to respond than your process can reasonably stay running, return the [`defer` hook decision](/docs/en/hooks#defer-a-tool-call-for-later), which lets the process exit and resume later from the persisted session.
column6: An approval that may outlive the process should return the defer hook decision so the run can end and resume later from the persisted session.
column7: The defer round trip exists on the Pi backend only. Under the Claude backend the PreToolUse translation emits allow/modify/block/ask and never permissionDecision:'defer', so an approval that outlives the host process has no documented exit — the tool call stays blocked until the query is cancelled.
column9: Sentence verified verbatim (user-input.md line 15), but the WHOLE line reverses the finding: 'The callback can stay pending indefinitely. Execution remains paused until your callback returns, and the SDK only cancels the wait when the query itself is cancelled. If a user might take longer to respond than your process can reasonably stay running, return the defer hook decision...'. Pending-forever is the documented NORM; defer is the conditional alternative for a process that cannot stay running. The identifier half of the claim is true (ClaudePreToolUseHookPipelineResult.hookDecision at claude-agent.ts:145 is typed 'allow' | 'ask' only, runClaudePreToolUseHookPipeline at :177 drops any other decision, the checkResult switch at :1450-1571 emits only allow/modify/block/ask/prompt, and grep -a finds no tool_deferred or deferred_tool_use anywhere under packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/). The CONSEQUENCE is false on two independent grounds. (1) One layer up, R7 Task 4 already provides exactly the capability defer exists to provide, and it is backend-agnostic: SessionManager.ts:12694 assigns managed.agent.onPermissionRequest = request => this.handleAgentPermissionRequest(managed, request) on the generic agent, and ClaudeAgent's case 'prompt' (claude-agent.ts:1518-1571) publishes through it; that handler persists PiPendingApprovalV1 into managed.pendingApproval (SessionManager.ts:6410-6430; 'pendingApproval' is in SESSION_PERSISTENT_FIELDS, sessions/types.ts:48), reprojectPendingApproval (:6622) re-fires the prompt through the production PermissionRequest band on open after restart, and settleDurableApproval (:6674) settles it with no live agent, an ALLOW re-driving the interrupted turn. The parity audit R7 row records this live-proven under CDP pass 11: a pending consent survives a SIGKILL, re-fires on open, and completes. So a Claude-backend approval that outlives the host process does have an exit, and it does not require cancelling the query. (2) The mechanism itself is scoped away from this surface by Claude's own contract: hooks.md:1587 states defer 'is for integrations that run claude -p as a subprocess and read its JSON output... Claude Code honors this value only in non-interactive mode with the -p flag. In interactive sessions it logs a warning and ignores the hook result.' Nessy's Pi implementation mirrors that gate exactly (pi-agent.ts:3872-3878, gated on this.config.isHeadless and on a single-tool-call turn), so 'the defer round trip exists on the Pi backend only' actually means 'on the headless surface only' — Pi does not defer in the desktop app either. On the interactive Claude surface the documented behavior IS to ignore a defer, which is what the pipeline does (a defer decision is neither block nor allow/ask at :167/:177, so the call falls through the normal permission flow). The claimed evidence line range is also off: claude-agent.ts:1428-1434 is the steer-message/continueWith block, not the decision translation. The only genuine residue is cosmetic/edge — no warning is logged when an ignored defer arrives, and a headless run on the Claude backend would not produce tool_deferred termination — neither of which is the claimed consequence.

The cited repo lines are also accurate as far as they go: packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:49 does describe maxAgents (default 1000) as 'maximum agent() calls per workflow run', and packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1497 does pass getMaxAgents into createWorkflowTool. column5: By default, when 20 subagents are running in a session, spawning another with the Agent tool fails with `Concurrent subagent limit reached`, and the error tells Claude not to retry.

column7: One shared semaphore, `DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY = 16`, further narrowed at runtime to `min(concurrency, cpuCores - 2)`. It is also the workflow ceiling, where 16 IS the documented number (`workflows.md`: "Up to 16 concurrent agents"), so the two documented limits are collapsed into one and the subagent side sits 4 below spec. There is no `Concurrent subagent limit reached` error — over-limit spawns queue on the semaphore instead of failing.
column9: All three legs survive the challenge. The rest of that line does not reverse it: 'Spawning succeeds again when the running count drops below the limit. To change the limit, set CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS to any positive whole number. Sessions with ultracode active are exempt: the limit isn't enforced there. Requires Claude Code v2.1.217 or later.' Line 905 makes the separation the finding depends on explicit: 'Agents that other features run, such as workflow agents and agent team teammates, follow their own limits instead.' (2) CITED LINES ARE ACCURATE: spawner.ts:103 'const DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY = 16'; :136-142 computeEffectiveConcurrency returns Math.max(1, Math.min(ceiling, cpuCores - 2)); :204 'let semaphore = new Semaphore(computeEffectiveConcurrency(DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY))' with :208 rebuilding it from nextRuntime.concurrency. column9: Quote verified verbatim at sub-agents.md:617 (whole line, nothing reverses it), and the identifier half of the claim is true: `hooks` is absent from `UserAgentDefinition` (packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:253-271) and from `AgentDefinition` (:58-122). The claim's subject is 'an imported Claude agent file', i.e. a plugin bundle; sub-agents.md:229 says plugin subagents do not support `hooks`/`mcpServers`/`permissionMode` and 'These fields are ignored when loading agents from a plugin.' column5: Names can't contain `:`, which is reserved for [plugin-scoped identifiers](/docs/en/plugins) such as `my-plugin:reviewer`.
column6: A subagent `name` containing `:` is refused at load, because `:` is reserved for plugin-scoped identifiers.
column7: `normalizeName` only trims and lowercases; no character validation. Our plugin capability keys DO contain colons (`qualifiedKey` joins with `::`, `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:263`) and become an agent's `name`/`aliases` (`runtime-agent-definitions.ts:153-154`). `resolveAgentDefinition` matches on exact `name` BEFORE searching `aliases`, so a workspace or project markdown agent file may declare a colon-bearing name equal to a plugin's capability key and be selected ahead of the alias lookup. Only the built-in and `fork` names are reserved.
column9: The quote is real and the cited lines say what was claimed, but the CONSEQUENCE is false and was measured false — the repo's recurring 'the identifier is unwired, but something upstream already handled it' shape, compounded by the finding naming the wrong field (frontmatter `name`) in the wrong subsystem.  1. DOC — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md` -> 1250 lines, 94956 bytes, md5 cf7b0c7d5ff8adff60f6a174cd6938f4. The claimed string is an exact substring of line 277 (checked in Python, not by eye). Reading the WHOLE line changes nothing against the finding — it reinforces it: `| `name` | Yes | Unique identifier using lowercase letters and hyphens. [Hooks](/docs/en/hooks#subagentstart) receive this value as `agent_type`. The filename doesn't have to match. {/* min-version: 2.1.218 */}Names can't contain `:`, which is reserved for [plugin-scoped identifiers](/docs/en/plugins) such as `my-plugin:reviewer`. Claude Code doesn't load a file whose name contains one and logs an error to the debug log. Before v2.1.218, such names were accepted |`. So the doc half stands, and the rule is version-gated at v2.1.218.  2. FILE — CONFIRMED AS WRITTEN, all four citations. `packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:281-283` is exactly `normalizeName(name) { return name.trim().toLowerCase(); }` with no character validation. `:725-726` is exactly `defs.find(def => def.name === normalized) ?? defs.find(def => def.aliases?.includes(normalized))`. `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:250-264` `qualifiedKey` does `.join('::')`. `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:153-154` is `name: hasUnqualifiedAlias ? descriptor.name : descriptor.key` / `aliases: [...new Set([descriptor.key, ...])]`. There is no colon check anywhere in the agents subsystem (`grep -ran` over `packages/shared/src/agents/` and `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/` for `includes(':')`, `indexOf(':')`, `/:/`, `[a-z0-9-]`, `colon`: zero non-test hits).  3. CONSEQUENCE — REFUTED ON THREE INDEPENDENT GROUNDS.  (a) The stated exploit path is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: markdown definitions and runtime (plugin-key-bearing) definitions are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE. `loadAgentDefinitions` guards the entire markdown block with `if (options.runtimeDefinitions === undefined)` (definitions.ts:670-684) and only then appends `options.runtimeDefinitions ?? []` (:686). Plugin capability keys reach this function ONLY as runtime definitions, so in any load where a plugin key exists, no workspace/project markdown file has been read at all. Every production caller supplies the field and never leaves it `undefined`: `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:513` and `workflow-tool.ts:591` both pass `options.getRuntimeAgentDefinitions?.() ?? []`, and `review-tool.ts:300` passes `[]`.  MEASURED, with a positive control (an ABSENCE needs one):   CONTROL (runtimeDefinitions omitted): a workspace `reviewer.md` DOES override the built-in -> systemPrompt "I AM THE OVERRIDE."   <- the rig can see shadowing   PROD SHAPE (runtimeDefinitions: []): same file on disk -> systemPrompt "You are a reviewer agent. Focu…"  <- markdown never loaded   IMPOSTOR TEST: workspace `impostor.md` with frontmatter `name: "agent::plugin::-::-::::reviewer"` alongside a runtime definition whose definitionKey is that same string -> `resolveAgentDefinition('agent::plugin::-::-::::reviewer')` returns "I am the REAL plugin agent." The impostor is absent from the map entirely.  (b) The finding names the WRONG FIELD for the path that carries plugin keys. In the capability/runtime pipeline an agent is named by its FILENAME, not by frontmatter `name`: `native-sources.ts:332` `const logicalName = entry.name.replace(/\.md$/i, '')`, and the runtime binding is `resolver.ts:965` `agent: { key, name: record.logicalName, … }` for native agents and `resolver.ts:1245` `name: candidate.logicalName` for plugin agents; the descriptor then carries `name: agent.name` (`pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:643`). The frontmatter `name` key is read only by `definitions.ts`'s own parser (`parseMarkdownAgentDefinition:534-536`) — i.e. exactly and only in the fallback path where, per (a), no plugin key can be present. So "a workspace or project markdown agent file may DECLARE a colon-bearing name equal to a plugin's capability key" cannot happen: in the path that has plugin keys, the declaration is ignored.  (c) The reservation's RATIONALE does not transfer. Claude reserves `:` because its plugin-scoped reference syntax is literally `my-plugin:reviewer`. This fork implements no such syntax — a plugin-scoped agent is referenced by its opaque `::`-joined qualified key or by its short logical name, and nothing else: `base-agent.ts:2557` (`candidate.key === agent || (candidate.selectedAsUnqualifiedAlias && candidate.name === agent)`) and `runtime-agent-definition.ts:224-225` (`value.key === reference` ?? `value.logicalName === reference`). A single `:` is therefore not a namespace separator here and cannot collide with one.  Not one of the nine §3 owner decisions in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` (read all nine: SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries — none touches agent name validation). Not a rebrand or a subscription-drop difference either. It is refuted on measurement, not on category.

column5: **Marker line**: the scan prepends a line starting with `[harness: subagent output matched instruction-shaped pattern(s):` when the report imitates a tag like `<system-reminder>` or mentions permission settings such as `bypassPermissions` or `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.
column6: The output scan prepends a marker line when a subagent report imitates a harness tag OR mentions permission settings such as `bypassPermissions` / `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, leaving the text itself unchanged.
column7: `scanSubagentOutput` defangs `<untrusted|system-reminder|nessy_agent_environment` tags and line-leading `Human:`/`Assistant:` by inserting a zero-width space, and strips C0/C1 control characters. It never prepends a marker line, and it has no permission-setting pattern at all — a child report containing `bypassPermissions` or `--dangerously-skip-permissions` reaches the parent with nothing flagged. Two secondary differences on the same sentence pair: we insert U+200B where the page specifies a backslash (invisible vs visible), and we DO remove control characters where the page says "The scan never removes or rewords anything".
column9: All three checks pass, so the gap survives the challenge. (1) VERBATIM: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md finds the sentence at line 799, inside the '### Subagent output scanning' section, character-for-character as quoted. The line is a two-sentence line and the SECOND sentence reinforces rather than reverses: 'Permission-setting mentions get the marker line, but the text itself stays as written.' The section preamble also states 'The scan never removes or rewords anything; it makes two kinds of change you may notice in a report:' followed by two bullets, 'Backslash insertion' and 'Marker line'. Feature is gated at v2.1.210+ per the page's own Note. (2) CITED FILE: packages/shared/src/prompts/untrusted-text.ts is 75 lines and is exactly as described. HARNESS_TAG = /<(\/?)(untrusted|system-reminder|nessy_agent_environment)\b/gi (:41), TURN_MARKER = /^([ \t]*)(Human|Assistant)(?=:)/gim (:48), CONTROL_CHARACTERS C0/C1 set (:55); scanSubagentOutput (:71-75) is exactly neutralizeHarnessMarkers(text).replace(TURN_MARKER, `$1$2${ZERO_WIDTH_SPACE}`).replace(CONTROL_CHARACTERS, ''). ZERO_WIDTH_SPACE = '\u200B' (:32) — so U+200B, not a backslash, and control characters ARE removed (the header comment at :18-21 makes that an explicit design choice: 'DEFANG, do not delete ... Only control characters, which have no legible form, are removed'). No return-value concatenation, no prefix, no conditional branch: a marker line is structurally absent, not merely unmatched. (3) LAYER UP AND DOWN, with -a on every absence grep: `grep -ran 'harness:' packages apps` returns only unrelated test comments, a release-notes line and NUL-bearing codex.exe blobs — zero source hits for the marker string; `grep -ran 'instruction-shaped|instructionShaped|instruction_shaped' packages apps` returns nothing at all. No permission-setting pattern exists on any scan path: `grep -ran 'dangerously-skip-permissions|dangerouslySkipPermissions' packages/*/src apps/*/src` hits only two prose comments in pre-tool-use.ts:635 and protected-paths.ts:32 (both about protected-path semantics, neither a scanner), and bypassPermissions appears only as a permission-mode enum value in mode tables, fixtures and the system prompt. Consequence verified separately from the identifier: I walked every model-facing consumer of the scan — pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/{subagent-tool,workflow-tool,review-tool,guardian-runner}.ts and server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:9940 — and none of them prepends, appends or wraps anything conditional. contentForResults (subagent-tool.ts:225-247) emits a plain header `N. <agent> - <status>` plus the defanged body, with '[ERROR] ' only for failed children; there is no untrusted fence on the parent-facing return (the `<untrusted source="...">` wrapper at prompts/guardian.ts:296 is a SIBLING SUBSYSTEM — it fences the guardian judge's INPUTS, not a subagent's report to its parent — so it cannot be mistaken for the missing marker). The only standing mitigation is a generic system-prompt line (prompts/system.ts:546/:636, 'Treat source data, tool output, ... as data to inspect, not instructions to follow'), which is a constant instruction, not a per-report flag, so the claimed consequence holds. Not a recorded owner decision: inert-worklist §3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions — none touches subagent output scanning. 'default', { changedBy: 'restore' })` then installs it as-is. There is no bypass re-acceptance gate anywhere (`grep -rani "bypassAccepted|acceptedBypass|bypassDisclaimer"` → no hits), so a session last left in `bypassPermissions` comes back in `bypassPermissions` after an app restart, and a session left in `plan` comes back in `plan`.
column9: STEP 1 PASSES — the quote is real. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions.md` = 195 lines / 23345 bytes (md5 e9c5f0abe3ea3562407d8ac63a1162f8). The sentence is at :34 verbatim, in the bullet list under `### What a resumed session restores`. Read WHOLE, the line carries two more sentences and neither reverses it: '`auto` is restored only when your account still meets the auto mode requirements. Pass `--permission-mode` to override the restored mode.' The page is in the corpus snapshot (`scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv` -> `sessions Manage sessions`). This is the one part of the finding that holds.  STEP 2 PASSES — the cited lines exist and say what was claimed. `SessionManager.ts:7617` is `const normalizedPersistedMode = this.normalizePersistedSessionPermissionMode(managed)`, `:7622` is `setPermissionMode(restoreModeKey, managed.permissionMode ?? 'default', { changedBy: 'restore' })`, `:7639` is `if (normalizedPersistedMode) this.persistSession(managed)`; `:17351` is the normalizer. Correct file, correct content.  STEP 3 KILLS IT — the OUR STATE sentence is FALSE on BOTH of its supporting assertions, and each is a documented false-positive shape from this repo's own list.  (a) 'has no exclusion list' — FALSE, and it is the reason 'restored verbatim' is wrong. `normalizePersistedSessionPermissionMode` (:17351) calls `normalizeSessionPermissionMode` (:17345), which for a Pi session calls `normalizePiPermissionMode` (:17341) = `normalizeManagedPermissionMode(mode, this.managedPiPolicy.disabledPermissionModes)`. `disabledPermissionModes` IS a permission-mode exclusion list, applied to the persisted mode at exactly the restore point, and it demotes rather than merely rejects (`mode-types.ts:134-151`, fallback chain). The repo PINS the demotion for this exact mode: `SessionManager.orchestration.test.ts:952-957` builds `restored = { permissionMode: 'bypassPermissions', previousPermissionMode: 'auto' }` under a policy with `disabledPermissionModes: ['allow-all']`, asserts the normalizer returns `true`, and asserts `restored` comes back `{ permissionMode: 'acceptEdits', previousPermissionMode: 'acceptEdits' }` — and the `true` drives `:7639`, which rewrites the demoted mode to disk. The list is EMPTY BY DEFAULT (`pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:1136` `disabledPermissionModes: Object.freeze([])`), which is a default, not an absence. Per audit row R30b, Claude's own `disableBypassPermissionsMode` settings key IS this list spelled `['allow-all']`, and `settings.md:386` says that key 'works from any scope' — so the org-level control Claude documents for exactly this is the control we ship.  (b) 'There is no bypass re-acceptance gate anywhere' — FALSE, and it is the wrong-identifier-names shape (inert-worklist §4 shape 4: name the subsystem, not a guessed identifier). The gate is `apps/electron/src/renderer/lib/bypass-permissions-gate.ts`: `needsBypassPermissionsAcknowledgment` / `recordBypassPermissionsAcknowledgment`, storage key `nessy:bypass-permissions-acknowledged`. It is wired at `App.tsx:1362` inside `handleSessionOptionsChange` — `if (updates.permissionMode === 'bypassPermissions' && needsBypassPermissionsAcknowledgment()) { setPendingBypassSwitch(...); return }` — held in state at `App.tsx:326`, rendered by `components/BypassPermissionsDialog.tsx` (mounted `App.tsx:2007`, accept records the ack `:2011`), and tested at `lib/__tests__/bypass-permissions-gate.test.ts:16-30`. Its docblock cites the very rule the finding invokes: 'Claude makes bypass launch-only and shows a one-time responsibility acknowledgment. The desktop analog: the FIRST activation of `bypassPermissions` on this install raises a confirmation dialog.' None of the three greps the finding ran (`bypassAccepted|acceptedBypass|bypassDisclaimer`) can hit any of those names.  RECORDED OWNER DECISIONS COVER BOTH HALVES. • PLAN half: a harvested category string at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:465` — 'Claude's plan mode exits on plan approval; ours stays persistent — accepting a plan transitions the session through one deliberate clamped force-set and re-entry is explicit, so a session never silently leaves plan merely because a plan was approved' — written in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-31-claude-mode-vocabulary.md:220-224` (§'Category strings — what stays stricter than Claude'), landed as commit `c4f71c17` under audit row V1. Plan is deliberately a PERSISTENT mode in this fork, the opposite framing from Claude's transient plan; restoring it is the stricter direction, not a weakening. • BYPASS half: audit row V1 (`2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md`, 'Owner decision 2026-07-31') adopts Claude's vocabulary plus 'gates (bypass reachable only behind an explicit enable with a responsibility dialog …)'. Carried in shipped source at `mode-types.ts:71-79`: 'permission-modes.md makes bypass launch-only ("can only be set at startup"), and the desktop analog is an explicit enable — a workspace `cyclablePermissionModes` that names it, or the mode menu behind the first-activation responsibility dialog.' The doc's remedy is CLI-launch-shaped ('one of its launch flags or `permissions.defaultMode`'); an Electron app has no launch flag, and the substitute was chosen deliberately, not missed.  WHAT SURVIVES, MUCH NARROWER (see correctedState). The ack is once-per-install in localStorage and is consulted only on the ACT of switching, never on restore; a NUL-safe `grep -ran bypassPermissions` over `apps/electron/src/main`, `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap` and `packages/server/src` returns zero non-test hits, so no startup path re-gates it. With the default empty `disabledPermissionModes`, a session last left in bypass does return in bypass after a restart without a second dialog. That residue is 'the one-time ack is not re-checked at restore' — not 'no gate and no exclusion list exist', which is what was filed and is false.

column5: # Bypass proxy for specific requests - space-separated format
column6: `NO_PROXY` accepts a space-separated list as well as a comma-separated one.
column7: Both NO_PROXY parsers split on commas only. `parseNoProxyRules` calls `splitCommaSeparated` (`str.split(',')`), and the Pi interceptor does `NO_PROXY.split(',')`. `NO_PROXY="localhost 192.168.1.1 example.com .example.com"` therefore yields one rule whose host is the whole string, which matches no hostname — every request goes through the proxy with no error or warning, the opposite of what the operator configured.
column9: All three checks pass and the consequence reproduces under a positive control.  (1) DOC — the quoted sentence exists VERBATIM at network-config.md:30, and the whole line is just that comment; the following lines are its payload: line 31 `export NO_PROXY="localhost 192.168.1.1 example.com .example.com"`, line 32 `# Bypass proxy for specific requests - comma-separated format`, line 33 the comma twin, line 34-35 `# Bypass proxy for all requests` / `export NO_PROXY="*"`. Both formats are presented as accepted spellings of the same variable, so the claimed behaviour is a fair reading, not a paraphrase. The page also states `All environment variables shown on this page can also be configured in settings.json`, so the settings-side field inherits the same contract. Our own earlier verification file already recorded this reading (2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:720).  (2) CODE — confirmed, with one line of drift in the citation. `splitCommaSeparated` is `network-proxy-utils.ts:11-13` and is literally `str.split(',')`. `parseNoProxyRules` calls it at :222, not :221 (the page-relative anchor drifted by one; the identifier and behaviour are exactly as claimed), and its own docblock at :210 says `Parse a comma-separated NO_PROXY string`. The Pi interceptor is verbatim as cited: `unified-network-interceptor.ts:84-86` does `NO_PROXY.split(',')`, fed by :69 `process.env.NO_PROXY || process.env.no_proxy`. No whitespace handling exists on any path; `normalizeProxyString` (storage.ts:2556-2559) only trims the outer edges of the whole string, and the Settings > Network field (AppSettingsPage.tsx:88) likewise only `.trim()`s.  (3) LAYER UP / LAYER DOWN — the consequence is real, not absorbed by anything upstream, and the claim if anything UNDERSTATES the surface. Layer up: `pi-agent.ts:1466` spawns the Pi subprocess with `env: { ...process.env, ...getProxyEnvVars(), ... }`, so an operator who exports the documented space-separated `NO_PROXY` in their shell has it inherited straight into the interceptor when no in-app proxy setting overrides it (`proxy-env.ts:70-73` emits NO_PROXY only when `settings.enabled` AND `settings.noProxy` are set). `network-runtime.ts:197-215` restores the launch environment's NO_PROXY on disable precisely so an operator-provided proxy survives — i.e. the env spelling is a supported input, not an internal-only channel. Layer down: `getProxyForUrl` (interceptor :106-109) returns PROXY_URL whenever bypass fails and the wrapper sets it explicitly as Bun's `proxy:` fetch option (:2386, :2432-2434), which overrides whatever Bun would have decided from the env itself — so the mis-parse actively forces the request through the proxy. There is also a THIRD surface the finding does not name: `apps/electron/src/main/network-proxy.ts:216-218` builds Chromium's `proxyBypassRules` as `splitCommaSeparated(settings.noProxy).join(',')`, so every Electron session partition (browser pane, update feed, default) gets the same single bogus rule. No warning anywhere: the only proxy logging is booleans (`hasNoProxy: true`, network-proxy.ts:245-251) and a debug-only line (interceptor :112).  POSITIVE CONTROL (required for a silent-failure claim) — ran both parsers against the doc's own two example strings. Space form: one rule `{host: "localhost 192.168.1.1 example.com .example.com"}`, and bypass=false for localhost:3000, example.com, api.example.com and 192.168.1.1. Comma form (the control on the same rig): four rules, bypass=true for all four URLs. The interceptor's replicated parser gives the same split (space -> false, comma -> true). So the failure is measured, not inferred. column5: The subagents the workflow spawns always run in `acceptEdits` mode and inherit your [tool allowlist](/docs/en/settings#permission-settings), regardless of your session's mode.
column6: Subagents spawned by a workflow run in `acceptEdits` regardless of the session's permission mode; file edits are auto-approved and only the launch prompt follows the session mode.
column7: No workflow-specific permission floor exists. Workflow `agent()` calls go through the same `spawnChildSession` as ordinary subagents, which forwards only `args.agentDef.permissionMode` and otherwise omits it so the host inherits the parent's mode. `grep -ran acceptEdits packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/workflow-tool.ts packages/shared/src/workflows/` returns nothing. A workflow launched from a `default`-mode session therefore prompts on every file edit its agents make — for a fan-out of dozens of agents, in a run the page describes as unattended.
column9: All three checks pass, and the challenge made the finding STRONGER rather than weaker.  (1) DOC SENTENCE — verbatim. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows.md` line 181, read whole: "Your permission mode controls only the launch prompt above. The subagents the workflow spawns always run in `acceptEdits` mode and inherit your [tool allowlist](/docs/en/settings#permission-settings), regardless of your session's mode. File edits are auto-approved." The quoted sentence is the middle of three; neither neighbour reverses it — the third sentence reinforces it. Line 183 scopes the floor ("Shell commands, web fetches, and MCP tools that aren't in your allowlist can still prompt you mid-run"), so the floor is edits-only, not blanket. The one apparent tension, line 125 ("a workflow started this way runs inside the session's existing permission mode, and its agents' tool calls receive the same permission checks and sandboxing as any other tool call"), is about the keyword route not changing the SESSION's mode and is consistent with 181+183: acceptEdits still runs every other check, it only auto-approves edits. Page is row 193 of `scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv`, so it is a Claude Code contract page.  (2) CITED CODE — accurate. `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:570-575` builds the child restrictions and forwards permissionMode only when the agent def carries one: `...(args.agentDef.permissionMode === undefined ? {} : { permissionMode: args.agentDef.permissionMode })`; the comment at :328-330 states the omission semantics outright — "`permissionMode` is OMITTED, which the host reads as 'inherit the parent's mode verbatim'". Absence re-verified with `-a` (NUL-byte trap): `grep -ran acceptEdits packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/ packages/shared/src/workflows/ packages/shared/src/config/workflow-settings.ts` → no output. `workflow-tool.ts:560-623` (`runAgent`) builds SpawnChildSessionArgs with agentDef/model/effort/cwd/signal/depth/ownerTaskId/background and NO permission field, so workflow agents take the identical path as ordinary subagents — confirmed by `options.spawn ?? spawnChildSession` at :466.  (3) ONE LAYER UP AND DOWN — consequence verified separately from the identifier, and the identifier check UNDERSTATED it. Up: the host does not merely inherit, it CLAMPS narrow-only. `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10406-10417` (`startPiChildRuntime`, depth 1): `childPermissionMode = record.restrictions.permissionMode ? clampPermissionModeToParent(requested, parentPermissionMode) : parentPermissionMode`, and `:10910-10934` applies the same narrow-only rule to nested child ceilings. Because `PERMISSION_MODE_ORDER` (mode-types.ts:63) ranks acceptEdits(4) above default(3), `clampPermissionModeToParent('acceptEdits','default')` returns `'default'` — so from a default-mode session the documented floor is unreachable EVEN IF an agent def explicitly requests acceptEdits. Down: the auto-approve is gated on the mode. `pre-tool-use.ts:1660` sets `autoAllowFileWrites` only when `effectivePermissionMode === 'acceptEdits'`, and `:1930-1948` returns a `file_write` PromptInfo for every FILE_WRITE_TOOLS call when that flag is false. And the prompt is not swallowed by the child being hidden: `SessionManager.ts:6452-6484` (`permissionSurfaceRouting`) deliberately walks to the nearest visible ancestor so a hidden child's prompt renders in the human's main session. So the claimed consequence — a default-mode workflow prompts per file edit, per agent, across the fan-out — is real end-to-end, not an unwired-identifier artefact.  NOT a recorded owner decision: absent from `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 (all nine read; none touches workflows or permission floors) and from §4's false positives. column5: If `args` is omitted, the global is `undefined` inside the script.

column7: The runtime substitutes an empty object: `compiledScript(makeApi(input.args ?? {}))`. A script that branches on `args === undefined` (or on `!args`) to supply defaults never takes that branch, because `{}` is truthy and defined.
column9: All three checks pass; the finding survives. (1) DOC VERBATIM: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows.md line 227 reads in full: "Claude passes the list as structured data, so the script can call array and object methods on `args` directly without parsing it first. If `args` is omitted, the global is `undefined` inside the script." The quoted sentence is exact, and the first half of the two-sentence line does not reverse it. (2) CITED SITE: packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/workflow-tool.ts:750 is exactly `returnValue = await compiledScript(makeApi(input.args ?? {}));`. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier and with a positive control: compiling `return JSON.stringify({typeofArgs: typeof args, isUndefined: args === undefined, falsy: !args, nullishDefault: (args ?? 'DEFAULT-BRANCH-TAKEN')})` through the real compileWorkflowScript gives, with our call-site expression (input.args undefined ?? {}): {"typeofArgs":"object","isUndefined":false,"falsy":false,"nullishDefault":{}}; the SAME script with args passed through unmodified (the documented Claude behaviour) gives {"typeofArgs":"undefined","isUndefined":true,"falsy":true,"nullishDefault":"DEFAULT-BRANCH-TAKEN"}. The control proves the sandbox itself does not default -- sandbox.ts:277-300 passes api.args straight in as the `args` Function parameter -- so the `?? {}` at the call site is the sole cause and the branch really is unreachable. column5: To copy them automatically when Claude creates a worktree, add a `.worktreeinclude` file to your project root.

column8: packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.ts:74-96 and :112-124; `grep -rai worktreeinclude --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist .` → only the spec doc

column5: For a `"fresh"` base, Claude Code keeps `origin/HEAD` current: when the repository hasn't been fetched in the last 24 hours, it fetches the default branch, capped at five seconds, and uses the locally cached ref if the fetch fails.
column6: Under the default `"fresh"` base, Claude Code refreshes `origin/HEAD` before branching — fetching the default branch when the repo has not been fetched in 24 hours, capped at five seconds, falling back to the cached ref.
column7: `worktreeBaseShaCandidates` for `baseRef: 'fresh'` emits exactly `git -C <root> rev-parse origin/HEAD` (allowFailure) then local `HEAD`. There is no fetch, no staleness check and no timeout anywhere on the worktree path (`grep -ran "'fetch'" packages/server-core/src` → no hit). A repository whose `origin/HEAD` was last updated weeks ago silently branches every "fresh" worktree off that stale commit — which is the pre-v2.1.208 behaviour the page calls out as changed.
column9: All three checks confirm the finding; nothing refutes it. (1) VERBATIM: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md line 112 opens with the quoted sentence character-for-character: "For a `\"fresh\"` base, Claude Code keeps `origin/HEAD` current: when the repository hasn't been fetched in the last 24 hours, it fetches the default branch, capped at five seconds, and uses the locally cached ref if the fetch fails." I read the WHOLE line: its two remaining sentences REINFORCE rather than reverse the claim - "If no remote is configured, or `origin/HEAD` isn't cached locally and can't be fetched, the worktree falls back to your current local `HEAD`" (the half we DO implement) and "Before v2.1.208, a fresh worktree used whatever `origin/HEAD` was already cached locally" (which names our current behaviour exactly). The page is row 194 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a Claude Code contract page, not Codex/MCP. (2) CITED CODE: worktree-git-plan.ts:39-53 is verbatim as claimed - for baseRef 'fresh' it returns exactly [{operation:'base-fresh', args:['-C',repoRoot,'rev-parse','origin/HEAD'], allowFailure:true}, {operation:'base', args:['-C',repoRoot,'rev-parse','HEAD']}]. No fetch, no last-fetch timestamp, no default-branch resolution. SessionManager.ts:10150 is the sole production call site (the only other hits are the import at :136 and worktree-git-plan.test.ts, which pins the exact argv - so the missing fetch is frozen by a test). Down: runWorktreeGit (SessionManager.ts:10020-10048) is the only git runner on this path; it spawns `git` with host-built argv under a read-only sandbox profile - it does not prepend or inject anything. Up: the WorktreeLeaseService policy.select at :10144-10161 just loops the candidates and takes the first non-empty sha; git.create (:10164) consumes that sha with `worktree add -b`. No fetch upstream. Repo-wide absence check with -a and a positive control: `grep -ranE "'fetch'|\"fetch\"" --include='*.ts' packages apps` returns only WebFetch permission-DSL tests and a schema fixture - zero git-fetch call sites; the same grep style DOES find `command: 'git'` at SessionManager.ts:10033 and eight git invocations in workspace/git-branches.ts (which also never fetches), so grep is reading these files. packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-lease-service.ts contains neither 'fetch' nor 'origin/'. The origin of the gap is visible: our contract distillation (2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:126) captured baseRef as '"fresh" default = origin/<default-branch>' with no fetch clause, and the implementing plan 2026-07-27-session-worktrees.md contains the word 'fetch' only in an instruction to fetch raw markdown - i.e. we built against the pre-v2.1.208 page and the upstream refresh behaviour landed afterwards. column5: The first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation.
column6: MEMORY.md is loaded truncated to whichever comes first of 200 lines or 25 KB.
column7: Only a 200-line constant exists (`MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200`); there is no byte cap anywhere in the repo. Worse, the LIVE path does not apply even the line cap: pinned memory layers are read through `materializer.readText`, which returns the whole file, and `composePinnedCapabilityContext` pushes that content verbatim. The 200-line `readMemoryFile` is only used by the legacy fallback composer and by the import-scan pass.
column9: Tried to refute on all three axes and could not. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md, line 384, word for word: 'The first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation.' Read the WHOLE line — it is a three-sentence line and the other two REINFORCE the claim ('Content beyond that threshold is not loaded at session start.' / 'Claude keeps `MEMORY.md` concise by moving detailed notes into separate topic files.'). :30 restates it in the comparison table ('Every session (first 200 lines or 25KB)'), :386 adds the post-write measurement against 'the 200-line and 25KB read limits', and :390 scopes it ('This limit applies only to `MEMORY.md`. CLAUDE.md files are loaded in full regardless of length'), which is the one qualifier that could have refuted this and does not — see (3). (2) CITED FILES: packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:8 is `export const MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200;` and :29-32 is `readMemoryFile(filePath, maxLines = MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT)` = `readFileSync(filePath,'utf-8').split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)` — a line slice, no byte check. capabilities/materializer.ts:181 is `const content = readFileSync(contentPath);` inside `readText` (169-186), a whole-file read returned at :186 with no cap. base-agent.ts `composePinnedCapabilityContext` (~976-1014) does `for (const layer of runtime.view.memory) { const content = await runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource); ... }` and pushes `content` verbatim into `<capability-layer>` bodies; the cited 989-1006 window is the rule-parse/import-strip tail of that same loop (the `readText` call itself sits a few lines above at ~977), so the line range is loose by ~12 lines but points at the right function and the right loop. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier, both directions. Live-path claim CONFIRMED end to end: prompts/system.ts:453-455 `const memoryContext = capabilityContextPinned ? '' : loadMemoryPromptBlock(...)`, and `capabilityContextPinned` is positional arg 12 of `getSystemPrompt`, passed as `this.capabilityTurnRuntime !== null` by BOTH live backends (pi-agent.ts:6607, claude-agent.ts:1256). So whenever the capability runtime is active — the normal turn — the 200-line `readMemoryFile` composer is skipped entirely and MEMORY.md rides the uncapped pinned path. `rg -na 'MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT|readMemoryFile'` over packages/ apps/ (with -a; native-sources.ts does carry NUL bytes) returns exactly three non-test consumers: memory-store.ts itself, the legacy `loadMemoryPromptBlock` chain, and capabilities/native-sources.ts:427, the `@import` scan — which matches the claim's last sentence precisely. The only test asserting the cap (memory-store.test.ts:47 'caps prompt reads to 200 lines') tests `readMemoryFile` directly, i.e. the dead branch. Byte-cap claim CONFIRMED: no 25KB constant exists on the memory path; the only instruction byte cap in the repo is MAX_NESTED_INSTRUCTION_FILE_BYTES = 10 * 1024 (capabilities/native-sources.ts:772, truncation at :875-877), and that is the SIBLING subsystem — lazily discovered nested AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md instruction files, never a MEMORY.md memory layer. (I nearly missed that constant by piping a grep through `head -30`, the exact trap AGENTS.md warns about.) The doc's :390 carve-out does not rescue us either: this fork's MEMORY.md is the auto-memory index, not a CLAUDE.md analogue — the `remember` session tool appends agent-written entries stamped `<!-- nessy:auto:YYYY-MM-DD -->` to session/project/user MEMORY.md (session-tools-core/src/handlers/remember.ts:21-49) and a scheduled auto-memory cleanup pass ages them out, while human project instructions live in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md on the separate nested-instruction path. The fork also already carries the 200-line constant lifted from this very page, so matching this limit was the intent, not an out-of-scope Claude-ism. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 — the only memory-adjacent row there is PiPendingApprovalV1.requestedAt, unrelated. Not a rebrand, gateway, or dropped-subscription product difference. Two imprecisions that do not refute: the pinned block is not literally 'the system prompt' on the Claude backend (it rides the pinned context block, not `presetAppend`), and the same uncapped read applies to `.agents/rules` layers, which the claim does not mention.

column5: To pull in a README, package.json, and a workflow guide, reference them with `@` syntax anywhere in your CLAUDE.md:

Both of the page's own examples — `See @README for project overview and @package.json ...` and `- git workflow @docs/git-instructions.md` — are silently not imported.
