(2) CODE AS CLAIMED, with three line-number corrections. `evaluateAtSettlement` commits at goal-service.ts:248-259 (not :246-259) spreading `...current`, so `status` stays `'active'`, and writes `evaluation('evaluator', parsed.complete ? 'complete_suggested' : 'not_complete', ...)` at :252-258. `action === 'complete'` is at :151-155 (not :149-153) and is one of only two callers of `terminalGoal` (the other is `cancel` at :157); `grep -ran terminalGoal packages/` finds no third. You have no tools and cannot change goal state.' is at :480 (not :476). `validTerminalState` (:555) additionally requires `source === 'manual'` and non-empty evidence for `status: 'complete'`, so an evaluator-sourced verdict structurally cannot be a terminal complete.  (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY, and it is real. `grep -ran complete_suggested apps/ packages/` (NUL-safe) finds the literal in exactly five places: the producer at goal-service.ts:254, three type/parser allowlists (core/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:114, shared/sessions/types.ts:106, shared/protocol/pi-harness-runtime.ts:139, goal-service.ts:608), one test (goal-service.test.ts:146, which LOCKS `status: 'active'` + `verdict: 'complete_suggested'`), plus built-bundle copies. Zero consumers. Nothing upstream or downstream short-circuits: SessionManager.schedulePiGoalContinuation (SessionManager.ts:3360-3411) calls `evaluateAtSettlement` at :3376, then re-reads `service.safeSnapshot()` at :3383 and gates only on `status !== 'active'`; `canContinue` (goal-service.ts:264-271) checks only settled + active + id/revision match and never looks at the verdict, so the fresh post-evaluation revision matches and :3398 dispatches another full turn. The only nudge is textual: `continuationPrompt` (:273-282) appends `Last evaluation: complete_suggested: <reason>` plus 'Use Goal complete only with concrete evidence'. So a satisfied condition does dispatch at least one more billed turn, and keeps dispatching until the model itself calls `Goal complete`.  NOT A RECORDED EXEMPTION. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions). RIGHT SUBSYSTEM, and the sibling-symbol trap does not apply: the Pi-harness GoalService is the only post-turn-evaluator + auto-continuation mechanism in the repo, and SessionManager's `goal_create` arm (:3279) even stamps `source: 'user', creator: 'desktop'`, so the protocol contemplates the user-set goal the page describes.

column5: If you stop a `claude -p` run with SIGTERM, for example from `kill`, a process supervisor, or an SDK host closing the session, Claude Code aborts the in-progress turn, terminates the process tree of any running Bash command, runs [`SessionEnd` hooks](/docs/en/hooks#sessionend), and exits with code 143.
column6: A SIGTERM'd non-interactive run must exit 143; ours exits 130 for both SIGINT and SIGTERM, so a supervisor cannot tell an operator interrupt from a shutdown signal.

column9: All three checks confirm the finding, and a positive control confirms the consequence. (1) DOC: `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless.md` returns the sentence VERBATIM at line 67, as a complete single-sentence paragraph under '### Background tasks at exit' — no second sentence reverses it, and the surrounding paragraphs are about the five-second background-task grace and the ten-minute background-subagent wait cap, neither of which qualifies the exit code. The page is row 114 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a Claude Code contract page, not a Codex/MCP page. (2) CODE: apps/cli/src/index.ts:795-804 says exactly what was claimed — `const onSignal = async () => { ... await cleanup(); process.exit(130) }` at :796-802, registered for BOTH signals at :803 (`process.on('SIGINT', onSignal)`) and :804 (`process.on('SIGTERM', onSignal)`), torn down at :861-862. This is inside `cmdRun`, which is our non-interactive/print surface (`spawnLocalServer(args, { printMode: true })` at :782) — the correct analogue of `claude -p`, so this is not the sibling-subsystem trap. (3) LAYER UP/DOWN + CONSEQUENCE: `grep -ran "process.on('SIG"` over apps/cli/src, packages/server/src, packages/server-core/src, packages/pi-agent-server/src and packages/shared/src finds exactly two registration sites in source — the CLI pair above, and packages/server/src/index.ts:376-377, which is the separate long-lived `nessy-server` daemon whose `shutdown` exits 0 for both signals (a different subsystem, correctly not the one cited). Positive control on the same rig: a Node script using our exact pattern exits 130 on SIGTERM, and the identical script with the handlers NOT registered exits 143 — Node's default disposition is already the documented number, so our explicit handler is what overwrites 143 with 130. SIGINT is unaffected (130 is correct there, 128+2). NOT an owner decision: none of the nine dated decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/foldSessionSummary) touches signals or exit codes. One scope note that does not rescue the finding: our own docs/cli.md:133 documents `interrupted — exit code 130` for the streamed `interrupted` event, so a fix must update that table too, and the doc sentence's other clauses (SessionEnd hooks, Bash process-tree termination) were not part of this claim and were not assessed.

column5: As of Claude Code v2.1.128, piped stdin is capped at 10MB. If you exceed the cap, Claude Code exits with a clear error and a non-zero status.
column6: Piped stdin is read unbounded into memory; the documented 10 MB cap and its clear-error/non-zero-exit behavior are absent.
column7: `readPrompt` loops `Bun.stdin.stream().getReader()` to `done`, pushing every decoded chunk into an array, with no running byte count and no cap.
column9: All three challenge steps confirm the finding. (1) The quote exists VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless.md` line 86, inside a <Note> block in the "Pipe data through Claude" section, reads in full: "As of Claude Code v2.1.128, piped stdin is capped at 10MB. If you exceed the cap, Claude Code exits with a clear error and a non-zero status. To work with larger inputs, write the content to a file and reference the file path in your prompt instead of piping it." The claimed quote is the first two sentences character-for-character; the unquoted third sentence is a workaround suggestion and does not reverse the conclusion. (2) The cited code says what was claimed. apps/cli/src/index.ts:423-442 `readPrompt` — it enters the stdin branch when `--stdin` is present or (no positional message and `process.stdin.isTTY` is false), then does `const chunks: string[] = []; const reader = Bun.stdin.stream().getReader()` and loops `while (true) { const { done, value } = await reader.read(); if (done) break; chunks.push(decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })) }` before `chunks.join('')`. There is no running byte counter, no length comparison, no throw, no `process.exit`. (3) Nothing one layer up or down supplies the cap. Layer up: the only two callers are `cmdSend` (:576) and `cmdRun` (:766) — `cmdRun` is this fork's `claude -p` analogue, spawning a local headless server in printMode — and both validate only `!message.trim()`; a binary-safe `grep -ran` over apps/cli/src finds `Bun.stdin`/`process.stdin` at exactly two lines (:427, :430), so there is no second stdin reader (no stream-json input path) that might cap. Layer down: the message travels the WsRpcServer (packages/server-core/src/transport/server.ts), which constructs `new WebSocketServer({ server })` (:294, :310) with no `maxPayload` option — a repo-wide `grep -ran maxPayload` over packages/server-core/src, packages/server/src and apps/cli/src returns zero hits — so the `ws` default is 100 MiB, well above 10 MB, and even that would surface as a connection close, not a clear error. No RPC handler enforces a text-message size limit (the only "too large" errors in packages/server-core/src/handlers are image-attachment resizes in files.ts:324-336). The nearest same-named constants are in a SIBLING subsystem and do NOT apply: `ProcessSupervisor.MAX_STDIN_DATA_BYTES = 1 MiB` and `MAX_STDIN_WRITE_BYTES = 64 KiB` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:25-27) bound what the host writes to a CHILD process's stdin, not what the CLI reads from its own. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) — none concerns stdin or the CLI. Not a de-brand, gateway or dropped-subscription product difference either: docs/cli.md:118-125 and :195-199 actively document piping stdin into both `nessy-general-agent send` and `nessy-general-agent run`, so the fork ships the surface the doc caps and simply never caps it.

For the SUBAGENT case specifically the fork is tighter than the claim, not looser: a child session's stop drains the child's OWN session key and rejects leftovers -- SessionManager.ts:10698-10707, `drainSession(record.childSessionKey)` then `child-session-process-residual:<agentId>` if anything is still running/lost -- and every spawned subagent already carries a default 30-minute wall-clock deadline (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:607, `deadlineAt: Date.now() + (cfg.timeoutMs ?? 30 * 60_000)`), enforced at SessionManager.ts:9968-9985 where expiry calls cancelProcessing on the child. So the default bound on a subagent-owned background shell here is 30 minutes to the subagent run plus a strict drain, against Claude's 60 minutes -- a different mechanism, not an absent one. (2) 'the background-shell path has none' is false. The background shell is bash_background (pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1402-1412, createBackgroundBashTool) -> requestSupervisedProcess({background:true}) -> ProcessSupervisor -> ProcessStore, and ProcessStore.append IS an output-byte ceiling: packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-store.ts:7 'const MAX_LOG_BYTES = 64 * 1024' and :126-131 compute 'drop = max(0, combined.byteLength - limit)', rewrite the log to combined.subarray(drop) and advance baseCursor by the dropped byte count. Production uses the default with no override (SessionManager.ts:3573 'new ProcessStore({ root: join(SESSIONS_DIR, ".pi-processes") })'); the only maxLogBytes argument in the tree is a test at process-supervisor.test.ts:698. Two more ceilings on the same path the finding also missed: ProcessSupervisor.MAX_FOREGROUND_STREAM_BYTES = 64*1024 (process-supervisor.ts:28, applied by appendBoundedStream at :750-754) and OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES in orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:171-177. So 'the only output-byte ceilings in the tree are X and Y' is wrong on its own terms. (3) The CONSEQUENCE is handled one layer up, which is this repo's recurring false-positive shape. Claude needs a 5GB kill switch because it accumulates the full background-task output; here accumulation is structurally impossible - the on-disk log is a fixed 64 KiB rolling window, so a task that floods output writes 64 KiB forever and the cursor accounting (baseCursor/nextCursor, readLog at :142-148, surfaced to the model as next_offset via handlers/bash-output.ts and pi-agent.ts:6141 requestBashOutput) keeps the gap visible rather than silently lying. Termination is not absent either: BACKGROUND_PROCESS_MAX_LIFETIME_MS = 24h caps every background shell (pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:952, applied at :1411 and :1590), and ProcessSupervisor.trackAppend (:675-681) SIGKILLs the whole process tree and marks the record 'lost' if the store write ever fails, which is the disk-exhaustion case the 5GB rule guards. The literal-number grep is a search for the wrong constant: verified binary-safe with grep -rain that no 5GB literal exists, which is true and irrelevant. column7: Both model-list fetches use bare `fetch(url, { headers })` with no `redirect` option, so the WHATWG default `"follow"` applies. The Anthropic-format fetch has the same shape with `x-api-key`. A gateway (or a captive proxy in front of one) that answers `/v1/models` with a 30x hands the credential to whatever host it names.

The two dominant LLM-gateway products namespace Anthropic models as `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` (LiteLLM, OpenRouter) or `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6-v1:0` (Bedrock-proxying gateways); every such id is dropped, so the picker comes back empty against a gateway whose model list Claude Code would populate. Path ships only in `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE=1` builds.
column9: Doc sentence verbatim: YES, line 166 of llm-gateway-protocol.md; the rest of the line does not reverse it. Cited line accurate: YES, packages/shared/src/agent/backend/internal/drivers/anthropic.ts:76 is `.filter(m => m.id.startsWith('claude-') && !m.id.startsWith('claude-2') && !m.id.startsWith('claude-instant') && !m.id.startsWith('claude-1'))`. The CONSEQUENCE is false, and it is the inert-worklist section 4 shape #3/#4 (enforcement one layer up + wrong sibling subsystem named). (1) Wrong subsystem. The doc's section is Claude Code CLI's opt-in gateway model discovery: `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1`, off by default, `GET /v1/models?limit=1000`, 3s timeout, redirects treated as failure, cached to `~/.claude/cache/gateway-models.json`, feeding the CLI's `/model` picker. That feature does not exist in the fork at all -- `grep -ran GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY` over the repo returns one docs line and zero code. `anthropicDriver.fetchModels` is a different mechanism: Nessy's own catalog refresh for the app's model list, always on, paginated `limit=100` + `after_id`, no 3s timeout, no redirect ban, no gateway-models.json cache. (2) The claimed failure path is unreachable. A `providerType: 'anthropic'` connection never carries a gateway baseUrl by construction: `createBuiltInConnection('anthropic-api', baseUrl)` returns `pi_compat` (server-core/src/domain/connection-setup-logic.ts:142), pinned by two tests (apps/electron/src/main/__tests__/connection-setup-logic.test.ts:83-88 and server-core/src/domain/connection-setup-logic.test.ts:165); the SETUP handler flips an existing anthropic api_key connection to `pi_compat` + `customEndpoint: {api:'anthropic-messages'}` the moment a baseUrl is set and back to `anthropic` when it is cleared (server-core/src/handlers/rpc/llm-connections.ts:78-89); and `resolveSetupTestConnectionHint` returns `pi_compat` whenever a baseUrl is present (shared/src/agent/backend/factory.ts:415). So every gateway connection routes to `piDriver.fetchModels` (drivers/pi.ts:311-333), which never calls `/v1/models` and applies no `claude-` prefix filter. (3) The picker does not come back empty: the setup UI REQUIRES a declared model list for a custom endpoint -- 'Default model is required for custom endpoints.' (apps/electron/src/renderer/components/apisetup/ApiKeyInput.tsx:441-445) -- and the pi_compat picker is populated from those user-declared models. (4) The fork is not blind to the namespaced ids the claim cites: `isClaudeModel` (shared/src/config/models.ts:345-347) matches `anthropic/claude-...` (OpenRouter/LiteLLM) and `anthropic.claude-...` (Bedrock) explicitly, and `isBareBedrockClaudeModel` (shared/src/config/models-pi.ts:98) handles the Bedrock form on the Pi path. Both namespaces are handled -- just in the sibling subsystem the finding named wrongly. (5) The routing is a recorded product decision, not an oversight: root AGENTS.md ('the `anthropic-api` template upgrades to `pi_compat` once a custom endpoint is present') and packages/shared/AGENTS.md ('Prefer routing new model vendors through the existing Pi path'). Not one of the nine section 3 owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md -- those are the seatbelt wildcard, availableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, and listSessionSummaries.

column9: Not refuted on its substance; one secondary clause is wrong and is corrected below. (1) DOC: curl -sL of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/output-styles.md returns the sentence VERBATIM as the first sentence of line 21. The whole line is two sentences and the second REINFORCES rather than reverses: '**Proactive**: Claude executes immediately, makes reasonable assumptions instead of pausing for routine decisions, and prefers action over planning. This is stronger autonomous-execution guidance than [auto mode](/docs/en/permission-modes#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode) applies, and it works without changing your permission mode, so you still see permission prompts before tools run.' Line 19 states 'There are three additional built-in output styles'; :21 Proactive, :23 Explanatory, :25 Learning (with the `TODO(human)` marker). The page is row 136 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a Claude contract page. (2) CODE: packages/shared/src/prompts/output-styles.ts:83-128 is BUILTIN_OUTPUT_STYLE_DEFINITIONS and contains exactly four entries with ids default/concise/explanatory/reviewer (labels Default, Concise, Explanatory, Reviewer). :562 is `const NO_OUTPUT_STYLE: OutputStyleComposition = { prompt: '', keepCodingInstructions: true }` and :570 returns it whenever resolveOutputStyle finds nothing. Both cited line numbers are exact. `grep -a` over packages/ and apps/ (excluding node_modules and dist) finds no Proactive or Learning built-in style and no TODO(human) marker convention anywhere; the only 'Proactive' hit is unrelated prose in system.ts:1149 about Mermaid diagrams. (3) LAYER UP / LAYER DOWN: no sibling subsystem supplies the missing styles. The Claude backend does not pass an outputStyle through to the SDK - system.ts:438-450 composes our own block and appends it to the claude_code preset, and grep for outputStyle across packages/shared/src/agent returns only base-agent.ts plugin-style plumbing. So the absence of Proactive/Learning is real end to end. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (that list is seatbelt wildcard, availableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries). NOT a rebrand or product-scope difference either: it has nothing to do with the dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows, the corporate gateway, or NESSY_ naming - Concise and Reviewer are Nessy-authored styles, not renamed Claude ones. Registration confirmed: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:224 and :225 are exactly these two rows, harvested from docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-output-style-contract.md:194-195, both categorised 'documented, not implemented' - a recorded gap, not a decided-against one. WHAT IS WRONG: the consequence clause 'a .md authored against the documented set names a style that does not resolve'. A user-authored .md DOES resolve. discoverCustomOutputStyles is name-agnostic and registers any .md under the user (CONFIG_DIR/output-styles), workspace or trusted-project directory as `custom:<slug>`, so dropping a Proactive.md or Learning.md there yields a working, selectable style; resolveOutputStyle (:526-542) only falls through to NO_OUTPUT_STYLE for a stored id that matches no built-in, plugin or custom style. Reaching the silent 'add nothing' path therefore requires hand-writing an unresolvable id into config.json:outputStyleId, and that key is a private Nessy field written by one RPC handler - we do not read the documented `outputStyle` settings key at all (itself a separate register row at :227), so a settings file authored against the docs is ignored outright rather than silently no-opped.

column5: To turn it off, set one of these environment variables to `1`:
column6: Prompt caching can be turned off entirely or per model family by setting one of five environment variables to `1`: `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING`, `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_HAIKU`, `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_SONNET`, `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_OPUS`, `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_FABLE`.
column7: No reader for any of the five, under the documented spelling or a `NESSY_`-prefixed one, and no config toggle either. `grep -rain "promptcach|prompt_cach" packages apps` returns only the `extendedPromptCache` TTL toggle and the interceptor's `cache_control` rewriters — every one of which upgrades or strips a TTL, none of which can remove the breakpoint. There is no way to disable caching for a model or provider while debugging, which is the page's stated use.
column8: grep -rain "DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING|PROMPT_CACHING_1H|PROMPT_CACHING_5M" packages apps scripts → no hits; the full toggle surface is packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:129 and packages/shared/src/unified-network-interceptor.ts:367,437
column9: Quote verified verbatim at prompt-caching.md:237, second sentence of a two-sentence line ('Disabling caching is occasionally useful when debugging caching behavior with a specific model or provider. To turn it off, set one of these environment variables to `1`:'), table at :241-245, plus :247 on the managed-settings `env` block. The identifier half of the finding is true — no file we own reads DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING or its four family variants, and the only Nessy-side knob is `extendedPromptCache` (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:134), which the interceptor uses to upgrade or strip a TTL (packages/shared/src/unified-network-interceptor.ts:368 stripPromptCacheTtl, :437 upgradePromptCacheTtl) and never to remove a breakpoint. But the CONSEQUENCE — 'there is no way to disable caching for a model or provider while debugging' — is false, and it is the classic 'unwired identifier, handled one layer up' shape. These are the upstream Claude runtime's own env vars, and we ship that runtime: `strings -a node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude` contains 19 occurrences of DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING — six bare, six each of _HAIKU/_SONNET/_OPUS/_FABLE, plus three of an undocumented _MYTHOS (positive control on the same dump: ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H, 4 hits; an earlier zero-hit run was a false negative from macOS lacking `timeout`). Our Claude backend hands it the whole host environment: buildClaudeSubprocessEnv (packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:236-265) spreads `...process.env` and deletes only the three Bedrock routing vars, and it is the single env builder for that path (only caller getDefaultOptions:276). So `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1` exported before launch reaches the runtime and works today. Nothing downstream re-adds a breakpoint: our interceptor only mutates `ttl` on cache_control objects that already exist (unified-network-interceptor.ts:447-486) and never creates one — its own comment at :324 names the SDK as the producer. The organization half of :247 is wired too: DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING is unlisted in MANAGED_ENV_CLASSIFICATION, and classifyManagedEnvVar (packages/shared/src/config/managed-env.ts:189-191) defaults an unlisted name to 'immediate', so applyManagedEnv writes it into process.env at startup — 'writing here is what carries the block into the Pi subprocess, the Claude subprocess and stdio MCP servers' (managed-env.ts:320-324). Sibling-subsystem check: the Pi runtime does not read these names (grep -rail over node_modules/@earendil-works: 0 hits, with cache_control present in pi-ai as the positive control), and the default product path is the Nessy Gateway's OpenAI-like endpoint, where Anthropic `cache_control` breakpoints do not exist — so on the fork's own default path there is no breakpoint to disable, and on the Claude path the documented variables work. Not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3.

column5: Set `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1` to force the five-minute TTL regardless of authentication.
column6: The one-hour TTL is opted into with `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1`, and `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1` forces the five-minute TTL back regardless of authentication — specifically so a managed-settings `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` can be overridden locally.
column7: Our counterpart is a single boolean, `extendedPromptCache` (default `false`), reachable only through the desktop Settings → AI toggle and its RPC pair. Neither env spelling is read, so there is no local override of a policy-delivered value and no way to set the TTL on the headless server or in CI. The auto-selection half of this section is already registered (deviation-register.md:406); the two override variables are not.
column9: The quote is verbatim (prompt-caching.md:204, whole line: 'Set `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1` to force the five-minute TTL regardless of authentication. This is useful when you're debugging cache behavior, comparing the two TTLs, or overriding an `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` set in managed settings.'). The identifier half of the finding also holds: a NUL-safe `grep -ra 'FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M|ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H' packages apps scripts` returns zero hits. But BOTH stated consequences are false, which is the classic 'identifier unwired, consequence already handled one layer up' shape. (1) 'No local override of a policy-delivered value' is wrong: `extendedPromptCache: false` is not a passive default, it is an ACTIVE force-5m. `upgradePromptCacheTtl` (unified-network-interceptor.ts:437) opens with `if (!isExtendedPromptCacheEnabled()) return stripPromptCacheTtl(body)`, and `stripPromptCacheTtl` (:367-414) deletes `ttl` from every ephemeral `cache_control` block in tools, system, message content and top-level. Its own comment names the exact scenario the doc names: 'When extendedPromptCache is disabled, the SDK may still send ttl: "1h" natively (via prompt-caching-scope beta). This function removes the ttl field so blocks fall back to the API default (5 min).' It is called unconditionally from the Anthropic provider's `modifyRequest` (:978), i.e. on the wire, DOWNSTREAM of the SDK -- so it overrides whatever the SDK chose from authentication or from an inherited env var, which is strictly more authoritative than `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M`, and it is the default. The doc's stated purpose (overriding a managed-settings `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H`) is therefore already satisfied: an unclassified key in a managed `env` block lands in `process.env` as category `immediate` (config/managed-env.ts) and is inherited by the SDK subprocess, and our strip removes the resulting 1h TTL anyway. `extendedPromptCache` itself is a per-user config.json key that no managed-policy path writes, so there is nothing policy-delivered to be trapped by. (2) 'Reachable only through the desktop Settings -> AI toggle and its RPC pair ... no way to set the TTL on the headless server or in CI' is wrong twice over. It is a documented user-editable config.json key -- docs-site/content/reference/config/config-file.md:169 and the ru mirror :172 -- living at `CONFIG_DIR/config.json`, where `CONFIG_DIR` honours `NESSY_CONFIG_DIR` (config/paths.ts:19-21). The consumer that applies the TTL is the interceptor inside the SDK subprocess, which reads that file straight off disk with a 100 ms cache (interceptor-common.ts:104-114) and never touches the renderer or the RPC layer; the repo's own suite drives both branches by writing the key into config.json (unified-network-interceptor.schema.test.ts:156,163), which is the CI recipe the finding says does not exist. And the RPC pair is registered in packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/settings.ts:401,407 -- the HEADLESS server's own handler table, allow-listed for remote at protocol/routing.ts:166-167; apps/electron/src/transport/channel-map.ts:358-359 is a client of it, not its owner. So the RPC pair is a headless-server surface, not a desktop-only one. Context that makes this naming rather than behaviour: this fork replaces CLAUDE_*/ANTHROPIC_* env knobs with config.json keys under `NESSY_CONFIG_DIR` repo-wide, and the same sweep already reached that conclusion for this exact knob on another page -- 2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json:3361: '`1h` prompt-cache TTL exists under our own `extendedPromptCache` config key rather than `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` ... env-var naming, not a behaviour gap.' f197 contradicts it. Also relevant, though not §3 of the inert worklist (this is not one of the nine): docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-prompt-cache-and-egress-disclosure.md:121, harvested into the deviation register, records that the knob only rewrites `cache_control`, which only the Anthropic adapter emits, while the shipped Pi/Nestor path is an OpenAI-like relay with implicit prefix caching and no cache writes -- and `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` is off by default -- so an env override would have nothing to act on for the shipped product. Cited line numbers had drifted (storage.ts:129/173/1030 are now :134/:178/:1035; interceptor-common.ts:143 is now :141-145); content matched, so that alone is not the refutation.

column5: As of v2.1.181, you can set [`CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE`](/docs/en/env-vars) to a marker file path to extend this to any time you are at the machine, even in another window: notifications are skipped while the file exists.
column6: The notification presence gate has a documented escape hatch: a marker-file path in CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE suppresses notifications whenever the file exists, extending suppression beyond "the focused window" to "the user is at the machine".
column7: Our PushNotification presence gate is window-focus only. `showAgentNotification` returns exactly three suppression reasons — `'window-focused' | 'notifications-disabled' | 'unsupported'` — and reads no presence-marker file and no env override. A user at the machine in another window still gets notified.
column8: apps/electron/src/main/notifications.ts:105 (reason union) and :117 (the only presence branch); repo-wide `grep -rain -e 'CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE' -e 'presenceFile'` over packages/ apps/ returns 0 hits
column9: The doc sentence is real and verbatim (remote-control.md line 263, and the page is a legitimate Claude contract page - row 150 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv). The repo facts are also broadly right: apps/electron/src/main/notifications.ts:105 carries the three-reason union, :116-117 is the only presence branch, and `grep -rain -e 'CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE' -e 'presenceFile' -e 'presence_file'` over packages/ apps/ returns 0 hits, as does a sweep for powerMonitor / getSystemIdleTime / getSystemIdleState / screen-lock. The finding is nevertheless refuted on subsystem and product-scope grounds. (1) WRONG SUBSYSTEM - the sibling-symbol trap. The quoted line sits under '## Mobile push notifications' on the Remote Control page and governs pushes delivered to your PHONE via the Claude mobile app while a Remote Control session runs on your machine. CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE exists precisely BECAUSE the delivery target is a second device: the CLI cannot otherwise tell whether you are at your desk in another window. Our `deliverModelNotification` (the claim names it `showAgentNotification`, which has 0 hits repo-wide) is the desktop-shell backend of the `PushNotification` TOOL, cited to `tools-reference.md:41` and described in packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:628 as 'Raise an OS notification on the user's desktop'. It is an Electron Notification on the SAME machine, reached via packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/push-notification.ts -> deliverDesktopNotification. Same-machine delivery and cross-device delivery are different subsystems with different presence semantics. (2) THE CONSEQUENCE IS FALSE, AND INVERTED. Read the whole line: the doc's own recommended wiring is 'create the file when your screen unlocks and delete it when your screen locks'. Applied to a local desktop notification that rule suppresses the banner exactly when the screen is unlocked and the banner would be SEEN, and delivers it exactly when the screen is locked and nobody is there. (1) WRONG SUBSYSTEM / deliberate product difference. `autoUpdatesChannel` governs the Claude Code CLI's own self-updater: the native installer's `~/.local/share/claude/versions/` tree, `claude update`, npm-global installs, Homebrew cask names (`claude-code` vs `claude-code@latest`), `minimumVersion`, `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` -- the whole surrounding section of setup.md is about that mechanism. Nessy Desktop has no such updater and no `nessy update` command (apps/cli/src has no self-update path at all); it is an Electron app updated by electron-updater from an internal T-Bank S3 feed of dmg/nsis/AppImage artifacts. `setup.md` is already row 152 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md with the recorded verdict `vne produkta` (out of product), alongside `platforms`, `quickstart`, `troubleshoot-install`, `vs-code`. So the finding both mis-states its own grep and mis-states the shipped enum. (3) THE CONSEQUENCE IS FALSE: a release channel DOES reach the updater. apps/electron/electron-builder.yml:80 sets `channel: "${env.NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_CHANNEL}"` in the `publish:` block; electron-builder bakes it into `app-update.yml` and electron-updater uses it to select the `dev-mac.yml` / `dev-arm64-mac.yml` / `dev-win.yml` metadata the feed publishes (the same names scripts/verify-update-feed.mjs:34-94 builds from its `--channel`). .gitlab-ci.yml:234-235 sets it (`NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_CHANNEL=dev`) and :368,:389 verify the feed against `${NESSY_DESKTOP_DEV_UPDATE_CHANNEL:-dev}`. column9: Quote is real and the cited line is accurate, but the CONSEQUENCE is false. (1) setup.md:246 reads verbatim 'The `minimumVersion` setting establishes a floor.' and the rest of that two-sentence line plus :260 support the claimed behaviour, so the finding is not refuted on the quote. (2) packages/shared/src/config/managed-version-gate.ts:89-94 does declare only requiredMinimumVersion/requiredMaximumVersion, and `grep -an minimumVersion` over packages/*/src apps/*/src scripts returns exactly one hit -- a doc-quote comment at managed-version-gate.ts:12 that itself names the distinction ('Differs from `minimumVersion`, which prevents downgrades but never blocks startup'). So the identifier really is unwired. (3) But 'nothing constrains what the updater is allowed to install' is wrong. Our updater is electron-updater (apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts). Its allowDowngrade defaults to false (node_modules/electron-updater/out/AppUpdater.js:138) and isUpdateAvailable returns true only when gt(latest,current), otherwise `allowDowngrade && lt(...)` -> false (AppUpdater.js:356-362). Nothing in our source sets allowDowngrade, allowPrerelease, or autoUpdater.channel -- the channel setter is the one thing that would flip allowDowngrade to true (AppUpdater.js:33-45) -- verified with grep -an over apps/electron/src, packages/*/src, apps/cli/src (zero hits). Both the background check and the manual 'Check Now' go through the same gate (checkForUpdates at auto-update.ts:327-370 calls autoUpdater.checkForUpdates), and installUpdate() (:381) only ever installs what that gate accepted. The floor therefore exists: it is the running version, enforced by construction instead of by a settings key. Layer up: the mechanism Claude's minimumVersion exists to guard -- a runtime 'latest' -> 'stable' switch that would downgrade you (setup.md:246, :248) -- has no analogue here. The channel is baked into the artifact at build time (apps/electron/electron-builder.yml:80 `channel: "${env.NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_CHANNEL}"`, set at .gitlab-ci.yml:235); there is no autoUpdatesChannel setting, no /config channel switch, and no `claude update`-equivalent manual installer (apps/cli has no self-update path). Layer down: the residual capability -- an admin-pinned floor ABOVE the running version -- is what the IMPLEMENTED requiredMinimumVersion startup gate already delivers, by refusing to start below the org minimum; the doc itself (setup.md:261) points admins at exactly those two keys for enforcement. Product difference: setup.md is CLI-installation surface (npm/native installer, Homebrew, WinGet, apt/dnf/apk, `claude update`, ~/.claude/settings.json autoUpdatesChannel); this fork ships a signed Electron .dmg/NSIS/AppImage from a corporate S3/R2 feed (scripts/prepare-release-assets.mjs, scripts/verify-update-feed.mjs), and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:268 already records row 152 `setup` as out of product. column9: (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: CONFIRMED. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup.md puts the sentence at line 275, byte-identical. Read the WHOLE line: it is three sentences, not two, and the uncited third reinforces rather than reverses -- 'Use this when you distribute Claude Code through your own channels and need users to stay on the version you provide.' Section context (:263 '### Disable auto-updates', :265-273 the settings.json env block) confirms the reading. But that third sentence is also what breaks the finding, because it names the exact deployment posture this fork already occupies. (2) CITED LINES: partially confirmed, with one dead line. auto-update.ts:130 `autoUpdater.autoInstallOnAppQuit = true` is genuinely an unconditional module-level assignment. auto-update.ts:47 is indeed the sole `process.env` read (`process.env.LOCALAPPDATA` in getUpdateCacheDir). But auto-update.ts:127 `autoUpdater.autoDownload = true` is a DEAD default: checkForUpdates() overwrites it at :334 from its own parameter and restores the previous value at :369 on every single check, and all four call sites pass an explicit `{autoDownload: true}` (auto-update.ts:448, menu.ts:75, menu.ts:200, handlers/system.ts:274). Deleting :127 changes nothing. The grep is accurate -- `grep -rain -e DISABLE_UPDATE -e DISABLE_AUTOUPDAT --include='*.ts' packages apps scripts` returns 0, and a repo-wide `grep -ain` across ts/tsx/json/md/mjs/js/yml finds the strings only inside this sweep's own artefacts. So the IDENTIFIER half of the claim is true. (3) LAYER UP AND DOWN -- the CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier, is FALSE, on two independent grounds. LAYER UP: there is no vendor-run update feed to opt out of. apps/electron/electron-builder.yml:77-80 sets `publish: {provider: generic, url: "${env.NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_URL}", channel: "${env.NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_CHANNEL}"}`, injected at build time from the deploying organisation's own CI secret (.gitlab-ci.yml:234-235, `export NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_URL="$NESSY_DESKTOP_DEV_UPDATE_URL"`; apps/electron/README.md:79 shows the same knob for local rehearsal). In Claude Code, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER/DISABLE_UPDATES exist because Anthropic runs the feed and the redistributing org does not -- the flags are how the org takes the vendor's updater out of the loop. Here the premise is inverted: the organisation that deploys Nessy Desktop is the organisation that builds it (AGENTS.md: internal desktop-agent fork rebranded for T-Bank), and it already decides which version every user can reach by controlling what it publishes to its own feed. A build with no URL has no working provider at all (GenericProvider.js:12 passes configuration.url straight to newBaseUrl). So the claimed harm -- 'A corporate deployment cannot pin users to a distributed version' -- is false; pinning is the fork's structural default, achieved by the mechanism the quoted third sentence prescribes rather than by an env flag. Also relevant one layer up: the launch probe is gated on `app.isPackaged` (index.ts:1259-1265, else-branch logs '[auto-update] Skipping auto-update in dev mode'), so even 'hardcoded on' is not literally unconditional. LAYER DOWN / SIBLING SUBSYSTEM: DISABLE_UPDATES is distinguished from DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER by exactly one thing -- blocking the MANUAL paths `claude update` and `claude install`, i.e. the native installer that manages ~/.local/bin/claude as a symlink into ~/.local/share/claude/versions/ (setup.md:205, :277-293). Nessy Desktop has no native installer, no versions/ directory and no self-update subcommand: apps/cli/src/index.ts parses only flags (--url, --token, --model, --version, ...) with no `update` or `install` verb, and `grep -rain -e self-update -e selfUpdate apps/cli/src` returns nothing. The entire reason the second flag exists as a separate flag has no counterpart to diverge from. Measuring a CLI-installer two-flag contract against an Electron electron-updater subsystem is the sibling-subsystem error this series warns about. (4) NOT an inert-worklist section 3 owner decision -- the nine are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions; none is this. (5) It IS partly a deliberate product difference: desktop Electron app with a build-time-injected generic feed vs a self-updating CLI binary. Refuted on the consequence, not on the identifier.

column5: Claude Code accepts only a file named `bash.exe`, `sh.exe`, `bash`, or `sh`; with any other name, such as Git for Windows' `git-bash.exe` launcher, it ignores the variable and auto-detects Git Bash as if it were unset, logging a warning visible with `--debug`.
column6: CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH accepts four filenames — bash.exe, sh.exe, bash, or sh — and ignores any other name.
column7: Our validator accepts only `bash.exe` — the regex is anchored to that single name — and returns the hard error "Path must point to bash.exe" for anything else. A user who points at Git for Windows' `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\sh.exe`, which the SDK we spawn would accept, is refused by our onboarding and by the persisted-path revalidation, which then clears the stored path. Strictly narrower than the documented enum on a value we write into the SDK's own env var.
column8: packages/server-core/src/services/git-bash.ts:8 (`/(?:^|[\\/])bash\.exe$/i`) and :17-19 (refusal); consumed at packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/system.ts:216, :224, :238, :272 where the value is assigned to process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH
column9: Could not refute on any of the three axes. (1) DOC VERBATIM: curl -sL of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install.md line 654 carries the quoted sentence character-for-character, prefixed by the MDX marker {/* min-version: 2.1.219 */}. Read whole: the remainder of the line is 'A path that doesn't exist gets the same fallback and warning. Before v2.1.219, Claude Code used any existing file as the shell without checking its name, and exited at startup with `Claude Code was unable to find CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH path` when the path didn't exist.' Nothing there reverses the conclusion; it only version-gates the four-name enum to >= 2.1.219. (2) CITED CODE: packages/server-core/src/services/git-bash.ts:8 is exactly /(?:^|[\\/])bash\.exe$/i and :18-19 returns {valid:false, error:'Path must point to bash.exe'}. Cited consumer line numbers are exact: packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/system.ts:216, :224, :238 (auto-detect assignments) and :272 (SET_PATH assignment), with :219 clearGitBashPath() on a persisted path that fails revalidation. (3) LAYER UP / LAYER DOWN, and the CONSEQUENCE tested separately from the identifier. Layer down gave a positive control for the claim's load-bearing half ('which the SDK we spawn would accept'): the bundled consumer, node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.183, bridge.mjs, resolves the variable as `if(process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH){if(existsSync(...))return process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH; console.error(`Claude Code was unable to find CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH path "..."`),process.exit(1)}` — no filename test whatsoever, so it would accept C:\Program Files\Git\bin\sh.exe (and bash, and sh). Our gate is therefore narrower than the documented enum AND narrower than the consumer we actually ship. Layer up: the narrowing is reached on three independent paths, not one — the onboarding SET_PATH handler (system.ts:266), the RPC auto-detect (system.ts:213-219), and the startup revalidation at apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:596-604, which on failure calls clearGitBashPath() and deletes the env var; the same code is duplicated at apps/electron/src/main/handlers/system.ts:137-196. The Browse dialog (system.ts:250-263) filters to extensions:['exe'], so the extension-less `bash`/`sh` names cannot even be selected, and the auto-probe list is four hardcoded bash.exe paths. Sibling-subsystem check: rg over the repo finds no second, broader Git Bash validator; isGitBashExecutablePath/validateGitBashPath/isUsableGitBashPath have exactly these consumers plus one test. The narrowing is locked in by apps/electron/src/main/__tests__/git-bash.test.ts:21, which asserts isGitBashExecutablePath('/tmp/git/bin/sh.exe') === false. Not an owner decision: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions — none is this, and grep for bash.exe/GIT_BASH across the parity audit and the deviation register returns no recorded ruling. Not a rebrand or dropped-subscription product difference either: CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH is written verbatim under Claude's own name for Claude's own subprocess, and the Git Bash onboarding step is not provider-gated. Only bound on the finding: practical exposure is limited to Windows hosts whose Git install is being pointed at by hand, and NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE is off by default (though the SDK JS core always ships).

column5: Then set `USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0` in your [environment](/docs/en/env-vars).
column6: A user whose bundled ripgrep will not run can force Claude Code onto a system ripgrep with the `USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0` environment variable.
column7: `resolveRipgrepPath` hard-resolves `node_modules/@vscode/ripgrep/bin/rg` through three fixed candidates (packaged app root, upward walk, cwd) and consults no environment variable. When none exists, `getRipgrepPath`/`searchSessions` throw `SearchUnavailableError` and session search is dead with no user-reachable recovery. `USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP` has 0 hits repo-wide (checked with `grep -ra`, per the NUL-byte trap).
column9: Quote is verbatim (troubleshooting.md:113), but the finding names the wrong subsystem and its consequence is false one layer up. (1) WRONG SUBSYSTEM. The doc scopes the knob in its own section opener at :77 -- 'If the Search tool, `@file` mentions, custom agents, or custom skills aren't finding files' -- and the second half of the very line quoted confirms it: 'run `claude doctor` ... and check that the Search line'. All of those are the AGENT's file-discovery surfaces inside the Claude Code process. The cited `resolveRipgrepPath` (runtime-resolver.ts:442) feeds only `packages/server-core/src/services/search.ts` -> `searchSessions`, which is the desktop shell's session-HISTORY full-text search: it greps `-g '**/session.jsonl'` under the sessions dir for transcript text. Claude Code has no session-history search feature at all, so USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP was never its knob. This is exactly the disallowed-tools-for-subagents-vs-skills trap. (2) CONSEQUENCE FALSE UPSTREAM. For the surface the doc IS about, the fork already honours the variable, by inheritance rather than by code of ours. The Claude backend runs the real Claude Agent SDK subprocess, and `buildClaudeSubprocessEnv` (packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:236-243) builds its env as `{...process.env, ...getProxyEnvVars(), ...envOverrides}` -- an open passthrough that deletes only three Bedrock vars (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL). A user who exports USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0 before launching gets it into the SDK subprocess, which implements the documented switch. The repo states this design explicitly for a sibling SDK knob at claude-agent.ts:310-318: MAX_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_RETRIES 'reaches the subprocess by env inheritance -- deliberately NOT renamed on the Claude side (the Nessy Pi loop has its own NESSY_-prefixed knob)'. So 0 repo hits for USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP is the CORRECT state, not a gap: the variable belongs to the SDK we embed, and re-implementing it here would be the defect. (3) THE CITED CODE IS MISREAD. The claim of 'three fixed candidates ... and consults no environment variable' undercounts: lines 457-466 add a FOURTH, resolving system `rg` from PATH via which/where whenever `!hostRuntime.isPackaged` (headless server, dev mode) -- i.e. the non-packaged host already does what the doc asks, without a flag. The packaged exclusion is a stated deliberate decision in the same comment: 'Packaged apps must use vendored binary only -- never resolve from PATH to avoid picking up an incompatible system install.' (4) 'DEAD WITH NO USER-REACHABLE RECOVERY' IS OVERSTATED. SearchUnavailableError is caught in apps/electron/src/renderer/hooks/useSessionSearch.ts:352-357, which sets isSearchUnavailable; SessionList.tsx:723 forwards it and SessionSearchHeader.tsx:99 renders the localized `session.searchUnavailable` notice. column5: Place an executable in a bin/ directory at your plugin root and Claude Code adds that directory to the Bash tool's PATH while the plugin is enabled.
column6: A `bin/` directory at the plugin root is added to the Bash tool's PATH while the plugin is enabled, making its executables invokable as bare commands.
column7: We detect `bin/` files and reason about which ones a manifest command already reaches, but we never extend the Bash tool's PATH from a bundle. An executable that no capability references by path is classified unrunnable and left deferred, so a plugin whose command/agent/hook invokes its helper as a bare name fails. The code states the deviation in its own comment.
column8: packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:2364 — "Nessy does not extend the Bash tool's PATH from a bundle, so an executable nothing else reaches really is unrunnable and stays deferred."
column9: The doc sentence is verbatim (w14.md:107, first of a three-sentence lede) and the cited line exists verbatim (claude.ts:2364) -- but the claim quoted the PREMISE of a doc-comment whose later paragraph reverses it, the exact 'second half of the line reverses the conclusion' trap. claude.ts:2379-2385 continues: '**The PATH half IS built** (`appendPluginBinPath`, wired at `claude-agent.ts` and `pi-agent.ts`), so on both shipping backends a `bin/` executable of an ENABLED plugin does resolve as a bare command. This function therefore no longer records the surface as deferred'. Both halves of the claimed state are false at HEAD (working tree clean for all four files). (1) PATH IS extended: `appendPluginBinPath` (data-paths.ts:247) appends `<bundleRoot>/bin` for every root of the turn's runnable capability view (`enabledPluginBundleRoots`, data-paths.ts:200), wired on the Claude backend at claude-agent.ts:691 and :736 (node shim stays first, plugin bins last) and on the Pi backend at pi-agent.ts:5187, composed for EVERY supervised child start because 'any Bash tool call' is the documented scope. Appended never prepended, so a plugin cannot shadow a system binary. (2) NOT deferred: `addClaudeBinSurfaceDeferral` (claude.ts:2392-2435) pushes no `deferred` row at all -- it returns early when every bin file is already reached (:2415) and again whenever the bundle declares any capability (:2422); the only remaining output is a `warning` diagnostic for the single residual case of a bundle declaring zero capabilities, hence carrying no runtime root. Consequence verified separately from the identifier by positive control: `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/plugin-bin-path.test.ts` (6 tests, all pass) asserts a bundle executable resolves as a bare command on both backends, appends rather than shadows, grants nothing while the plugin is disabled, and reaches every Pi supervised child start; `format-adapters.test.ts:2817` ('defers every file-backed Claude surface it cannot run') passes with deferred kinds `['settings','theme']` -- no `bin` row. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 and not a Nessy product difference: it is a shipped fix (tracked as C6), whose stated motive was that a `bin` deferral set compatibility.state to `partial`, and management-service-v2.ts:553 purges every durable activation grant for a partial bundle on repair.

The IDENTIFIER half of the finding is true: no `showThinkingSummaries` exists in our source or settings schema, and the cited lines check out with minor drift (storage.ts:56 `defaultThinkingLevel`, storage.ts:189 workspaceDefaults `thinkingLevel: 'medium'`; the claim said :55/:184). (1) The default posture is the SAME, not opposite. `type: 'thinking'` renders only inside the turn's activity section, which is collapsed by default: the live chat passes a controlled `isExpanded` from `useTurnCardExpansion` initialized to an empty Set (apps/electron/src/renderer/hooks/useTurnCardExpansion.ts:59-64), TurnCard's own fallback is `defaultExpanded = false` (packages/ui/src/components/chat/TurnCard.tsx:2780, mirrored at SessionViewer.tsx:81), and the collapsed header preview surfaces `intent`, `intermediate` content and running tool names but never `thinking` content (getPreviewText, TurnCard.tsx:721-753). column5: Hook output over 50K saved to disk with a path + preview instead of injected into context
column6: Hook output above 50K is written to disk and replaced with a path plus a preview, rather than being injected into context or dropped.
column7: We buffer hook stdout+stderr to a hard 8,192-byte ceiling and silently discard the remainder (a `truncated: true` flag is set on the result but no content is preserved and nothing is written to disk). Because `getHookCommandPreToolDecision` JSON-parses that same truncated stdout, a hook that emits a decision object larger than 8 KiB has its JSON cut mid-object and its decision is lost entirely — a fail-open on any hook with a verbose payload.
column8: packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:26 (`const OUTPUT_LIMIT = 8_192;`) with the truncating appender at :215-221
column9:
1) QUOTE: genuine. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w14.md` line 131 is exactly `
Hook output over 50K saved to disk with a path + preview instead of injected into context
` in the `Other wins` grid; the whole line is that one sentence and nothing in it reverses the conclusion. The companion contract page is stricter still: hooks.md:765 `Hook output strings, including additionalContext, systemMessage, and plain stdout, are capped at 10,000 characters. Output that exceeds this limit is saved to a file and replaced with a preview and file path, the same way large tool results are handled.` and hooks.md:845 repeats it for additionalContext (`writes the full text to a file in the session directory and passes Claude the file path with a short preview`). 2) EVIDENCE: the identifier is real. packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:26 is `const OUTPUT_LIMIT = 8_192;` and appendCapped at :215-221 truncates to it and returns `truncated`. 3) CONSEQUENCE: false on the path that actually executes the hooks this page governs - the classic wrong-subsystem shape. `runHookCommand` is the FALLBACK execution authority and the shipped host never selects it. packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:1103 reads `const runner = options.runner ?? (options.allowDirectCommandRunner ? runHookCommand : undefined);`, and `options.runner` is always present: SessionManager.ts:11297 sets `pluginCommandHookRunner: this.pluginCommandHookRunner(managed, capabilityRuntime)` UNCONDITIONALLY, outside the `provider === 'pi' ? ... : { allowDirectCommandRunner: true }` ternary at :11287-11296, so the `allowDirectCommandRunner` half is vestigial on every provider. runtime-automations.ts:178 forwards it as `pluginCommandRunner`, hooks-automation.ts:515 re-emits it as `runner` from `pluginRunnerOptions()`, and every one of the four execution sites (executeAgentEventInner :582/:585/:593 and buildSdkHooksForConfig :540) spreads those options. The other `runHookCommand` gate, automation-system.ts:671, needs `allowDirectCommandHooks`, which `grep -a` over packages/*/src and apps/*/src sets ONLY in test files (automation-system.test.ts, task-hooks.test.ts, task-hook-decision.test.ts, hook-stdout-context.test.ts); the production construction at SessionManager.ts:7083 passes neither option, and `PluginScopedAutomationSystem.nativeSystem` is never passed in production at all. The live authority is SessionManager.pluginCommandHookRunner (:4184-4515), which spawns through `this.piWorkspaceDrainParticipant.processSupervisorPort.start({... background: false, persistOutput: false ...})` (:4466-4489) - and piWorkspaceDrainParticipant is built in the constructor (:3596), so it is available on Claude/Codex/nestor turns too. Its ceiling is `ProcessSupervisor.MAX_FOREGROUND_STREAM_BYTES = 64 * 1024` (process-supervisor.ts:28) applied by appendBoundedStream (:750-755) to the foreground capture (:273, :284). So BOTH operative halves of the claimed state are wrong for shipped behaviour: the ceiling is 65,536 bytes per stream, 8x the claimed 8,192, and NO `truncated` flag is set at all on that path - the result literal at :4505-4514 has no `truncated` key, and `grep -a '\.truncated'` finds no consumer of HookCommandActionResult.truncated anywhere (SessionManager.ts:1729 is DIRECT_SHELL_OUTPUT_LIMIT, the `!` shell subsystem, not hooks). The stated failure mode (`a hook that emits a decision object larger than 8 KiB has its decision lost entirely - a fail-open on any hook with a verbose payload`) is therefore false: 8-64 KiB decision objects parse fine. The fail-open shape survives only above 64 KiB. And because 65,536 > 50,000, the exact band the quoted sentence is about (50K to 64K) is injected inline in full by this fork rather than dropped - the doc's threshold sits BELOW our cap. 4) Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (checked - seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete/listSubkeys/listSessionSummaries; none concerns hook output size).
