column5: PreCompact hooks can block compaction by exiting with code 2 or returning {"{"}"decision":"block"{"}"}
column6: A `PreCompact` hook can stop a compaction, either by exiting 2 or by returning a top-level `decision: "block"`.
column7: PreCompact cannot block anything, and the two halves of our own contract disagree. `hook-decision-contract.ts` lists PreCompact in `TOP_LEVEL_BLOCK_EVENTS`, so its parsed output is allowed to carry `block`/`deny` + `reason` — but the frozen event table declares it `kind: 'observational'`, and its single emission site awaits `options.emit('PreCompact', …)` whose signature returns `Promise<void> | void`, so any decision the parser produced is discarded before compaction proceeds. A hook author writing the documented blocker sees it accepted and parsed, and the context is compacted anyway.
column8: packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:83 (`kind: 'observational'`) vs packages/shared/src/automations/hook-decision-contract.ts:49 (PreCompact in TOP_LEVEL_BLOCK_EVENTS); emission at packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:151 with the void-returning `emit` declared at :28
column9: The finding survives all three checks, but two of its sub-claims are wrong and must not travel with it. (1) QUOTE: verbatim at whats-new/2026-w16.md:125, a single-clause <div> in the 'Other wins' grid with nothing after it that reverses the conclusion. It is not an isolated release note either: hooks.md:730 carries the row '| `PreCompact` | Yes | Blocks compaction |' in the exit-code-2 table; hooks.md:865 and :890 list PreCompact among the nine top-level-`decision` events ('The only value is "block"'); and hooks.md:2613 states 'Exit with code 2 to block compaction. For a manual `/compact`, the stderr message is shown to the user. You can also block by returning JSON with "decision": "block".' hooks.md:2615 even specifies what a blocked auto-compact does. whats-new/2026-w16 is row 178 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a Claude contract page. (2) CITED LINES: all accurate. types.ts:83 is `{ version: 1, event: 'PreCompact', owner: 'lifecycle-bridge', kind: 'observational', ... }`; hook-decision-contract.ts:49 has 'PreCompact' as the ninth entry of TOP_LEVEL_BLOCK_EVENTS; lifecycle-bridge.ts:150-153 is the sole emitter (`pi.on('session_before_compact', ...)` -> `await options.emit('PreCompact', ...)`) and :28 declares `emit(event, input): Promise<void> | void`. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifiers and confirmed on the default Pi runtime: the two host-side sites that act on a block are `runPiPromptGate` (pi-agent.ts:6430), which is gated by `hookBlockEndsTurn(event)` — false for PreCompact, since ALWAYS_TERMINAL_BLOCK_EVENTS is only UserPromptSubmit/UserPromptExpansion/PostToolBatch — and only iterates PI_PROMPT_GATE_EVENTS; and `toTaskEventDecision` (SessionManager.ts:2195), which serves TaskCreated/TaskCompleted only. There is no compaction consumer anywhere: the projected `block`/`reason` from projectHookDecisionForEvent is produced and dropped, and the emit is fire-and-forget through createPiLifecycleSinkGate (lifecycle-bridge.ts:37-48), so compaction proceeds. CORRECTION A — the claim's 'the two halves of our own contract disagree' is a misreading and should be struck. `kind` in AGENT_EVENT_CONTRACTS_V1 is a permission-receipt axis, defined at lifecycle-bridge.ts:19-21: '`kind`: `decision` for the frozen decision-bearing hooks (PreToolUse receipt/epoch and PermissionRequest); every other hook is `observational` and can never block or bypass a permission receipt.' PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop and ConfigChange are ALL `kind: 'observational'` and ALL in TOP_LEVEL_BLOCK_EVENTS, and TaskCreated/TaskCompleted are `kind: 'decision'` yet deliberately NOT in it (they are exit-code-only). The two tables are orthogonal axes, so there is no internal contradiction — only one missing consumer. CORRECTION B — the finding missed the internal staleness that IS real: hook-decision-contract.ts:236 asserts '`ConfigChange`/`PreCompact` are advisory', which hooks.md now contradicts for BOTH events (:719 'ConfigChange | Yes | Blocks the configuration change from taking effect (except `policy_settings`)' and :730 for PreCompact). CORRECTION C — Pi is not the blocker the R9 plan assumed. pi-agent-core/dist/harness/agent-harness.js `compact()` awaits `emitHook({ type: 'session_before_compact', preparation, branchEntries, customInstructions, signal })` and then `if (hookResult?.cancel) throw new AgentHarnessError('compaction', 'Compaction cancelled')`; `SessionBeforeCompactResult` is `{ cancel?: boolean; compaction?: CompactResult }` (harness/types.d.ts:488-491) and emitHook keeps the last defined handler return. Our handler simply returns nothing, exactly as the `tool_result` handler two blocks above DOES return a value Pi consumes. So the veto primitive exists in-process; the missing piece is an awaited host round trip that maps a block to `{ cancel: true }`, not a new Pi capability. SCOPE CAVEAT — the consequence is false on the Claude backend: automationResultToSdkHookResult (hooks-automation.ts:1673-1681) maps ANY blocking decision, PreCompact included, to `{ continue: false, decision: 'block', reason }` for the Claude Agent SDK, which enforces compaction blocking itself. That backend is off by default (NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE), so the gap is Pi-specific. NOT REFUTED BY A RECORDED DECISION: PreCompact is not among the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries), and it is not a rebrand or a dropped-subscription-flow difference. It IS already logged as an R9 deviation (2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:140 'Parsed then discarded on Pi (one-way ...)'; 2026-07-27-hook-decision-patterns.md:113, :257, :410) — the deviation register is the index of real divergences, so that corroborates the finding rather than refuting it.

column5: Hooks now receive the active effort level via the `effort.level` JSON input field and the `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` environment variable, and Bash tool commands can read $CLAUDE_EFFORT
column6: Hooks receive the session's active effort level, both as an `effort.level` field in the hook JSON input and as a `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` environment variable; Bash tool commands can read the same variable.
column7: `SdkAutomationInput` — the exact object serialised to hook stdin by `hookCommandStdinPayload` — has no `effort` member of any spelling, and the hook env builder emits only NESSY_EVENT/NESSY_EVENT_DATA/NESSY_SESSION_ID/NESSY_SESSION_NAME/NESSY_WORKSPACE_ID plus payload fields. `CLAUDE_EFFORT`/`NESSY_EFFORT` exist ONLY as skill-body substitution placeholders (runtime-skill-content.ts:136), never as a real env var, so neither a hook nor a Bash command can read one.
column9:
Doc sentence verified VERBATIM. curl -sL of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w19.md line 47 (an 'Other wins'
, one sentence, nothing after it that reverses it): 'Hooks now receive the active effort level via the `effort.level` JSON input field and the `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` environment variable, and Bash tool commands can read \$CLAUDE\_EFFORT' — identical modulo the wrapper and Mintlify backslash escapes in the trailing clause. Independently corroborated on the canonical contract page: hooks.md:635 documents `effort` as a common input field, 'Object with a `level` field holding the active effort level for the turn', 'Present for events that fire within a tool-use context, such as `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, and `SubagentStop`', and 'The level is also available to hook commands and the Bash tool as the `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` environment variable.' Repo side verified at the cited lines. `SdkAutomationInput` spans packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:742-902; `sed -n '742,902p' | grep -i effort` returns zero hits, so there is no `effort` member of any spelling in the object `hookCommandStdinPayload` (hook-command.ts:641) serialises — it emits `{...input, hook_event_name, cwd?}` and adds nothing. `buildBaseEventEnv` (utils.ts:392) emits NESSY_EVENT/NESSY_EVENT_DATA/NESSY_SESSION_ID/NESSY_SESSION_NAME/NESSY_WORKSPACE_ID/NESSY_SESSION_METADATA plus snake-cased payload mirrors — no effort key. One citation imprecision that does NOT change the consequence: the env builder that actually feeds a command hook is `buildHookCommandEnv` (hook-command.ts:46-81), not `buildBaseEventEnv`; I read it too and it emits NESSY_EVENT, NESSY_EVENT_DATA, six SAFE_INHERITED_ENV_KEYS (HOME/PATH/SHELL/TMPDIR/TEMP/TMP) and fourteen NESSY_* field mirrors, with no effort variable either. So both hook-relevant builders lack it. `grep -rna` (with -a, for the NUL-byte files) over packages/ and apps/ for CLAUDE_EFFORT|NESSY_EFFORT hits exactly three non-test production lines: capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:136 (the SKILL_VARIABLE_SPELLINGS map, `effort: ['NESSY_EFFORT','CLAUDE_EFFORT']`), a comment at :851, and a comment at agent/base-agent.ts:2192 — all describing skill-BODY text substitution (`expandSkillVariables`), which rewrites `${CLAUDE_EFFORT}` inside markdown and never sets a process env var. Layer up and layer down both checked. Layer down: the Bash tool runs inside the Pi subprocess, whose env is built at agent/pi-agent.ts:1462-1477 as process.env + proxy vars + envOverrides + AWS + NESSY_SESSION_DIR/NESSY_SESSION_ID/NESSY_DEBUG — no effort variable, so a Bash command cannot read $CLAUDE_EFFORT. Layer up: nothing upstream already supplies it; the value plainly EXISTS and is resolvable at dispatch time (agent/thinking-levels.ts:200 `resolveEffortLevel`, `BaseAgent._thinkingLevel`, consumed at base-agent.ts:2635 and pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:292), and the skill path already consumes exactly this value — so this is an unwired plumbing gap, not a false consequence. Sibling-subsystem check: the identically-spelled `CLAUDE_EFFORT` in runtime-skill-content.ts is the SKILLS subsystem (skills.md:299 `${CLAUDE_EFFORT}` body substitution), a different surface from hooks/Bash; the finding names the right subsystem and explicitly disclaims the skills one. Not an owner decision: inert-worklist.md section 3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions — none touches hook effort. The nearest recorded deviations, in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-effort-precedence.md:177/188/193/197, cover model-config.md's CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL precedence tier and other model-config keys, NOT the hook `effort.level` input field or $CLAUDE_EFFORT on the hook/Bash surfaces. Not a deliberate product difference either: the fork implements effort levels end to end and already ships the Nessy-aliased `${NESSY_EFFORT}`/`${CLAUDE_EFFORT}` skill variable, so this is the same variable simply absent from two other surfaces, not a dropped subscription flow or a rebrand artefact. Only caveat, not load-bearing: under the off-by-default Claude backend the Anthropic Agent SDK may supply its own $CLAUDE_EFFORT to SDK-internal hooks; Nessy's own automations pipeline on the shipped Pi default does not.

column5: Subprocesses such as Bash, hooks, MCP, and LSP no longer inherit OTEL_* environment variables, so OTEL-instrumented apps run via the Bash tool no longer pick up the CLI's own OTLP endpoint
column6: Bash, hook, MCP and LSP subprocesses no longer inherit OTEL_* environment variables from the host process.
column7: Every subprocess inherits the host env wholesale. MCP stdio filters only a fixed 12-entry credential blocklist that contains no OTEL_ key; the Pi subprocess (which hosts the Bash tool) spawns with `...process.env`; the hook runner env is built from the full `process.env`. `grep -ran -a "OTEL_" packages apps` finds no scrubbing site at all — only settings/telemetry readers.
column9: The quote is real but the CLAIMED OUR STATE is false for three of the four subprocess classes the doc names, and for the majority of the fourth. (1) QUOTE: `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w19.md` carries it in the `digest-wins-grid`, as `Subprocesses such as Bash, hooks, MCP, and LSP no longer inherit OTEL\_\* environment variables, so OTEL-instrumented apps run via the Bash tool no longer pick up the CLI's own OTLP endpoint`. One sentence, whole div read, nothing reverses it. (2) THE ABSENCE CLAIM IS TRUE BUT IRRELEVANT: `grep -ran -a -i OTEL packages apps scripts` (non-dist, non-test) really does find no scrub site -- because this fork does not scrub OTEL_* by DENYLIST, it ALLOWLISTS host env per subprocess, which is strictly stronger. (3) BASH: `packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1577` runs shell commands through `requestSupervisedProcess`, which round-trips to the host `handleProcessStartRequest` (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:5138`). That rebuilds the request through `pickSupervisedChildStartFields`, and `SupervisedProcessChildStartRequest` (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/process-supervisor-port.ts:105-113`) OMITS `environmentProfile`, `inheritHostEnv` and `env` -- a child provably cannot set them. So `resolveEnvironmentProfile` (`packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:716-724`) returns `restricted`, and `hostEnvironment` (:726-732) filters `process.env` down to `RESTRICTED_HOST_ENVIRONMENT` (:703-710) -- 26 keys plus `LC_*`, no OTEL_ key. The Bash tool inherits NO OTEL_* variable. `process-supervisor.test.ts:228-260` is the live control for exactly this filter. (4) HOOKS: the supervised plugin-hook path passes `environmentProfile: 'explicit'` (`packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4489`), and `hostEnvironment('explicit')` returns `{}` -- zero host inheritance. The direct path `runHookCommand` builds env via `buildHookCommandEnv` (`packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:46-59`), which reads only `SAFE_INHERITED_ENV_KEYS = ['HOME','PATH','SHELL','TMPDIR','TEMP','TMP']` (:34). No OTEL_*. (5) THE CITED HOOK EVIDENCE IS A SIBLING SUBSYSTEM: `packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:380` is `cleanEnv()`, the AUTOMATIONS env builder, not the hook runner. Its only two consumers never become a subprocess environment -- `buildEnvFromSdkInput` feeds webhook URL/header/body template substitution (`automation-system.ts:751`, comment: 'Webhook-safe env'), and `buildEnvFromPayload` feeds `${VAR}` expansion in prompt text (`handlers/prompt-handler.ts:86`). Identifier and consequence both fail. (6) LSP: `LspService.start` (`packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/lsp-service.ts:112-130`) calls `processPort.start` with no `environmentProfile`, so it also lands on `restricted`. No OTEL_*. (7) MCP: plugin stdio servers go through `SupervisedStdioClientTransport` with `environmentProfile: 'explicit'` and `env: { ...getDefaultEnvironment(), ... }` (`packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:739-749`); `getDefaultEnvironment()` is a 6-key POSIX allowlist (HOME, LOGNAME, PATH, SHELL, TERM, USER). No OTEL_*. Also cite-accurate correction: `BLOCKED_ENV_VARS` (`client.ts:197-212`) has 11 entries, not 12. (8) RESIDUAL: only NATIVE/PROJECT (user-configured, non-plugin) stdio MCP servers still inherit `process.env` minus that credential denylist (`client.ts:383-390`), and the Pi agent subprocess itself spawns with `...process.env` (`pi-agent.ts:1465`) -- but Pi is the agent-runtime host, the analogue of the Claude Code CLI process, not one of the four tool subprocess classes, and its Bash tool does not spawn from Pi's env. The scenario is live, not hypothetical: this fork DOES ship OTLP exporters keyed on ambient `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` (`packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/otlp-telemetry.ts:198-226`, `packages/shared/src/telemetry/usage-metrics.ts:332-362`, wired at `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:272-273`) -- which incidentally makes neighbouring row f069's 'there is no telemetry emitter' stale. Not an owner decision in `2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` section 3 (checked: none of the nine concerns subprocess env), and not a de-brand/product difference.

column5: Agent tool subagent_type now matches case- and separator-insensitively, so "Code Reviewer" resolves to code-reviewer
column6: The Agent tool's `subagent_type` resolves case-insensitively AND separator-insensitively, so "Code Reviewer" reaches the agent named code-reviewer.
column7: `resolveAgentDefinition` normalises with `normalizeName` = `name.trim().toLowerCase()` only. No separator folding: spaces and underscores are not collapsed to hyphens, so "Code Reviewer" normalises to "code reviewer", misses both the name match and the author-declared alias list, and throws `Unknown agent "Code Reviewer"`. This is the same class as the Task→Agent rename that broke every turn.
column9:
All three legs check out, and the consequence was MEASURED with a positive control. 1. DOC — VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w20.md` -> 6878 bytes, 95 lines. The claim is line 91, the last cell of the `digest-wins-grid`, in full: `
Agent tool subagent\_type now matches case- and separator-insensitively, so "Code Reviewer" resolves to code-reviewer
`. Modulo Mintlify's `` wrappers and the `\_` escape, the quoted sentence is exact. It is a one-sentence line — there is no second clause reversing it, and no version gate or research-preview pill on this row (the pills sit on the three feature blocks above, not on `Other wins`). The page is row 182 of `scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv`, so it is a Claude Code contract source, not a Codex/MCP page. 2. FILE — AS CITED. `packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:281-283` is exactly `function normalizeName(name: string): string { return name.trim().toLowerCase(); }` — trim and lowercase, no separator folding. `:718-731` is `resolveAgentDefinition`: `const normalized = normalizeName(name)`, fork short-circuit, then `defs.find(def => def.name === normalized) ?? defs.find(def => def.aliases?.includes(normalized))`, then `throw new Error(`Unknown agent "${name}". Available agents: …`)` at :728. `normalizeName` is the ONLY normalizer in the file (all 6 call sites: :235, :441, :688, :690, :699, :719), and the stored `name` is itself only trim+lowercased at load (:441), so nothing slugifies either side of the comparison. Author-declared aliases (:698-701) are passed through the same `normalizeName`, so they do not fold separators either. 3. CONSEQUENCE — MEASURED TRUE, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. Ran `resolveAgentDefinition` against a runtime definition named `code-reviewer` (bun, real module, no mocks): "code-reviewer" => OK code-reviewer "CODE-REVIEWER" => OK code-reviewer <- CONTROL: case-insensitivity really is live on this rig " Code-Reviewer " => OK code-reviewer <- CONTROL: trim really is live "Code Reviewer" => THROW Unknown agent "Code Reviewer". Available agents: scout, planner, worker, reviewer, code-re… "code_reviewer" => THROW Unknown agent "code_reviewer". … The doc's own example is the failing case. Because the two controls pass on the same rig, the absence is a real absence and not a broken harness. LAYER UP — nothing upstream folds separators. `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts` takes the model's string raw: `asTask` (:101-110) only type-checks `typeof value.agent !== 'string'`, `normalizeSubagentRequest` (:122) never touches the value, and :512 passes `taskInput.agent` straight into `resolveAgentDefinition`. The JSON schema at :382/:419/:432 is a bare `agent: { type: 'string' }` — no `enum` of live agent names that would keep the model on canonical spellings. `orchestrator/agent-defs.ts` is a 10-line re-export, not a second resolver. `prerequisite-manager.ts:450` (the skill agent ceiling) reads both `agent` and `subagent_type` and applies `.trim().toLowerCase()` — the same case-only fold, so the sibling path has the identical gap rather than compensating for it. LAYER DOWN — the separator-insensitive normalizer this repo already owns is in a SIBLING subsystem and is not shared: `packages/shared/src/agent/mode-types.ts:242`, `parsePermissionMode`, does `mode.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[-_ ]/g, '')` and its doc comment at :238 literally says "case- and separator-insensitively". So the pattern, the regex and the vocabulary exist here for permission modes and were simply never applied to agent names. Naming the subsystem: this is `packages/shared/src/agents` (agent-name resolution), not `agent/mode-types` (permission modes). NOT A RECORDED DECISION. Read all nine dated owner decisions in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries) — none touches agent-name matching. `grep -a` over `docs/superpowers/plans` and `specs` for `normalizeName`/slugify finds only the sibling verdict f220's own sweep rows and f088, whose measured verdict independently confirms `normalizeName` is trim+lowercase only. Not a rebrand either: the tool being spelled `subagent`/`agent` here instead of `Agent`/`subagent_type` is a rename, but the behaviour under test (tolerant matching of a requested agent type) is orthogonal to the spelling, and the fork already implements the case half of the same rule. SEVERITY CORRECTION, which is why the finding's own framing overshoots: this is NOT "the same class as the Task->Agent rename that broke every turn". The throw is not fatal — it surfaces as a failed tool result whose message enumerates the available agents (`Available agents: scout, planner, worker, reviewer, …`), so the model can retry with a canonical spelling on the next tool call. It is a one-round-trip robustness gap on a free-form string field, not a turn-killer.

NOT an owner decision: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions -- none touch the project-dir env. column7: `shouldEnableFastMode` returns true for exactly one literal — `model === 'claude-opus-4-7'`. A session on `claude-opus-4-8` (which IS in our model table and IS the current default upstream) never gets the fast-mode beta header, so the fast toggle is silently inert on the model fast mode now defaults to. Stale pin, not a policy decision — the comment still reads "Only activates for Opus 4.7".
column9: Sentence verified verbatim at whats-new/2026-w22.md:89 (the raw MDX escapes the dollars as \$10/\$50 and \$30/\$150; wording is otherwise identical, and the line is a self-contained three-sentence lede that does not reverse itself). The identifier half of the finding is also correct: unified-network-interceptor.ts:496-499 is exactly `if (!FEATURE_FLAGS.fastMode) return false; return typeof model === 'string' && model === 'claude-opus-4-7';`, and the doc comment at :493-494 still says 'Only activates for Opus 4.7'. The CONSEQUENCE is false, which is inert-worklist shape 3 (enforcement one layer up) plus shape 4 (wrong subsystem named). (1) Line :497 short-circuits on FEATURE_FLAGS.fastMode, which is a hardcoded `fastMode: false` literal in feature-flags.ts:182 — the ONLY non-getter in that object; every sibling flag (developerFeedback, embeddedServer, codexRuntime) is a getter reading a NESSY_FEATURE_* env override, and fastMode has none. `grep -rna FAST_MODE|FASTMODE` over packages/apps/scripts/docs returns only FAST_MODE_BETA, the beta string itself. So shouldEnableFastMode returns false for EVERY model, Opus 4.7 included; the model literal at :498 is unreachable, not a live discriminator that works on 4.7 and misses 4.8. (2) There is no 'fast toggle' to be silently inert: no /fast command, no setting, no IPC, no i18n key (the only 'fast' hits in en.json are the Guardian fast-model rows). /fast is a Claude Code CLI slash command; this fork drives the Claude Agent SDK, and NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE defaults off. (3) Even with the flag flipped, the Anthropic adapter's fast-mode branch (:991-999) can never fire for a Claude session: the interceptor's only consumer is agent/backend/internal/drivers/pi.ts:290 via resolveInterceptorBundlePath, i.e. it Bun --preloads into the Pi subprocess (and the headless server's own process) only. packages/shared/AGENTS.md records this as a decision with a reason: 'The Claude SDK no longer runs under Bun (since 0.2.113 it spawns a per-platform native `claude` binary), so --preload is not available there. Features that used to live in the interceptor for Claude (rich tool intent, fast-mode override, MalformedBodyError validation, etc.) are Phase-2 work.' (4) 'Stale pin, not a policy decision' is therefore wrong on the record: both the hardcoded-off flag and the 4-7 literal date from the same baseline commit 845cf0a4 (2026-07-05), and no fast-mode UI has ever existed. Not one of the nine §3 owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md (no 'fast' hit in that file), but the Phase-2 deferral in packages/shared/AGENTS.md is an equivalent recorded decision. Incidental confirmation: claude-opus-4-8 IS a real MODEL_REGISTRY entry (config/models.ts:133) and claude-opus-4-6 remaps forward to it (:62), so the model-table half of the claim holds — it is only the fast-mode consequence that does not.

column5: New /reload-skills command re-scans skill directories without restarting, and SessionStart hooks can return reloadSkills: true to make skills they install available in the same session
column6: A SessionStart hook can return `reloadSkills: true` to make skills it installed available in the same session, and `/reload-skills` re-scans skill directories without a restart.
column7: `reloadSkills` has zero occurrences in any .ts/.tsx in the repo (grep -ran -a, node_modules excluded) — the only hit anywhere is a docs file listing it as an open R9 item. The hook output parser reads `additionalContext`, `updatedInput`, `updatedToolOutput`, `worktreePath`, `retry`, elicitation `action`/`content` and the universal five, and ignores anything else, so a SessionStart hook that installs a skill cannot surface it this session.
column9:
The quote is verbatim and the identifier absence is real, but the stated CONSEQUENCE is false, and the consequence is what the finding asserts. This is the exact recurring shape AGENTS.md warns about: the identifier is genuinely unwired while something upstream already produces the documented effect. (1) QUOTE — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. curl -sL of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w22.md, line 106, inside the 'Other wins' digest grid: '
New /reload-skills command re-scans skill directories without restarting, and SessionStart hooks can return reloadSkills: true to make skills they install available in the same session
'. Read the whole line and both neighbours (`plugin init` scaffolding above, skill/command `disallowed-tools` below) — nothing reverses it. (2) IDENTIFIER — CONFIRMED. `grep -ran 'reloadSkills' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'` (with -a, node_modules excluded) → 0. `grep -ran 'reload-skills'` over packages/ apps/ → 0. The only repo hits are this sweep's own docs/JSON. packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:313-407 (`parseHookCommandOutput`) extracts exactly permissionDecision/permissionDecisionReason, the PermissionRequest `decision` band (behavior/interrupt/updatedPermissions/updatedInput/message), reason, additionalContext, updatedInput, retry, worktreePath, updatedToolOutput and elicitation action/content; `parseUniversalHookOutput` (:443-454) adds continue/stopReason/suppressOutput/systemMessage/terminalSequence. No `reloadSkills`, and `parseHookOutputForEvent` (:464) has no unknown-field passthrough. The cited file:line says what was claimed. (3) CONSEQUENCE — REFUTED BY EXECUTION. The claim 'a SessionStart hook that installs a skill cannot surface it this session' is wrong, because Nessy never caches the agent's skill list for the session the way Claude Code does — so there is nothing for `reloadSkills` to reload. - The skill inventory that feeds the agent is rebuilt FROM DISK ON EVERY TURN. `SessionManager.withCapabilityRuntime` (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:5881) calls `createCapabilityTurn` (:3983) per turn, which calls `resolver.resolve(context)` (:4045); that runs `buildCapabilityResolutionInputsV2` (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:624, inventory built at :635) → `buildNativeCapabilityInventory` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:880) → `skillRecords` (:266), which does a bare `existsSync`/`readdirSync` over every skill root (~/.agents/skills :903, /skills :904, workspace skills/ :949, project .nessy-agent/skills :1016 and .agents/skills :1065). No memo, no TTL on that path. - POSITIVE CONTROL (the finding is an absence claim, so it needs one). Ran `buildNativeCapabilityInventory` twice in one process against a temp workspace, writing skills/hook-installed/SKILL.md between the calls — i.e. simulating a hook installing a skill after the turn's snapshot was taken. Result: BEFORE ['find-skills','officecli'], AFTER ['find-skills','officecli','hook-installed']. 1 pass, 2 expect() calls. The control half (absent before) fired, so the observation is not a vacuous pass. - Nessy ALSO has the disk watcher Claude's /reload-skills exists to replace. packages/shared/src/config/watcher.ts watches `/workspaces/{id}/skills/{slug}/SKILL.md` recursively (header :15, routing :504-520); `handleSkillsDirChange` (:772) calls `emitWorkspaceInvalidation('skill')` (:775 → `emitNativeSourceInvalidation` :263) and `invalidateSkillsCache()` + `loadAllSkills()` (:824-826). storage-runtime.ts:347 turns that bus event into `capabilityResolver.invalidate(..., 'refresh-before-next-turn')`. So a skill dropped on disk mid-session is picked up automatically, with no restart and no command. SUBSYSTEM CHECK. The finding cites the right subsystem — packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts is the LIVE parser, not the unreachable `plugins/hooks-runtime.ts` executor that is owner-decision §3 item 5. No mis-naming there. NOT AN OWNER DECISION, NOT A BRAND DIFFERENCE. None of the nine dated decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 covers reloadSkills (they are SEATBELT wildcard, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions). It is also unrelated to the dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows, the corporate gateway, or the NESSY_ rename. The finding is refuted on its consequence alone.

Down: the sibling exporter is the same shape -- packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/otlp-telemetry.ts:309 also hardcodes resource attributes to service.name='nessy-desktop'. No renamed NESSY_ equivalent exists (grep of NESSY_[A-Z_]* over all src: only NESSY_ENABLE_TELEMETRY is telemetry-related; NESSY_RESOURCES* are app-bundle paths). grep -ran -a over packages/ and apps/ confirms zero source hits; the only hits in the tree are inside vendored third-party binaries (apps/electron/resources/bin/codex/*/codex-app-server and the bundled OTel JS SDK in packages/pi-agent-server/dist), i.e. runtimes whose own OTel SDK would honour the variable, never our metrics path. So the claimed state is factually accurate. WHY IT IS STILL REFUTED: this exact variable is named in a recorded deviation with a reason, so it is a decision, not a gap. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-observability-and-cost.md:182 carries the category string 'documented, not implemented -- monitoring-usage.md:446 to :455 define the standard attribute set every metric shares: session.id, app.version, app.entrypoint, organization.id, user.account_uuid, user.account_id, user.id, user.email, terminal.type, and OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES passthrough, each with its own OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_* toggle. Ours carries none of them, and that is a decision rather than an omission: this is a bank fork ... A future operator who wants it should get the toggles, not a default', harvested into the generated register at 2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:210. I verified the row is the right one: monitoring-usage.md:455 is literally 'Keys from OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES | Custom attributes you set, such as department or team.id' with toggle OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES (default true), and :138 is the same toggle in the cardinality table -- the w23 'other win' is the release note for that row, not a new contract. The decision is also restated in shipped source at usage-metrics.ts:31-39: 'This fork exports NEITHER, nor any other row of that table: data points carry exactly backend, model, type, cost_reporting ... Any widening toward :442's table is a privacy decision to be made on purpose, not an omission to be patched.' It is additionally a duplicate of the residue already recorded in the sibling verdict data/phase2-verdicts/f069.json ('OTEL_SERVICE_NAME and OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES are not read; service.name is hardcoded nessy-desktop'). Not an inert-worklist section 3 row (I read all nine; none is telemetry). Honest caveat, so the refutation is not overstated: the recorded reason is a privacy argument that fits the identity rows (user.id, user.email, session.id) more squarely than the operator-set passthrough, which carries no user identity by default. column5: fallbackModel configures up to three fallback models tried in order when the primary is overloaded or unavailable, and --fallback-model now applies to interactive sessions too
column6: `fallbackModel` holds an ordered list of up to three models, each tried in turn when the primary is overloaded or unavailable.
column7: `fallbackModel` is a single string in both the schema (`z.string()`) and the default (`''`), and the runtime does exactly one hop: `getRetryFallbackModel` returns that one id, `setModel`s to it, and retries once with `fallbackModelRetry: true` — a second failure has nowhere to go. There is no `fallbackModels` array anywhere in the repo.
column9:
All three checks pass, so the finding survives. STEP 1 (verbatim): curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w24.md puts the sentence on line 69, the whole line being one
in the 'Other wins' grid: 'fallbackModel configures up to three fallback models tried in order when the primary is overloaded or unavailable, and `--fallback-model` now applies to interactive sessions too'. Nothing else on the line; no second sentence reverses it. The linked section corroborates rather than softens it -- model-config.md:365 'Configure one or more fallback models and Claude Code tries them in order ... Chains are capped at three models after duplicate removal, and extra entries are ignored', :373 'set `fallbackModel` in settings as an array', :381 'The `--fallback-model` flag takes precedence ... `"default"` expands to the default model.' STEP 2 (cited lines): validators.ts:135 is exactly `fallbackModel: z.string()`. storage.ts:189 has drifted -- the default `fallbackModel: ''` is at :194 (FALLBACK_CONFIG_DEFAULTS.workspaceDefaults), with the load-time coercion at :273-276; the shipped apps/electron/resources/config-defaults.json:28 is `"fallbackModel": ""` too, and config-defaults-schema.ts types it `fallbackModel: string` with the docstring 'Pi model ID to retry once after model/network drain errors. Empty disables fallback.' pi-agent.ts:6291-:6320 also drifted by ~22 lines (6291 is inside the requestSubtaskFork docblock) but the range does reach the cited function: `getRetryFallbackModel` is :6313-6324 and `retryWithFallbackModel` :6326-6344, and both say what was claimed. STEP 3 (consequence, tested separately from the identifier): the one-hop cap is real, not merely an unwired identifier. `getRetryFallbackModel` bails at :6314 on `options?.fallbackModelRetry`, and `retryWithFallbackModel` re-enters `chatImpl` with `fallbackModelRetry: true` (:6342) after `setModel(fallbackModel)` (:6335) -- so the second failure returns null and falls through to `emitStopFailureHookOnce` + `typed_error` at both call sites (:6755-6761 in the event loop, :6795-6801 in the catch). Even a fresh outer retry cannot get a second hop, because :6319 also returns null once `fallbackModel === this.getModel()`. The repo's own test is literally named 'retries once with the configured fallback model for a typed drain error' (pi-agent-fallback-model.test.ts:85). No upstream or downstream layer supplies the missing hops: `normalizePiFallbackModelId` (models-pi.ts:20-22) is `typeof x === 'string' ? x.trim() : ''` with no comma split, `grep -a` for `fallbackModels` returns zero source hits (only the sweep's own JSON), and greps for modelChain/failover/tryNextModel/fallbackChain across shared, server-core and pi-agent-server return nothing. Sibling-subsystem check: this is the only fallbackModel in the repo -- packages/server, packages/server-core, packages/ui, apps/electron/src and packages/pi-agent-server have no reference at all, and apps/cli has no `--fallback-model` flag, so the sentence's second clause diverges as well. Not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3 (none concerns fallback), and not a de-brand or subscription-drop difference -- a model chain on overload is orthogonal to dropping Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows. It IS already a recorded deviation (deviation-register.md:110, 'not implemented -- model-config.md:361 configures an ordered chain ... Neither exists'), whose tail 'read by nothing' is now stale: pi-agent.ts:6257 reads it. NOTE on f106: the same underlying gap on the model-config page was refuted, but on grounds specific to that claim's wording -- it asserted an array 'fails validation' (false: ConfigDefaultsSchema is test-only) and framed the key as Claude's settings.json. f226 asserts neither, and f106's own correctedState calls the arity gap 'Real'.

column5: New sandbox.allowAppleEvents opt-in setting lets sandboxed commands send Apple Events on macOS
column6: A `sandbox.allowAppleEvents` opt-in setting lets sandboxed commands send Apple Events on macOS.
column7: No occurrence of `allowAppleEvents` (or `AppleEvent` at all) anywhere in the repo. `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS` is a closed seven-entry list — excludedCommands, deniedReadRoots, deniedWriteRoots, additionalWritableRoots, allowUnsandboxedCommands, network, filesystem — and unknown keys are rejected/stripped, so an admin or user who writes the documented key gets a validation drop rather than the opt-in. We do ship the macOS sandbox this governs.
column9: The quote is verbatim (w25.md:79, a one-sentence <div>, nothing after it reverses it) and the identifier half is correct, but the finding fails on its own evidence and on its consequence, and its true residue is already adjudicated.  1. THE STATED EVIDENCE IS FALSE. 'grep -ran -a "AppleEvent" . -> 0' does not reproduce. `allowAppleEvents` occurs four times on disk, in bundles the app ships: packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js:350289, apps/electron/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js:350289, apps/electron/dist/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js:350289 and apps/electron/resources/session-mcp-server/index.js:176630. It is the vendored Pi SDK's own sandbox zod schema, carrying the full describe(): 'macOS only: Allow sandboxed commands to send Apple Events (and look up the appleeventsd Mach service) ... Removes code-execution isolation ... Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (--settings) settings ... Default: false'. They are untracked build artifacts, so 'absent from first-party tracked source' survives; 'no occurrence anywhere in the repo' does not.  2. THE CONSEQUENCE NAMES THE WRONG SANDBOX. Claude's setting governs sandboxed *commands*, i.e. Bash. Nessy has two macOS profiles and the finding conflates them.    - The Bash-tool seatbelt (packages/shared/src/agent/core/bash-seatbelt.ts) is what the doc line is about. It is OFF BY DEFAULT (`getMacosSeatbeltBashSandboxEnabled`, storage.ts:1124, `?? false`), and when a user turns it on `buildMacosBashSeatbeltProfile` returns `(version 1) (allow default)` because `SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD = true` (bash-seatbelt.ts:88, owner decision 2026-07-21, REAFFIRMED 2026-07-29 — inert-worklist section 3 item 1). So a sandboxed Bash command in Nessy can already send Apple Events today; the documented opt-in would be a no-op on that path, and the -600 symptom it exists to relieve does not arise.    - The profile that does deny them is `buildDarwinSandboxProfile` (session-tools-core/src/runtime/filesystem-isolation.ts:128) — `(deny default)` plus a filtered `machLookupRule`, governing supervised processes and `script_sandbox`, not the model's Bash tool.  3. THE NON-GRANT IS DELIBERATE, PROBE-BACKED AND RECORDED. mach-services.ts:27-35 withholds the LaunchServices names (`com.apple.CoreServices.coreservicesd`, `com.apple.lsd.mapdb`, `com.apple.lsd.modifydb`) and `com.apple.pasteboard.1` because `sandbox-exec -p '<profile>' /usr/bin/pbpaste` returned 0 — a sandboxed command read the pasteboard and could `open` an app outside the sandbox. That is precisely the hazard the Pi describe() names ('sandboxed commands can launch other applications unsandboxed with no user prompt'). Recorded in plan 2026-07-30-sandbox-mach-and-protected-paths.md and deviation-register.md:430-435.  4. THE DOC'S OWN ALTERNATIVE IS IMPLEMENTED. `excludedCommands` is the first accepted key and is enforced end to end (SessionManager.ts:3579 -> process-supervisor.ts:476 -> downgrade receipt :211 + risky-band prompt), so `open`/`osascript` can be run outside the sandbox.  5. DUPLICATE OF AN ADJUDICATED ROW. f035 covers the same key and its verdict (docs/superpowers/specs/data/phase2-verdicts/f035.json) already dropped it from `gap` to 'at most a narrow documented, not implemented note on allowAppleEvents ... with the security rationale attached'.  Minor: the cited range is off — SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS is sandbox-settings.ts:172-180; :182-183 are SANDBOX_NETWORK_KEYS and SANDBOX_FILESYSTEM_KEYS. The rejection mechanism is right: `assertKnownKeys` (:216-221) throws on any other key, and the tolerant managed sink drops it as 'tightened'.

column5: To keep the earlier behavior, where the output is added to context without a response, set respondToBashCommands to false in settings.json.
column6: Output from a `!`-prefixed command now gets a model response by default; `respondToBashCommands: false` in settings.json restores the old context-only behavior.
column7: We ship `!` shell mode in the composer, and it is stuck on the pre-change behavior: `runShellCommand` spawns the command, records the result and returns — it never queues a turn — and `respondToBashCommands` has zero occurrences in the repo, so there is neither the new default nor the escape hatch.
column9:
All three checks positively confirm the finding. (1) DOC — curl -sL of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w26.md returns a 4471-byte page; the quoted sentence exists verbatim on line 37 (inside the

of the feature block titled 'Shell mode responds to command output', v2.1.186). With the inline markup stripped the sentence is character-for-character the claimed quote: 'To keep the earlier behavior, where the output is added to context without a response, set respondToBashCommands to false in settings.json.' Reading the WHOLE line: it is a three-sentence lede and neither of the other two reverses the conclusion — 'Commands you run with the ! prefix now get a response from Claude once the output lands in the transcript, so you can run ! npm test and get an explanation of the failures without a second prompt.' establishes the new default, and 'The response costs the same as sending a normal prompt.' is a cost note. The feature links to /docs/en/interactive-mode#shell-mode-with-prefix. (2) CITED FILES — apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/FreeFormInput.tsx:1399-1416 says exactly what was claimed: inside submitMessage, `if (trimmedInput.startsWith('!')) { const command = trimmedInput.slice(1).trim(); if (!command || !sessionId || !runShellCommand) return false; setIsShellCommandRunning(true); void runShellCommand(sessionId, command).then(...clearSubmittedDraft...).catch(...).finally(...); return true }` — it returns before ever reaching the onSubmit(...) calls that queue a turn (the customSlashCommand branch at :1419 and the normal path below it). packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:16372 is `async runShellCommand(sessionId, rawCommand, workspaceId?): Promise`, and its body (16372-16495) does exactly what was claimed: permission/mode gates, executeDirectShellCommand, then push a role:'user' message whose content is formatDirectShellTranscript(...) with a '!' command badge, persistSession + flushSession, sendEvent({type:'user_message', status:'accepted'}), and return the result. No turn is started, managed.isProcessing is never set, and no agent invocation follows. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier. One layer up: the renderer's only owner of this path, ChatDisplay.tsx:1242-1255 handleRunShellCommand, just RPCs `{type:'runShellCommand'}` and toasts on !executed — it does not follow with a prompt. One layer down: packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:566-567 is a straight pass-through, and the contract test packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.shell-command.test.ts:148-180 ('appends executed shell output as a command-badged user message') PINS the pre-change behaviour — it asserts exactly one message, role user, persisted, flushed, one user_message event, and nothing else. So the output genuinely IS added to context without a response: our state is precisely the 'earlier behavior' the doc sentence describes. Absence check with -a: `grep -rna -a respondToBashCommands . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=docs` and `git grep -In -a respondToBashCommands -- . ':!docs'` both return zero; the only hits anywhere are the sweep's own docs/specs rows. Searched for the false-positive shapes and found neither: no differently-named equivalent (respondToShell|bashModeRespond|shellModeRespond|respondToCommand|autoRespond → 0 across apps, packages, docs-site) and no sibling subsystem owning it (no shell-respond key in packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts; the only shell-related config key there is useAutoModeDuringPlan). NOT one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 — those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions. §3 item 3 is autoMode.classifyAllShell, a DIFFERENT key that happens to appear in this same page's 'Other wins' list; do not conflate them. Nor is it in §4's false positives. No plan or doc in docs/ mentions runShellCommand or the composer '!' mode at all, so no decision to keep the old behaviour is recorded anywhere. NOT a deliberate product difference either — it is unrelated to the dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows, to the corporate-gateway targeting, and to the NESSY_/@nessy-agent/ renaming. Note the repo's coverage map grades this page 🟩 at 2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:292 on the strength of the 2026-07-29 weekly-changelog pass, but that pass filtered only for renames/new component types and its findings file (2026-07-29-weekly-changelog-findings.md) contains no w26 shell-mode row — this changed default slipped through that filter, so the green verdict is not evidence against the finding.

column5: New sandbox.credentials setting blocks sandboxed commands from reading credential files and secret environment variables
column6: A `sandbox.credentials` setting blocks sandboxed commands from reading credential files and secret environment variables, with `files` and `envVars` sub-keys.
column7: `credentials` is not a member of `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS`, so the key is stripped as unknown. The name appears in this repo only as a shape ANALOGY in two comments ("an individual invalid entry in `files` or `envVars` is stripped… a wholly invalid `credentials` value is dropped") borrowed to describe tolerant parsing of `sandbox.network` and of the permission DSL — the setting itself has no reader and no enforcement.
column9:
REFUTED on four independent grounds. The quote is real and the two cited lines say what was claimed, but the row is a duplicate of an already-adjudicated finding, it is a dated parked owner decision, its stated mechanism is factually wrong, and BOTH halves of the claimed exposure are already delivered one layer up. 1) QUOTE — CONFIRMED VERBATIM, and the whole line carries no reversing second half. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w26.md` line 53 is a single-item grid cell in the 'Other wins' section: `
New sandbox.credentials setting blocks sandboxed commands from reading credential files and secret environment variables
`. Stripping the `` markup gives the claimed sentence character-for-character. One sentence, no qualifier. The `files`/`envVars` sub-key claim is independently supported by settings.md:421-:424 (`credentials.files`, `credentials.envVars`, `credentials.envVars[].injectHosts`, `credentials.allowPlaintextInject`). No refutation here. 2) CITED FILE:LINE — accurate on the letter, wrong on the reading. packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:172-180 is exactly `['excludedCommands','deniedReadRoots','deniedWriteRoots','additionalWritableRoots','allowUnsandboxedCommands','network','filesystem']` — no `credentials`. `grep -ran credentials` on that file (NUL-safe) returns only :321 and :324. But the claim that the name appears 'only as a shape ANALOGY … borrowed' framed as a defect inverts what the comments do: :318-327 says '`settings.md:200`\'s `sandbox.credentials` row applied to the sub-block we actually have', a deliberate, argued borrow of the doc's ONLY published nested-block tolerance rule, quoted in full with its reason ('Returning `undefined` for a wholly invalid `network` is what makes the rest of `sandbox` still apply'). managed-policy.ts:1164 states it outright: 'Shaped like `settings.md:200`\'s `sandbox.credentials` row, which is the doc's only nested-document case'. And settings.md:200 really is that row, verbatim. Citing the one published precedent for a tolerance shape is not evidence of a gap. 2b) THE CLAIMED MECHANISM IS WRONG. 'the key is stripped as unknown' is false on the strict path. Ran the real parser: `parseManagedSandboxSettingsV1({credentials:{files:[…],envVars:[…]}})` → `THREW: invalid sandbox setting: credentials` (assertKnownKeys, :216-221). Positive control on the same rig: `parseManagedSandboxSettingsV1({deniedReadRoots:['/Users/x/.aws']})` → parses clean, so the throw is about the key name, not a broken probe. Stripping happens only on the tolerant managed-delivery path. A row whose mechanism is wrong cannot be dispatched as written. 3) OWNER DECISION — this is parity row R19, PARKED. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:690: row R19, status ⏸, scope 'Egress proxy and domain policy: … `mask` mode for named env vars', marked 'PARKED by owner decision 2026-07-28 — «нужно всё разрешить, ограничения будут потом»', with the plan deliberately retained at docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-egress-proxy.md (:15 'there is no mask/deny path for `credentials.envVars` today — Task 4 adds `deny` there'; :31 lands the documented `mask`-without-`tlsTerminate` failure). docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:218 carries 'R19 — `credentials.envVars` `mask` … Half-shipped, then parked by owner decision — so nothing is live'. Audit :478 records an earlier finder hitting this same row and being told it belonged to R19. Not one of inert-worklist §3's nine (those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions), but an equivalent dated owner decision recorded in three places. 4) CONSEQUENCE REFUTED UPSTREAM ON BOTH HALVES (trap shape #3 — the identifier is unwired, the consequence is false). The doc sentence names two protections; this fork ships both unconditionally, by other names, and is STRICTER than a default Claude install on each. (a) CREDENTIAL FILES. `credentialDenyRoots` (packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/credential-deny-roots.ts:96) is a host-seeded, unremovable floor covering the doc's own two examples (~/.ssh, ~/.aws) plus ~/.nessy, ~/.netrc, ~/._netrc, ~/.docker, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.config/git/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.pypirc, ~/.kube, ~/.gnupg, ~/.config/gh, ~/.config/gcloud, ~/.azure, ~/Library/Keychains, the per-vendor browser cookie/login stores and the Windows DPAPI trio. It is seeded into `deniedReadRoots` at packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/host-sandbox-settings.ts:61 and independently at packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/script-sandbox.ts:83, composed into the isolation funnel as `unconditionalDeniedReadRoots` (filesystem-isolation.ts:136-184), and passed as `credentialFloor` at bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:225 so /doctor and the funnel agree. sandbox-settings.ts:708-716 makes a user `filesystem.allowRead` unable to re-open a floor path, and :798-815 RETAINS the floor even when `filesystem.disabled` turns the layer off, with the reason written in-line ('so releasing it here would let one boolean in a user file hand over ~/.ssh, ~/.aws and the gateway token under ~/.nessy'). Claude documents the opposite default at sandboxing.md:271 — 'There is no built-in credential deny list, so only the files and variables you list are restricted' — which credential-deny-roots.ts:20-22 quotes as its rationale. (b) SECRET ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES. This half was NOT covered by the earlier sibling verdict and I verified it directly. Supervised processes get their host env through `hostEnvironment(profile)` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:726-732), and the DEFAULT profile is `restricted` (`resolveEnvironmentProfile` :716-724 — `restricted` unless a caller explicitly asks otherwise). `restricted` is an ALLOWLIST, not a deny list: `RESTRICTED_HOST_ENVIRONMENT` (:703-711) admits 25 names plus an `LC_*` pattern — HOME/PATH/SHELL/USER/LOGNAME, locale and terminal vars, toolchain roots, the Windows quartet, and four NESSY_* doc-path vars. Nothing else from process.env crosses. So AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and NESSY_DP_AUTH_TOKEN are absent from a sandboxed command's environment by construction. `grep -ran "'trusted-host'"` over production source returns only the type declaration, the two enum validators and the supervisor's own comparison — no production caller requests it, and no bash path sets `inheritHostEnv: true` (local-tools/runtime.ts:398-404 is `processBinding`, a result-REPORTING projection back onto the observability record, not a start request). Claude's default is the inverse: the whole environment passes unless a variable is named in `credentials.envVars`. So what is absent is the CONFIGURABILITY — an administrator cannot name extra files or extra variables, and `mask` (which needs the TLS-terminating proxy R19 parked) has no analogue. The protection the doc sentence describes is not absent; it is on by default and not removable. 5) NOT a brand/gateway/subscription product difference — this is a settings-schema question, not renaming. 6) PROVENANCE. This row is the whats-new restatement of docs/superpowers/specs/data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json:3573-3574, and its `sandboxing.md` twin (phase1 :388-390) was already challenged and REFUTED in docs/superpowers/specs/data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase2-partial.json on grounds 3 and 4(a). I re-derived both from source rather than inheriting them, and added 4(b), the env-var half that verdict left as the one unrefuted piece.

column6: A response stream that emits no events for 5 minutes must be aborted and retried; the watchdog is on by default for every provider and is disabled by an env var.
column7: No streaming idle watchdog exists on any provider path. There is no abort-and-retry on stream silence and no on/off knob for one. The only 'watchdog' in the agent layer is the stdio-death watchdog for the Pi subprocess (pi-agent.ts:6053), which fires on process death, not on a silent stream; the compact RPC has an unrelated 300s timeout.

column9: 1) The sentence IS verbatim on the page (curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w27.md, last <div> of the 'Other wins' grid). The whole line was read; nothing in it reverses the claim. 2) The cited repo evidence does not say what the row says. packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6053 is inside requestCompact's 300s RPC timeout; the ONLY occurrence of 'watchdog' in that whole file is a COMMENT at :6076 ('truly hung subprocesses are caught by the stdio death watchdog') -- there is no stdio-death watchdog implementation in the agent layer, so the row's 'nearest neighbour' is a comment, not a mechanism. 3) The decisive error is the absolute 'no streaming idle watchdog exists on ANY provider path ... and no on/off knob for one'. The grep deliberately excluded node_modules, which is exactly where the Claude provider's turn loop lives. Our Claude provider path does not stream over its own HTTP client: packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1 imports query() from @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk and :1636 reads options.pathToClaudeCodeExecutable, which packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:271-296 points at the NATIVE upstream binary ('This is the native `claude` binary, not a JS file'). That binary implements the documented feature verbatim: grep -ra -l STREAM_WATCHDOG node_modules/ returns exactly one file, node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude, whose bundle carries the env registry entries CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS / CLAUDE_ENABLE_STREAM_WATCHDOG / CLAUDE_ENABLE_BYTE_WATCHDOG and, in the streaming turn loop, `Cr=je.CLAUDE_ENABLE_STREAM_WATCHDOG??ct("tengu_event_watchdog_default_on",!1)`. buildClaudeSubprocessEnv (options.ts:236-264) spreads process.env and deletes only the three Bedrock vars, so CLAUDE_ENABLE_STREAM_WATCHDOG=0 reaches the subprocess unchanged -- the on/off knob demonstrably exists on that path. Positive control for the absence half: the same grep over node_modules returns exactly one hit, so the search works; and the fork does have idle watchdogs in sibling subsystems (MCP connect-phase idle watchdog, packages/shared/src/mcp/validation.ts:230-419; MCP tool-call idle timeout NESSY_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT, packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:237-241), so 'no idle watchdog anywhere' would also be wrong -- naming the subsystem matters here. 4) Not an owner decision: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 lists nine decisions and none is this. column5: Transient server rate-limit errors unrelated to your usage limit are now retried automatically with backoff for subscribers instead of failing the turn
column6: A transient server rate-limit error that is not the account usage limit must be retried automatically with backoff rather than ending the turn.
column7: Both backends classify a rate limit and surface it to the user instead of retrying. claude-agent.ts carries the explicit comment 'Rate limit errors - don't retry immediately, surface to user' and then yields typed_error + complete; pi-agent.ts returns a `rate_limited` diagnostic with a manual 'Retry' action and retryDelayMs 5000. No backoff loop, and no distinction between a transient server 429 and the account usage limit. (Backoff retry does exist elsewhere — MCP connect, webhooks, session mirror — so the absence is specific to the model turn.)
column9: Doc sentence is verbatim (w27.md line 98, a single-clause <div> in 'Other wins'; no second sentence reverses it). Both cited code sites exist roughly as described, with line drift: the claude-agent.ts comment is at :2045 not :2023, and pi-agent.ts's rate_limited block is at :7644-7662 — the cited :7621-7636 is the invalid_api_key block, not the rate-limit one. But the CONSEQUENCE is false, and it is exactly the 'enforcement one layer down' false-positive shape that inert-worklist §4.3 warns about: both handlers are POST-EXHAUSTION terminal paths, not the first response to a transient 429. (1) PI BACKEND (the fork's default): the shipped Pi runtime auto-retries with exponential backoff, on by default. apps/electron/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js:590052 _prepareRetry computes `delayMs = settings.baseDelayMs * 2 ** (this._retryAttempt - 1)`; defaults are enabled:true (:599429 `return this.settings.retry?.enabled ?? true`), maxRetries:3, baseDelayMs:2000 (:599442-599443). _handlePostAgentRun (:589014) returns true after a successful _prepareRetry and the caller runs `await this.agent.continue()` (:589001) — the turn continues rather than failing. The transient-vs-usage-limit distinction the claim says does not exist is explicit and in the source: NON_RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_LIMIT_ERROR_PATTERN (:538149) = GoUsageLimitError, FreeUsageLimitError, 'Monthly usage limit reached', 'available balance', insufficient_quota, 'out of budget', 'quota exceeded', billing; RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN (:538159) = overloaded, rate.?limit, 'too many requests', 429, 500/502/503/504, and more; isRetryableAssistantError (:538194) retries only when the error matches the retryable set and NOT the usage-limit set. The HTTP layer enforces the same split independently: isRetryableError (:106449) returns false for `status===429 && isTerminalRateLimitError(errorText)` and true for other 429/5xx, and the loop at :107424 applies `BASE_DELAY_MS * 2 ** attempt` or the honored retry-after / retry-after-ms header. Nessy's own host is wired to surface this: packages/shared/src/agent/backend/pi/event-adapter.ts:900-915 maps auto_retry_start to a 'Retrying (attempt N/M)...' status and auto_retry_end to an error only when !success. packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js carries the identical code at shifted offsets. So parsePiError's rate_limited + manual Retry is what the user sees only after 3 backed-off retries have already failed. (2) CLAUDE BACKEND: the bundled Claude Agent SDK's HTTP client already retries 429 with backoff before any error reaches claude-agent.ts. node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.mjs shouldRetry: `if(e.status===408)return!0;if(e.status===409)return!0;if(e.status===429)return!0;if(e.status>=500)return!0;return!1`, with `maxRetries = n.maxRetries ?? 2` and a retryRequest that reads retry-after-ms then retry-after. The comment 'don't retry immediately, surface to user' is therefore correct in context — a host-level retry there would be a second, uncoordinated loop on top of the SDK's. (3) The fork's own error taxonomy contradicts the claim in plain text: packages/shared/src/agent/errors.ts:105-112 defines rate_limited with the message 'Rate limit reached. Will auto-retry shortly.' (4) Secondary: the doc sentence is scoped 'for subscribers' — a Claude Pro/Max subscription behaviour — and this fork ships NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE off by default and targets the Nestor corporate gateway, so the subscriber-scoped surface is largely outside the fork's default build anyway. Not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist §3. Positive control for the absence claim was established and it failed: the claim asserted backoff exists only in MCP connect / webhooks / session mirror and is absent from the model turn; grepping the model-turn path found it present in both backends.

column9: The doc sentence exists verbatim (2026-w28.md:50, a single-sentence <div> in 'Other wins'; the whole line was read and its second clause is the unrelated rm -rf item). The claimed OUR STATE is wrong on both of its load-bearing consequences.  (1) FILE TOOLS -- the decisive error. The claim says the protected-path floor fires on the .nessy-agent segment 'but in auto mode its outcome is routed to the classifier'. That is the CLAUDE DOC's table row (permission-modes.md:435-441), not our code. Our fork deliberately deviates and is STRICTER, and says so at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/protected-paths.ts:181-186: 'auto prompts, and the prompt reaches the HUMAN: the protected-path floor is nonNegotiable, and pi-agent.ts's autoBorderlineEligible refuses non-negotiable prompts, so the guardian classifier is never consulted for it. This is a deliberate deviation from the doc table's Routed to the classifier row -- a judge no_objection must not convert a floor into an allow.' Verified end to end, not from the comment: pre-tool-use.ts:1580-1590 emits the prompt with nonNegotiable:'protectedPath'; promptIsNonNegotiable (pre-tool-use.ts:681-687) returns true for it; pi-agent.ts:4051-4054 gates autoBorderlineEligible on !promptIsNonNegotiable(checkResult), so the guardian consult at :4094 is unreachable for this class. Positive probe of the real function on the real transcript path: findProtectedPathWrite('/Users/me/.nessy-agent/sessions/ws-1/sess-1/session.jsonl') returns {entry:'.nessy-agent', kind:'directory'}, and protectedPathOutcome('auto')='prompt', ('dontAsk')='deny', ('bypassPermissions')='allow'. A committed test pins it: pre-tool-use-checks.isolated.ts:2180-2186 loops ['ask','acceptEdits','auto'] and asserts prompt + nonNegotiable==='protectedPath' EVEN WITH an allow rule naming the path. So auto mode does not auto-approve a file-tool write to the transcript; it stops for a human, and dontAsk denies outright. That satisfies -- and exceeds -- the documented behaviour.  (2) BASH -- the claim's inference from self-config-deny.ts:31-34 is a misreading of what that deny list is for. The quoted comment is accurate on disk, but deniedWriteRoots is the belt for paths INSIDE a writable grant; it is not the only guard. The darwin/linux/win32 profiles are deny-by-default for writes: filesystem-isolation.ts:167-176 emits '(deny file-write*)' and then opens ONLY /dev/null, the writableRoot and additionalWritableRoots, and darwin.ts:34-48 sets writableRoot = workspaceRoot (networked/workspace profiles; credential-deny-roots.ts:15 names 'networked' as 'the shipped default for the foreground shell') plus scratchRoot. And scratchRoot is NOT <configDir>/sessions: process-store.ts:60 puts it at <SESSIONS_DIR>/.pi-processes/scratch, and process-supervisor.ts:138-145 narrows it further to a per-session sha256 subdirectory. <configDir>/sessions/<ws>/<id>/session.jsonl is therefore outside every writable grant and is denied by the floor -- no transcript-specific deny rule is needed. A measured positive control for exactly this already exists in-repo, in the sibling subsystem's note (bash-seatbelt.ts:74-80, the phase-4 sandbox probe under the real shipped profile): 'writes are still contained (a write to ~ returns Operation not permitted)'. ~/.nessy-agent/sessions/... is such a path.  Sibling-subsystem trap checked: the SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD owner decision (inert-worklist §3 item 1) belongs to packages/shared/src/agent/core/bash-seatbelt.ts, a DIFFERENT wrapper; its own comment states that buildDarwinSandboxProfile -- the profile the supervised-process isolation actually composes -- 'has no wildcard branch', so the wildcard does not open the transcript path.  The one literally-true fragment ('no rule names session transcript files as a protected target', and guardian.ts has no transcript-tampering rule -- confirmed, its only transcript mentions are :128 and :130 treating it as untrusted evidence) carries no consequence: coverage comes from the .nessy-agent segment one layer up, and the guardian is never consulted for this class anyway.

column9: Sentence and citation both check out; the finding still fails on subsystem and on consequence. (1) The quoted sentence exists VERBATIM at w28.md:50, as a whole one-clause <div> with nothing after it that reverses the conclusion. (2) removal-circuit-breaker.ts:71 and :83-86 say exactly what was claimed. (3) But that module is the WRONG SUBSYSTEM. It implements the permissions.md root/home floor (S4) — the breaker that fires in EVERY mode including bypassPermissions, whose documented scope is precisely 'removals targeting the filesystem root or home directory' (permissions.md:63). Its call site, pre-tool-use.ts:1186-1200, cites exactly that. Declining to fire on an unresolvable target is the CORRECT reading of that page: the qualifier is part of the contract, and the module's own rationale at :34-37 explains that a breaker firing on every computed argument gets routed around and then protects nothing. The w28 line is about AUTO MODE's classifier, a different and looser mechanism. This is the sibling-subsystem false positive the repo guide names. (4) The CONSEQUENCE, verified separately, is false — auto mode DOES prompt. An `rm -rf $VAR` in auto mode: AUTO_RISKY_BASH_PATTERNS[0] (pre-tool-use.ts:1751) matches `\brm\b`, so isRiskyAutoBashCommand (:2055-2065) returns true and the call lands in the prompt band. The guardian is then consulted, and GUARDIAN_POLICY_PROMPT orders exactly the documented behaviour: ':177' — 'When evaluating destructive local filesystem actions, especially rm -rf, attempt a read-only inspection of the target path first'; ':178' — 'If important context is missing and cannot be verified, lean conservative'; ':190' — 'Emit unsure when you genuinely cannot reach a confident no_objection or deny — missing evidence you could not resolve ... unsure routes the decision to the human; it is the correct fail-closed choice under real uncertainty. NEVER emit no_objection to resolve doubt.' An unresolvable variable is precisely a target the read-only inspection cannot resolve. `unsure` maps to GuardianConsultOutcome { kind: 'ask' } (guardian-consult.ts:68, :75), and the module contract at :23-27 states that a missing port, a disabled setting, an open circuit, an `unsure` verdict or any judge failure 'all resolve to the band's existing ASK behavior — fail-closed to a human, never to auto-run.' So the prompt happens whether the guardian runs, is disabled, or errors. The finding dismissed guardian.ts:150/:177 as 'about inspecting a specific local path' while skipping :178 and :190, which are the two lines that carry the unresolved-target case. (5) Not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist.md section 3 (checked; the nearest, #3 autoMode.classifyAllShell, is a different control and its band now exists at pre-tool-use.ts:2129+). Not a Nessy product difference either.

column7: The spawner enforces only a DEPTH limit (DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1, error 'Subagent depth limit exceeded'). There is no per-session spawn COUNT budget and no concurrency limit — a depth-1 loop can spawn unboundedly. Neither MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION nor MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS has a reader.
column8: packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:110 and :518-519; grep -ra -F for MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION / MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS over packages/ apps/ → 0 source hits
column9: Doc sentence verified verbatim (curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w29.md, line 63; it is a one-clause <div> in the digest-wins-grid, no second half that reverses it). The cited spawner lines are also accurate as far as they go: packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:110 is `export const DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1`, :518-519 is the `Subagent depth limit exceeded` return, and `grep -ra -F` for MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION / MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS over packages/ apps/ really is 0 hits. But the CONSEQUENCE is false, and it is false exactly in the recurring shape this repo's trap list names: the enforcement lives one layer up, in the host, not in the spawner. (1) A per-session spawn COUNT budget DOES exist. spawner.ts:600-608 forwards `budgets: { fanout: cfg.maxFanout ?? 100, concurrency: cfg.concurrency ?? DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY, ... }` to the host, and packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:148 enforces it inside the persisted-state commit: `if (children.length >= input.budgets.fanout) throw new Error('child-session-fanout-limit')`. `children` is the parent session's FULL child-record list; records are removed only on the cancelled-start rollback (:154), never on completion, so `children.length` is a CUMULATIVE per-session spawn count, not an active count. child-session-service.test.ts:178-184 proves the cumulative semantics: child-1 is stopped first, and a subsequent start with `fanout: 1` still throws `child-session-fanout-limit`. The value comes from `orchestrator.maxAgents` (pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1280 `maxFanout: config.orchestrator?.maxAgents`), default 1000 in DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:109); the spawner's own fallback when the host supplies nothing is 100. (2) A concurrency limit DOES exist, in BOTH layers. spawner.ts:144-208 defines a `Semaphore` sized by `computeEffectiveConcurrency(cfg.concurrency ?? 16)` = `max(1, min(ceiling, cpuCores - 2))`, rebuilt on every `configureSpawner` (:208), and every spawn goes through `semaphore.run(...)`. The host re-checks independently at child-session-service.ts:149: `if (active.length >= input.budgets.concurrency) throw new Error('child-session-concurrency-limit')`. Both are covered by tests (spawner.test.ts imports `computeEffectiveConcurrency`/`Semaphore`; child-session-service.test.ts:172 and :370 assert `child-session-concurrency-limit`). (3) 'A depth-1 loop can spawn unboundedly' is therefore false on two counts: the Nth spawn of a session is refused once N reaches the fanout budget, and at most min(16, cores-2) run at once meanwhile. Budgets are additionally clamped monotonically down the tree (SessionManager.ts:11142-11143 `Math.min(input.budgets.fanout, inherited.fanout)` / same for concurrency, and :4933-4934 pins a child's fanout/concurrency to 1), and the workflow tool carries its own per-run cap (workflow-tool.ts:562-563, `workflow maxAgents exceeded`). This is not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) and it is not a subscription/brand product difference; it is simply a wrong consequence drawn from a true identifier absence. What actually survives is a naming/default difference, not a missing mechanism.

The identifier half of the finding is true -- no key literally named `disableAutoMode` exists in our source -- but the CONSEQUENCE is false, and it is a recorded dated decision, which is the exact false-positive shape AGENTS.md warns about. (1) CONSEQUENCE REFUTED, wired end to end: an administrator disables auto mode with `disabledPermissionModes: ['auto']` in the host-owned managed policy. `ManagedPiPolicyV1.disabledPermissionModes` is a REQUIRED admin key (managed-policy.ts:81); `DISABLEABLE_MODES` (managed-policy.ts:649) admits `auto`; `disabledPermissionModeList` (managed-policy.ts:662) accepts Claude's spellings as well as ours. Enforcement is production, not test-only: SessionManager.normalizePiPermissionMode (:17342) -> normalizeManagedPermissionMode (mode-types.ts:133-152) demotes a request for `auto` down to acceptEdits/default/plan, which IS settings.md:258's 'Removes `auto` from the cycle and rejects `--permission-mode auto` at startup'. SessionManager.ts:4127-4129 additionally sets `autoModeUnavailable: true` on the turn runtime, and pi-agent.ts:4071 gates plan mode's classifier route off it, citing permission-modes.md:210 'Administrators can turn it off for the organization' and :156. So the finding's 'Auto mode can only be removed by ... the disabled-permission-mode list' is itself the admin-settable mechanism it says does not exist -- it names the answer and then calls it absent because the key spelling differs. (2) RECORDED DECISION with a reason: parity audit R30 (2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:698, the source of truth) -- 'Two of the five keys were already shipped under a better name -- `disableBypassPermissionsMode` and `disableAutoMode` are `disabledPermissionModes: ['allow-all']`/`['auto']`, and one list is strictly more expressive than two booleans, so no alias keys were added.' Restated as a verdict table row in plans/2026-07-29-doctor-surface.md:111 -- '`disableAutoMode` | documented, implemented -- as `disabledPermissionModes: ['auto']` | same set, same normalizer' -- and in specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:99 (R1). Commits 1f7c509b, 67a9b48d, e40c1ded, 4b55cb06, 92208602. Not one of the nine inert-worklist section 3 items (item 3 there is `autoMode.classifyAllShell`, a different key), but an equally binding dated decision. (3) THE FINDING'S OWN EVIDENCE LINE IS WRONG: it asserts 'grep -ra -F -l disableAutoMode lists only dist/resource bundles'. It does not. `grep -ra -F -l disableAutoMode .` also returns six tracked docs -- the parity audit, doctor-surface plan, deviation-unit-4, deviation-audit, deviation-worklist and r-queue-doc-verification -- which is precisely where the decision is recorded. The grep that would have refuted the finding was run and its hits were dropped. Cited line 405-420 is also drifted: the ManagedPiPolicyV1 interface opens at :79, and :405-420 is the availableModels/enforceAvailableModels block. Only :662 landed. (4) PRODUCT DIFFERENCE: the sentence's first clause (Bedrock / Google Agent Platform / Microsoft Foundry no longer needing the CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AUTO_MODE opt-in) is out of scope by design -- this fork targets the Nestor corporate gateway, drops those enterprise cloud provider paths, and renames CLAUDE_CODE_* to NESSY_* throughout.

column7: No reader for either name. This is the exact surface a corporate deployment (which is what this fork is) would need.
