column9: Step 1 passes, steps 2 and 3 fail. (1) The quoted sentence EXISTS VERBATIM at whats-new/2026-w29.md line 60 (raw markdown escapes the underscores exactly as quoted); it is a one-sentence <div> in the 'Other wins' grid with no reversing second half. The linked page corporate-launcher.md confirms the mechanism. (2) The cited evidence is wrong on both halves. packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts is NOT 'the Pi subprocess supervisor' - it is the supervisor for the shell/tool processes the agent runs on the user's behalf (ProcessSupervisorPort, matchExcludedCommand, resolveProcessIsolation). And its spawn is NOT unwrapped: line 244 reads `child = (this.options.spawnProcess ?? spawn)(plan?.command ?? request.command, plan?.args ?? args, { ... env: plan?.environment ?? processEnvironment ... })`, where `plan` comes from resolveProcessIsolation and rewrites the command into a sandbox invocation - the comment at :232 says so in as many words ('The REQUESTED command line, before isolation rewrote it into a sandbox invocation'). That spawn site already has wrapper indirection, just a sandbox one rather than a corporate launcher. This is the sibling-subsystem refutation shape: the file named is Claude's CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX territory, not CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER's - corporate-launcher.md:137 draws exactly that line ('CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER wraps Claude Code's own processes ... CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX wraps the shell commands Claude runs on your behalf, such as Bash tool calls, hooks, and the commands that start stdio MCP servers'). By that same sentence the claim's second example, 'the session MCP server', is also misfiled under this page. (3) The third example is false outright: background agent sessions in this fork spawn no executable at all. packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts drives children through an in-process ChildRuntime interface (start/resume/steer/stop/monitor) with zero child_process usage in the file. The consequence therefore does not follow from the identifier. Structurally, the process classes corporate-launcher.md:23-31 enumerates - the background service `claude agents` starts on demand, the terminal host and session in every agent view row plus warm standby, respawns after update or crash, the self-relaunch that finishes an update, Remote Control workers, agent-teams tmux/iTerm2 teammate panes - have no analog here. This is an Electron app whose update relaunch is autoUpdater.quitAndInstall (apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts:420), performed by Squirrel/electron-updater rather than by a spawn we control, which is the same category the page itself excludes for launchd/systemd-started services. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md row 129 already records corporate-launcher as a dated verdict, marked out of product. The identifier absence itself is real - grep -a over packages/ and apps/ for PROCESS_WRAPPER, processWrapper, SHELL_PREFIX, launcherPath, wrapperExecutable and processLauncher returns zero source hits - but the finding as written names the wrong subsystem, asserts an unwrapped spawn at a site that is wrapped, and attributes a consequence to two surfaces that either belong to a different Claude mechanism or spawn nothing.

Our CLI does render in-place spinner frames on a TTY (the exact 'spinners and in-place redraws' the mode is meant to replace) and exposes only `--no-spinner`/`--disable-spinner`, which suppresses the animation but does not switch to labelled linear output. column8: apps/cli/src/index.ts:266-275 (spinner) and :116-118 (--no-spinner); grep -ra -F for axScreenReader / AX_SCREEN_READER → 0 hits
column9:
Steps 1 and 2 pass on the identifiers; step 3 fails on the CONSEQUENCE, on three independent grounds. This is the repo's recurring shape #3 (identifier genuinely absent, asserted consequence false) compounded with shape #4 (the wrong subsystem named). (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: confirmed. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w29.md line 41 carries the sentence exactly, including the escaped underscores, as the SECOND sentence of a two-sentence

. Reading the whole line, the first sentence does not reverse the conclusion but it does scope it decisively: 'Screen reader mode replaces the visual terminal interface with plain, linear text: instead of boxes, spinners, and in-place redraws, Claude Code prints labeled lines that a screen reader such as VoiceOver or NVDA reads in order, so you can approve permissions and review output end to end.' The feature's pill (line 38) is 'CLI', and the flag is shown at line 46 as `claude --ax-screen-reader`. The mode is a replacement for Claude Code's full-screen Ink conversation TUI. (2) CITED FILE:LINE: confirmed. apps/cli/src/index.ts:116-118 is `case '--disable-spinner': case '--no-spinner': noSpinner = true`. :266 is the comment 'Spinner (TTY only - skipped when piped or NO_COLOR)', :269 the braille frame array, :271 createSpinner, :275 the first-frame write. `grep -ra` (with -a, so the NUL-byte trap does not apply) for axScreenReader / AX_SCREEN_READER returns 17 hits and ZERO are product code: every one is this doc-sweep's own JSON/markdown rows, plus one unrelated 'screen-reader focus' prose comment in CompactPanelTransition.tsx:40. The three identifiers really are absent. (3a) WRONG SUBSYSTEM. The doc's own sentence scopes the mode to the surface where you 'approve permissions and review output end to end'. In this fork that surface is the Electron GUI, not the CLI - and a GUI is the case screen reader mode does not apply to, because VoiceOver/NVDA read the DOM accessibility tree natively. Claude's text mode exists precisely because a TUI has no accessibility tree. The fork's GUI does have one: 286 ARIA/role attributes across apps/electron/src/renderer + packages/ui/src (113 aria-label, 47 aria-hidden, 8 role="dialog" with 5 aria-modal, 7 role="alert" and 5 role="status" live regions, 5 aria-activedescendant, plus role=listbox/option/menu/radiogroup). Naming the CLI as the diverging subsystem is the `disallowed-tools`-for-subagents-not-skills error. (3b) THE PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD FOR OUR CLI EITHER. `nessy-general-agent` is declared a 'Terminal client for Nessy Desktop server' (apps/cli/package.json), and it is not a TUI: `grep -acP '[\x{2500}-\x{257F}]'` over index.ts returns 0 box-drawing characters; no ink / blessed / ora / boxen appears in any package.json in the repo; and the ONLY in-place redraw escape sequences in the entire apps/cli/src tree are the two ` \x1b[2K` writes inside createSpinner (:277, :284) - client.ts, doctor.ts, plugin.ts and server-spawner.ts have none. The spinner has exactly ONE call site in the whole CLI, :1905-1906 inside runValidation, i.e. the `--validate-server` command's per-step progress display. It never appears on the conversational path at all: that path (:470-539) is strictly append-only - `text_delta` appends raw text (:476), and a tool start prints ` [tool: - ] ` (:488), which is literally a labelled line read in order. So the CLI already emits, unconditionally and with no flag, the output shape the mode is designed to produce. There is no 'visual terminal interface' here to replace. (3c) THE STATED CONSEQUENCE IS BACKWARDS. 'suppresses the animation but does not switch to labelled linear output' is measurably false. Suppressing the spinner is exactly what leaves labelled linear output, because runValidation's non-spinner path prints nothing but -terminated labelled lines: ensureHeader :1921 `[i/N] `, :1923 ` -> ""`, flushText :1914 ` |> `, :1959 ` |> tool: `, the per-step result :1981 `[i/N] ..... OK (time)` with failures to stderr :1992, and the summary :2006/:2008 `OK 3/3 passed in 1.2s`. Every line is newline-terminated and prefixed with an explicit `[i/N]` step label. The spinner is the single thing standing between this command and that output, and --no-spinner removes it. (3d) 'NONE OF THE THREE EXISTS' ALSO OVERSTATES. The gate at :1905 is `_useColor && !noSpinner`, where `_useColor = !process.env.NO_COLOR && process.stdout.isTTY !== false` (:254). So the flag half exists twice (--no-spinner, --disable-spinner), a per-shell environment variable (NO_COLOR) reaches the same suppression, and piping does too; --json (:1899) disables the event printer entirely. Two of the doc's three axes - per-session flag and per-shell env var - have working counterparts for the only animated output the CLI has. Only the persistent settings key has none. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 - all nine are unrelated (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, and three SessionMirrorStore rows). It is, however, a consequence of the deliberate product shape: the fork's primary surface is an Electron GUI and its CLI is a thin RPC client rather than a conversational TUI, which is the same TUI-vs-GUI mismatch already recorded for the sibling accessibility rows (see the phase-1 note on `accessibility`: 'the screen-reader half describes a TUI and does not bind an Electron GUI').

column9: The quote is real and the identifier really is absent, but the stated CONSEQUENCE is demonstrably false and inverted — this is trap shape #3 from inert-worklist.md §4 ('the identifier really is unwired while the consequence is false, because something upstream already handled it'). (1) QUOTE — verbatim at whats-new/2026-w29.md:62, fetched with curl -sL. It is a one-sentence <div> in the 'Other wins' grid; nothing in the line or its neighbours (:61 vimInsertModeRemaps, :63 session-wide caps) reverses it. (2) IDENTIFIER — confirmed absent. grep -ran -F over the whole repo for 'forward-subagent-text', 'FORWARD_SUBAGENT' and 'forwardSubagent' returns hits ONLY in docs/superpowers/specs sweep artifacts; zero in packages/, apps/, scripts/, and zero even in the vendored Claude Agent SDK bundles. No flag, no env var, no camelCase reader. (3) CONSEQUENCE — FALSE, and inverted. The claim says we have 'no way to include subagent text or thinking blocks' in stream-json. In fact BOTH are included unconditionally. apps/cli/src/index.ts:469-471 is the entire stream-json path: `if (streamJson) { process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(ev) + '\n') }` — every session:event is serialised verbatim, and the only guard above it is the same-session check at :467. The parentToolUseId filtering that would exclude subagent text exists but is scoped exclusively to the NON-stream-json branches (:481 `!streamJson && !structuredMode && !sawTextDelta && !ev.parentToolUseId`, :485). The comment at :479-480 makes the intent explicit: 'Subagent (Task) child turns emit non-intermediate text_complete with parentToolUseId set'. Nothing upstream strips them either: SessionManager.sendEvent (:18449-18460) forwards every SessionEvent unconditionally, and parentToolUseId is CARRIED ONTO the emitted event (:17698, :17740), never used to suppress. Both backends populate it (claude/event-adapter.ts:398,409 from parent_tool_use_id; tool-matching.ts:189,207). THINKING likewise: there is no separate 'thinking' member of the AgentEvent union (core/src/types/message.ts:966-999) because pi/event-adapter.ts converts it into ordinary text events — :554-564 yields `text_delta` with turnId 'thinking-N' on thinking_delta, and flushThinking (:316-333) yields `text_complete` with isIntermediate:true on thinking_end (the file's own header comment at :144 states 'message_update (thinking_delta/thinking_end) -> intermediate text_delta/text_complete'). Those are session:events, so :470 dumps them too. EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED by executing sendAndStream against a stub client: with outputFormat 'stream-json' the output contained all four lines including {"type":"text_complete",...,"text":"SUBAGENT SAID THIS","parentToolUseId":"toolu_99"} and {"type":"text_complete",...,"text":"INNER THINKING","isIntermediate":true,"turnId":"thinking-1"}. POSITIVE CONTROL (required for an absence-of-filtering claim): the identical event sequence with outputFormat 'text' printed only 'plan-a' — the subagent line and the thinking completion were both suppressed. So the filtering machinery exists and demonstrably works on the same rig; it simply does not apply to stream-json. NOT an owner decision: none of the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) touches the CLI output surface. NOT a de-brand artifact for the flag half (the fork adopts Claude's exact spellings where it has implemented the headless contract — --output-format, --json-schema, --safe-mode), though the CLAUDE_CODE_ env prefix would never be adopted verbatim given the NESSY_ convention. The finding is refuted on its consequence: it reports a missing capability where the capability is unconditionally on.

column9:

(1) DOC: curl -sL of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w29.md yields the sentence VERBATIM at line 59, inside the 'Other wins' grid: 'New claude auto-mode reset restores the default auto-mode configuration, and `--yes` skips the confirmation prompt'. The whole line is that single

(2) CITED STATE: literally accurate. `grep -ra -F 'auto-mode reset' packages/ apps/ scripts/` (with -a, so NUL-byte files are not skipped) returns 0 hits. apps/cli/src/index.ts:2120-2168 dispatches help, version, run, validate, doctor, plugin ahead of the server-URL requirement and the switch at :2186-:2240 adds ping/health/versions/workspaces/sessions/connections/sources/session/send/cancel/invoke/listen — no auto-mode group anywhere, and printHelp (:2019-2105) lists none. It requires Claude Code v2.1.212 or later and removes the `autoMode` section from your user settings file' — and the line after the code block pins the boundary: 'Reset changes only `~/.claude/settings.json`: `autoMode` rules from managed settings or the `--settings` flag still apply.' In Nessy, `autoMode` exists ONLY as a host-owned managed-policy block — the exact scope reset explicitly does NOT touch. It is a member of MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:522), there is no `autoMode` key anywhere in packages/shared/src/config, and `resolveAutoMode` has exactly ONE production caller, packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4109 — `resolveAutoMode({ managed: this.managedPiPolicy.autoMode })` — which passes no `user` scope and no `defaults` argument (the `project` scope is deliberately parsed and discarded as a supply-chain hole, pinned by managed-policy.test.ts:1030-1032). So (a) there is no user-settings autoMode section for `reset` to remove, and (b) there is no built-in default rule list to 'restore': the '$defaults' sentinel (AUTO_MODE_DEFAULTS_SENTINEL, managed-policy.ts:478) splices an empty array in the production call shape, pinned by managed-policy.test.ts:1025 expecting ['x']. Nessy's auto mode is a guardian LLM judge fed admin-authored prose (prompts/guardian.ts:382-383 appends an '## Organization policy' section to an unconditional built-in GUARDIAN_POLICY_PROMPT), not Claude's classifier with a user-editable prose rulebook. Sibling-subsystem check: `managedAutoMode` is Pi-only (SessionManager.ts:4108 gates on provider === 'pi'); no second implementation elsewhere. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in inert-worklist §3 — item 3 there is `autoMode.classifyAllShell`, a different key — but it IS a plan-recorded scope decision: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-auto-mode-policy.md:430-436 'Deliberately out of scope … The denial-review flow and `auto-mode` CLI subcommands — a UI and CLI surface, not a decision path.' It is already carried in the generated deviation register (2026-07-29-deviation-register.md, plans/2026-07-30-manifest-mode-and-aliases.md section: 'auto-mode-config.md:246 gives the classifier three CLI subcommands … reset removes the autoMode section from user settings. Nessy resolves those sets into the judge prompt and has no surface that prints or resets them'). Finally, f241 is a strict subset of f122 (auto-mode-config, the same four-subcommand family including reset), which this series already adjudicated refuted=true on the same grounds.

Not an owner decision: 'fallback' does not appear anywhere in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md, and none of the nine dated decisions in section 3 touches it. Not a de-brand or dropped-subscription product difference either — this is a Pi-runtime retry knob our fork implements itself, on its primary runtime. Sibling-subsystem check: the key is Pi-only; packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts never sets `fallbackModel`, so naming Pi is correct and the Claude backend has no fallback at all. f242 duplicates f226 (whats-new/2026-w24) and overlaps f106 (model-config) and f113 (admin-setup) — same underlying single-string arity, restated by the digest index; duplication corroborates rather than refutes. column6: A configured MCP server can be authenticated and de-authenticated from the shell, outside the interactive menu.
column7: The CLI has no `mcp` subcommand at all, so neither `login` nor `logout` exists. MCP OAuth is reachable only through the app's interactive surfaces; there is no shell path to authenticate a server or to clear its stored credentials.

column9: Quote verified verbatim at line 36 of the fetched page (curl, not WebFetch); the whole line is that one sentence and the block's second paragraph is a separate 'Also this week' line, so nothing reverses it. The cited file is accurate too: apps/cli/src/index.ts:2120-2245 dispatches help/version/run/validate/doctor/plugin/ping/health/versions/workspaces/sessions/connections/sources/session/send/cancel/invoke/listen and has no 'mcp' branch. But the finding's CONSEQUENCE is false, which is the exact 'identifier unwired, consequence handled one layer up' shape this repo's audit history warns about. The headless server the CLI talks to registers the OAuth handlers (packages/server/src/index.ts:265 -> registerCoreRpcHandlers -> registerOAuthHandlers in packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/index.ts), and those channels take an MCP-server target directly: oauth:start accepts pluginServer {pluginKey, serverName} (oauth.ts:467-495) and oauth:revoke accepts the same (oauth.ts:728-747), calling deletePluginMcpServerCredentials, which deletes both the oauth and bearer credential rows (packages/shared/src/plugins/mcp-credentials.ts:71-83). Neither needs an interactive surface: assertPendingAuthRequestBinding returns early when sessionId and authRequestId are both absent (oauth.ts:776-778), so there is no session or pending auth-request prerequisite. The CLI reaches them through its documented raw-RPC verb, 'invoke <channel> [json-args...]' (apps/cli/src/index.ts:915-935, listed in printHelp), which applies no channel allowlist. So `nessy-general-agent invoke oauth:revoke '{"pluginServer":{...}}'` is a complete, non-interactive, shell-only equivalent of `claude mcp logout`, and `invoke oauth:start '{"pluginServer":{...}}'` starts the login flow from the shell and returns {authUrl,state,flowId}; only the authorization-code capture is manual, because oauth:complete takes {flowId, code, state} (oauth.ts:580-584) and the local callback listener is run by the desktop/electron client rather than by the CLI. Two secondary points. (1) The stated evidence 'grep -ra -F "mcp login" over packages/ apps/ -> 0 hits' is itself wrong: hits exist in apps/electron/dist/resources/bin/codex/darwin-x64/codex-app-server, but they are Codex's own `codex mcp login` strings, i.e. a sibling subsystem, so they do not support the finding either. (2) The absence of a named CLI mcp namespace is a product-shape difference already on record, not an unnoticed gap: this fork's CLI is a thin websocket client to the desktop/headless server and carries no mcp verbs at all (no add/list/remove either), and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-deviation-unit-3.md:291 already records 'documented, impossible on Nessy - no `claude mcp list` equivalent' for exactly this surface, with docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-31-plugin-install-usability.md:341 recording the related per-server-vs-one-system-login deviation for dp-backed servers. It is not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3.

column9: All three checks pass, and the one layer down makes our state WORSE than claimed, not better.  1. QUOTE — CONFIRMED verbatim. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/index.md` line 92, inside the `<Update label="Week 19" ... tags={["v2.1.128-v2.1.136"]}>` block: "**Plugins load from `.zip` archives and URLs**: `--plugin-dir` now accepts `.zip` files, and `--plugin-url` fetches a plugin archive for the current session." Read the WHOLE line: it is a single sentence, no second half, nothing that reverses the conclusion. The next paragraph is the unrelated `Also this week:` line (worktree.baseRef, auto-mode hard deny, `$CLAUDE_EFFORT`). Corroborated by the coverage map's own row 164 summary for `whats-new/2026-w19` ("Load plugins from .zip archives and URLs...").  2. OUR STATE — CONFIRMED, with the evidence command corrected. `grep -rna --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' -a` for `plugin-dir` over `packages/*/src apps/*/src` -> 0 hits; `plugin-url` and `pluginUrl` -> 0 hits anywhere in the tree (checked with `-a`, so NUL-byte files are not silently skipped). The only `plugin-dir` hits are vendored/binary, exactly as claimed: `packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js:344897` and `:350336`, plus the mirrored `apps/electron/{,dist/}resources/...` copies and the Codex binaries. Line 344897 is worth naming precisely, because it is the bundled Claude Agent SDK's OWN argv builder -- `V3.push(je3.skipMcpDiscovery ? "--plugin-dir-no-mcp" : "--plugin-dir", je3.path)` for its `plugins: [{type:'local', path}]` option (`node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:1683 plugins?: SdkPluginConfig[]`). So the capability is physically present in a dependency we ship and we do not use it. `apps/cli/src/index.ts:2060-2066` confirms the CLI surface is only `plugin validate <path>` / `plugin list` / `plugin details <name>` -- all read-only inspection, no side-load.  3. CONSEQUENCE, tested separately from the identifier.    ONE LAYER UP (does something upstream already handle it?) -- partly, and the claim already concedes the right half. We DO classify a URL and a local path as install sources: `packages/shared/src/plugins/source-resolver.ts:85` (`kind: 'url'`) and `:97` (`kind: 'local-path'`), mapped at `:461-470` to `archive-url` / `local-path` artifacts and dispatched in `packages/shared/src/plugins/install-service.ts:503-537`. So "acquire a plugin from a URL or a local path" exists. What does NOT exist is the session-scoped half: `packages/shared/src/plugins/types.ts:4` is `export type PluginScope = 'user/global' | 'workspace' | 'project'` -- every scope is persistent, there is no ephemeral/session scope, and a repo-wide search for a session/side-load plugin concept returns only unrelated `session-scoped tools` hits. The Claude backend additionally shuts the SDK's own route off on purpose: `packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1627-1629` hardcodes `plugins: []` with the comment "No plugins -- skills are handled by BaseAgent.chat() via read-before-execute (the model reads SKILL.md files directly, enforced by PrerequisiteManager)".    ONE LAYER DOWN (is the `.zip` half as good as claimed?) -- NO, it is weaker. The claim's parenthetical "which does handle .zip and .mcpb archives internally" is too generous. Zip extraction is MCPB-ONLY: both call sites gate on `isZipArchive(...) && (hasMcpbArchiveExtension(path) || await hasRootMcpbManifest(path))` -- `install-service.ts:569-573` (local path) and `:805-809` (archive URL) -- and `hasRootMcpbManifest` requires a ROOT `manifest.json` (`packages/shared/src/plugins/mcpb-archive.ts:33-39`, `extractMcpbArchive` throws "MCPB archive must contain a valid root manifest.json"). A Claude-layout plugin zip is rooted at `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, so it misses that gate: locally it falls to `copyInside(...)` and is stored as an opaque FILE, and over a URL it falls to `extractArchiveFile` (`install-service.ts:1314-1352`), which is a **tar** extractor (`extractTar({file, cwd, strip})`) and cannot read a zip at all.    POSITIVE CONTROL for that absence, committed in-repo: `packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/mcpb.test.ts:77-88`, "preserves the legacy local-file path for an ordinary ZIP" -- a zip containing `plugin/plugin.json` stages to `readdirSync(staged.rawDirectory) === ['ordinary.zip']` and `existsSync(join(rawDirectory,'plugin','plugin.json')) === false`. The sibling test at `:90-100` proves the rig CAN unpack a zip when a root `manifest.json` is present, so the absence is a real gate, not a broken harness.  NOT AN OWNER DECISION. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` section 3 carries nine dated decisions (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions). None concerns plugin side-loading or archive formats.  NOT A DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE. This is not a Claude/ChatGPT subscription flow, not gateway-specific, and not a rename. AGENTS.md puts plugins and the format adapters squarely inside the Claude-docs contract scope, and the fork already invested in a full multi-format install pipeline (repository, npm, manifest-url, archive-url, local-path, mcpb, gitlab-skill, skill-files) -- an archive format it cannot open is a gap in that pipeline, not a scoping choice. That was filed as f019 and refuted there on a different ground (wrong consequence for `pluginTrustMessage`); it is not this row.
